records.title: CALGB 9344 (INT 0148)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2003
records.body: Node-positive early breast cancer (HER2 status retrospective) AC ×4 followed by paclitaxel ×4 vs AC ×4 alone (adjuvant); factorial comparison of three doxorubicin dose levels Disease-free survival Factorial phase III Intergroup trial (N=3,121, node-positive) testing doxorubicin dose escalation (60/75/90 mg/m²) and four cycles of paclitaxel after four cycles of cyclophosphamide-doxorubicin. Dose escalation gave no survival gain (5-year DFS 69%/66%/67%) but more long-term cardiotoxicity (16%/13%/11% at 90/75/60 mg/m², P=.0032 trend). Paclitaxel reduced recurrence 17% (HR 0.83, P=.0023) and death 18% (HR 0.82, P=.0064); 5-year DFS 70% vs 65%, OS 80% vs 77%. An unplanned, author-cautioned subset found larger benefit in receptor-negative (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.86) than receptor-positive disease (HR 0.91, 0.78-1.07). A HER2 companion analysis (Hayes 2007) found the paclitaxel benefit concentrated in HER2-positive disease regardless of ER status (interaction HR 0.59 for recurrence), with little gain in HER2-negative/ER-positive tumors (>50% of patients). Authors framed CA→paclitaxel as a reasonable choice for some patients, not a new standard.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2003;21:976-983   N Engl J Med 2007;357:1496-1506 HER2 predictive companion analysis 17928597

records.title: CALGB 9741
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2003
records.body: Node-positive early breast cancer Dose-dense AC → paclitaxel (Q2W with G-CSF) vs conventional Q3W scheduling, in a 2×2 also comparing sequential (doxorubicin → paclitaxel → cyclophosphamide) vs concurrent (AC → paclitaxel); adjuvant Disease-free survival 2×2 factorial Intergroup trial (N=2,005, node-positive) varying schedule (every 2 weeks with filgrastim vs every 3 weeks) and sequence (sequential doxorubicin→paclitaxel→cyclophosphamide vs concurrent AC→paclitaxel) at fixed doses. Dose-dense scheduling improved DFS (RR 0.74, P=.010; 4-year DFS 82% vs 75%) and OS (RR 0.69, P=.013), with no effect of sequence and no density-by-sequence interaction. Grade 4 granulocytopenia was less frequent with dose density (6% vs 33%, P<.0001). First report at 36 months' median follow-up with 315 of 515 expected events; the authors state confidence in the OS benefit at longer follow-up "remains to be firmly established".

records.title: NSABP B-28
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2005
records.body: Node-positive early breast cancer AC ×4 followed by paclitaxel ×4 vs AC ×4 alone; adjuvant, node-positive Disease-free survival Phase III adjuvant trial (N=3,060, node-positive) of four cycles of paclitaxel 225 mg/m² after four cycles of AC vs AC alone; median follow-up 64.6 months. Paclitaxel reduced DFS events 17% (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95, P=.006; 5-year DFS 76% vs 72%) with no significant OS gain (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.78-1.12, P=.46; 5-year OS 85% both arms). Hormone-receptor subgroups showed no significant interaction (DFS P=.30) but ran opposite to CALGB 9344's on DFS (receptor-positive RR 0.77 vs receptor-negative 0.90), agreeing in sense only on recurrence-free interval. An independent second test of CALGB 9344's question in a better-prognosis population (70% with one to three positive nodes vs 46%); its mortality result is not statistically different from CALGB 9344's.

records.title: ECOG E1199
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2008
records.body: Node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer After AC ×4: paclitaxel vs docetaxel, each given weekly vs every 3 weeks (2×2 taxane type × schedule); adjuvant Disease-free survival 2×2 factorial Intergroup trial (N=4,950, node-positive or high-risk node-negative) of paclitaxel vs docetaxel, weekly vs every 3 weeks, after four cycles of AC. Both prespecified primary comparisons were null: taxane type HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.91-1.17, P=.61) and schedule HR 1.06 (P=.33), with a significant taxane-by-schedule interaction (P=.003 DFS) the authors say complicates interpretation. Against the shared paclitaxel-every-3-week reference (HR >1 favours the experimental arm), weekly paclitaxel improved DFS (1.27, 98.3% CI 1.03-1.57, P=.006) and OS (1.32, P=.01); docetaxel every 3 weeks improved DFS only (1.23, 1.00-1.52, P=.02; OS 1.13, P=.25); weekly docetaxel neither. Grade 2-4 neuropathy 27% vs 20% with weekly paclitaxel. No experimental arm was tested against another.

records.title: US Oncology 9735
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2006
records.body: Stage I-III early breast cancer (node-neg and node-pos) TC ×4 (docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) vs AC ×4 (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²), each IV Q3W; adjuvant Disease-free survival TC (docetaxel/cyclophosphamide) significantly improved 5-year disease-free survival versus AC (doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide) in operable stage I-III breast cancer (86% vs 80%; HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.50-0.94, p=0.015), with a favorable trend in overall survival (90% vs 87%; HR 0.76, p=0.13) and no cardiotoxicity signal. At the 7-year update both endpoints were significant: DFS 81% vs 75% (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.56-0.98, P=.033) and OS 87% vs 82% (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50-0.97, P=.032), with no interaction by hormone-receptor or HER2 status. Established TC as a standard anthracycline-free adjuvant option.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2006;24:5381-5387   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:1177-1183 7-yr OS update 19204201

records.title: ABC trials (USOR 06-090/B-46-I/B-49)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2017
records.body: High-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer Pooled analysis of three adjuvant trials: TC ×6 (docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², Q3W) vs standard taxane-plus-anthracycline (TaxAC) regimens ×6 (e.g. TAC, or AC → paclitaxel) Invasive disease-free survival Joint analysis of three adjuvant trials (N=4,242, high-risk HER2-negative) of TC ×6 vs a standard taxane-plus-anthracycline regimen (TaxAC), testing noninferiority of TC against a prespecified 1.18 margin (HR >1 favours TaxAC). The interim futility boundary was crossed (HR 1.202) and the ITT analysis showed statistical inferiority of TC: IDFS HR 1.23 (95% CI 1.01-1.50, P=.04), 4-year IDFS 88.2% vs 90.7%. At 6.9 years noninferiority still could not be declared (HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.99-1.32, P=.08; prespecified 80% CI 1.04-1.25 does not exclude 1.18); recurrence-free interval stayed significant (HR 1.38, P=.0003) while OS did not differ (HR 1.05, P=.64), TaxAC's recurrence reduction offset by more leukaemias (7 vs 1) and non-breast-cancer deaths. Benefit concentrated in hormone-receptor-negative disease (RFI HR 1.90).
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2647-2655   J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1344-1349 long-term follow-up 38335467

records.title: EBCTCG 15-year overview
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · N/A · 2005
records.body: Early breast cancer (194 randomized trials of adjuvant chemotherapy or hormonal therapy begun by 1995) Anthracycline-based or CMF polychemotherapy vs none or each other; ~5 vs 1–2 years vs no tamoxifen Recurrence; breast cancer mortality (15-year) Foundational EBCTCG overview showing that the proportional risk reductions from adjuvant systemic therapy persist to 15 years. About 6 months of anthracycline-based polychemotherapy reduced the annual breast cancer death rate by ~38% in women <50 and ~20% at age 50–69, largely independent of ER and nodal status, and significantly more than CMF. In ER-positive disease, ~5 years of tamoxifen reduced the annual breast cancer death rate by 31%; because annual mortality is similar in years 0–4 and 5–14, the cumulative 15-year mortality benefit is more than double that at 5 years (carry-over effect). Superseded in regimen- and endocrine-specific detail by the later EBCTCG polychemotherapy (2012) and tamoxifen (2011) meta-analyses.

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · N/A · 2012
records.body: Early breast cancer (123 randomized trials) Various polychemotherapy regimens vs no chemo or each other Recurrence; breast cancer mortality Individual-patient meta-analysis of 123 trials (~100,000 women) comparing chemotherapy regimens; dose-density and stem-cell trials excluded. Adding four cycles of a taxane to a fixed anthracycline backbone reduced breast cancer mortality (RR 0.86, 2p=0.0005), but not where controls received counterbalancing extra non-taxane cycles (RR 0.94, 2p=0.33). Standard 4AC and standard CMF were equivalent (RR 0.98, 2p=0.67), while higher-cumulative-dose regimens (CAF/CEF) beat CMF (RR 0.78, 2p=0.0004) on a significant dose-response trend (2p=0.005); cardiac mortality rose with any anthracycline (RR 1.56, 2p=0.02). Proportional reductions were little affected by age, ER status, or nodal status. The "about one-third" headline is a calculated product of two measured RRs (0.775 × 0.825 = 0.64), not a direct comparison; absolute gain depends on baseline risk without chemotherapy.

records.title: NSABP B-18 & B-27
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · III · 2008
records.body: Operable breast cancer (neoadjuvant) B-18: preoperative vs postoperative AC ×4 (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², Q3W). B-27: preoperative AC ×4 then surgery, ± docetaxel 100 mg/m² Q3W ×4 given either before surgery (neoadjuvant) or after (adjuvant); tamoxifen 20 mg/d ×5 years in all Disease-free / overall survival B-18 (n=1,493 eligible) randomised operable breast cancer to identical AC given before or after surgery: at 16 years neither overall survival (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.85-1.16, P=.90) nor disease-free survival (HR 0.93, 0.81-1.06, P=.27) differed, a null superiority comparison the authors report as equivalence, while preoperative therapy raised breast-conserving surgery (68% vs 60%, P=.001). A significant treatment-age interaction for OS (P=.01) favoured preoperative timing under age 50 (HR 0.81, P=.06) and postoperative timing at 50+ (HR 1.23, P=.07). In B-27 (8.5 years), adding preoperative docetaxel doubled pCR (13% to 26%, P<.001) without improving DFS (HR 0.92, 0.78-1.08, P=.29). pCR was strongly prognostic in both (OS HR 0.32 in B-18, 0.36 in B-27; both P<.0001). Establishes neoadjuvant timing, and the founding instance of the pCR trial-level surrogacy gap CTNeoBC later confirms at pooled scale.

records.title: EBCTCG neoadjuvant meta-analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2018
records.body: Early breast cancer (10 randomised trials begun before 2005) Neoadjuvant chemotherapy vs identical adjuvant chemotherapy Tumour response; local & distant recurrence; breast cancer mortality Patient-level meta-analysis of ten trials (4,756 women, entry 1983-2002, median follow-up 9 years) comparing NACT with the identical adjuvant regimen. NACT raised breast-conserving therapy (65% vs 49%) but increased 15-year local recurrence (21.4% vs 15.9%; RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.17-1.61, p=0.0001), with no significant difference in distant recurrence (RR 1.02, 0.92-1.14), breast cancer mortality (RR 1.06, 0.95-1.18) or all-cause mortality (RR 1.04, 0.94-1.15; all p>0.3). The local-recurrence excess is not wholly explained by good responders skipping surgery: it was largest in the two trials that permitted omission of surgery (10-year RR 1.62, 1.20-2.19) but persisted in the other eight, where surgery was scheduled irrespective of response (RR 1.28, 1.06-1.55), with no significant heterogeneity between the two sets (p=0.19). Timing costs no survival; the local-control cost is real, and dated to a largely pre-taxane, pre-trastuzumab evidence base.

records.title: CTNeoBC pooled analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2014
records.body: Early breast cancer across subtypes (12 neoadjuvant trials) Neoadjuvant chemotherapy ± trastuzumab (pCR vs no pCR; patient- & trial-level analysis) pCR association with EFS & OS; trial-level surrogacy FDA-led pooled analysis of 12 neoadjuvant trials (11,955 patients, all subtypes) underpinning accelerated-approval use of pCR. It settled the definition: clearing tumour from breast and nodes (ypT0 ypN0 or ypT0/is ypN0) predicted OS better (HR 0.36 for both) than clearing the breast alone (ypT0/is, HR 0.51). At patient level pCR (ypT0/is ypN0) strongly predicted EFS (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.43-0.54) and OS (HR 0.36, 0.31-0.42), strongest in TNBC (EFS HR 0.24) and in HER2+/HR-negative disease given trastuzumab (EFS HR 0.15). But at trial level, larger pCR gains did not predict EFS (R2=0.03, 95% CI 0.00-0.25) or OS (R2=0.24, 0.00-0.70) gains, far below the ~0.75 conventionally required to validate a surrogate. The filed 2023 HER2-positive re-analysis (11 trials, 3,980 patients) reproduced the same split within a single subtype: strong patient-level association (EFS OR 2.64, OS OR 3.15; OR >1 favours pCR) but weak trial-level R2 (0.23 EFS, 0.02 OS).
records.keywords: Lancet 2014;384:164-172   J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2988-2997 HER2+ re-evaluation 36977286

records.title: Residual Cancer Burden (Symmans)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2017
records.body: Breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (5 cohorts; HR+/HER2-, HER2+, TNBC) Residual Cancer Burden index after NACT (RCB-0/pCR, RCB-I, RCB-II, RCB-III) Relapse-free survival by RCB class Pooled five-cohort validation at a single institution (n=1,158; retrospective pathology review with prospective follow-up, not a randomised trial) establishing Residual Cancer Burden as a continuous, graded index of residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (pCR = RCB-0; predefined cut points 1.36 and 3.28). 10-year RFS by class (pCR/RCB-I/II/III): triple-negative 86/81/55/23%; HR+/HER2- 83/97/74/52%, not monotonic, with pCR itself entering the multivariable model as a paradoxical predictor (HR 5.03, 95% CI 1.60-15.78) on small numbers; HER2+ treated with trastuzumab 95/77/47/21%. RCB index was the sole independently prognostic variable in triple-negative (HR 1.92, 1.49-2.46) and trastuzumab-treated HER2+ disease (HR 1.80, 1.26-2.59), but dropped out of the model in HER2+ disease given chemotherapy alone, where RCB-II and RCB-III did not separate (10-year RFS 44% vs 47%). Grades the non-pCR bin that B-18/B-27 and CTNeoBC treat as one; prognostic only, and the authors call for external validation.

records.title: EBCTCG adjuvant bisphosphonate meta-analysis
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Bone-targeted adjuvant therapy (bisphosphonates) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Early breast cancer randomised to adjuvant bisphosphonate vs control (postmenopausal subgroup of interest) Bisphosphonate (zoledronate, clodronate, ibandronate, etc.) vs control Recurrence; bone recurrence; breast cancer mortality Individual-patient meta-analysis of 18,766 women in 26 trials (median follow-up 5.6 woman-years). Overall reductions were only borderline: recurrence RR 0.94 (2p=0.08), distant recurrence 0.92 (2p=0.03), breast cancer mortality 0.91 (2p=0.04); the bone-recurrence reduction was definite (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.73-0.94, 2p=0.004). Among 11,767 postmenopausal women, recurrence (RR 0.86, 0.78-0.94, 2p=0.002), distant recurrence (0.82, 0.74-0.92), bone recurrence (0.72, 0.60-0.86; 10-year gain 2.2%) and breast cancer mortality (0.82, 0.73-0.93; 10-year gain 3.3%) all fell significantly; premenopausal women showed no apparent effect on any outcome. The postmenopausal boundary is less secure than those figures suggest: heterogeneity for bone recurrence was only borderline by menopausal status (2p=0.06 for trend) and correlated with age (2p=0.03), and no preferred agent, schedule or duration was established. Fractures fell (RR 0.85, 2p=0.02); osteonecrosis of the jaw could not be assessed from the data provided.

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Visvanathan et al.)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Primary prevention — endocrine chemoprevention · N/A · 2019
records.body: Women without a personal history of breast cancer who are at increased risk of developing the disease N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A ASCO guideline update on pharmacologic breast cancer risk reduction, incorporating the IBIS-II trial of anastrozole. In postmenopausal women at increased risk, anastrozole (1 mg/day for 5 years) is now an option alongside exemestane, raloxifene, or tamoxifen; IBIS-II showed anastrozole halved breast cancer incidence versus placebo (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.32-0.68), driven by ER-positive tumors. Anastrozole, exemestane, and raloxifene should not be prescribed for risk reduction in premenopausal women. Tamoxifen 20mg/day for 5 years remains standard of care for risk reduction in premenopausal women ≥35 years who have completed childbearing. Women most likely to benefit have atypical hyperplasia/LCIS, a 5-year BCRAT risk ≥3%, or a 10-year IBIS/Tyrer-Cuzick risk ≥5%. Choice of agent should weigh age, comorbidities, and adverse-effect profile (bone density loss and musculoskeletal symptoms with aromatase inhibitors vs thromboembolic/endometrial risk with tamoxifen). No survival advantage has been shown for any of these agents in primary prevention (IBIS-II deaths balanced, 18 vs 17); the demonstrated benefit is reduced incidence, not reduced mortality.

records.title: SUBITO
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · High-dose chemotherapy & autologous stem-cell transplant · III · 2026
records.body: Stage IIIA-C, HER2-negative breast cancer with homologous recombination deficiency (germline BRCA1/2 mutation or HRD tumour testing), newly diagnosed, age 18-66 (Netherlands + France) Intensified alkylating chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue (dose-dense AC then high-dose cyclophosphamide–thiotepa–carboplatin + ASCT) vs standard-of-care (dose-dense AC then carboplatin–paclitaxel) followed by adjuvant olaparib ×1 year Overall survival (intention-to-treat) Open-label phase 3 in stage III, HER2-negative, HRD breast cancer (n=174). 4-year OS did not differ (77.0% intensified chemo+ASCT vs 76.4% chemo+olaparib; HR for death 1.11, 95% CI 0.57-2.17, p=0.37), nor did 4-year RFS (76.8% vs 70.0%; HR 0.91, 0.48-1.71) or pCR (40% vs 44%). This is a null superiority result, not demonstrated equivalence: the trial was powered to detect HR 0.353 on 30 events, and its authors state it might have been underpowered to detect smaller effects. Toxicity was not close: grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia 99% vs 19% and febrile neutropenia 44% vs 12%, serious AEs 47% vs 26%, no treatment-related deaths. Intensified chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue adds toxicity without advantage over contemporary chemotherapy plus olaparib; with both arms HRD-directed and no non-olaparib control, olaparib's own contribution is untested here.

records.title: SENOMAC
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2024
records.body: Clinically node-negative T1–3 breast cancer with 1–2 sentinel-node macrometastases (>2 mm); mastectomy or BCS; ~89% received nodal radiotherapy Completion axillary-lymph-node dissection vs sentinel-node biopsy only (omission of completion ALND); adjuvant systemic therapy and radiotherapy per national guidelines Overall survival (non-inferiority) Non-inferiority trial in cN0 T1–3 breast cancer with 1–2 sentinel-node macrometastases (2,766 enrolled; per-protocol 2,540), the axis's only trial to reach its prespecified event target. The 2024 primary publication reports the prespecified secondary endpoint of recurrence-free survival, released ahead of the primary because overall-survival power had not yet been reached: 5-year RFS 89.7% (SLNB only) vs 88.7% (ALND), country-adjusted HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.66–1.19), P<0.001 against a non-inferiority margin of 1.44. The primary endpoint matured in an ASCO 2026 abstract (196 deaths against 190 required; median follow-up 60.1 months): 5-year OS 94.4% vs 93.4%, HR 0.84 (0.64–1.12); 5-year BCSS 97.8% vs 97.3%, HR 0.86 (0.55–1.34) — both CI upper bounds below the margin. Omission significantly improved patient-reported arm function and symptoms at 3 and 5 years, with no difference in global quality of life. With nodal-target irradiation given to ~89% of both arms, the trial states its results are comparable with AMAROS rather than Z0011.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;390:1163-1175  38598571 J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl):LBA503 (ASCO 2026 abstract) overall survival & arm morbidity

records.title: ACOSOG Z0011 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2011
records.body: Women with clinical T1–T2 invasive breast cancer (≤5 cm), no palpable axillary adenopathy, and 1–2 sentinel lymph nodes with metastases on H&E (IHC-only detected nodes excluded). All underwent lumpectomy with planned tangential whole-breast irradiation (third-field/nodal RT prohibited) and adjuvant systemic therapy at physician discretion. Median age 55; majority postmenopausal and hormone receptor–positive. 115 US academic and community sites; enrolled May 1999–December 2004; last follow-up 29 Sep 2015. Median follow-up 9.3 years (IQR 6.93–10.34). NCT00003855; ACOSOG (now Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology). Randomised after a positive sentinel node to sentinel lymph node dissection (SLND) alone (no further axillary surgery) vs completion axillary lymph node dissection (ALND, levels I–II). Both arms received breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast tangential-field radiotherapy, and adjuvant systemic therapy (chemotherapy and/or endocrine therapy) at the treating team's discretion; no protocol-specified systemic regimen or dose. Overall survival, tested for non-inferiority of SLND alone vs ALND (1-sided HR non-inferiority margin 1.3). Secondary endpoint: disease-free survival. At a median 9.3 years, SLND alone was non-inferior to ALND for 10-year overall survival: 86.3% vs 83.6% (HR 0.85; 1-sided 95% CI 0–1.16; non-inferiority P=.02), against a dual criterion requiring 5-year survival ≥75% and HR ≤1.3. 10-year disease-free survival 80.2% vs 78.2% (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.62–1.17; P=.32). Despite additional non-sentinel nodal macrometastases in 27.3% of ALND-arm patients, omitting ALND did not compromise survival or regional control — 1 regional recurrence between years 5 and 10 in the SLND-alone arm, and 10-year locoregional recurrence did not differ significantly. The result is less secure than it reads: the trial closed early at 891 of 1,900 planned patients with 110 of an estimated 500 deaths needed for 90% power, and the paper states that the overall-survival analysis after completion of follow-up was not prespecified. Does not support routine completion ALND for cT1–T2, cN0, 1–2 sentinel-node-positive disease treated with breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast irradiation and systemic therapy — a window narrowed further by the 18.9% who received protocol-prohibited nodal irradiation.

records.title: AMAROS
records.subtitle: EBC General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2014
records.body: Clinically node-negative (no palpable lymphadenopathy) T1–2 primary invasive breast cancer (initially unifocal ≤3 cm; amended Feb 2008 to include ≤5 cm and/or multifocal) with a tumour-positive sentinel node; ~82% breast-conserving surgery, ~18% mastectomy; 34 centres, 9 European countries; enrolled 2001–2010. Median follow-up 6.1 years (IQR 4.1–8.0) in sentinel-node-positive patients. EORTC 10981-22023; NCT00014612. Randomised 1:1 BEFORE sentinel-node biopsy to: axillary lymph node dissection (levels I–II, ≥10 nodes) vs axillary radiotherapy (all 3 axillary levels + medial supraclavicular fossa; 25 × 2 Gy) — allocated treatment delivered only if sentinel node positive. Both arms received breast surgery (BCS + whole-breast RT, or mastectomy ± chest-wall RT) and adjuvant systemic therapy at the MDT's discretion. 5-year axillary recurrence (non-inferiority; axillary RT not to exceed 4% vs expected 2% with ALND; one-sided HR non-inferiority margin 2.0) Both strategies gave excellent, comparable axillary control. 5-year axillary recurrence 0.43% (95% CI 0.00–0.92) ALND vs 1.19% (0.31–2.08) axillary RT (4/744 vs 7/681 events over follow-up). The planned non-inferiority test was underpowered (one-sided 95% CI for HR 0.00–5.27 vs margin 2.0) due to the low event rate, so formal non-inferiority was not statistically established. No significant difference in 5-year DFS (86.9% vs 82.7%; HR 1.18, 95% CI 0.93–1.51; p=0.18) or OS (93.3% vs 92.5%; HR 1.17, 0.85–1.62; p=0.34). Lymphoedema was significantly less frequent after axillary RT at 1, 3, and 5 years (clinical lymphoedema at 5 yr 11% RT vs 23% ALND; at 1 yr 15% vs 28%). 33% (220/672) of ALND patients had additional positive non-sentinel nodes. Conclusion: for cN0, sentinel-node-positive patients needing axillary treatment, axillary RT provides comparable regional control with significantly less arm morbidity than ALND.

records.title: MINDACT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2016
records.body: Early breast cancer, 0-3 nodes (mostly HR+/HER2-) Chemo decision by 70-gene MammaPrint vs clinical risk 5-yr distant metastasis-free survival Phase 3 (N=6693); adjuvant chemotherapy directed by the 70-gene MammaPrint signature vs clinicopathological risk in early breast cancer with 0-3 nodes, mostly HR+/HER2-. The primary analysis tested a single-arm rate against a fixed noninferiority threshold, not a between-arm comparison: among the 1550 women (23.2%) at high clinical risk but low genomic risk who forwent chemotherapy, 5-year survival without distant metastasis was 94.7% (95% CI 92.5-96.2), clearing the prespecified 92% boundary. The secondary randomised chemotherapy-vs-no-chemotherapy comparison in that discordant group was underpowered (95.9% vs 94.4%; adjusted HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.50-1.21, P=0.27). About 46% of clinically high-risk women could safely avoid chemotherapy, validating MammaPrint for chemo de-escalation.

records.title: TAILORx
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2018
records.body: HR+/HER2-, axillary node-negative early breast cancer Endocrine therapy vs chemoendocrine therapy (RS 11-25 randomized) Invasive disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=10273) of 21-gene Recurrence-Score-guided therapy in HR+/HER2-, node-negative early breast cancer; the 6711 women (69%) with a midrange RS 11-25 were randomised to endocrine therapy alone vs chemoendocrine therapy. Endocrine therapy alone was noninferior for invasive disease-free survival (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.94-1.24, P=0.26; 9-year iDFS 83.3% vs 84.3%), sparing chemotherapy in most patients. A prespecified age interaction (P=0.004) showed residual chemotherapy benefit in women 50 or younger with RS 16-25 - freedom from distant recurrence higher by up to 6.5 percentage points at 9 years (RS 21-25) - without a demonstrated survival difference. Practice-changing chemotherapy de-escalation.

records.title: RxPONDER (SWOG S1007)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2021
records.body: HR+/HER2-, 1-3 positive nodes, recurrence score <=25 Endocrine therapy vs chemoendocrine therapy Invasive disease-free survival Phase 3 extending the 21-gene assay to HR+/HER2- disease with 1-3 positive nodes and recurrence score <=25; endocrine therapy alone vs chemoendocrine therapy. The recurrence-score-by-treatment interaction was not significant (P=0.35) - recurrence score stayed prognostic but stopped predicting relative chemotherapy benefit - while a prespecified menopausal-status interaction was significant (P=0.008) and became the governing variable. Postmenopausal women (66.8%) derived no chemotherapy benefit (iDFS HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.82-1.26, P=0.89); premenopausal women (33.2%) derived a clear benefit (iDFS HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.43-0.83, P=0.002; distant relapse-free HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.87, P=0.009) even at low recurrence scores. Extended genomic chemo de-escalation to node-positive disease.

records.title: Paik et al. (NSABP B-20 validation)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2006
records.body: Node-negative, estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, from patients randomized in NSABP B-20 (tamoxifen alone vs tamoxifen plus chemotherapy) Retrospective 21-gene Recurrence Score (Oncotype DX) testing on archived tumor tissue from both randomized arms, to test for interaction between RS and chemotherapy benefit Freedom from distant recurrence; interaction between chemotherapy treatment and Recurrence Score First study to show that the 21-gene Recurrence Score (RS) predicts not just prognosis but also the magnitude of chemotherapy benefit. Patients with high-RS (≥31) tumors had large chemotherapy benefit (relative risk 0.26, 95% CI 0.13-0.53; absolute 10-year distant recurrence reduction 27.6%), whereas low-RS (<18) patients derived minimal benefit (relative risk 1.31, 95% CI 0.46-3.78; absolute difference -1.1%). Interaction between RS and chemotherapy benefit was statistically significant (p=0.038). Established the biological rationale and evidentiary basis for using Oncotype DX to guide adjuvant chemotherapy decisions in HR+/HER2- breast cancer, directly underpinning the subsequent prospective validation trials MINDACT, TAILORx, and RxPONDER.

records.title: OPTIMA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2026
records.body: High clinical-risk ER+/HER2- early breast cancer (0-9 involved nodes; 73% pN1; T>=30 mm if node-negative); women & men >=40 Standard chemotherapy → endocrine therapy (control) vs Prosigna (PAM50) ROR-directed: ROR >60 → chemo→ET, ROR <=60 → endocrine therapy alone; premenopausal ET included ovarian function suppression 5-yr invasive breast-cancer-free survival (IBCFS), non-inferiority (3% margin, per-protocol) Prosigna/PAM50 ROR test-directed chemo de-escalation non-inferior in high-clinical-risk ER+/HER2- EBC (mostly node-positive). n=4429; median f/u 3.9 y; 280 IBCFS events. 5-yr IBCFS 90.4% (test-directed) vs 91.5% (control), HR 0.99 (90% CI 0.81-1.20), NI p=0.013. Low-ROR (<=60) tumours (68% of pts): 93.7% vs 94.9%, HR 1.06 (0.78-1.46), NI p=0.0051. No heterogeneity by menopausal/nodal status; ~68% with low ROR can safely avoid chemotherapy. ASCO 2026 abstract - not yet a full publication.

records.title: ASTER 70s
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2025
records.body: Women >=70 years, ER-positive HER2-negative early breast cancer with genomic-grade-index (GGI) high-risk tumours (France, Belgium) Adjuvant chemotherapy then hormonotherapy vs hormonotherapy alone (1:1) Overall survival 8-year OS 72.7% vs 68.3% (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.63-1.11, p=0.21) - no significant survival benefit from adding chemotherapy; grade >=3 AEs 34% vs 9%. Supports omitting chemotherapy in older HR+/HER2- patients even with genomically high-risk tumours.

records.title: MA.17 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2003
records.body: Postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer, disease-free after ~5 years of tamoxifen Extended letrozole x5 yr vs placebo Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=5187); extended letrozole x5 years vs placebo in postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer disease-free after ~5 years of tamoxifen. Stopped early at the first interim analysis (median follow-up 2.4 years): letrozole improved 4-year disease-free survival (93% vs 87%; HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.43-0.75, P=0.00008), a benefit at least as large in node-negative (HR 0.47) as node-positive disease (HR 0.60). Overall survival showed a favourable but non-significant trend (4-year 96% vs 94%; HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.48-1.21, P=0.25) - the recurrence benefit was clearer than any survival benefit at this early readout. Established extended aromatase-inhibitor therapy beyond 5 years of tamoxifen; the placebo comparator makes its toxicity non-comparable to aromatase-inhibitor-vs-tamoxifen trials.

records.title: NSABP B-33
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2008
records.body: Postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer, node-negative or node-positive (clinical T1-3 N0-1 M0), disease-free after 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen Extended exemestane 25 mg once daily ×5 years vs placebo, after 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=1,598 randomised); extended exemestane 25 mg daily x5 years vs placebo after 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen in postmenopausal, node-negative or node-positive early breast cancer. Accrual was stopped early and the trial unblinded after MA.17 reported, with 44% placebo-to-exemestane crossover; median follow-up 30 months. In the primary eligible-with-follow-up analysis (n=1,562), original exemestane assignment gave a borderline 4-year DFS gain (91% vs 89%; HR 0.68, P=.07) and a significant 4-year RFS gain (96% vs 94%; HR 0.44, P=.004); the broader analysis including all patients with follow-up showed a 29% DFS-event reduction (P=.09) and a 52% RFS-event reduction (P=.008). The DFS benefit was confined to node-positive disease (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.30-0.86) with none node-negative (HR 1.13). Supports extended aromatase-inhibitor therapy after tamoxifen alongside MA.17, read through crossover dilution.

records.title: BIG 1-98
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2005
records.body: Postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer Letrozole vs tamoxifen (monotherapy and sequential arms) Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=8010, postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer); letrozole vs tamoxifen, with two additional sequential-switch arms. At a first-results median follow-up of 25.8 months, upfront letrozole improved disease-free survival over tamoxifen (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.93, P=0.003) and reduced distant recurrence specifically (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.60-0.88, P=0.001). This primary report compares the two monotherapies only; the sequential letrozole-then-tamoxifen arms were not yet matured here (reported later in an unfiled 2009 update). A second, independent confirmation of aromatase-inhibitor superiority over tamoxifen in postmenopausal disease, alongside ATAC.

records.title: ATAC
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2002
records.body: Postmenopausal early breast cancer, anastrozole and tamoxifen arms (2618 + 2598 HR+) Anastrozole vs tamoxifen x5 yr Disease-free survival At 10 years (median 120 mo), anastrozole improved DFS (HR 0.86) and time to recurrence (HR 0.79) over tamoxifen in HR+ disease, with the absolute recurrence difference widening over time (2.7% at 5 yr to 4.3% at 10 yr) and recurrence rates remaining significantly lower after treatment completion (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67-0.98, p=0.03), although the carryover benefit was smaller after 8 years; no overall-survival difference (HR 0.95, 0.84-1.06, p=0.4). Established aromatase inhibitors over tamoxifen for postmenopausal women.

records.title: EBCTCG tamoxifen meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2011
records.body: ER+ early breast cancer (20 randomized trials) ~5 years of tamoxifen vs no adjuvant tamoxifen Recurrence; breast-cancer mortality Five years of tamoxifen roughly halved the recurrence rate during years 0-4 (RR 0.53) and cut breast-cancer mortality by about a third throughout 15 years (RR 0.70), largely irrespective of age, nodal status or chemotherapy; benefit was confined to ER-positive disease. Quantified the foundational benefit of adjuvant tamoxifen.

records.title: EBCTCG aromatase inhibitor vs tamoxifen meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Postmenopausal ER-positive early breast cancer (randomised AI vs tamoxifen trials) 5y aromatase inhibitor vs 5y tamoxifen vs sequential tamoxifen→AI Recurrence; breast cancer mortality Patient-level meta-analysis of 31,920 postmenopausal ER-positive women. Versus 5 years of tamoxifen, 5 years of an aromatase inhibitor reduced recurrence by ~30% (proportionately) while treatments differed and cut 10-year breast-cancer mortality from 14.2% to 12.1% (RR 0.85) — about 15% relative to tamoxifen and ~40% relative to no endocrine therapy. AIs gave fewer endometrial cancers but more bone fractures. Established the AI mortality advantage over tamoxifen in postmenopausal disease.

records.title: ATLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2013
records.body: ER+ early breast cancer, disease-free after 5 years of tamoxifen (6846 ER+) Adjuvant tamoxifen 20 mg once daily continued to 10 years vs stopped at 5 years Recurrence; breast-cancer mortality Continuing tamoxifen to 10 years further reduced recurrence (years 5-14 21.4% vs 25.1%) and breast-cancer mortality (12.2% vs 15.0%; absolute reduction 2.8%), with benefit emerging mainly after year 10, at the cost of more endometrial cancer and pulmonary embolism. Established extended tamoxifen to 10 years.

records.title: TEXT & SOFT (exemestane)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2014
records.body: Premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer receiving ovarian suppression Exemestane 25 mg once daily + ovarian suppression (triptorelin) vs tamoxifen 20 mg once daily + ovarian suppression; ×5 years Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=4690, premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer on ovarian suppression); exemestane + ovarian suppression vs tamoxifen + ovarian suppression x5 years (combined TEXT and SOFT analysis). At 68 months, exemestane+OFS improved disease-free survival (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.60-0.85, P<0.001; 28% fewer events) and freedom from breast cancer (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.55-0.80, P<0.001; 34% reduction), without an overall-survival difference at this early readout (HR 1.14). At 13 years, the recurrence advantage held (12-year DFS HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.70-0.90; distant recurrence-free HR 0.83, 0.70-0.98) but overall survival still did not differ overall (HR 0.93, 0.78-1.11); the OS hazard was time-varying - early harm (years 0-5 HR 1.34) reversing to later benefit - and concentrated in the HER2-negative majority (86%). Established aromatase inhibitor plus ovarian suppression as an option in premenopausal women.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2014;371:107-118   J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1376-1382 long-term follow-up 36521078

records.title: SOFT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2015
records.body: Premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer Tamoxifen 20 mg once daily vs tamoxifen 20 mg once daily + ovarian suppression vs exemestane 25 mg once daily + ovarian suppression (triptorelin); ×5 years Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=3066, premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer); 3-arm randomisation of tamoxifen vs tamoxifen + ovarian suppression (OFS) vs exemestane + OFS x5 years. Adding OFS to tamoxifen showed a significance trajectory across readouts, not a settled answer: no significant DFS benefit at the 5.6-year primary analysis (86.6% vs 84.7%; HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.66–1.04, p=0.10), a significant DFS and OS benefit at 8 years (8-year DFS 83.2% vs 78.9%, p=0.009; OS 93.3% vs 91.5%), and a persisting but attenuated benefit at 12 years (DFS HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.69–0.98; OS HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.60–1.01, borderline). The benefit concentrated in women who remained premenopausal after chemotherapy; in the lower-risk chemo-naive cohort more than 95% of every arm remained free from breast cancer at 5 years and tamoxifen alone stayed appropriate. Exemestane+OFS improved outcomes further (HR vs tamoxifen 0.65, 0.49–0.87). Established OFS as beneficial in premenopausal women at sufficient recurrence risk.

records.title: EBCTCG extended AI meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2025
records.body: Postmenopausal ER+ early breast cancer, recurrence-free after ≥5 years of endocrine therapy (12 randomised trials) Further aromatase inhibitor therapy (2–3 or 5 years) vs no further adjuvant endocrine therapy Recurrence; breast-cancer mortality Meta-analysis (22,031 postmenopausal ER+ women, recurrence-free after >=5 years of prior endocrine therapy); further aromatase-inhibitor therapy (2–3 or 5 years) vs no further treatment. Any further AIT reduced recurrence by 27% (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.67–0.80, p<0.0001). In the narrower subgroup with some previous AIT (7,511 women), 5 further years cut recurrence (RR 0.71, 0.61–0.81; year 5–15 risk 11.6% vs 15.2%) and distant recurrence (RR 0.73, 0.61–0.88; 6.6% vs 8.6%), but breast-cancer mortality fell only non-significantly (RR 0.90, 0.70–1.15, p=0.40; 4.4% vs 5.0%). In a separate analysis of 10 vs 5 years of AIT, the absolute recurrence reduction was larger in node-positive (16.3% vs 20.1%) than node-negative disease (9.1% vs 11.8%), reflecting higher baseline risk rather than a different proportional effect. Five-year fracture risk rose (RR 1.35, 1.13–1.61); non-adherence was widespread and similar in both arms (39.0% vs 37.6%).

records.title: lidERA (BC)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2026
records.body: ER+/HER2- stage I-III early breast cancer after surgery +/- (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy Giredestrant 30 mg PO once daily vs standard-of-care endocrine therapy (anastrozole/letrozole/exemestane or tamoxifen) for 5 years; premenopausal pts on giredestrant or AI received an LHRH agonist Invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) Adjuvant giredestrant (next-gen oral SERD) improved iDFS vs standard-of-care endocrine therapy in ER+/HER2- stage I-III eBC (primary iDFS readout Bardia, SABCS 2025). This ASCO 2026 analysis (menopausal status; n=4170, 40.7% premenopausal): iDFS benefit and higher 3-yr rates in both premenopausal and postmenopausal subgroups, similar DRFI trend, consistent despite higher baseline risk in premenopausal pts. Fewer AE discontinuations with giredestrant than AI (musculoskeletal-pain discontinuation 1.6% vs 4.5%). ASCO 2026 abstract, subgroup analysis - primary results not yet a full publication.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl):502 (ASCO 2026 abstract) menopausal-status subgroup; primary iDFS readout Bardia SABCS 2025

records.title: POSITIVE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2023
records.body: Women <=42 years with prior stage I-III HR-positive early breast cancer desiring pregnancy, after 18-30 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy Temporary interruption of endocrine therapy (up to 2 years) to attempt pregnancy vs external control cohort (SOFT/TEXT) Breast cancer-free interval (breast cancer events) Single-group, non-randomised safety trial (N=516) of temporarily interrupting adjuvant endocrine therapy (up to 2 years) to attempt pregnancy, in women <=42 with prior stage I-III HR+ early breast cancer after 18-30 months of endocrine therapy. The primary analysis was a fixed-threshold safety design, not a hazard-ratio comparison: 44 breast-cancer events occurred against a prespecified 46-event boundary over 1,638 patient-years. A secondary external-control comparison (SOFT/TEXT cohort) found no excess 3-year breast-cancer-event incidence (8.9% vs 9.2%; adjusted HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.57-1.15). 74.0% achieved at least one pregnancy and 63.8% at least one live birth. Temporary interruption to conceive did not increase short-term recurrence risk, but median follow-up was only 3.4 years against a protocol-specified 10-year endpoint - the long-term question remains open.

records.title: EBCTCG premenopausal AI vs tamoxifen (ovarian suppression) meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · N/A · 2022
records.body: Premenopausal ER-positive early-stage breast cancer receiving ovarian function suppression (goserelin or triptorelin) or ablation; individual patient data from 4 randomised trials (ABCSG XII, SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE). N=7030 is the ER-positive analysis set (ER-negative/PR-positive women excluded; ~7230 randomised across the four trials). IPD meta-analysis — aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole, exemestane, or letrozole) + ovarian suppression (goserelin or triptorelin) or ablation vs tamoxifen + ovarian suppression; endocrine therapy for 3 years (ABCSG XII) or 5 years (SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE). Breast cancer recurrence (distant, locoregional, or contralateral); breast cancer mortality; death without recurrence; all-cause mortality Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of 7030 premenopausal ER-positive women from four randomised trials (ABCSG XII, SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE); median follow-up 8.0 years. Versus tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor (both with ovarian suppression) reduced any breast cancer recurrence (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.69–0.90; p=0.0005), with benefit concentrated in years 0–4 when treatments differed (RR 0.68, 99% CI 0.55–0.85; p<0.0001) and no further gain or loss in years 5–9 (RR 0.98, 99% CI 0.73–1.33; p=0.89). The absolute 5-year recurrence risk fell 3.2% (6.9% vs 10.1%; 10-year 14.7% vs 17.5%). Distant recurrence was reduced (RR 0.83, 0.71–0.97; p=0.018). No difference in breast cancer mortality (RR 1.01, 0.82–1.24; p=0.94) or all-cause mortality (RR 1.04, 0.86–1.27; p=0.68) at this follow-up. More bone fractures with an AI (227 [6.4%] of 3528 vs 180 [5.1%] of 3502; RR 1.27, 1.04–1.54; p=0.017); endometrial cancer rare (0.2% vs 0.3%). Establishes an aromatase inhibitor over tamoxifen for recurrence reduction in premenopausal ER+ women receiving ovarian suppression; any mortality impact awaits longer follow-up.

records.title: MA.17R
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2016
records.body: Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive primary breast cancer, disease-free after 4.5-6 yr of adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor therapy (mostly preceded by tamoxifen); randomized within 2 yr of stopping the AI to 5 more yr of letrozole or placebo (1:1). ECOG <3; no age-only exclusion Extended letrozole 2.5 mg daily x5 yr vs Placebo Disease-free survival 5 more years of letrozole after prior AI improved 5-year disease-free survival (95% vs 91%; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.48-0.91) and reduced contralateral breast cancer (HR 0.42, 0.22-0.81), with no overall-survival difference (HR 0.97, 0.73-1.28). The recurrence benefit carried a bone cost: fractures 14% vs 9%, new osteoporosis 11% vs 6%, bone pain 18% vs 14%. Established extending AI therapy beyond 5 years as a duration option in postmenopausal women who tolerate it.

records.title: NSABP B-42
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2019
records.body: Postmenopausal women with stage I-IIIA ER- and/or PR-positive invasive ductal breast cancer, ECOG 0-1 and no recurrence after 57-63 months of an AI or <=3 years of tamoxifen followed by an AI; randomised within 6 months of therapy completion. Prior non-traumatic osteoporotic fracture and bilateral breast cancer were excluded. Letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily x5 yr vs Matching placebo orally once daily x5 yr Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, breast-cancer-free interval, distant recurrence, osteoporotic fractures, arterial thrombotic events At median 10.3-year follow-up, the unplanned 10-year update showed a 3.3-point disease-free survival benefit with extended letrozole: 75.9% vs 72.6%, HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74-0.96), nominal P=0.01; the protocol primary had previously missed its adjusted boundary. Overall survival was unchanged (86.1% vs 86.2%; HR 0.97, 0.82-1.15). Breast-cancer-free interval (HR 0.75, 0.62-0.91) and distant recurrence (HR 0.72, 0.55-0.92) favoured letrozole. Osteoporotic fractures (HR 1.12, 0.86-1.45) and arterial thrombotic events (HR 1.11, 0.82-1.51) did not differ.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2019;20:88-99   J Natl Cancer Inst 2023;115:1302-1309 10-yr update

records.title: IDEAL (Investigation on the Duration of Extended Adjuvant Letrozole treatment); BOOG 2006-05
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2018
records.body: Postmenopausal HR-positive early breast cancer, disease-free after completing 5 years (plus or minus 3 months) of tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or sequential tamoxifen then an aromatase inhibitor; randomised within 2 years of stopping, with WHO performance status 0-1. Letrozole 2.5 mg once daily x2.5 years vs Letrozole 2.5 mg once daily x5 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant metastasis-free interval, new primary breast malignancy, safety Extending letrozole from 2.5 to 5 years after 5 years of prior endocrine therapy was not superior for disease-free survival (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74-1.16; P=0.49). Overall survival (HR 1.04, 0.78-1.38; nominal P=0.79) and distant metastasis-free interval (HR 1.06, 0.78-1.45; nominal P=0.71) also did not differ. In the primary ITT analysis, the nominal secondary endpoint of second primary breast cancer favoured 5 years (10/913 [1.1%] vs 27/908 [3.1%]; HR 0.39, 0.19-0.81; nominal P=0.01). No treatment-by-subgroup interaction was observed for DFS. During active treatment in the 1,806-patient safety population, grade 3/4 events comprised 10.0% vs 8.8% of reported adverse events; 23.5% vs 17.3% of patients discontinued for toxicity. Separately, 388/913 (42.5%) in the 5-year ITT arm stopped early overall.

records.title: ABCSG-16 / SALSA (Secondary Adjuvant Long-Term Study with Arimidex [anastrozole])
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy (HR+/HER2-) · III · 2021
records.body: Postmenopausal women aged <=80 years with stage I-III invasive HR-positive early breast cancer, recurrence-free after completing 5 years (+/-12 months) of tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or sequential therapy; prior endocrine therapy completed within 12 months before randomisation. Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily x2 years vs Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily x5 years; no dose modification; temporary interruption of up to 3 months permitted Primary: disease-free survival from the 2-year landmark. Secondary: overall survival, contralateral breast cancer, second primary cancer, clinical bone fracture At median 118 months, extending anastrozole from 2 to 5 additional years after 5 years of prior endocrine therapy did not improve disease-free survival in the protocol-defined 3,208-patient population still on trial and disease-free at the 2-year landmark: DFS 8 years after that landmark (10 years since randomisation) was 73.9% vs 73.6%, HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.85-1.15), P=0.90. Secondary endpoints had no alpha protection: OS did not differ (87.3% vs 87.5%; HR 1.02, 0.83-1.25), while clinical fractures were more frequent with 5 years (6.3% vs 4.7%; HR 1.35, 1.00-1.84); the post hoc number needed to harm was 63 (95% CI 32-953). Across the unequal 5- versus 2-year exposure periods, at least one serious adverse event (recorded until 30 days after the last dose) occurred in 40.2% (687/1,710) vs 26.5% (452/1,705), and investigator-attributed anastrozole-related serious events in 4.0% (69 patients) vs 2.3% (40 patients).

records.title: monarchE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2020
records.body: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- node-positive, high-risk early breast cancer Abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily ×2 years + standard adjuvant endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone Invasive disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=5637), node-positive high-risk HR+/HER2- early breast cancer; abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily x2 years added to standard adjuvant endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone. At the 2020 primary analysis, abemaciclib significantly improved invasive disease-free survival (2-year iDFS 92.2% vs 88.7%; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60–0.93, P=.01), and the benefit deepened with maturity (7-year iDFS HR 0.734, 0.657–0.820). At the 2026 primary overall-survival analysis (median follow-up 6.3 years, 661 deaths), abemaciclib reached statistical significance on OS (HR 0.842, 95% CI 0.722–0.981, P=0.027; 7-year OS 86.8% vs 85.0%), meeting the prespecified boundary - the first adjuvant CDK4/6-inhibitor trial to convert a recurrence benefit into a demonstrated survival benefit, in contrast to the negative palbociclib trials PALLAS and PENELOPE-B.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3987-3998   Lancet Oncol 2023;24:77-90 4-yr interim OS 36493792 Ann Oncol 2026;37:155-165 primary OS analysis 41110697

records.title: NATALEE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2024
records.body: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- stage II-III early breast cancer (broad, incl. selected node-negative) Ribociclib 400 mg once daily 3 weeks on / 1 week off ×3 years + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg once daily, ≥5 years) vs nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor alone Invasive disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=5101), stage II-III HR+/HER2- early breast cancer including selected node-negative disease; ribociclib 400 mg daily (3 weeks on, 1 week off) x3 years plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor vs the aromatase inhibitor alone (goserelin in premenopausal women and men). At the 2024 primary analysis, ribociclib improved 3-year iDFS (90.4% vs 87.1%; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.91, P=0.003). At the prespecified 5-year follow-up (median iDFS follow-up 55.4 months), the benefit deepened rather than faded (HR 0.716, 95% CI 0.618-0.829; absolute gap widening from 2.7 to 4.5 percentage points between years 3 and 5) and held in node-negative disease (HR 0.606, 95% CI 0.372-0.986), while overall survival remained a non-significant trend (HR 0.800, 95% CI 0.637-1.003). Extended adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition to a broader early-breast population, with monarchE still the only trial in the class carrying a mature significant survival benefit.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;390:1080-1091   ESMO Open 2025;10:105858 5-yr follow-up, updated OS 41320342

records.title: PALLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2021
records.body: Stage II-III HR+/HER2- early breast cancer Palbociclib 125 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle ×2 years + standard adjuvant endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone Invasive disease-free survival Two years of adjuvant palbociclib added to endocrine therapy in stage II-III HR+/HER2- disease. Negative: 3-year iDFS 88.2% vs 88.5% (HR 0.93), crossing the prespecified futility boundary, so palbociclib was discontinued. Adjuvant palbociclib cannot be recommended — the counterpoint to the positive abemaciclib monarchE result.

records.title: PENELOPE-B
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (HR+/HER2- high-risk) · III · 2021
records.body: HR+/HER2- residual invasive disease with high CPS-EG score after neoadjuvant chemotherapy Palbociclib 125 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle ×13 cycles (~1 year) + endocrine therapy vs placebo + endocrine therapy Invasive disease-free survival One year of palbociclib added to endocrine therapy in high-risk HR+/HER2- patients with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Negative: iDFS HR 0.93 (p=.53), with no benefit in any subgroup. With PALLAS, established that palbociclib has no role in the adjuvant/post-neoadjuvant setting — in contrast to abemaciclib (monarchE).

records.title: OlympiA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Escalation for BRCA-mutated disease (PARP inhibition) · III · 2021
records.body: Germline BRCA1/2, HER2-negative (TNBC or HR+) high-risk early breast cancer after (neo)adjuvant chemo Adjuvant olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily ×1 year vs placebo Invasive disease-free survival Olaparib improved 3-yr iDFS (85.9% vs 77.1%, HR 0.58) with later OS benefit; first targeted adjuvant therapy for BRCA-mutated HER2-negative disease after chemotherapy.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:2394-2405   Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-1268 overall survival analysis 36228963

records.title: NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831 (joint analysis)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2005
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive (later high-risk node-negative) operable breast cancer AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide) ×4 → paclitaxel + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly, begun with the first dose of paclitaxel, to complete 52 weeks) vs AC → paclitaxel alone (joint analysis of the concurrent-trastuzumab and control arms) Disease-free survival Joint analysis of two phase III adjuvant trials (N≈4046), HER2+ node-positive/high-risk node-negative disease: AC→paclitaxel ± concurrent trastuzumab ×1yr. Adding trastuzumab roughly halved recurrence — interim DFS HR 0.48 (P<0.0001), crossing the early-stopping boundary (absolute DFS +12% at 3yr). Mature joint analysis (Perez 2014, 8.4yr): DFS HR 0.60 (0.53-0.68) and OS HR 0.63 (0.54-0.73); 10-yr OS 84% vs 75.2%, 10-yr DFS 73.7% vs 62.2%, benefit across all subgroups. Cardiac cost: 3-yr class III/IV CHF or cardiac death 4.1% (B-31)/2.9% (N9831), concentrated in the anthracycline arms. The origin point of adjuvant anti-HER2 therapy; the concurrent-only design made concurrent (not sequential) chemotherapy–trastuzumab standard.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2005;353:1673-1684   Perez EA et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3744-3752 joint 10-yr OS analysis 25332249 Chumsri S et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:3425-3435 late-relapse combined analysis (N9831/B-31) 31622131

records.title: HERA (BIG 1-01)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2005
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer after primary therapy (chemo +/- surgery/RT) After locoregional therapy and at least 4 cycles of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy: observation vs trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W for 1 year vs the same for 2 years Disease-free survival Phase III, N=5102, HER2+ EBC after completion of chemotherapy: sequential trastuzumab 1yr vs 2yr vs observation. 1yr vs observation reduced DFS events — initial HR 0.54 (0.43-0.67) at 1yr follow-up, settling to HR 0.76 (0.68-0.86) at the 11-yr final analysis, with OS HR 0.74 (0.64-0.86); 10-yr DFS 69% vs 63% (diluted by 52% observation-arm crossover). 2yr gave no added benefit over 1yr (DFS HR 1.02, 0.89-1.17). Severe cardiotoxicity was low (0.5%), consistent with post-chemotherapy sequential dosing. Fixed 1 year as the standard adjuvant trastuzumab duration and the reference against which PHARE, ShortHER and PERSEPHONE test shorter courses.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2005;353:1659-1672   Cameron D et al. Lancet 2017;389:1195-1205 11-yr final analysis 28215665

records.title: FinHer
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2006
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer (subgroup of 1010-pt node+/high-risk trial) Docetaxel or vinorelbine then FEC, +/- 9 weeks trastuzumab Recurrence-free survival Just 9 weeks of trastuzumab improved 3-yr RFS (89% vs 78%, HR 0.42); raised the question of shorter durations, though later trials confirmed 1 year as standard.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2006;354:809-820   Joensuu H et al. J Clin Oncol 2009;27:5685-5692 final results, median 62 mo 19884557

records.title: BCIRG 006
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2011
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide) → docetaxel (AC-T, control) vs AC-T + trastuzumab (AC-TH) vs docetaxel–carboplatin + trastuzumab (TCH); trastuzumab given as 4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly during chemotherapy, then 6 mg/kg Q3W to complete 1 year Disease-free survival Phase III, N=3222, HER2+ node-positive/high-risk node-negative disease: AC→docetaxel (AC-T) vs AC-T+trastuzumab (AC-TH) vs non-anthracycline docetaxel/carboplatin+trastuzumab (TCH). Both trastuzumab arms superior to chemotherapy alone (5-yr DFS 84% AC-TH, 81% TCH vs 75%; 5-yr OS 92%/91% vs 87%), with no significant efficacy difference between them. CHF and cardiac dysfunction were significantly higher with AC-TH than TCH (P<0.001); acute leukaemia occurred in 7 anthracycline-arm patients vs 1 with TCH. Established non-anthracycline TCH as an effective, less cardiotoxic option — completing the foundation that anti-HER2 therapy works, 1 year is the duration, and it need not carry an anthracycline.

records.title: EBCTCG trastuzumab meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · N/A · 2021
records.body: Early-stage, node-negative or node-positive HER2-positive breast cancer (7 randomized trials) Meta-analysis of 7 randomised trials (13,864 women) — chemotherapy plus trastuzumab (adjuvant or neoadjuvant) vs the same chemotherapy alone Breast cancer recurrence; breast cancer mortality; all-cause mortality Individual patient-data meta-analysis of 13,864 women across 7 randomized trials (including NSABP B-31/N9831, HERA, FinHer and BCIRG 006), median follow-up 10.7 years. Trastuzumab cut breast cancer recurrence (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.62-0.71) and breast cancer mortality (RR 0.67, 0.61-0.73) by about one-third, with absolute 10-year reductions of 9.0% in recurrence, 6.4% in breast cancer mortality and 6.5% in all-cause mortality, and no increase in death without recurrence (0.4%, P=0.35). The proportional reduction was similar irrespective of ER and nodal status, while absolute benefit scaled with baseline risk (5-yr recurrence reduction 10.7% in N4+ vs 5.7% in N0) — uniform relative benefit with risk-proportional absolute benefit, the quantitative basis for escalating high-risk and de-escalating low-risk disease. Confirms the foundational adjuvant trastuzumab trials at long-term follow-up.

records.title: PHARE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer who received adjuvant trastuzumab Adjuvant trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W: 6 months vs 12 months total duration (non-inferiority) Disease-free survival Phase III non-inferiority trial (N=3384, France), 6 vs 12 months of adjuvant trastuzumab; landmark randomisation between months 3-6, non-inferiority margin HR 1.15. Six months failed to prove non-inferiority: the final 7.5-yr analysis gave HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.93-1.25, P=0.39), the CI still crossing the 1.15 margin (interim 2013 HR had been 1.28). Read against PERSEPHONE — near-identical mature HR (1.08 vs 1.07) but opposite verdict — the difference is the pre-specified margin, not the biology: shortening carries a small, real excess hazard. Concluded 12 months should remain the standard adjuvant duration.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2013;14:741-748   Pivot X et al. Lancet 2019;393:2591-2598 final analysis, 7.5-yr 31178155

records.title: ShortHER
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2018
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer (adjuvant) 9 weeks vs 1 year of adjuvant trastuzumab (with chemotherapy) Disease-free survival Phase III non-inferiority trial (1254 randomised, 1253 analysed, Italy), 9 weeks vs 1 year of adjuvant trastuzumab with anthracycline–taxane chemotherapy; co-primary DFS and OS. Non-inferiority of the 9-week arm was not met: DFS HR 1.13 (90% CI 0.89-1.42) against a prespecified margin of 1.29. Read that against the trial's power — planned accrual was cut from 2332 to 1252 patients on funding timelines. EVERY PAIR BELOW IS 1 YEAR vs 9 WEEKS. 10-yr outcomes were close overall (DFS 77% vs 78%; OS 89% vs 88%). Nodal status was a randomisation stratification factor, so the nodal subgroups are protocol-defined: for node-negative and 1-3 node disease the difference was negligible and numerically favoured 9 weeks (10-yr DFS N0 81% vs 85%, N1-3 77% vs 79%), whereas ≥4 positive nodes favoured 1 year (10-yr OS 84% vs 64%, HR 1.87; DFS 63% vs 53%, HR 1.84). No interaction test is reported for any subgroup, and the paper labels these intervals 95% CI in Figure 1 and 90% CI in Figure 2. Supports 12 months for high nodal burden; the authors offer the short course as an option for patients with cardiac events during treatment and those at low risk of relapse.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2018;29:2328-2333   Conte P et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:4976-4981 10-yr update 37748109

records.title: PERSEPHONE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer receiving adjuvant trastuzumab + chemotherapy Adjuvant trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W (or 600 mg SC): 6 months (9 cycles) vs 12 months (18 cycles) total duration (non-inferiority) Disease-free survival Phase III non-inferiority trial (N=4089, UK), pragmatic design (all chemotherapy regimens, neo/adjuvant, concurrent or sequential), 6 vs 12 months of adjuvant trastuzumab; non-inferiority margin 3% DFS. Six months non-inferior: 4-yr DFS 89.4% vs 89.8%, HR 1.07 (90% CI 0.93-1.24, non-inferiority P=0.011). The shorter course caused less harm — severe adverse events 19% vs 24% (P=0.0002) and early stopping for cardiotoxicity 3% vs 8% (P<0.0001). The only duration trial to demonstrate clear non-inferiority; near-identical HR to PHARE (1.07 vs 1.08) but a more lenient margin, so 6 months is a defensible, evidence-backed option for similar-risk patients rather than the default.
records.keywords: Lancet 2019;393:2599-2612   Earl HM et al. Health Technol Assess 2020;24:1-190 HTA final report 32880572

records.title: NeoSphere
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2012
records.body: HER2-positive locally advanced, inflammatory or early (>2 cm) breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Four neoadjuvant cycles Q3W: trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + docetaxel (group A) vs pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) + trastuzumab + docetaxel (group B) vs pertuzumab + trastuzumab, no chemotherapy (group C) vs pertuzumab + docetaxel (group D); all then surgery, adjuvant FEC, and trastuzumab to complete 1 year Pathologic complete response (pCR) Phase II, open-label, four-arm neoadjuvant trial (N=417) in treatment-naive HER2+ operable/locally advanced/inflammatory disease. Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab+docetaxel raised breast pCR from 29.0% (95% CI 20.6-38.5) to 45.8% (36.1-55.7), P=0.0141; the chemotherapy-free dual-blockade arm (HP) still gave pCR 16.8% and pertuzumab+docetaxel 24.0%. Grade ≥3 events were mainly neutropenia, concentrated in the docetaxel arms, with far fewer serious events in the chemo-free HP arm. Established neoadjuvant dual HER2 blockade and validated pCR as the fast in-vivo readout (basis for pertuzumab's accelerated approval); adjuvant efficacy confirmation came later from APHINITY.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2012;13:25-32   Gianni L et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:791-800 5-yr PFS/DFS analysis 27179402

records.title: TRYPHAENA
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive operable, locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Neoadjuvant trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) added to 6 cycles of chemotherapy: FEC → docetaxel with dual blockade throughout (Arm A) vs FEC → docetaxel with dual blockade during docetaxel only (Arm B) vs docetaxel–carboplatin (TCH) with dual blockade throughout (Arm C); trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year Cardiac safety; pCR Phase II, three-arm cardiac-safety study (N=225) in operable/locally advanced/inflammatory HER2+ disease: pertuzumab+trastuzumab with FEC→docetaxel (concurrent), FEC→docetaxel (sequential), or anthracycline-free TCH. Primary endpoint was cardiac tolerability — symptomatic LV systolic dysfunction was rare (2 patients during neoadjuvant treatment) and LVEF declines ≥10% to <50% occurred in 3.9-5.6% across arms, so dual blockade added no cardiac spike even alongside anthracyclines. Secondary, descriptive pCR (ypT0/is) was high in every arm: 61.6% / 57.3% / 66.2% (anthracycline-free TCH+P numerically highest). Showed dual blockade is deliverable with or without anthracycline and put anthracycline-free TCH+P on the map, setting up TRAIN-2.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2013;24:2278-2284   Schneeweiss A et al. Eur J Cancer 2018;89:27-35 long-term (3-yr) DFS analysis 29223479

records.title: TRAIN-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer Neoadjuvant trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) concurrent throughout, with FEC ×3 → paclitaxel–carboplatin ×6 (anthracycline) vs paclitaxel–carboplatin ×9 (anthracycline-free); trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year pCR (breast and axilla) Phase III (N=438, Netherlands), stage II-III HER2+ disease: anthracycline (FEC→paclitaxel/carboplatin) vs anthracycline-free (paclitaxel/carboplatin ×9), both with concurrent trastuzumab+pertuzumab. pCR was identical — 67% vs 68% (P=0.95) — across every subgroup. Survival confirmed the equivalence on hard endpoints (van der Voort 2021, median 48.8mo): 3-yr EFS 92.7% vs 93.6% (HR 0.90, 0.50-1.63) and OS 97.7% vs 98.2%, irrespective of nodal and HR status. Toxicity favoured dropping the anthracycline: grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia 10% vs 1% (P<0.0001), severe LVEF decline 7.7% vs 3.2% (P=0.04), and two acute leukaemias in the anthracycline arm. Removed anthracyclines from neoadjuvant dual-blockade HER2+ therapy; KRISTINE marks the opposite limit (the chemotherapy cannot be dropped).
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2018;19:1630-1640   van der Voort A et al. JAMA Oncol 2021;7:978-984 3-yr EFS/OS analysis 34014249

records.title: TRAIN-3
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer (hormone receptor-negative and hormone receptor-positive cohorts); multicentre, Netherlands Neoadjuvant paclitaxel + carboplatin + trastuzumab + pertuzumab, up to 9 cycles, with MRI-guided early surgery once a complete radiological response is reached (imaging-adapted duration); residual invasive disease continued chemotherapy to 9 cycles then adjuvant T-DM1 3-year event-free survival (hormone receptor-negative and -positive analysed separately) Single-arm test of MRI-guided personalisation of neoadjuvant chemotherapy duration: patients were sent to surgery once MRI showed a complete radiological response. One-third of hormone receptor-negative and one-sixth of hormone receptor-positive patients reached pCR after only 3 cycles. 3-year EFS was 92.2% (HR-negative) and 92.0% (HR-positive); among those who needed only 1-3 cycles it was 96.1% (n=91) and 98.6% (n=69) — but those patients reached that group BY responding early on MRI, so this is a favourable-prognosis selection and not an effect of shorter treatment; the paper tests no comparison between cycle groups. Grade 3-4 adverse events and grade >=2 neuropathy rose with increasing cycle number, with no treatment-related deaths. Supports MRI-guided shortening of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in a subset of HER2+ EBC to cut toxicity without compromising 3-year outcomes.
records.keywords: Louis FM et al. Lancet Oncol 2026;27:349-360

records.title: KRISTINE (TRIO-021)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: HER2-positive stage II-III operable breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Six neoadjuvant cycles Q3W: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) vs docetaxel–carboplatin + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (TCHP); after surgery the assigned HER2 regimen continued for 12 more cycles (18 cycles total, ~1 year) Pathologic complete response (pCR) Phase III, open-label (N=444), stage II-III operable HER2+ disease testing a chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant regimen: T-DM1+pertuzumab vs docetaxel/carboplatin+trastuzumab+pertuzumab (TCHP). Dropping chemotherapy cost pCR — 44.4% vs 55.7% (absolute difference -11.3%, 95% CI -20.5 to -2.0, P=0.016). Toxicity ran the other way (grade 3-4 AEs 13% vs 64%, serious AEs 5% vs 29%), but better tolerability did not rescue the efficacy gap. TCHP remains the neoadjuvant standard; KRISTINE is the boundary that the chemotherapy cannot be dropped — and the instructive contrast with KATHERINE, where the same drug used post-neoadjuvant for residual disease halved recurrence.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2018;19:115-126   Hurvitz SA et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:2206-2216 3-yr outcomes 31157583

records.title: DESTINY-Breast11
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2026
records.body: High-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Neoadjuvant T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W ×8 cycles (alone), or T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg Q3W ×4 → paclitaxel + trastuzumab (6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) ×4 (T-DXd-THP), vs dose-dense AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide Q2W) ×4 → THP ×4 (standard of care); post-neoadjuvant trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to 1 year, or T-DM1 ×14 cycles if residual disease Pathologic complete response (pCR) Phase III, open-label (N=927), high-risk HER2+ EBC (≥cT3cN0 or cT0-4cN1-3): neoadjuvant T-DXd→THP vs dose-dense AC→THP (the T-DXd-alone arm was closed early for inferiority). T-DXd-THP improved pCR 67.3% vs 56.3% (absolute difference 11.2%, 95% CI 4.0-18.3, P=0.003), with benefit in both HR-positive (61.4% vs 52.3%) and HR-negative (83.1% vs 67.1%) subgroups; T-DXd alone was insufficient (pCR 43.0%). More favourable safety: grade ≥3 AEs 37.5% vs 55.8%, all-grade LV dysfunction 1.3% vs 6.1%, and drug-related ILD low and similar across arms (~4-5%, unlike the 9.6% in DESTINY-Breast05). EFS immature (4.5% maturity, HR 0.56). Candidate new neoadjuvant standard for high-risk disease — an ADC front end beating dose-dense anthracycline on both efficacy and safety.

records.title: neoCARHP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive invasive breast cancer, previously untreated (neoadjuvant); multicentre China Six 3-weekly cycles of investigator-selected taxane (docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel) + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W), without carboplatin (THP; docetaxel 100 mg/m²) vs with carboplatin AUC 6 (TCbHP; docetaxel 75 mg/m²); adjuvant trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to complete 1 year, or T-DM1 ×14 cycles if residual disease pCR (ypT0/is ypN0) in the mITT population; noninferiority Phase III noninferiority trial (N=774; stage II-III HER2+): taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab with (TCbHP) or without carboplatin (THP), 6 cycles. Omitting carboplatin was noninferior for pCR: 64.1% (THP) vs 65.9% (TCbHP), absolute difference -1.8% (95% CI -8.5 to 5.0; OR 0.93; P-noninferiority = .0089; mITT n=766). THP had fewer grade 3-4 AEs (20.7% vs 34.6%) and serious AEs (1.3% vs 4.7%), with no treatment-related deaths. Continues the neoadjuvant de-escalation ladder — TRAIN-2 dropped the anthracycline, neoCARHP the carboplatin — toward a taxane + dual-blockade core, with KRISTINE marking the floor (the taxane cannot also go). Noninferiority rests on pCR; EFS/survival still immature.

records.title: PHERGain-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive, centrally confirmed HER2-positive (IHC 3+), node-negative early breast cancer, tumours 5-30 mm by MRI 8 cycles neoadjuvant trastuzumab + pertuzumab (HP) (plus endocrine therapy if HR-positive), then pathological-response-guided adjuvant therapy: HP if pCR (cohort A), T-DM1 if residual invasive disease / ypN0(i+/mol+) / ypN1mi (cohort B), or chemotherapy then T-DM1 if ypN1-3 (cohort C) Co-primary: 1-year health-related quality-of-life decline (EORTC QLQ-C30) and 3-year recurrence-free interval pCR-guided, chemotherapy-free de-escalation strategy. 236/396 (59.6%) achieved pCR with neoadjuvant HP alone (plus endocrine therapy if HR+) and continued chemo-free adjuvant HP; 37.8% entered the T-DM1 cohort (B) and 1.8% cohort C (both of the 391 who reached surgery). Global HRQoL declined by >=10% in 42.8% at 1 year (154 of the 360 who returned 1-year questionnaires; 37.3% with pCR vs 51.9% with residual disease, an outcome-defined comparison with no test reported). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 86.6% (5.6% grade >=3); one T-DM1-attributed death (pneumonitis). The pCR rate was comparable to chemotherapy plus HP with meaningful quality-of-life preservation, supporting chemo-free neoadjuvant HP with response-adapted adjuvant escalation in selected node-negative HER2+ EBC (recurrence-free-interval follow-up maturing).
records.keywords: Garrigós L et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:837-848

records.title: WSG-ADAPT-TP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive early breast cancer, clinical stage I-III 12 weeks of neoadjuvant T-DM1, or T-DM1 + endocrine therapy, or trastuzumab + endocrine therapy (1:1:1); adjuvant chemotherapy optional at investigator discretion after pCR (76 of 117 received it) and mandatory after non-pCR pCR (primary, reported 2017); here 5-year invasive disease-free survival and overall survival (secondary survival endpoints) Chemotherapy-free de-escalated neoadjuvant therapy in HR+/HER2+ EBC. Despite higher pCR with T-DM1 +/- endocrine therapy than with trastuzumab + endocrine therapy, 5-year iDFS (88.9% / 85.3% / 84.6%) and OS (97.2% / 96.4% / 96.3%) did not differ detectably across arms — the trial states it was not powered for the survival endpoints, on 46 iDFS events and 19 deaths — because non-pCR patients received mandatory standard chemotherapy. pCR vs non-pCR was associated with 5-year iDFS (92.7% vs 82.7%; HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.85, nominal p=.014) — an outcome-defined grouping pooled across arms whose members received systematically different adjuvant chemotherapy, so it cannot be read causally. Among 117 patients with pCR, the 41 who omitted adjuvant chemotherapy had 5-year iDFS (92.1%) similar to those who received it (93.0%). Shows that pCR after 12 weeks of chemo-free de-escalated neoadjuvant therapy identifies patients with excellent outcomes who may safely omit chemotherapy; PIK3CA-wild-type, luminal-A and immune-high tumours fared best.
records.keywords: Harbeck N et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3796-3804

records.title: WSG-TP-II
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive early breast cancer 12 weeks neoadjuvant trastuzumab + pertuzumab (HP) + endocrine therapy vs HP + weekly paclitaxel (1:1); all received adjuvant dual HER2 blockade; standard chemotherapy mandatory if non-pCR, optional after pCR pCR (primary: HP + paclitaxel 56.4% vs HP + endocrine therapy 23.7%); here final 5-year survival Randomised de-escalation comparing an entirely chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant backbone (HP + endocrine therapy) with HP + weekly paclitaxel in HR+/HER2+ EBC.
