Although pCR was far higher with paclitaxel (56.4% vs 23.7%), 5-year outcomes were excellent in both: OS 100% (endocrine arm) vs 97.9% (paclitaxel arm), untested. The PRESPECIFIED secondary invasive-DFS endpoint (reported as EFS-DCIS) was 92.1% vs 94.8%, numerically favouring paclitaxel; a separate EXPLORATORY landmark iDFS analysis gave 97.7% vs 79.8% in the opposite direction, but rests on 7 events in 196 patients with HR 2.31 (95% CI 0.45-11.93, p=.316) and establishes nothing. Supports the feasibility and safety of pCR-guided de-escalated neoadjuvant therapy - including a chemo-free HP + endocrine option - in HR+/HER2+ EBC, with adjuvant escalation reserved for non-pCR. Note that the chemotherapy-free label applies to the NEOADJUVANT phase only: about 70% of that arm went on to receive adjuvant chemotherapy.
records.keywords: Gluz O et al. J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1974-1980

records.title: Neoadjuvant HER2+ therapy NMA (Villacampa)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · N/A · 2023
records.body: Operable / local-regionally advanced HER2+ breast cancer (neoadjuvant; 46 RCTs, 32 regimens) Network meta-analysis of neoadjuvant anti-HER2 regimens (trastuzumab +/- pertuzumab or TKI; +/- anthracycline; +/- carboplatin) pCR, EFS, OS (network meta-analysis of direct + indirect evidence) Dual HER2 blockade (pertuzumab or TKI) + chemotherapy was superior to trastuzumab + chemotherapy for pCR, EFS and OS, but with more cardiotoxicity. Anthracycline-based chemotherapy was NOT more effective than non-anthracycline-based; in anthracycline-free regimens, adding carboplatin gave numerically better outcomes. Conclusion: dual HER2 blockade + chemotherapy is the recommended neoadjuvant approach for HER2+ breast cancer, preferably anthracycline-free with carboplatin.

records.title: APHINITY
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2017
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer Standard adjuvant chemotherapy (anthracycline → taxane, or docetaxel–carboplatin ×6) + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) vs + placebo; anti-HER2 therapy from the first taxane cycle to complete 1 year (max 18 cycles) Invasive disease-free survival Phase III, double-blind (N=4805), HER2+ node-positive/high-risk node-negative disease (neoadjuvant-treated patients excluded): chemotherapy+trastuzumab + adjuvant pertuzumab vs placebo ×1yr. Pertuzumab improved invasive DFS (primary HR 0.81, 0.66-1.00, P=0.045), benefit concentrated in node-positive disease (8-yr node-positive iDFS 86.1% vs 81.2%, HR 0.72) and absent in node-negative (iDFS HR 1.13). OS was not significant at the 8.4-yr peer-reviewed analysis (HR 0.83, P=0.078), reaching significance only at the final 11.3-yr analysis (HR 0.83, P=0.044; 10-yr OS 91.6% vs 89.8%) — congress-level (ESMO Breast Cancer 2025 LBA1), pending full publication. No cardiac penalty (<1%); grade ≥3 diarrhoea ~10% vs 4%. Established adjuvant dual blockade for node-positive disease, now largely bypassed by neoadjuvant-first, response-adapted management.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2017;377:122-131   Loibl S et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3643-3651 third interim OS / 8.4-yr 39259927 Loibl S et al. ESMO Breast Cancer 2025, LBA1 final analysis 11.3-yr (congress abstract, pending full publication)

records.title: KATHERINE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemo + HER2 therapy Adjuvant T-DM1 (trastuzumab emtansine) 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W vs trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (8 mg/kg loading), ×14 cycles, for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane + trastuzumab Invasive disease-free survival Phase III, open-label (N=1486), HER2+ EBC with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane (±anthracycline)+trastuzumab: adjuvant T-DM1 vs trastuzumab ×14 cycles. T-DM1 halved recurrence — 3-yr iDFS 88.3% vs 77.0%, HR 0.50 (0.39-0.64, P<0.001). The final 8.4-yr analysis sustained the iDFS gain (HR 0.54; 7-yr iDFS 80.8% vs 67.1%) and delivered a now-significant OS benefit (HR 0.66, 0.51-0.87, P=0.003; 7-yr OS 89.1% vs 84.4%). More grade ≥3 AEs with T-DM1 (26.1% vs 15.7%: thrombocytopenia, transaminitis, neuropathy). Established response-adapted escalation and made T-DM1 the standard for residual disease — since superseded by T-DXd for high-risk residual disease (DESTINY-Breast05).
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2019;380:617-628   Geyer CE et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:249-257 OS analysis 39813643

records.title: DESTINY-Breast05
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2026
records.body: High-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease (breast and/or axilla) after neoadjuvant therapy Post-neoadjuvant T-DXd (trastuzumab deruxtecan) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs T-DM1 (trastuzumab emtansine) 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W, ×14 cycles, for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane + trastuzumab Invasive disease-free survival Phase III, open-label (N=1635), high-risk HER2+ EBC with residual invasive disease (node-positive at surgery or inoperable at diagnosis) after neoadjuvant therapy: post-neoadjuvant T-DXd vs T-DM1 (the KATHERINE standard). T-DXd cut invasive recurrence/death by about half — iDFS events 6.2% vs 12.5%, HR 0.47 (0.34-0.66, P<0.001); 3-yr iDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%. Toxicity split by class (T-DXd mainly GI/haematologic), the defining risk being interstitial lung disease — adjudicated drug-related ILD 9.6% vs 1.6%, with two ILD deaths. Positions T-DXd as the new post-neoadjuvant standard for high-risk residual disease (escalation beyond KATHERINE); OS immature (~30mo).

records.title: ExteNET
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Extended adjuvant therapy · III · 2016
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer after adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy Extended adjuvant neratinib 240 mg orally once daily ×1 year vs placebo, begun after completion of trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy Invasive disease-free survival Phase III, double-blind (N=2840), extended adjuvant neratinib ×1yr vs placebo started after completed trastuzumab-based (neo)adjuvant therapy in stage 1-3 HER2+ disease. Neratinib improved invasive DFS — 5-yr iDFS 90.2% vs 87.7%, HR 0.73 (0.57-0.92, P=0.0083); 2-yr iDFS HR 0.67. Benefit concentrated in hormone-receptor-positive disease and in patients starting within ~1yr of trastuzumab. Diarrhoea dominates toxicity — grade 3 in 40% without prophylaxis, the leading cause of early discontinuation (mitigated by loperamide prophylaxis). The only therapy to improve iDFS beyond a completed trastuzumab year (contrast HERA's null 2nd year); a selective option for high-risk HR-positive disease outside the response-adapted pathway; OS not established.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2016;17:367-377   Martin M et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1688-1700 5-yr iDFS analysis 29146401

records.title: APT (Adjuvant Paclitaxel + Trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · II · 2015
records.body: HER2-positive invasive tumours <=3 cm, node-negative, or one nodal micrometastasis after axillary dissection with no further involvement (small, low-risk) Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly ×12 + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly ×12), then trastuzumab monotherapy (6 mg/kg Q3W or weekly) to complete 1 year (single-arm) Disease-free survival Single-arm phase II (N=406) in small (≤3 cm), node-negative HER2+ disease (predominantly stage I): weekly paclitaxel + trastuzumab ×12 weeks → trastuzumab to complete 1 year, no comparator by design (these patients were largely excluded from the pivotal trials). Excellent long-term outcomes at the final 10-yr analysis (median 10.8yr): iDFS 91.3% (95% CI 88.3-94.4), recurrence-free interval 96.3%, OS 94.3%, breast-cancer-specific survival 98.8%. Low toxicity — grade 3 neuropathy 3.2%, symptomatic heart failure 0.5% (both reversible). Established paclitaxel + trastuzumab as the de-escalation standard for small node-negative HER2+ tumours — the low-risk floor of the stream.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2015;372:134-141   Tolaney SM et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:1868-1875 7-yr DFS analysis 30939096 Lancet Oncol 2023;24:273-285 10-yr final analysis 36858723

records.title: ATEMPT
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · II · 2021
records.body: Centrally confirmed HER2-positive stage I invasive breast cancer, tumour <=2 cm, node-negative or one nodal micrometastasis (N1mi) Adjuvant T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W ×17 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly ×12 + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly), then trastuzumab 6 mg/kg Q3W ×39 weeks (TH); both to complete 1 year Invasive disease-free survival; toxicity Randomised phase II (3:1; 512 randomised, 497 treated) in stage I HER2+ disease: adjuvant T-DM1 ×17 cycles vs paclitaxel + trastuzumab (TH). T-DM1 efficacy was excellent — 5-yr iDFS 97.0% (95% CI 95.2-98.7), recurrence-free interval 98.3%, breast-cancer-specific survival 99.4% (median 5.8yr; primary 3-yr iDFS 97.8%). It did not de-escalate toxicity, though: the co-primary endpoint of clinically relevant toxicities was 46% (T-DM1) vs 47% (TH), P=0.83, so overall toxicity was unchanged — the profile shifted (less neuropathy/alopecia, more thrombocytopenia/transaminitis) rather than shrank. Establishes T-DM1 as a validated alternative to APT's TH for stage I disease, chosen on which toxicities a patient most wants to avoid.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2375-2385   Tarantino P et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3652-3665 5-yr results 38935923

records.title: GeparSixto
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · II · 2014
records.body: Neoadjuvant stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC cohort of GeparSixto) Paclitaxel + liposomal doxorubicin +/- carboplatin (weekly AUC-1.5) for 18 weeks Pathologic complete response (pCR) Randomised phase 2 (GBG 66; TNBC cohort N=315) adding carboplatin to weekly paclitaxel and non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. Carboplatin raised pCR (ypT0 ypN0) in TNBC from 36.9% to 53.2% (P=0.005) and, on the 2018 survival analysis, significantly improved 3-year DFS (86.1% vs 75.8%, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.34–0.93, P=0.022); the OS gain was not significant. Added grade 3/4 haematologic toxicity (neutropenia 65% vs 27%); the HRD score did not predict platinum benefit. First randomised evidence for neoadjuvant platinum in TNBC; its DFS benefit contrasts with CALGB 40603's flat long-term survival.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2014;15:747-756   Ann Oncol 2018;29:2341-2347 final survival analysis + HRD score 30335131 JAMA Oncol 2017;3:1378-1385 germline mutation status, pCR & DFS 28715532 PLoS One 2020;15:e0238021 MGMT promoter methylation (exploratory) 32841306

records.title: CALGB 40603 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · II · 2015
records.body: Stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant; 2x2 randomization) Weekly paclitaxel → dose-dense doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide (ddAC) as neoadjuvant backbone; 2×2 factorial ± carboplatin AUC 6 IV Q3W ×4 and/or bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV Q2W ×9 pCR (long-term outcomes secondary) 2×2 factorial randomised phase 2 (N=443, stage II–III) of carboplatin and/or bevacizumab added to weekly paclitaxel then dose-dense AC. Carboplatin raised pCR (breast/axilla 54% vs 41%, OR 1.71, P=0.003; breast 60% vs 46%) but at 7.9-year median follow-up did not significantly improve EFS (HR 0.94) or OS (HR 1.12) — the trial was underpowered for survival. pCR was strongly prognostic (5-year EFS 85.5% vs 56.6% for residual disease; even minimal RCB-I fared worse). Immune activation (TILs, low B-cell-receptor evenness) independently predicted pCR and EFS. Landmark case of a pCR gain not translating to a proven survival benefit; the survival question was later tested by Gupta 2026.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2015;33:13-21   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1323-1334 long-term outcomes 35044810

records.title: BrighTNess
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · III · 2018
records.body: Neoadjuvant stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer Paclitaxel → AC; + carboplatin; + carboplatin + veliparib (PARP inhibitor) Pathologic complete response (pCR) Double-blind phase 3 (N=634) randomising (2:1:1) neoadjuvant paclitaxel + carboplatin + veliparib vs paclitaxel + carboplatin vs paclitaxel alone, each followed by AC. Carboplatin raised pCR (58% carboplatin arm vs 31% paclitaxel alone); adding veliparib gave no further gain (53% vs 58%, P=0.36). At 4.5-year follow-up EFS favoured the carboplatin-containing arm (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.43–0.92, P=0.02 vs paclitaxel; carboplatin-alone-vs-paclitaxel post-hoc HR 0.57), with no OS difference and no excess MDS/AML. Added haematologic toxicity (grade 3/4 neutropenia 56%, febrile neutropenia 15%). Confirmed carboplatin's independent contribution; veliparib added nothing.

records.title: TMC TNBC Platinum Trial (Gupta)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · III · 2026
records.body: Neoadjuvant stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + weekly paclitaxel ×8 weeks → anthracycline (doxorubicin or epirubicin)–cyclophosphamide Q3W ×4 (neoadjuvant) vs the same taxane–anthracycline backbone without carboplatin Event-free survival (EFS) Single-centre phase 3 (N=717, Tata Memorial) adding weekly carboplatin (AUC-2) to sequential paclitaxel then anthracycline. The primary endpoint, EFS, was not significantly improved (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03, P=0.081 — formally negative); OS was nominally better (5-year 74.4% vs 66.8%, HR 0.74, P=0.029) and pCR higher (54.5% vs 40.3%). A significant menopausal-status interaction confined the whole benefit to premenopausal patients (EFS HR 0.61, OS HR 0.57, pCR 61.7% vs 40.6%), with none in postmenopausal disease. Only the primary EFS was alpha-controlled, so the OS and subgroup P-values are nominal. Phase-3 survival test of the carboplatin question: supports platinum in premenopausal TNBC, argues against it postmenopausally.

records.title: KEYNOTE-522
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2020
records.body: High-risk stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant/adjuvant) Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin–paclitaxel ×4 cycles → pembrolizumab + AC/EC ×4 cycles, then adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×9 cycles vs placebo + the same chemotherapy backbone → adjuvant placebo pCR (co-primary) and event-free survival (EFS); OS (final analysis) Phase 3 (N=1174, stage II–III): neoadjuvant pembrolizumab + carboplatin–paclitaxel then anthracycline, continued as adjuvant pembrolizumab, vs the same chemotherapy + placebo. Every link of the pCR-to-EFS-to-OS chain was formally tested and cleared its own alpha boundary. pCR 64.8% vs 51.2% in the first 602 randomised (+13.6 points, 95% CI 5.4–21.8; P<0.001 vs a 0.003 boundary). EFS at the fourth interim (2022 update) HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.48–0.82), P<0.001 vs a 0.01034 boundary. At the final OS analysis (median follow-up 75.1 months) the whole-period stratified log-rank gave P=0.002 vs a 0.00503 boundary, deaths 14.7% vs 21.8%; no overall OS hazard ratio is reported — 5-year survival 86.6% vs 81.7% is a descriptive landmark pair, untested, and the weighted HR 0.66 an unstratified non-proportional-hazards sensitivity analysis with no interval or p-value. Benefit was PD-L1-independent (across all CPS strata on the 22C3 assay). Outcome-defined subgroups are nonrandomised exploratory analyses carrying no alpha and no test between categories: no-pCR stratum EFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.52–0.95); by residual disease RCB-1 0.92, RCB-2 0.52 (95% CI 0.32–0.82), RCB-3 1.24. Grade ≥3 immune-mediated adverse events 13.0% vs 1.5%. Established perioperative chemo-immunotherapy as standard for high-risk early TNBC; the neoadjuvant-versus-adjuvant contribution is not separable.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;382:810-821   N Engl J Med 2022;386:556-567 event-free survival interim analysis 35139274 N Engl J Med 2024;391:1981-1991 final overall survival (filed col K) 39282906 Ann Oncol 2024;35:429-436 RCB exploratory analysis 38369015

records.title: NeoPACT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · II · 2024
records.body: Stage I-III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant; single-arm) Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin–docetaxel ×6 cycles (anthracycline-free; single-arm, no randomised comparator) Pathological complete response (pCR) Single-arm phase 2 (N=115, stage I–III) of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab on an anthracycline-free carboplatin–docetaxel backbone (6 cycles). pCR 58% (95% CI 48–67) and RCB 0+1 69%, with 3-year EFS 86% (98% if pCR vs 68% if not) and low grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs (3.5%, no hypophysitis or adrenal insufficiency); sTILs, PD-L1, DDIR and TIM signatures each independently predicted pCR. Supports an anthracycline-free de-escalation option for patients unsuitable for anthracyclines, but needs randomised confirmation (no comparator vs KEYNOTE-522; SCARLET is the test).

records.title: GeparNuevo (durvalumab)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · II · 2019
records.body: Early triple-negative breast cancer (cT1b-cT4a-d) Durvalumab 1.5 g IV Q4W (0.75 g window dose 2 weeks before chemotherapy) + nab-paclitaxel → dose-dense epirubicin–cyclophosphamide (neoadjuvant) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy backbone; no adjuvant checkpoint continuation pCR (primary); long-term iDFS/DDFS/OS Randomised, double-blind phase 2 (N=174) adding neoadjuvant durvalumab to a nab-paclitaxel then dose-dense EC backbone (no carboplatin), with no adjuvant checkpoint continuation. The pCR gain was modest and non-significant (53.4% vs 44.2%, OR 1.45, P=0.287), yet at 86.4-month median follow-up durvalumab improved iDFS (HR 0.56), distant DFS (HR 0.41) and OS (HR 0.33), sustained and irrespective of pathologic response — a pCR-versus-survival disconnect that generalises the checkpoint benefit to the anti-PD-L1 class. Being neoadjuvant-only, it feeds the question of whether adjuvant continuation (as in KEYNOTE-522) is required. Hypothesis-generating given the phase 2 size.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2019;30:1279-1288   J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1580-1586 long-term analysis 42008768

records.title: CREATE-X (JBCRG-04)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — post-neoadjuvant therapy (residual disease) · III · 2017
records.body: HER2-negative (TNBC and HR+) residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 Q3W ×8 cycles vs observation (standard postsurgical therapy without capecitabine) Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=910, Japan/Korea) of adjuvant capecitabine vs observation in HER2-negative residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane. Capecitabine improved 5-year DFS (74.1% vs 67.6%, HR 0.70, P=0.01) and OS (89.2% vs 83.6%, HR 0.59, P=0.01), with the benefit concentrated in the triple-negative subset (DFS HR 0.58, OS HR 0.52) and smaller and non-significant in HR-positive disease (DFS HR 0.81, OS HR 0.73). Established adjuvant capecitabine as standard for TNBC residual disease and, with KATHERINE, a pillar of response-directed post-neoadjuvant escalation; how to sequence it with adjuvant pembrolizumab is untested.

records.title: RJBC-1501
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin) · III · 2026
records.body: Resected early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (adjuvant setting) Adjuvant EC x4 → taxane + carboplatin (AUC-2 weekly or AUC-5–6 q3wk with docetaxel) vs EC x4 → taxane alone Disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=786) of adjuvant epirubicin–cyclophosphamide then taxane with or without carboplatin in resected early TNBC. Adding carboplatin improved DFS (3-year 93.1% vs 89.8%, HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44–0.97, P=0.034), distant DFS (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.38–0.98, P=0.040) and OS (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.16–0.94, P=0.029) at 4.5-year median follow-up. More grade 3/4 haematologic toxicity (any grade 3/4 AE 49.9% vs 38.7%, neutropenia 47.0% vs 37.8%) with no new safety signals. Supports adjuvant platinum as an option in early TNBC — the adjuvant counterpart to the neoadjuvant carboplatin question (GeparSixto, BrighTNess, Gupta 2026).

records.title: OlympiA
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — adjuvant targeted therapy (germline BRCA-mutated) · III · 2021
records.body: Germline BRCA1/2, HER2-negative (TNBC or HR+) high-risk early breast cancer after (neo)adjuvant chemo Adjuvant olaparib 300 mg twice daily ×1 year vs placebo Invasive disease-free survival Phase 3 (N=1836) of one year of adjuvant olaparib vs placebo in germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative, high-risk early breast cancer (predominantly triple-negative) after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Olaparib improved 3-year iDFS (85.9% vs 77.1%, +8.8 points, HR 0.58, P<0.001) and distant DFS (HR 0.57), and at the second interim delivered a significant OS benefit (4-year 89.8% vs 86.4%, HR 0.68, 98.5% CI 0.47–0.97, P=0.009). Anaemia the signature toxicity; no excess MDS/AML. First targeted adjuvant therapy in this population and the only germline-BRCA escalation with a proven OS benefit; sequencing with adjuvant pembrolizumab or capecitabine is untested.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:2394-2405   Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-1268 overall survival analysis 36228963

records.title: IMpassion130
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated metastatic/unresectable locally advanced TNBC (PD-L1 IC+ subgroup primary) Atezolizumab 840 mg IV days 1 & 15 of a 28-day cycle + nab-paclitaxel vs placebo + nab-paclitaxel; to progression Progression-free survival & overall survival Phase 3 (N=902), first-line atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel vs placebo + nab-paclitaxel. PFS favoured atezolizumab in the ITT population (7.2 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.80, P=0.002) and more so in PD-L1-positive (SP142 IC≥1%) disease (7.5 vs 5.0 months, HR 0.62). Because ITT OS was not significant (final HR 0.87, P=0.077), the PD-L1-positive OS benefit (25.4 vs 17.9 months, HR 0.67) could only be reported descriptively. First immunotherapy in mTNBC; the survival win its testing hierarchy left untested is what KEYNOTE-355 (22C3 CPS ≥10) later proved. The atezolizumab mTNBC indication was withdrawn after the negative IMpassion131.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2018;379:2108-2121   Lancet Oncol 2020;21:44-59 updated efficacy / 2nd interim OS 31786121 Ann Oncol 2021;32:983-993 final overall survival analysis 34272041

records.title: KEYNOTE-355
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2020
records.body: Untreated locally recurrent inoperable/metastatic TNBC (PD-L1 CPS ≥10 subgroup) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) + chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy Progression-free survival & overall survival Phase 3 (N=847), first-line pembrolizumab + investigator's-choice chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) vs placebo + chemotherapy. In PD-L1 CPS ≥10 disease (22C3) pembrolizumab improved PFS (9.7 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.65, P=0.0012) and OS (23.0 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55–0.95, P=0.0185) — a formally significant survival benefit. The benefit was confined to CPS ≥10: it did not reach significance at CPS ≥1 (OS HR 0.86), the ITT population went untested, and CPS 1–9 showed no gain. Established pembrolizumab + chemotherapy as the durable first-line standard for PD-L1-high mTNBC, proving the survival win IMpassion130's hierarchy could not test.
records.keywords: Lancet 2020;396:1817-1828   N Engl J Med 2022;387:217-226 final OS analysis 35857659

records.title: IMpassion131
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC (PD-L1 IC+ primary analysis) Atezolizumab + paclitaxel vs placebo + paclitaxel Progression-free survival Phase 3 (N=651), first-line atezolizumab + solvent-based paclitaxel vs placebo + paclitaxel. Adding atezolizumab did not improve PFS in PD-L1-positive (SP142 IC≥1%) disease (6.0 vs 5.7 months, HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.60–1.12, P=0.20), and OS numerically favoured placebo (22.1 vs 28.3 months, HR 1.11); negative in both the PD-L1-positive and ITT populations. Directly discordant with IMpassion130 (same antibody, nab-paclitaxel there), implicating the taxane formulation and its corticosteroid premedication; the atezolizumab mTNBC indication was withdrawn. KEYNOTE-355's success including with paclitaxel later weakened the steroid explanation.

records.title: ASCENT-04 (KEYNOTE-D19)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated PD-L1+ (CPS ≥10) locally advanced/metastatic TNBC Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs chemotherapy (physician's choice — taxane or gemcitabine–carboplatin) + pembrolizumab Progression-free survival Phase 3 (N=443), first-line PD-L1 CPS ≥10 mTNBC: sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab vs the KEYNOTE-355 regimen (chemotherapy + pembrolizumab). SG + pembrolizumab improved PFS (11.2 vs 7.8 months, HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51–0.84, P<0.001) with much longer response duration (16.5 vs 9.2 months) and far less discontinuation for toxicity (12% vs 31%); ORR similar (60% vs 53%). Overall survival was immature and untested (crossover-confounded), so no survival claim. First trial to improve on the chemo-immunotherapy standard by substituting the ADC for the chemotherapy on a retained pembrolizumab backbone — a PFS-led, provisional challenge pending OS.

records.title: ASCENT-03
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line TROP2 ADCs (immunotherapy-ineligible) · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC ineligible for PD-(L)1 inhibitors (PD-L1-negative or prior IO) Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs chemotherapy (physician's choice — paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) Progression-free survival Phase 3 (N=558), first-line SG monotherapy vs single-agent chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible mTNBC (99% PD-L1-negative). SG improved PFS (9.7 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50–0.77, P<0.001) with similar ORR (48% vs 46%) but far more durable responses (DoR 12.2 vs 7.2 months); OS was immature and untested (21.5 vs 20.2 months, heavy crossover), so no survival claim. Grade ≥3 neutropenia 43%, with early neutropenic-sepsis deaths prompting primary G-CSF prophylaxis; discontinuation for toxicity 4% vs 12%. Here the control genuinely is chemotherapy alone, so SG beat chemotherapy first-line for the PD-L1-negative group that chemo-immunotherapy leaves behind.

records.title: TROPION-Breast02
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line TROP2 ADCs (immunotherapy-ineligible) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC for whom immunotherapy was not an option Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6 mg/kg IV Q3W vs investigator's choice chemotherapy (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, eribulin, or capecitabine) Progression-free survival & overall survival Phase 3 (N=644), first-line datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible mTNBC (~90% PD-L1-low). Meeting both dual primary endpoints, Dato-DXd improved PFS (10.8 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.57, 99% CI 0.44–0.73, P<0.0001) and OS (23.7 vs 18.7 months, HR 0.79, 95.01% CI 0.64–0.98, P=0.029), with more than doubled ORR (63% vs 29%). Deruxtecan-class toxicity (stomatitis, ocular surface events, adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis 3%) with no treatment-related deaths and lower discontinuation (4% vs 7%). First first-line TROP2 ADC to prove OS in TNBC; sits beside SG (ASCENT-03) as a payload/toxicity choice, never compared head-to-head.

records.title: ASCENT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — pretreated disease (antibody-drug conjugates) · III · 2021
records.body: Relapsed/refractory metastatic TNBC, ≥2 prior chemotherapy lines (no active brain metastases) Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs single-agent chemotherapy (physician's choice — eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine) Progression-free survival Phase 3 (N=468, brain-metastasis-negative primary population) of sacituzumab govitecan vs single-agent chemotherapy in relapsed/refractory mTNBC (median 3 prior anticancer regimens, all taxane-exposed). SG improved PFS (5.6 vs 1.7 months, HR 0.41) and OS (12.1 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.48, both P<0.001), with ORR 35% vs 5%. The final ITT analysis (N=529, including brain-metastasis-positive patients) confirmed the benefit — OS 11.8 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.51 (0.42–0.63). Signature toxicity neutropenia (grade ≥3 51%) and diarrhoea (grade ≥3 10%); no treatment-related deaths. First TROP2 ADC to prove survival in TNBC and the origin of the SG story; its mature pretreated OS is the contrast with SG's still-immature first-line survival (ASCENT-03/-04).

records.body: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (≤2 prior chemotherapy lines) Olaparib 300 mg twice daily vs single-agent chemotherapy (physician's choice — capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine) Progression-free survival Phase 3 (N=302, 2:1) of olaparib vs single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice in germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (about half triple-negative, half HR-positive — selected by genotype, not receptor phenotype). Olaparib improved PFS (7.0 vs 4.2 months, HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43–0.80, P<0.001) and roughly doubled ORR (59.9% vs 28.8%); final OS was not improved overall (19.3 vs 17.1 months, HR 0.90, not powered, crossover-confounded), with a non-alpha-controlled first-line-metastatic subgroup signal (HR 0.51). Better tolerated than chemotherapy (grade ≥3 AEs 36.6% vs 50.5%). First PARP inhibitor approved in breast cancer; olaparib-versus-platinum left untested.

records.body: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (≤3 prior chemotherapy lines) Talazoparib 1 mg once daily vs single-agent chemotherapy (physician's choice — capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine) Progression-free survival Phase 3 (N=431, 2:1) of talazoparib vs single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice in germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (~44% triple-negative, 56% HR-positive; selected by genotype). Talazoparib improved PFS (8.6 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41–0.71, P<0.001) and more than doubled ORR (62.6% vs 27.2%); interim OS was not significant (22.3 vs 19.5 months, HR 0.76, immature). Reproduces OlympiAD's shape with a second, more potent PARP inhibitor — a class effect, not a head-to-head ranking.

records.title: TNT (CRUK/07/012)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — germline BRCA-mutated disease (PARP inhibitors & platinum) · III · 2018
records.body: First-line advanced/metastatic TNBC or germline BRCA1/2 breast cancer Carboplatin vs docetaxel Objective response rate Phase 3 (N=376), first-line carboplatin vs docetaxel in advanced TNBC or germline BRCA1/2 breast cancer; primary endpoint objective response. In unselected TNBC the two were equivalent (ORR 31.4% vs 34.0%, P=0.66), but in germline BRCA carriers carboplatin doubled response over docetaxel (68% vs 33%, treatment-biomarker interaction P=0.01). BRCA1 promoter methylation, low BRCA1 mRNA and a Myriad HRD score did not predict platinum benefit. Establishes that germline BRCA status selects TNBC patients for platinum, whereas broader 'BRCAness' assays do not; the platinum comparator the PARP trials (OlympiAD, EMBRACA) never included.

records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · CDK4/6-inhibitor sequencing & continuation · III · 2024
records.body: First-line HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer (early vs deferred CDK4/6i strategy) First-line vs second-line CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy Second progression-free survival (PFS2) Strategy trial: identical AI-then-fulvestrant sequence in both arms, only the CDK4/6 inhibitor's timing randomized (first line vs deferred to second line). records.title: H0648g (pivotal trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2001
records.body: Untreated HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer First-line trastuzumab 4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg IV weekly (to progression) added to chemotherapy — doxorubicin (or epirubicin)–cyclophosphamide, or paclitaxel if prior adjuvant anthracycline, Q3W for 6 cycles — vs the same chemotherapy alone Time to progression Phase III, N=469, first-line HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer; trastuzumab added to chemotherapy (anthracycline-cyclophosphamide, or paclitaxel after prior adjuvant anthracycline) vs chemotherapy alone. Adding trastuzumab prolonged time to progression (7.4 vs 4.6 months, p<0.001), raised objective response (50% vs 32%, p<0.001), and, uniquely for its era, improved overall survival (25.1 vs 20.3 months, p=0.046). Concurrent anthracycline-trastuzumab caused cardiac dysfunction in 27% (vs 8% with anthracycline alone), which is why the durable HER2 backbone became a taxane rather than an anthracycline; the founding proof that blocking HER2 works, and the backbone CLEOPATRA's dual blockade later layered onto.

records.title: CLEOPATRA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2012
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer Pertuzumab 840 mg loading then 420 mg IV Q3W + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W + docetaxel (≥6 cycles); antibodies to progression vs placebo + trastuzumab + docetaxel (same) Progression-free survival Phase III, N=808, first-line HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer; pertuzumab added to trastuzumab + docetaxel vs trastuzumab + docetaxel. Dual HER2 blockade improved the primary independently-assessed progression-free survival (18.5 vs 12.4 months, HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51-0.75; p<0.001) and final overall survival (56.5 vs 40.8 months, HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.84), with a durable 8-year landmark survival of 37% vs 23% and no added cardiotoxicity. THP set the first-line standard for a decade and remains the comparator every later first-line trial uses; DESTINY-Breast09 now beats it on interim progression-free survival, but with overall survival and guideline status pending, that is a contest rather than a settled displacement.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast09
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive advanced/metastatic breast cancer First-line trastuzumab deruxtecan + pertuzumab vs taxane (paclitaxel or docetaxel) + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (THP); to progression Progression-free survival T-DXd + pertuzumab markedly improved PFS, extending median PFS from 26.9 to 40.7 months (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.44-0.71); sets a new first-line benchmark (OS immature).

records.title: PERUSE
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH-positive) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer, with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease except <=2 endocrine lines; stable treated CNS metastases allowed; excluded progression during (neo)adjuvant trastuzumab/lapatinib or recurrence within 6 mo of adjuvant non-hormonal therapy (single-arm) Investigator-selected docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel weekly or Q3W + pertuzumab 840 mg loading then 420 mg Q3W + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W; to progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or death Safety and tolerability: incidence and severity of adverse events and LVEF measurements Mature single-arm PERUSE suggests paclitaxel is a practical taxane alternative with first-line pertuzumab-trastuzumab; at 5.7 years' median follow-up, PFS was 20.7 mo and OS 65.3 mo overall. Paclitaxel and docetaxel subgroups had descriptively similar PFS (23.2 vs 19.4 mo) and OS (64.0 vs 66.5 mo); taxane choice was not randomised and no formal comparisons were performed. ORR was 79%. Grade 3+ neutropenia was 5% with paclitaxel vs 15% with docetaxel and febrile neutropenia 1% vs 11%, while grade 3+ diarrhoea was 9% vs 8%; fatal AEs occurred in 2%.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2019;30:766-773  30796821 Ann Oncol 2021;32:1245-1255 final efficacy and safety analysis 34224826

records.title: EMILIA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Second-line metastatic disease · III · 2012
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after trastuzumab + a taxane T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W; to progression vs lapatinib 1250 mg once daily + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle Progression-free survival and overall survival Phase III, N=991, HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after trastuzumab and a taxane; T-DM1 vs lapatinib + capecitabine. T-DM1 improved progression-free survival (9.6 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.55-0.77) and overall survival (30.9 vs 25.1 months, HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.85; second interim crossed the efficacy boundary), with less toxicity than the oral doublet. The first antibody-drug conjugate shown to extend life in breast cancer, it set the second-line standard and moved the HER2 backbone from blocking the receptor to using it as a delivery address, a standard DESTINY-Breast03 later refined rather than overturned.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast03
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Second-line metastatic disease · III · 2022
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab + a taxane T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W; to progression Progression-free survival Phase III, N=524, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab and a taxane; T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg vs T-DM1. At the primary analysis median progression-free survival with T-DXd was not reached (95% CI 18.5-NE) vs 6.8 months (HR for progression or death 0.28, 95% CI 0.22-0.37; p<0.001), with confirmed objective response 79.7% vs 34.2%; overall survival was immature, the prespecified interim boundary not crossed. This decisive second-line result displaced T-DM1 as the EMILIA-defined standard, the clearest proof in this stream that an antibody-drug conjugate's payload and linker, not the shared trastuzumab antibody, decide its reach.

records.title: EGF100151 (lapatinib + capecitabine)
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2006
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer progressing after anthracycline, taxane, and trastuzumab Lapatinib 1250 mg once daily + capecitabine 2000 mg/m² daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle vs capecitabine 2500 mg/m² daily days 1–14 alone; to progression Time to progression Phase III, N=324, HER2-positive advanced breast cancer progressing after anthracycline, taxane, and trastuzumab; lapatinib + capecitabine vs capecitabine alone. The interim analysis stopped early: lapatinib roughly doubled independently-assessed time to progression (8.4 vs 4.4 months, HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34-0.71). Fewer patients had the central nervous system as the first site of progression (4 vs 11, p=0.10), a statistically soft signal but the first hint that a small-molecule HER2 inhibitor might reach the brain. The first oral HER2-directed regimen active after trastuzumab failure, and the origin of the HER2 tyrosine-kinase-inhibitor modality whose own regimen NALA later used as its comparator.

records.title: TH3RESA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2014
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after ≥2 HER2-directed regimens (incl. trastuzumab and lapatinib) T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W; to progression vs treatment of physician's choice Progression-free survival and overall survival Phase III, N=602, HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after at least two HER2-directed regimens (including trastuzumab and lapatinib); T-DM1 vs treatment of physician's choice. T-DM1 improved progression-free survival (6.2 vs 3.3 months, HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.42-0.66; p<0.001) and, on the 2017 final analysis, overall survival (22.7 vs 15.8 months, HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.54-0.85; p=0.0007), with a distinctive haemorrhage signal (grade 3 or worse in 4% vs <1%). The confirmatory bookend that carried T-DM1 beyond second line into the third, before the more potent conjugates and CNS-active tyrosine-kinase inhibitors overtook that position.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2014;15:689-699; Lancet Oncol 2017;18:743-754   Krop et al. - 2017 - Trastuzumab emtansine versus treatment of physician's choice in patients with previously treated [664afd5c]

records.title: DESTINY-Breast01
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · II · 2020
records.body: Heavily pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after T-DM1 (median 6 prior lines) Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W (single-arm); to progression or toxicity Objective response rate Single-arm phase II, N=184, heavily pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after T-DM1 (median six prior lines); T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg. Confirmed objective response was 60.9% (95% CI 53.4-68.0) with median progression-free survival 16.4 months and no comparator arm, the result that won T-DXd its first (accelerated) approval. It also surfaced the drug's defining risk: interstitial lung disease in 13.6% of patients, including four fatal (grade 5) events (2.2%), the first T-DXd-related deaths in this stream. The single-arm origin later confirmed with randomised, hazard-ratio-bearing evidence by DESTINY-Breast02 and DESTINY-Breast03.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast02
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2023
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after T-DM1 T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs treatment of physician's choice — capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W, or capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 + lapatinib 1250 mg once daily; to progression Progression-free survival Phase III, N=608, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after T-DM1 (median two prior lines); T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg vs treatment of physician's choice (capecitabine with trastuzumab or lapatinib). T-DXd improved progression-free survival (17.8 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.28-0.45; p<0.001) and overall survival (39.2 vs 26.5 months, HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.86). DESTINY-Breast01's randomised successor at a materially lighter pretreatment burden, it is the first randomised proof that one antibody-drug conjugate can overcome acquired resistance to a prior one built on the same trastuzumab antibody.

records.title: HER2CLIMB
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2020
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and T-DM1 (~48% with brain metastases) Tucatinib 300 mg twice daily + trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (8 mg/kg loading) + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle; to progression vs placebo + trastuzumab + capecitabine (same) Progression-free survival Phase III, N=612, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and T-DM1, enrolling patients with brain metastases (about half), including active lesions by design; tucatinib added to trastuzumab + capecitabine vs placebo added to the same. Tucatinib improved progression-free survival (7.8 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.42-0.71; p<0.001) and overall survival (21.9 vs 17.4 months, HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.88; p=0.005), and among patients with brain metastases reduced the risk of progression or death (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.34-0.69). The first HER2-selective tyrosine-kinase inhibitor and the CNS-directed anchor of the stream.

records.title: NALA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2020
records.body: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after ≥2 HER2-directed regimens Neratinib 240 mg once daily + capecitabine 750 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle (with loperamide prophylaxis) vs lapatinib 1250 mg once daily + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14; to progression Progression-free survival and overall survival (co-primary) Phase III, N=621, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after at least two HER2-directed regimens; neratinib + capecitabine vs lapatinib + capecitabine, the first head-to-head of two HER2 tyrosine-kinase inhibitors and against EGF100151's own regimen. Centrally-reviewed progression-free survival improved (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63-0.93; p=0.006; 12-month rate 29% vs 15%, medians flat at 5.6 vs 5.5 months), as did duration of response, and fewer patients required intervention for central nervous system disease (cumulative incidence 22.8% vs 29.2%; p=0.043). Overall survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72-1.07; restricted-mean 24.0 vs 22.2 months).

records.title: SOPHIA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2021
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after ≥2 HER2-directed therapies Margetuximab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W + physician's-choice chemotherapy (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine) vs trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (8 mg/kg loading) + the same chemotherapy; to progression Progression-free survival Phase III, N=536, HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after at least two HER2-directed therapies; the Fc-engineered anti-HER2 antibody margetuximab plus chemotherapy vs trastuzumab plus the same chemotherapy (an active anti-HER2 comparator). Margetuximab modestly improved progression-free survival (5.8 vs 4.9 months, HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59-0.98; p=0.03); overall survival was not significantly improved at the second interim analysis (21.6 vs 19.8 months, HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.69-1.13), with the final analysis pending. Its prespecified but non-alpha-controlled CD16A-158F genotype signal is hypothesis-generating only, under prospective test (MARGOT). The softest effect in the third-line cluster, and a distinct axis: re-engineering the antibody's effector function rather than its payload or intracellular target.

records.title: HORIZON-Breast01
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2026
records.body: HER2-positive unresectable/metastatic breast cancer previously treated with a taxane and trastuzumab (advanced-stage) or progressing within 12 months of (neo)adjuvant anti-HER2 antibody + taxane (China, 50 hospitals) Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) 4.8 mg/kg IV day 1 Q3W vs pyrotinib 400 mg once daily + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle; to progression Progression-free survival (BICR) Interim analysis: trastuzumab rezetecan markedly improved PFS vs pyrotinib+capecitabine (30.6 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.15-0.34, p<0.0001); 12-month PFS rate 84.7% vs 35.5%. Distinct safety profile (more haematologic toxicity; ILD in 3%) vs the oral TKI-chemo doublet. China-only interim readout of a new HER2 ADC positioned to displace pyrotinib+capecitabine in later-line HER2+ MBC; OS immature.

records.title: PRECIOUS
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Third-line & later — ADCs, TKIs & antibodies · III · 2022
records.body: HER2-positive locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer progressing after prior pertuzumab-containing 1st/2nd-line therapy (Japan) Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + physician's-choice chemotherapy (PTC) vs trastuzumab + physician's-choice chemotherapy (TC) (1:1) Progression-free survival (investigator-assessed) Phase III, N=219, HER2-positive advanced breast cancer progressing after a prior pertuzumab-containing regimen (Japan); pertuzumab re-added to trastuzumab + physician's-choice chemotherapy vs trastuzumab + physician's-choice chemotherapy. Investigator-assessed progression-free survival favoured retreatment (5.3 vs 4.2 months, HR 0.76, one-sided 95% CI upper 0.97; p=0.022), but on the 2025 analysis independent-review PFS was flat (4.4 vs 4.4 months, HR 1.03), a stated investigator-versus-blinded-review discordance. Final overall survival favoured retreatment (36.2 vs 26.5 months, HR 0.73, one-sided 95% CI upper 0.97; no p value, alpha spent on PFS). The only randomised evidence for pertuzumab retreatment, but underpowered by design, single-country and open-label.
records.keywords: Cancer Sci 2022;113:3169-3179  35754298 J Clin Oncol 2025;43:1631-1637 final overall survival analysis 39854662

records.title: DESTINY-Breast12
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · CNS / brain metastases · N/A · 2024
records.body: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer with or without brain metastases (BM cohort n=263, incl. active BM) Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W (single-arm); to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival (brain-metastases cohort) Prospective single-arm cohort, N=263 with baseline brain metastases (including active lesions), tucatinib-naive by design; T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg with no comparator arm, so no hazard ratio exists. In the brain-metastases cohort median progression-free survival was 17.3 months (12-month rate 61.6%) with confirmed intracranial objective response 71.7%, the largest prospective dataset confirming T-DXd's intracranial activity for stable and active brain metastases. Investigator-reported interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis occurred in 16% (brain-metastases cohort; grade 5 in 2.3%) and 13% (no brain metastases; grade 5 in 1.2%), with no central adjudication committee. Whether T-DXd or tucatinib better serves brain-metastasis disease remains untested: the trial excluded prior tucatinib by design.

records.title: PATINA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · HR-positive / HER2-positive — endocrine-containing maintenance · III · 2026
records.body: HR-positive/HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer without progression after first-line induction chemotherapy + HER2 therapy Maintenance palbociclib 125 mg once daily (3 weeks on, 1 week off) + anti-HER2 therapy (trastuzumab + pertuzumab) + endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant); to progression vs anti-HER2 + endocrine therapy alone Progression-free survival Adding maintenance palbociclib prolonged PFS (44.3 vs 29.1 months, HR 0.75); first CDK4/6-inhibitor benefit shown in HR+/HER2+ disease, supporting endocrine-based maintenance.

records.title: NLST (National Lung Screening Trial)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Screening · N/A · 2011
records.body: Age 55-74 years; >=30 pack-year smoking history; current smokers or former smokers who quit within 15 years. Excluded previous lung cancer, chest CT within 18 months, haemoptysis, or unexplained recent weight loss Low-dose multidetector chest CT, three screens (T0, T1, T2) at 1-year intervals; positive if noncalcified nodule at least 4 mm or another suspicious abnormality vs Single-view posteroanterior chest radiography, three screens at the same 1-year intervals; positive if any noncalcified nodule/mass or another suspicious abnormality Primary: Lung-cancer-specific mortality. Secondary: All-cause mortality; lung-cancer incidence; screening performance; diagnostic-evaluation complications Annual low-dose CT screening reduced lung-cancer mortality versus chest radiography: 247 vs 309 deaths per 100,000 person-years, a 20.0% relative reduction (356 vs 443 deaths). All-cause mortality was 6.7% lower. Positive screens occurred in 24.2% vs 6.9%, and 96.4% of CT-positive results were false positive; 1 lung-cancer death was prevented per 320 people screened.

records.title: NELSON (Dutch-Belgian Lung Cancer Screening)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Screening · N/A · 2020
records.body: Age 50-74 years; current smokers or former smokers who quit within 10 years; >15 cigarettes/day for >25 years or >10/day for >30 years. Excluded moderate/severe health limitation, inability to climb two flights, weight >140 kg, specified prior cancers, lung cancer within 5 years, or chest CT within 1 year Volume-based low-dose CT at baseline, year 1, year 3, and year 5.5, with repeat CT for indeterminate nodules and pulmonology referral for positive tests vs No lung-cancer screening Primary: Lung-cancer-specific mortality. Secondary: All-cause mortality; lung-cancer incidence; screening performance; lung-cancer-specific mortality in women 4-round volume-based low-dose CT screening reduced 10-year lung-cancer mortality in men: 2.50 vs 3.30 deaths per 1,000 person-years (rate ratio 0.76). All-cause mortality was unchanged (rate ratio 1.01, 95% CI 0.92-1.11). In women, the lung-cancer mortality rate ratio was 0.67 (0.38-1.14). Across 22,600 CT scans, 1.2% were false positive; no screening adverse events were reported.

records.title: PLUS trial (van Tinteren et al.)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2002
records.body: Suspected operable NSCLC undergoing preoperative staging Conventional workup vs conventional workup + whole-body FDG-PET Futile thoracotomy (surgery not resulting in cure) Adding PET to conventional staging reduced futile thoracotomies from 41% to 21% (relative reduction ~51%) by detecting unsuspected advanced/metastatic disease; established PET in preoperative NSCLC staging.

records.title: Fischer et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2009
records.body: Age 18-80 years; newly diagnosed or highly suspected NSCLC considered operable after conventional staging. Excluded confirmed distant metastases, another malignancy, type 1 diabetes, claustrophobia, or estimated postoperative FEV1 <30% Conventional staging plus integrated PET-CT, then mandatory mediastinoscopy and other invasive staging as indicated vs Conventional staging alone, then mandatory mediastinoscopy and other invasive staging as indicated Primary: Futile thoracotomy. Secondary: Total and justified thoracotomies; diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for operability; relapse; overall survival Adding PET-CT to conventional preoperative staging reduced futile thoracotomy from 42% to 21%, avoiding 1 futile operation per 5 PET-CT scans. Among patients undergoing thoracotomy, futile procedures were 35% vs 52%. Total thoracotomy was also lower (61% vs 80%), without an overall-survival improvement (median 31 vs 49 months).

records.title: Maziak et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2009
records.body: Clinical stage I-IIIA NSCLC considered resectable Conventional staging vs conventional + PET-CT Correct upstaging / disease stage PET-CT more often correctly upstaged disease and identified patients who would not benefit from surgery, refining selection for thoracotomy.

records.title: Schoenmaekers et al. (brain MRI vs CE-CT)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2019
records.body: Stage III NSCLC staged by FDG-PET/CE-CT, neurologically asymptomatic Dedicated contrast-enhanced brain CT vs additional brain MRI Occult brain metastases on MRI missed by CE-CT Brain MRI detected occult brain metastases not seen on dedicated CE-CT in a meaningful proportion of asymptomatic stage III patients, supporting brain MRI over CT for staging of locally advanced NSCLC.

records.title: Streamline L trial (Taylor et al.)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2019
records.body: Histologically proven or clinically diagnosed NSCLC on chest CT, referred for staging and potentially radically treatable (TNM7 stage <=IIIB, T1-4 N0-2 M0). Non-NSCLC histology was excluded; clinically diagnosed NSCLC remained eligible. Excluded MRI contraindication, pregnancy, severe systemic disease, or inappropriate further workup Whole-body MRI staging pathway (diffusion, T2, and pre/post-gadolinium T1 sequences) plus additional tests generated by multidisciplinary review vs Contemporaneous standard NHS staging investigations selected in usual care, interpreted without WB-MRI findings Primary: Sensitivity for metastatic disease. Secondary: Specificity; treatment-decision agreement; staging time; test number and cost; per-organ accuracy; T-stage and N-stage agreement Whole-body MRI did not improve per-patient sensitivity for metastatic disease versus standard staging: 50% vs 54%, difference -4 points (95% CI -15 to 7; P=.73); specificity was 93% vs 95%. It shortened median staging time from 19 to 13 days and reduced mean cost from £620 to £317, but N-stage agreement was lower (65% vs 75%). No imaging-pathway adverse events were reported.

records.title: IALT (International Adjuvant Lung Cancer Trial)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Pathologically documented AJCC 1986 stage I-III NSCLC after complete resection; age 18-75 years; each centre prospectively selected eligible stages. Excluded previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy, chemotherapy contraindication, or prior cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ 3-4 cycles of centre-selected cisplatin plus vindesine, vinblastine, vinorelbine, or etoposide; optional conventional PORT <=60 Gy by centre policy after chemotherapy vs Observation; optional conventional PORT <=60 Gy by centre policy Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival; second primary cancers; adverse effects Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved 5-year OS (44.5% vs 40.4%), but the benefit attenuated with longer follow-up: whole-period OS HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81-1.02; P=.10). OS favoured chemotherapy during years 0-5 (HR 0.86) and reversed beyond 5 years (HR 1.45, 1.02-2.07; interaction P=.006). Whole-period DFS improved (HR 0.88). Non-lung-cancer mortality was higher beyond 5 years (HR 2.46, 1.15-5.28).
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2004;350:351-360   J Clin Oncol 2010;28:35-42 7.5-yr long-term OS (post-5-yr HR 1.45) 19933916

records.title: JBR.10 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2005
records.body: Completely resected pathological stage IB (T2N0) or II (T1-2N1) NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy with specified nodal sampling. Excluded incomplete staging/resection, station 10 or central mediastinal nodal disease, mixed histology, T3 tumours, diffuse/multifocal bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, or recent other cancer Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 every 4 weeks for 4 cycles plus vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 weekly for 16 weeks (initially 30 mg/m2 before August 1995 amendment) vs Observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Relapse-free survival; Safety; Quality of life Adjuvant cisplatin-vinorelbine improved OS versus observation: 5-year OS 69% vs 54%, median 94 vs 73 months, HR 0.69. Grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 73%, febrile neutropenia in 7%, and 2 treatment-related deaths (0.8%) occurred.

records.title: ANITA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2006
records.body: Histologically proven primary NSCLC other than bronchoalveolar carcinoma; pathological stage I (T2N0 only), II, or IIIA by 1986 TNM; age 18-75 years; complete R0 resection. Excluded concurrent malignancy except adequately treated nonmelanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ, and other previous primary tumours Vinorelbine 30 mg/m² days 1,8,15,22 every 4 weeks up to 16 doses plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² days 1,29,57,85; optional postoperative RT by center policy vs Observation; optional postoperative RT by center policy Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Safety Adjuvant cisplatin-vinorelbine improved OS versus observation: median 65.7 vs 43.7 months, HR 0.80, with an 8.6-point absolute 5-year benefit; DFS also improved (HR 0.76). Among 368 treated patients, grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 85%, febrile neutropenia in 9%, and 7 treatment-related deaths occurred.

records.title: CALGB 9633
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Completely resected pathological T2N0 stage IB NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy; no planned adjuvant radiotherapy Paclitaxel 200 mg/m2 IV over 3 hours plus carboplatin AUC 6 IV over 45-60 minutes every 3 weeks for 4 cycles vs Observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Treatment delivery and toxicity Adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin did not improve OS in resected stage IB disease: median 95 vs 78 months, HR 0.83 (90% CI 0.64-1.08); DFS also did not improve. An unplanned tumour >=4 cm subgroup suggested benefit (OS HR 0.69) but is hypothesis-generating. Grade 3 and grade 4 maximum toxicity occurred in 41% and 28%; there were no treatment deaths.

records.title: LACE (Lung Adjuvant Cisplatin Evaluation) meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · N/A · 2008
records.body: Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of five trials since 1995 with >300 patients randomised after complete NSCLC resection to postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy vs no chemotherapy. Excluded incomplete resection, neoadjuvant or non-cisplatin chemotherapy, preoperative chemotherapy, and concurrent chemoradiotherapy Cisplatin-based postoperative chemotherapy as assigned in ALPI, BLT, IALT, JBR.10, or ANITA vs No adjuvant chemotherapy control as assigned in the constituent trial Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Lung-cancer mortality; Non-lung-cancer mortality; Treatment delivery and toxicity Postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved OS versus no chemotherapy across 5 trials (HR 0.89), an absolute 5.4-point benefit at 5 years; DFS also improved (HR 0.84). Non-lung-cancer mortality increased (HR 1.36), concentrated in the first 6 months (HR 2.41); 19 chemotherapy deaths (0.9%) occurred, 18 within 6 months.

records.title: NSCLC Meta-analysis Collaborative Group (preoperative chemo)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · N/A · 2014
records.body: Resectable NSCLC across 15 randomised trials Neoadjuvant (preoperative) chemotherapy + surgery vs surgery alone Overall survival Neoadjuvant chemotherapy improved OS (HR 0.87; 5-yr absolute benefit ~5%, 40% to 45%), comparable to adjuvant chemotherapy; established preoperative chemotherapy as a valid alternative strategy.

records.title: ADAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Completely resected nonsquamous AJCC 7th-edition stage IB-IIIA NSCLC with centrally confirmed EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R. Adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed but not mandatory; preoperative, postoperative, or planned radiotherapy was prohibited Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for 3 years or until recurrence/discontinuation, after optional adjuvant chemotherapy vs Matched placebo orally once daily for 3 years or until recurrence/discontinuation, after optional adjuvant chemotherapy Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; health-related quality of life; safety; site of recurrence; CNS disease-free survival Adjuvant osimertinib improved final 5-year OS after resection of EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R NSCLC: 85% vs 73% in stage II-IIIA and 88% vs 78% in stage IB-IIIA (HR 0.49 for both). Earlier stage II-IIIA 24-month DFS was 90% vs 44% (HR 0.17). Grade >=3 AEs were 20% vs 13%; interstitial lung disease occurred in 3% vs 0 and was mild/moderate.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;383:1711-1723   N Engl J Med 2023;389:137-147 overall survival 37272535

records.title: ALINA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Resectable NSCLC — (neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Completely resected AJCC 7th-edition stage IB (tumour >=4 cm)-IIIA ALK-positive NSCLC; eligible for platinum chemotherapy; no previous systemic anticancer therapy Alectinib 600 mg orally twice daily for 24 months or until recurrence/toxicity/withdrawal vs Four 21-day cycles of IV platinum doublet: cisplatin 75 mg/m2 day 1 (carboplatin AUC 5-6 if intolerant) plus vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 days 1,8, gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 days 1,8, or pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 day 1 Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; safety; CNS disease-free survival Adjuvant alectinib improved DFS versus platinum chemotherapy: stage II-IIIA 2-year DFS 93.8% vs 63.0% (HR 0.24); ITT HR was 0.24. records.body: Completely resected NSCLC with N2 disease proven at surgery or documented before downstaging, after lobectomy, bilobectomy, or pneumonectomy with mediastinal exploration. records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then osimertinib + pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity vs osimertinib 80 mg once daily until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, BICR PFS, ORR, duration of response, disease control, CNS outcomes, safety Osimertinib-chemotherapy improved final OS vs osimertinib alone (47.5 vs 37.6 months; HR 0.77) after improving PFS (25.5 vs 16.7 months; HR 0.62). At final OS follow-up, grade >=3 AEs were 70% vs 34%, serious AEs 46% vs 27%, fatal AEs 8% vs 4%, and any-treatment discontinuation 54% vs 7%.

records.title: MARIPOSA
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant (ex19del/L858R) NSCLC First-line amivantamab (1050 mg IV, 1400 mg if ≥80 kg; weekly ×4 then Q2W) + lazertinib 240 mg once daily vs osimertinib 80 mg once daily; to progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival for amivantamab-lazertinib vs osimertinib. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, symptomatic progression, subsequent-treatment outcomes, intracranial efficacy, safety Amivantamab-lazertinib improved OS vs osimertinib (HR 0.75; 3-year OS 60% vs 51%) after improving PFS (23.7 vs 16.6 months; HR 0.70). Grade >=3 AEs were 80% vs 52%; venous thromboembolism 40% vs 11%, and fatal AEs 9% vs 8%.

records.title: AURA3
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced EGFR T790M-positive NSCLC after progression on prior EGFR TKI Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles, then optional pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, disease control, tumour shrinkage, OS, patient-reported outcomes, safety Osimertinib improved PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed after T790M-positive progression (10.1 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.30), including baseline CNS metastases (8.5 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.32); ORR was 71% vs 31%. Grade >=3 AEs were 23% vs 47%; ILD-like events were 4% vs 1%, including one osimertinib-arm death.

OS was immature (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.42-1.09). Grade >=3 AEs were 75% vs 54%; fatal AEs 5% vs 3%, including one considered amivantamab related.

records.title: Sampath (osimertinib + consolidative RT)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2025
records.body: Advanced EGFR exon 19/21-mutant NSCLC, treatment-naive to EGFR or checkpoint inhibitors Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily; after 8-10 weeks, responders/stable disease received radiotherapy to residual disease at up to 6 sites, then continued osimertinib until progression/toxicity (single-arm) Primary: investigator-assessed PFS from osimertinib initiation. Secondary: OS, response, duration of osimertinib, radiotherapy delivery, progression patterns, safety including pneumonitis Response-adapted consolidative radiotherapy with osimertinib produced median PFS 32.3 months and OS 45.0 months; 76% received radiotherapy. The uncontrolled design precludes comparison with osimertinib alone. Pneumonitis occurred in 2/42 (5%), including one grade 4 event; no other grade >=3 radiation-related or late radiation events were reported.

records.title: ACHILLES/TORG1834
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2025
records.body: Treatment-naive nonsquamous NSCLC with sensitizing uncommon EGFR mutations (excluding exon 20 insertions and T790M) Afatinib 30 or 40 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 6 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed PFS from randomisation. Secondary: ORR, disease control, time to treatment failure, OS, duration of response, safety PFS improved with afatinib vs platinum-pemetrexed (10.6 vs 5.7 months; HR 0.421; P=.0010). Mutation-specific ORRs (major uncommon 55.8%, compound 72.7%, other 60.0%) were exploratory without an interaction test. OS was immature (29 deaths). Grade >=3 AEs were 44% vs 37%; one afatinib-related death occurred.

records.title: Robichaux et al. (structure-based EGFR classification)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2021
records.body: EGFR-mutant NSCLC (all mutation subtypes, exons 18-21) N/A — retrospective structure-function analysis of drug sensitivity across EGFR-TKIs Structural EGFR classification, mutation prevalence, drug-response associations, time to treatment failure, duration of treatment, objective response, preclinical sensitivity Retrospective structure-function grouping classified EGFR mutations as classical-like, T790M-like, exon20ins-loop or PACC and predicted TKI sensitivity better than exon grouping. In PACC mutations, time to treatment failure was 21.7 months with second-generation vs 10.0 with first-generation and 4.1 with third-generation TKIs (second vs third HR 0.23). This retrospective/preclinical analysis did not assess comparative treatment safety.

records.title: LUX-Lung 2/3/6 pooled (Yang)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2015
records.body: EGFR mutation-positive advanced (stage IIIb-IV) NSCLC adenocarcinoma, TKI-naive, with uncommon EGFR mutations (75 of 600 afatinib-treated patients across LUX-Lung 2/3/6) Afatinib 40 or 50 mg orally once daily in LUX-Lung 2 and 40 mg once daily in LUX-Lung 3/6, until progression/toxicity/withdrawal (pooled treated cohort) Objective response rate, PFS and OS by uncommon EGFR mutation group Post-hoc pooled analysis of afatinib-treated uncommon EGFR mutations: point mutations/duplications (n=38) had ORR 71.1%, PFS 10.7 months and OS 19.4 months; de-novo T790M (n=14) and exon 20 insertions (n=23) had ORR 14.3%/8.7%, PFS 2.9/2.7 months and OS 14.9/9.2 months. No formal comparisons or interaction test were performed; this publication did not provide a comparative safety analysis.

records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2020
records.body: Metastatic/recurrent NSCLC with uncommon EGFR mutations; exon 19 deletion, L858R, T790M and exon 20 insertion excluded Osimertinib 80 mg once daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: investigator-assessed objective response rate. Secondary: PFS, OS, duration of response, disease control, CNS response, safety Single-arm osimertinib produced ORR 50% and median PFS 8.2 months in uncommon EGFR-mutant NSCLC; exploratory ORRs were 78% for L861Q, 53% for G719X and 38% for S768I. OS was immature (7/36 deaths). Grade 3/4 AEs occurred in 2/36 (6%); no ILD, QT prolongation, AE discontinuation or treatment-related death was reported.

records.title: CHRYSALIS-2 Cohort C (Tomasini)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · I · 2026

Secondary: duration of response, clinical benefit rate, PFS, OS, time to treatment discontinuation, safety Single-arm amivantamab-lazertinib produced ORR 52%, median response duration 14.1 months and PFS 11.1 months; OS was not estimable. Grade >=3 AEs occurred in 70%, venous thromboembolism in 30% (grade 3, 10%), and treatment-related death in 1%.

records.title: Marcoux et al. (EGFR-mutant SCLC transformation)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2019
records.body: Retrospective 8-centre cohort of 67 patients with EGFR-mutant SCLC or high-grade neuroendocrine lung cancer treated in 2006-2018: 58 had initial NSCLC, predominantly adenocarcinoma, followed by transformation after EGFR-TKI exposure; 9 had de novo SCLC or mixed histology N/A — retrospective multicentre cohort; treatment was clinician-selected before and after transformation or, for de novo/mixed cases, after SCLC diagnosis; platinum-etoposide was the most common post-SCLC regimen Clinical response to systemic therapy after SCLC transformation or de novo SCLC diagnosis, Progression-free survival, Overall survival, CNS progression, Histologic and molecular characteristics At progression, repeat tissue biopsy is important if SCLC transformation is suspected. Retrospective cohort: 58 EGFR-mutant NSCLC cases transformed to SCLC/high-grade neuroendocrine disease; 9 were de novo/mixed (N=67). During pooled post-SCLC treatment, platinum-etoposide response was 54% (46 evaluable); transformed-case PFS was 3.4 months (48 at risk). Taxane response was 50% (20 evaluable); transformed-case PFS was 2.7 months (17 at risk). Checkpoint response was 0/17; cohorts were uncontrolled/non-comparative. Of 59 with follow-up radiographic information after SCLC diagnosis, 38 (64%) developed CNS progression. Pooled median OS from SCLC transformation/diagnosis was 10.9 months (95% CI 8.0-13.7). All 59 patients genotyped at first SCLC evidence retained founder EGFR; 15/19 previously T790M-positive cases lost T790M. Responses were investigator-estimated using general RECIST principles, without formal measurement/confirmation or standard intervals; no safety table was reported.

records.title: PROFILE 1014
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · III · 2014
records.body: Untreated advanced ALK-positive non-squamous NSCLC Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5-6 IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles Primary: independent-review progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, OS, patient-reported outcomes, safety Crizotinib improved independent-review PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed (10.9 vs 7.0 months; HR 0.45) and ORR (74% vs 45%). OS was immature and inconclusive (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.54-1.26) with 70% crossover. Grade 3/4 aminotransferase elevation occurred in 14% vs 2%; one fatal treatment-related pneumonitis occurred after crossover to crizotinib.

Grade 3 treatment-related hypophosphataemia and neutropenia each occurred in 10%, ALT elevation in 4%, and no treatment-related grade 4/5 events occurred. records.title: Entrectinib (integrated ALKA/STARTRK)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ROS1-positive · I/II · 2020
records.body: Adults with locally advanced/metastatic ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC, ROS1-inhibitor naive, RECIST 1.1 measurable disease, ECOG 0-2, treated with at least one 600 mg entrectinib dose and followed at least 12 months; prior non-ROS1 therapy and asymptomatic or controlled brain metastases were allowed (single-arm pooled efficacy n=53) Entrectinib at least 600 mg orally once daily in 4-week cycles, continued until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal (single-arm pooled efficacy analysis). ALKA-372-001 and STARTRK-1 included other dose levels/schedules, but efficacy eligibility required at least one 600 mg dose; STARTRK-2 used 600 mg once daily. Dose reductions for toxicity were in 200 mg decrements, maximum two. Primary: BICR objective response rate and duration of response. Secondary: BICR PFS, OS, safety; prespecified CNS endpoints: intracranial response, intracranial duration of response, intracranial PFS, time to CNS progression In this descriptive single-arm pooled efficacy population (n=53), BICR ORR was 77% (41/53; 95% CI 64–88), median DOR among 41 responders 24.6 months (95% CI 11.4–34.8) and median PFS 19.0 months (95% CI 12.2–36.6; 25 events). In the BICR baseline-CNS subgroup, intracranial ORR was 55% (11/20; 95% CI 32–77); radiotherapy-timing subgroups were small, descriptive and had no interaction test. In the safety set (n=134), 34% had grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs, 11% serious treatment-related AEs, 5% discontinued for treatment-related AEs, and all 9 deaths were deemed unrelated to treatment.

ORR was 59% with G2032R and intracranial ORR 89%/38% in the two cohorts. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 122/426; fatal AEs in 19/426, with none treatment related.

records.title: LIBRETTO-431

records.title: KEYNOTE-024
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 >=50%, no EGFR/ALK First-line pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles / 2 years) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy (4–6 cycles) Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, PFS2, safety At 5 years, pembrolizumab improved OS vs platinum chemotherapy in untreated PD-L1 TPS >=50% NSCLC (26.3 vs 13.4 months; HR 0.62; 5-year OS 31.9% vs 16.3%); updated PFS HR was 0.50. Treatment-related grade 3-5 AEs were 31.2% vs 53.3% and related deaths 1.3% vs 2.0%.

records.title: KEYNOTE-042
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 >=1%, no EGFR/ALK First-line pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy (4–6 cycles) Primary: OS in PD-L1 TPS >=50%, >=20% and >=1% populations. records.title: Di Federico high-PD-L1 meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · N/A · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive advanced/metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 (24 phase 3 RCTs; TPS >=50%, except IMpower TC >=50% or IC >=10%) PD-(L)1 inhibitor + platinum-based chemotherapy vs PD-(L)1 inhibitor monotherapy (indirect comparison; no head-to-head RCT) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: PFS, treatment-related toxicity and discontinuation Indirect and reconstructed-IPD comparisons favoured chemoimmunotherapy over checkpoint monotherapy in high-PD-L1 disease: OS HR 0.85 by meta-regression and 0.74 in reconstructed IPD; PFS HR 0.61 and 0.67. records.title: SACHI
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2026
