records.body: EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified locally advanced/metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC after first-line EGFR-TKI failure Savolitinib 600 mg (>=50 kg) or 400 mg (<50 kg) + osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 21 days for 4-6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: investigator-assessed PFS hierarchically in third-generation EGFR-TKI-naive then ITT populations. Secondary: IRC PFS, ORR, disease control, duration of response, OS, safety Savolitinib-osimertinib improved PFS vs chemotherapy in the third-generation-TKI-naive population (9.8 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.34) and ITT population (8.2 vs 4.5 months; HR 0.34). OS was immature and inconclusive (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.55-1.29). Grade >=3 AEs were 57% in both arms; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 0%.

records.title: HERTHENA-Lung02
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Advanced EGFR-mutant (Ex19del or L858R) NSCLC after progression on a 3rd-generation EGFR TKI Patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd) vs platinum-based chemotherapy; dose, component drugs, schedules and treatment duration were not stated in the filed conference abstract Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, intracranial PFS, safety Conference-abstract evidence: patritumab deruxtecan improved BICR PFS vs platinum chemotherapy (5.8 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.77) and ORR was 35.2% vs 25.3%; OS was immature. Grade >=3 AEs were 73% vs 57%; adjudicated ILD occurred in 5%, including two grade 5 cases. Full publication remains unfiled.

records.title: OptiTROP-Lung04
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2026
records.body: EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression Sacituzumab tirumotecan 5 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 every 28 days until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 21 days for up to 4 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety Sacituzumab tirumotecan improved PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed (8.3 vs 4.3 months; HR 0.49) and interim OS (median not reached vs 17.4 months; HR 0.60; 18-month OS 65.8% vs 48.0%). Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 58.0% vs 53.8%; no drug-related ILD was reported.

records.title: ATTLAS (KCSG-LU19-04)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Stage IV EGFR-mutated or ALK-translocated NSCLC after relevant TKI progression Atezolizumab 1200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5/5.5 IV every 21 days for 4 or 6 cycles, then atezolizumab-bevacizumab maintenance until progression vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 70 mg/m² for 4 or 6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, landmark PFS and OS, safety Atezolizumab-bevacizumab-carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS vs pemetrexed-platinum (8.48 vs 5.62 months; HR 0.62; P=.004); ORR was 69.5% vs 41.9%. OS was negative (20.63 vs 20.27 months; HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.69-1.46). PD-L1 subgroup estimates were exploratory without an interaction test. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 35.1% vs 14.9%; related deaths 3/151 vs 0/74.

records.title: CURB
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · II · 2024
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed metastatic NSCLC or breast cancer after at least one systemic-therapy line, with extracranial oligoprogression in up to five RECIST/PERCIST lesions all safely amenable to SBRT; prior brain metastases/radiotherapy were allowed, but same-site re-irradiation was not. Standard-of-care systemic therapy per physician discretion (no protocol SBRT) vs SBRT to all oligoprogressive sites plus standard-of-care systemic therapy per physician discretion; SBRT dose/fractionation selected by the treating radiation oncologist, usually 27-30 Gy in 3 fractions or 30-50 Gy in 5 fractions, with other schemes used infrequently for organ-at-risk constraints Primary: PFS to 12 months from randomisation to systemic disease progression. Secondary: OS, time to new systemic therapy and PFS by disease site, SBRT toxicity, quality of life, paired-blood biomarkers At the planned interim analysis, SBRT improved the alpha-protected pooled primary PFS endpoint vs standard of care (7.2 vs 3.2 months; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.81; P=.0035, crossing the P<.006 boundary). In the prespecified NSCLC subgroup, median PFS was 10.0 vs 2.2 months (nominal HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.75; P=.0039); 86% had no actionable driver alteration. The breast-cancer subgroup was negative (4.4 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.43-1.43), with no treatment-by-disease interaction reported. Pooled OS was inconclusive (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.55-1.81); grade >=2 adverse events occurred in 62% vs 41%, including SBRT-attributed grade >=2 toxicity in 16%.

records.title: Pignon Meta-Analysis
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · N/A · 1992
records.body: Individual-patient data from 13 randomised trials of chemotherapy plus or minus thoracic RT in limited-stage SCLC; extensive-disease patients were excluded; trial eligibility, chemotherapy, RT timing/dose/fractionation and PCI varied Trial-defined chemotherapy + thoracic RT (32–50 Gy in 8–25 fractions; start day 1–224; concurrent/alternating or sequential; some PCI) vs the same chemotherapy without thoracic RT Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: 3-year survival, sensitivity analyses, indirect RT timing/sequence comparisons, exploratory modifiers Adding thoracic RT reduced mortality (RR 0.86; p=.001) and improved 3-year OS 14.3% vs 8.9% (+5.4 points). Indirect comparisons did not show a clear early-vs-late or sequential-vs-nonsequential advantage. Nonfatal toxicity could not be pooled reliably

records.title: INT-0096 (Turrisi)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · III · 1999
records.body: Previously untreated, histologically/cytologically confirmed LS-SCLC confined to one hemithorax and ipsilateral supraclavicular fossa, without pleural effusion or contralateral hilar/supraclavicular adenopathy; ECOG 0–2 with adequate marrow, renal, hepatic, pulmonary and cardiac function Thoracic RT from chemotherapy cycle 1: 45 Gy/30 BID fractions (1.5 Gy) over 3 weeks vs 45 Gy/25 QD fractions (1.8 Gy) over 5 weeks; both with cisplatin 60 mg/m² day 1 + etoposide 120 mg/m² days 1–3 Q21D ×4; complete responders offered PCI 25 Gy/10. No haematopoietic growth factors or cycle 1–2 dose adjustment; in cycles 3–4 reduce etoposide for grade-4 toxicity, febrile neutropenia/infection or bleeding thrombocytopenia, and cisplatin for creatinine 1.6–2.5 mg/dL with further reduction at ≥2.6 mg/dL. Interrupt RT only for platelets <50,000/mm³, weight loss ≥4.5 kg or admission for neutropenic fever/sepsis; not for dysphagia or fever with leukopenia alone. Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Treatment failure/local failure, response and toxicity; no prespecified secondary alpha hierarchy or multiplicity adjustment. Twice-daily RT improved primary OS versus once-daily: median 23 vs 19 months; HR for death with once-daily vs twice-daily 1.2 (95% CI 1.0–1.6), p=.04; 5-year OS 26% vs 16%. This benefit came with more grade-3 oesophagitis (27% vs 11%; the nominal p<.001 applied to the overall ordinal/incidence comparison, not grade 3 alone). There were 11 treatment-related deaths (6 vs 5).

records.title: CONVERT
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · III · 2017
records.body: Adults with cytologically/histologically confirmed LS-SCLC encompassable in a radical RT portal, ECOG 0–1 or disease-related ECOG 2; no malignant pleural/pericardial effusion; acceptable RT volume, FEV1 >1 L or 40% predicted and DLCO >40%; no more than one adverse factor (ALP >1.5×ULN, sodium <LLN, LDH >ULN) Thoracic RT from day 22/cycle 2: 45 Gy/30 BID 1.5-Gy fractions ≥6 h apart over 19 days vs 66 Gy/33 QD 2-Gy fractions over 45 days; both with cisplatin–etoposide Q3W for 4 or 6 cycles (etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–3 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 or 25 mg/m² IV days 1–3), mandatory 3D conformal RT without elective nodal irradiation, and PCI within 6 weeks of final chemotherapy for eligible non-progressors. Delay then full dose was preferred. For first grade-4 febrile neutropenia, grade-4 thrombocytopenia requiring intervention or grade ≥2 bleeding with thrombocytopenia, full-dose chemotherapy with G-CSF or 20% reduction was allowed; second episode prompted 30% reduction, third removed the patient from trial. Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Treatment compliance, acute/late toxicity, local/metastatic progression-free survival; response was prespecified but not analysed. No secondary multiplicity adjustment or alpha hierarchy. Once-daily RT did not improve modified-ITT primary OS versus twice-daily: median 25 vs 30 months; HR for death 1.18 (95% CI 0.95–1.45), p=.14. This negative superiority result does not establish equivalence. Grade 3–4 oesophagitis was 47/246 vs 47/254 (19% in each arm; nominal p=.85). Grade 3–4 pneumonitis was 4/246 vs 4/254 (nominal p=.70); grade 3–5 counts were 6 vs 5, including 2 vs 1 deaths, with no separate p value. The headline reported 11 treatment-related deaths (8 vs 3), but detailed causes enumerate 12 instances; the discrepancy remains unresolved.

records.title: PCI Overview Collaborative Group (Aupérin)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) · N/A · 1999
records.body: IPD from 7 randomised trials of histologically proven SCLC in complete remission after induction chemotherapy ± thoracic RT, with no brain metastases or prior cranial RT; trials included both limited- and extensive-stage disease PCI (n=526; trial-defined 8–40 Gy in 1–20 fractions, most commonly 24 Gy/8 fractions) vs no PCI (n=461); one cranial-irradiation course after complete response Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, brain and other metastases, local/regional recurrence PCI improved OS (RR death 0.84; p=.01) and 3-year OS 20.7% vs 15.3% (+5.4 points). Brain metastases were reduced (RR 0.46; p<.001; 3-year incidence 33.3% vs 58.6%). Only 140 patients had extensive-stage disease, limiting stage-specific certainty. Neurotoxicity evidence was limited and longer follow-up was needed

records.title: ADRIATIC
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — consolidation immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Adults with medically inoperable stage I–II or stage III LS-SCLC, WHO 0–1, no progression after definitive concurrent platinum–etoposide CRT, and no unresolved grade ≥2 CRT toxicity; prior PCI allowed After concurrent platinum–etoposide CRT ± PCI: durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W vs durvalumab 1500 mg + tremelimumab 75 mg IV Q4W ×4 then durvalumab Q4W vs placebo; continue to progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or 24 months Primary: Overall survival and progression-free survival for durvalumab. Secondary: Overall survival and progression-free survival for durvalumab+tremelimumab, objective response, response duration, survival landmarks, safety including pneumonitis Both primary endpoints were met with durvalumab vs placebo: interim median OS 55.9 vs 33.4 mo (HR 0.73; p=.01) and median PFS 16.6 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.76; p=.02). The durvalumab+tremelimumab OS endpoint was not met and that arm remained blinded. Grade 3/4 all-cause AEs were 24.4% vs 24.2%, AE deaths 2.7% vs 1.9%, and pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis 38.2% vs 30.2%, including one grade-5 event with durvalumab

records.title: ACHILES
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — consolidation immunotherapy · II · 2025
records.body: LS-SCLC, PS 0–2, without progression after concurrent platinum–etoposide plus BID thoracic RT, randomised 3–7 weeks after CRT; complete protocol eligibility is unavailable from this one-page conference abstract Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W for 1 year, starting 3–7 weeks after CRT, until progression/unacceptable toxicity vs observation; CRT responders in either arm were offered PCI 25–30 Gy, which could begin after atezolizumab started Primary: Overall survival from post-CRT randomisation. Secondary: Response rate, progression-free survival and toxicity; no secondary multiplicity control or gatekeeping sequence was reported in the conference abstract. Consolidation atezolizumab did not improve primary OS versus observation: median 43.3 vs 38.8 months; HR for death 1.14 (95% CI 0.76–1.72), alpha-protected p=.5. Secondary PFS was 21.1 vs 15.9 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.60–1.28; nominal p=.5). Post-randomisation grade 3–4 toxicity was 34% vs 20%, with unspecified denominators; treatment-related deaths were 3 vs 0. Evidence is limited to a one-page conference abstract without formal analysis-set definitions or complete safety detail.

records.title: JCOG9511 (Noda)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · III · 2002
records.body: Japanese patients age ≤70 with untreated ES-SCLC and ECOG 0–2; symptomatic brain metastases requiring WBRT or steroids were excluded Irinotecan 60 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 15 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² day 1 Q4W ×4 vs etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1–3 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1 Q3W ×4 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Complete response rate, overall response rate, progression-free survival, relapse sites, toxicity Irinotecan–cisplatin improved final median OS to 12.8 vs 9.4 mo (RR death 0.60; p=.002) and 2-year OS to 19.5% vs 5.2%. Secondary PFS was 6.9 vs 4.8 mo (p=.003) and ORR 84.4% vs 67.5% (p=.02); PFS monitoring could be biased. In safety sets of 75 vs 77, grade 3/4 neutropenia was 65.3% vs 92.2%, thrombocytopenia 5.3% vs 18.2%, and diarrhoea 16.0% vs 0%; treatment-related deaths were 3 vs 1

records.title: SECSG CAV/EP (Roth)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · III · 1992
records.body: ≥18; SCLC histology/cytology; no prior chemo/RT; beyond primary/mediastinum/ipsilateral SC nodes; bidimensionally measurable; Zubrod 0–3. Pleural effusion alone excluded; effusions/positive bone/liver scans not indicator lesions. Brain mets required concurrent WBRT. Excluded cancer except treated NMSC/cervical CIS; CHF, treated arrhythmia or MI <3 mo. WBC/platelets >4000/100,000 per µL (>3000/50,000 with marrow involvement); bilirubin <2 mg/dL; creatinine <1.8 men/<1.5 women mg/dL; consent. EP: cisplatin 20 mg/m²/day + etoposide 80 mg/m²/day IV days 1–5 Q3W ×4; CAV: cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m² + doxorubicin 40 mg/m² + vincristine 1 mg/m² (max 2 mg) IV day 1 Q3W ×6; alternating CAV/EP: CAV day 1 then EP days 22–26, repeating the 6-week sequence ×3. Brain metastases received concomitant WBRT. Cisplatin hydration targeted urine output ≥100 mL/h before and for 4 h after dosing, with optional mannitol/loop diuretic. Delay 1 week for day-1 leukocytes <4000/µL or platelets <100,000/µL. After fever/infection with nadir granulocytes <500/µL or significant bleeding with nadir platelets <50,000/µL, reduce etoposide (EP), cyclophosphamide+doxorubicin (CAV), or all three (alternating) 25%; do not reduce cisplatin/vincristine for haematologic toxicity. If creatinine exceeded 150% of baseline, omit cisplatin for one course, resume only at baseline and cross to CAV if persistent. At progression, EP crossed to CAV up to 6 cycles, CAV to EP up to 4; alternating-arm salvage was investigator-selected Primary: Overall survival from registration. Secondary: Objective/complete response, time to best response, time to progression, crossover response and toxicity. Pairwise three-group comparisons used Bonferroni alpha .017; no sequential gatekeeping hierarchy linked endpoints. In 437 eligible patients, EP, CAV and alternating CAV/EP showed no primary OS advantage: medians 8.6, 8.3 and 8.1 months (stratified p=.425); this was not an equivalence/noninferiority test. Response was 60.7%, 50.6% and 59.4% among 140, 140 and 138 assessable patients (nominal p=.175). In this 140+140+138 response-assessable population, alternating-vs-CAV TTP p=.008 met the paper's pairwise .017 threshold, but treatment was not retained in the final Cox model. Therapy-related deaths were 9/159, 6/156 and 11/162.

records.title: Japanese CAV/PE trial (Fukuoka)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · N/A · 1991
records.body: Histologically/cytologically proven SCLC reviewed by ≥2 pathologists; no prior therapy; measurable/evaluable disease; ECOG 0–3; age <75. Required leukocytes ≥4000/mm³, platelets ≥100,000/mm³, bilirubin ≤1.5 mg/dL, ALP/AST/ALT ≤2×ULN, creatinine ≤1.5 mg/dL and BUN ≤25 mg/dL; excluded active second cancer, MI <3 months or cardiac disease requiring treatment. Limited disease was confined to one hemithorax including bilateral mediastinal/supraclavicular nodes; pleural effusion was extensive. CAV: cyclophosphamide 800 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m² and vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (max 2 mg) IV day 1 Q3–4W. PE: cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1 with hydration/diuretics/antiemetics plus etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1, 3 and 5 Q3–4W. Alternating CAV/PE used the same doses Q3–4W. WHO grade-4 toxicity reduced all drugs to 75%; renal failure stopped cisplatin. Nonresponders after 2 cycles could cross from CAV to PE or PE to CAV; responders continued for 1 year and later treatment at progression was discretionary. After 4 cycles, limited-stage patients received thoracic RT to the initial chest-x-ray field including ipsilateral hilum/bilateral mediastinum and involved supraclavicular nodes only: 200 cGy daily, 5 days/week for 4–5 weeks, total 40–50 Gy. PCI was not scheduled. Primary: Overall survival from treatment start. Secondary: Initial objective/complete response, response duration, crossover response/non-cross-resistance, stage-defined survival and toxicity. Pairwise OS comparisons used two-sided alpha .05, with no multiplicity adjustment; the study was not powered for subset analyses and specified no sequential testing hierarchy. Alternating CAV/PE did not show a robust primary OS advantage over CAV or PE in 288 eligible mixed-stage patients: medians 11.8, 9.9 and 9.9 months. Alternating-vs-CAV p=.027 was nominal without multiplicity control and became p=.147 after prognostic adjustment; alternating-vs-PE p=.056. Two-year OS was 21.4%, 10.4% and 11.5%. Limited- and extensive-stage analyses were unpowered, with no treatment-by-stage interaction test. Treatment-related deaths were 7/286 (1 alternating, 3 CAV, 3 PE), plus fatal radiation pneumonitis in 2/118 irradiated limited-stage patients.

records.title: Norwegian EP vs CEV (Sundstrøm)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemotherapy · III · 2002
records.body: Histologically/cytologically confirmed untreated LS- or ES-SCLC; age 18–75; ECOG 0–2; WBC ≥3000/µL, platelets ≥125,000/µL, creatinine <125 µmol/L; no serious cardiovascular disease or malignancy except basal-cell carcinoma/cervical carcinoma in situ; brain metastases permitted. LS disease had to fit tolerable RT portals; beyond this was ES. Thirteen incorrectly randomised ECOG-3 patients remained in analyses; four incorrect diagnoses were excluded after randomisation, leaving 436 eligible. EP: etoposide 100 mg/m² IV then cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 with standard pre/posthydration, plus oral etoposide 200 mg/m² days 2–4 fasting, Q3W for ≤5 courses. CEV: epirubicin 50 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m² and vincristine 2 mg IV day 1 Q3W for ≤5 courses, with standard dose reductions. Response was assessed before course 3; progression stopped protocol therapy and crossover chemotherapy was recommended. LS patients received thoracic RT 42 Gy/15 QD fractions between courses 3–4; complete responders received PCI 30 Gy/15 QD. ES patients had no protocol RT; chest/cranial irradiation was allowed only for severe symptoms not palliated by chemotherapy. Primary: Overall survival from randomisation, tested by one-sided log-rank alpha .05. Secondary: HRQOL, induction-treatment delivery, crossover, relapse pattern and subsequent palliative treatment; HRQOL used a one-sided .01 threshold for multiple comparisons. No gatekeeping hierarchy or treatment-by-stage interaction test was reported. EP improved primary OS versus CEV in 436 eligible patients (218/arm): median 10.2 vs 7.8 months, one-sided p=.0004; 2-year OS 14% vs 6% and 5-year OS 5% vs 2%. Stage-stratified comparisons were descriptive without an interaction test: LS median OS 14.5 vs 9.7 months, with an internal prose/abstract-versus-Figure 2 p-value discrepancy (Figure 2 p=.0001); ES 8.4 vs 6.5 months, nominal p=.21. Toxicity stopped induction in 19% vs 7% (nominal one-sided p<.0001), whereas progression stopped it in 16% vs 24% (nominal one-sided p<.0001).

records.title: IMpower133
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: Previously untreated adults with ES-SCLC and ECOG 0–1; treated asymptomatic CNS metastases were permitted; autoimmune disease and prior checkpoint/CD137 therapy were excluded Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin AUC5/etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1–3 for 4 cycles → atezolizumab maintenance vs placebo + the same 4-cycle chemotherapy → placebo; continue to progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: Overall survival and progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response, response duration, 1-year survival, safety, blood tumour mutational burden Both primary endpoints were met with atezolizumab + carboplatin/etoposide: interim median OS 12.3 vs 10.3 mo (HR 0.70; p=.007) and final median PFS 5.2 vs 4.3 mo (HR 0.77; p=.02). Confirmed ORR was 60.2% vs 64.4%. Treatment-related grade 3/4 AEs were 56.6% vs 56.1%, regimen-related deaths 1.5% vs 1.5%, and immune-related AEs 39.9% vs 24.5%

records.title: CASPIAN
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Treatment-naive adults with ES-SCLC and WHO 0–1; asymptomatic or treated stable brain metastases allowed; prior or planned chest RT and active autoimmune/inflammatory disease excluded Durvalumab 1500 mg Q3W + EP ×4 → durvalumab Q4W; durvalumab 1500 mg + tremelimumab 75 mg Q3W + EP ×4, one further tremelimumab dose → durvalumab Q4W; or EP Q3W ×6 ± PCI; immunotherapy continued to progression/toxicity Primary: Overall survival for durvalumab+EP and durvalumab+tremelimumab+EP. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response, survival landmarks, safety, symptoms, quality of life The OS primary endpoint was met with durvalumab+EP at interim (median 13.0 vs 10.3 mo; HR 0.73; p=.0047); updated OS was 12.9 vs 10.5 mo (HR 0.75; p=.0032). Durvalumab+tremelimumab+EP did not meet its OS primary: 10.4 vs 10.5 mo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68–1.00; p=.045). PFS was 5.1 vs 5.4 mo (HR 0.80) for durvalumab and 4.9 vs 5.4 mo (HR 0.84) for tremelimumab. Serious AEs were 45%/32%/36% and treatment-related deaths 5%/2%/1% for tremelimumab/durvalumab/EP
records.keywords: Lancet 2019;394:1929-1939   Goldman et al. - 2020 - Durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus platinum-etoposide versus platinum-etoposide alone [e3b0fafd]

records.title: KEYNOTE-604
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2020
records.body: Adults with previously untreated AJCC7 stage IV SCLC and ECOG 0–1; treated stable brain metastases allowed after treatment and steroid-free neurological stability Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W for up to 35 cycles + etoposide/platinum for the first 4 cycles vs placebo Q3W for up to 35 cycles + the same 4-cycle chemotherapy; optional PCI after cycle 4; stop for progression, toxicity or decision Primary: Progression-free survival and overall survival. Secondary: Objective response, response duration, safety The PFS primary endpoint was met with pembrolizumab+EP (median 4.5 vs 4.3 mo; HR 0.75; p=.0023), but the OS primary endpoint was not met (10.8 vs 9.7 mo; HR 0.80; p=.0164). Secondary ORR was 70.6% vs 61.8% and DOR 4.2 vs 3.7 mo. Grade 3/4 all-cause AEs were 76.7% vs 74.9%, discontinuation 14.8% vs 6.3%, AE deaths 6.3% vs 5.4%, and immune-mediated AEs 24.7% vs 10.3%

records.title: ASTRUM-005
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Adults with previously untreated ES-SCLC and ECOG 0–1; stable asymptomatic treated brain metastases allowed; prior limited-stage therapy allowed after ≥6 months Serplulimab 4.5 mg/kg IV Q3W + etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1–3/carboplatin AUC5 day 1 for up to 4 cycles vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; serplulimab/placebo continued to progression, death, toxicity, withdrawal or protocol stop Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response, response duration, adverse events, PD-L1–efficacy relationship At interim, the OS primary endpoint was met with serplulimab: 15.4 vs 10.9 mo (HR 0.63; p<.001; median follow-up 12.3 mo). Secondary PFS was 5.7 vs 4.3 mo (HR 0.48), ORR 80.2% vs 70.4%, and DOR 5.6 vs 3.2 mo. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 33.2% vs 27.6%; treatment-emergent AE deaths 7.7% vs 10.2% and study-drug-attributed deaths 0.8% vs 0.5%

records.title: EORTC 08993-22993 (Slotman)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — radiotherapy & prophylactic cranial irradiation · III · 2007
records.body: Adults age 18–75 with ES-SCLC, WHO 0–2 and any response after 4–6 chemotherapy cycles, randomised within 5 weeks; no clinical brain/leptomeningeal metastases, prior head/neck RT or corticosteroid use PCI (20 Gy/5 or 8 fractions, 24 Gy/12, 25 Gy/10, or 30 Gy/10 or 12; start 4–6 weeks after chemotherapy) vs observation with the same symptom-triggered brain-imaging policy Primary: Time to symptomatic brain metastases. Secondary: Overall survival, disease-free survival, quality of life, acute and late toxicity, costs PCI reduced symptomatic brain metastases (HR 0.27; p<.001; 1-year risk 14.6% vs 40.4%). Secondary median OS was 6.7 vs 5.4 mo (HR 0.68; p=.003), with 1-year OS 27.1% vs 13.3%. Among 134 irradiated patients, grade-3 headache occurred in 5 and severe headache/CNS dysfunction after 3 months in 3; hair loss and fatigue worsened (p<.001 each), with QoL completion falling to 46.3% at month 9

records.title: CREST
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — radiotherapy & prophylactic cranial irradiation · III · 2015
records.body: Adults with ES-SCLC, WHO 0–2 and any response after 4–6 platinum–etoposide cycles, with safely treatable thoracic volume and randomisation within 6 weeks; no clinical brain, leptomeningeal or pleural metastases; all received PCI Thoracic RT 30 Gy/10 daily fractions + centre-selected PCI vs the same PCI alone; start preferably within 6 weeks after chemotherapy and continue follow-up/progression treatment per centre policy Primary: 1-year overall survival. Secondary: Median and landmark overall survival, intrathoracic control, progression-free survival, toxicity Thoracic RT did not meet the 1-year OS primary: 33% vs 28% (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69–1.01; p=.066), with median OS 8 mo in both arms. Secondary results favoured RT for 2-year OS (13% vs 3%; p=.004), PFS (4 vs 3 mo; HR 0.73; p=.001), and intrathoracic control (isolated progression 19.8% vs 46.0%; p<.0001). Grade ≥3 toxicity occurred in 26 vs 18 patients (p=.28), including grade-3 oesophagitis in 4 vs 0; no severe late toxicity was reported

records.title: Takahashi (ES-SCLC PCI)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — radiotherapy & prophylactic cranial irradiation · III · 2017
records.body: Japanese adults with ES-SCLC, ECOG 0–2, response after ≥2 platinum-doublet cycles, no regrowth on thoracoabdominal CT and no brain metastases on protocol-mandated MRI PCI 25 Gy/10 daily fractions vs observation; both arms underwent brain MRI every 3 months through month 12 and at months 18 and 24, with salvage brain RT allowed; systemic therapy deferred until imaging-detected progression Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Brain-metastasis incidence, progression-free survival, adverse events, Mini-Mental State Examination PCI did not improve final OS under scheduled MRI surveillance: median 11.6 vs 13.7 mo (HR 1.27, 95% CI 0.96–1.68; p=.094). PCI reduced 12-month brain-metastasis incidence (32.9% vs 59.0%; p<.0001), while PFS was 2.3 vs 2.4 mo (HR 0.98; p=.75). At 3 months, grade ≥3 anorexia was 6% vs 2%, malaise 3% vs <1%, and lower-limb weakness <1% vs 5%; no treatment-related deaths. The result is conditional on scheduled MRI and salvage access

records.title: IMforte
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line maintenance therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with untreated ES-SCLC and ECOG 0–1 who had response/stable disease after 4 cycles of atezolizumab–carboplatin–etoposide; maintenance entrants had ECOG 0–1, no CNS metastases and no consolidative thoracic RT After 4-cycle atezolizumab–carboplatin–etoposide induction: lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m² IV + atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W with prophylactic G-CSF vs atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W; continue to progression, toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival and overall survival. Secondary: Objective response, response duration, survival landmarks, safety, quality of life, immunogenicity Both primary endpoints were met from maintenance randomisation with lurbinectedin+atezolizumab: final PFS 5.4 vs 2.1 mo (HR 0.54; p<.0001) and planned-interim OS 13.2 vs 10.6 mo (HR 0.73; p=.017). In safety sets of 242 vs 240, grade 3/4 all-cause AEs were 38% vs 22%, serious AEs 31% vs 17%, AE deaths 5% vs 3%, and treatment-related deaths 1% vs <1%

records.title: CheckMate 451
records.subtitle: SCLC · Extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC) — first-line maintenance therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Adults with histologically/cytologically confirmed AJCC7 ED-SCLC, ECOG 0–1 and no progression after first-line platinum chemotherapy: ongoing CR/PR after 3–4 cycles or stable disease after 4. Randomisation was ≤9 weeks after chemotherapy, extended to 11 weeks with PCI/brain RT; treatment began ≥3 weeks after chemotherapy and ≥2 weeks after RT. Complete eligibility/exclusions are in the online supplement, which is not filed. Nivolumab+ipilimumab: nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 over 12 weeks, then nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W. Nivolumab: 240 mg IV Q2W. Placebo: matching nivolumab placebo Q2W + ipilimumab placebo Q3W during the first 12 weeks, then nivolumab placebo Q2W. Continue each arm for ≤2 years or until progression/unacceptable toxicity; crossover was not permitted. Primary: Overall survival from maintenance randomisation, nivolumab+ipilimumab vs placebo. Secondary: In the fixed hierarchical sequence, nivolumab OS vs placebo, then blinded-central-review PFS for nivolumab+ipilimumab vs placebo, then nivolumab PFS vs placebo; other OS/PFS comparisons were combination vs nivolumab and by TMB; exploratory OS subgroups/multivariable analyses, ORR/DOR, PD-L1 prediction and safety; failure of primary OS stopped the hierarchy Maintenance nivolumab+ipilimumab did not improve primary OS versus placebo in the ITT population (279 vs 275): median 9.2 vs 9.6 months; HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.75–1.12), p=.37. The fixed hierarchy stopped: nivolumab OS in 280 vs 275 (10.4 vs 9.6 months; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69–1.02) and blinded-central-review PFS for combination vs placebo in 279 vs 275 (1.7 vs 1.4 months; HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.60–0.87) and nivolumab vs placebo in 280 vs 275 (1.9 vs 1.4; HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.56–0.81) were not formally tested. In treated combination/nivolumab/placebo sets of 278/279/273, grade-three/four TRAEs were 52.2%/11.5%/8.4%, TRAEs led to discontinuation in 28.8%/7.9%/0.4%, and treatment-related deaths were 7/278, 1/279 and 1/273.

records.title: von Pawel
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · III · 1999
records.body: Patients with recurrent limited- or extensive-stage SCLC progressing ≥60 days after one first-line chemotherapy regimen and ECOG ≤2; symptomatic steroid-requiring brain metastases and prior topotecan excluded Topotecan 1.5 mg/m² IV over 30 min days 1–5 Q3W vs CAV (cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m², doxorubicin 45 mg/m², vincristine 2 mg IV day 1) Q3W; continue responders to progression/toxicity and manage stable disease after 4 courses per protocol Primary: Objective response rate and duration of response. Secondary: Time to progression/response, overall survival, symptom improvement/worsening, toxicity Statistical significance was not reached for either co-primary endpoint: ORR 24.3% vs 18.3% (p=.285) or DOR 14.4 vs 15.3 weeks (p=.300); median OS was 25.0 vs 24.7 weeks (p=.795). Secondary symptom results favoured topotecan for dyspnoea, anorexia, hoarseness, fatigue and activity interference. Grade-4 neutropenia was 70.2% vs 71.7%, grade-4 thrombocytopenia 28.8% vs 5.0%, and grade 3/4 anaemia 42.3% vs 19.8%. Seven deaths (4 vs 3) were associated with myelosuppression/sepsis; two additional topotecan deaths were related or possibly related

records.title: PM1183-B-005 (Lurbinectedin)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · II · 2020
records.body: Adults with relapsed SCLC after one chemotherapy-containing line and ECOG 0–2; baseline CNS screening mandatory and known CNS involvement excluded (single-arm) Lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m² IV over 1 hour Q3W until RECIST progression or unacceptable toxicity; antiemetic prophylaxis, no primary G-CSF, secondary G-CSF allowed; reductions to 2.6 then 2.0 mg/m² Primary: Objective response. Secondary: Response duration, disease control, progression-free survival, overall survival, survival landmarks, safety Single-arm lurbinectedin produced ORR 35.2%, all partial responses. Secondary results were median DOR 5.3 mo, PFS 3.5 mo and OS 9.3 mo; ORR was 45.0% with chemotherapy-free interval ≥90 days vs 22.2% below 90 days. Grade 3/4 neutropenia was 46% and febrile neutropenia 5%; serious treatment-related AEs occurred in 10%, with no treatment-related deaths

records.title: DeLLphi-301
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Adults with SCLC relapsed/refractory after one platinum regimen and ≥1 additional line, ECOG 0–1; DLL3 expression not required; treated stable asymptomatic brain metastases allowed Tarlatamab step-up 1 mg IV cycle 1 day 1 then 10 mg or 100 mg days 8 and 15 and Q2W in 28-day cycles until progression; dexamethasone premedication, post-dose hydration and protocol monitoring; beyond-progression treatment allowed for benefit Primary: Objective response. Secondary: Response duration, disease control, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, pharmacokinetics, biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes In this noncomparative dose study, selected-dose 10-mg ORR was 40% (40/100); 100-mg ORR was 32% (28/88). Median DOR was not evaluable; median PFS was 4.9 vs 3.9 mo and OS was immature (10-mg median 14.3 mo; 100-mg not estimable). At 10 vs 100 mg, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 26% vs 33%, CRS 51% vs 61% (grade 3: 1% vs 6%), and ICANS-associated events 8% vs 28% (grade ≥3: 0% vs 5%); one treatment-related respiratory-failure death occurred at 10 mg

records.title: DeLLphi-304
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with SCLC progressing during/after first-line platinum treatment and ECOG 0–1 at screening; stable asymptomatic treated or untreated brain metastases allowed; DLL3 expression not required Tarlatamab step-up 1 mg IV cycle 1 day 1 then 10 mg days 8 and 15 and Q2W in 28-day cycles vs investigator-intended topotecan, lurbinectedin or amrubicin Q3W; continue to progression/toxicity/withdrawal/death, no crossover Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, week-19 dyspnoea, cough and chest pain, physical functioning, global health, objective response, response duration, safety At interim, the OS primary endpoint was met with tarlatamab (13.6 vs 8.3 mo; HR 0.60; p<.001), and 12-month PFS RMST was 5.3 vs 4.3 mo (p=.002). ORR was 35% vs 20%. Dyspnoea and cough improved, but chest pain did not. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 27% vs 62% and treatment-related deaths <1% vs 2%. Tarlatamab CRS was 56% (grade 3, 1%; no grade 4/5); ICANS was 6%, including one grade-5 death

records.title: BL-B01D1-101 (iza-bren ES-SCLC)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · I · 2026
records.body: Adults with relapsed ES-SCLC after at least one platinum-based regimen; article eligibility text also required prior PD-(L)1 therapy, but baseline table recorded prior anti-PD-(L)1 exposure in 44/52; ECOG 0-1; active brain metastases excluded. (single-arm) Iza-bren 2.5 mg/kg IV once daily on days 1 and 8 Q3W Primary: Objective response rate by RECIST v1.1, Safety and tolerability. Secondary: Duration of response, Disease control rate, Progression-free survival, Overall survival. Exploratory: Associations between EGFR/HER3 expression and clinical outcomes First-in-class iza-bren showed substantial but exploratory activity in this single-arm phase Ib cohort: ORR 48.1% (25/52; 95% CI 34.0-62.4), median DOR 4.9 mo, PFS 4.1 mo and OS 12.2 mo; the unplanned second-line subgroup had ORR 72.7% (16/22; 95% CI 49.8-89.3). No comparator or formal hypothesis test supports a comparative efficacy claim. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 75%, treatment-related serious AEs in 50.0%, dose reductions in 46.2% and delays in 63.5%; 2/52 (3.8%) treatment-related deaths.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print; JCO-26-00243)  42497381

records.title: GFPC 01-13
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Adults with histologically/cytologically confirmed SCLC, stage IV or locally relapsed outside the prior chemoradiotherapy field, with RECIST 1.1 response to first-line platinum–etoposide and relapse ≥90 days from day 1 of its last cycle; measurable disease, ECOG 0–2. Asymptomatic brain metastases were allowed; stable disease after first line was excluded. Full exclusions are in an unfiled appendix; printed bilirubin and liver-enzyme criteria lack visible inequality signs and remain unresolved. Carboplatin–etoposide: carboplatin AUC5 IV day 1 + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–3 Q3W, ≤6 cycles. Topotecan: 2.3 mg/m² orally days 1–5 Q3W, ≤6 cycles. No minimum number of cycles. Primary prophylactic filgrastim was recommended for both arms; protocol delays/reductions applied for cytopenias, febrile neutropenia, diarrhoea and other grade-three/four toxicity. Subsequent therapy was unrestricted. Primary: Centrally reviewed RECIST 1.1 PFS from randomisation to progression/death in the ITT population, stratified log-rank superiority test at one-sided α=.05; final analysis planned after 142 PFS events, with no interim analysis. Secondary: OS, centrally reviewed ORR and DOR, treatment-related adverse events and quality of life, explicitly exploratory at two-sided α=.05 without multiplicity control or hierarchy; quality of life was not reported because data were available for only 22 patients For sensitive-relapse SCLC, carboplatin–etoposide rechallenge improved primary centrally reviewed PFS versus topotecan in the 81-per-arm ITT set: median 4.7 vs 2.7 months; HR 0.57 (90% CI 0.41–0.73), one-sided p=.0041. The analysis observed 160 PFS events (79 vs 81), despite the article separately stating a 142-event final-analysis trigger; abstract/Results/Figure 2A report p=.0041, while Discussion prints a discrepant tenfold-smaller p value. Exploratory OS was not improved: 7.5 vs 7.4 months; HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.87–1.19), nominal p=.94. Exploratory central ORR was 49% (39/81) vs 25% (19/81), nominal p=.0024. Grade-three/four neutropenia was 14% vs 22%, thrombocytopenia 31% vs 36%, and febrile neutropenia 6% vs 11%; drug-toxicity discontinuation was 17% vs 12%. Treatment-related deaths were 0 vs 2, both febrile neutropenia with sepsis on topotecan.

records.title: EMPHACIS
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line chemotherapy · III · 2003
records.body: Untreated advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV, day 1 Q3W, to progression vs cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV Q3W alone Overall survival Pemetrexed/cisplatin improved OS (12.1 vs 9.3 months, HR not reported; p=0.020) and TTP (5.7 vs 3.9 months); established pemetrexed-platinum as the first-line standard for MPM.

records.title: MAPS (IFCT-GFPC-0701)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line chemotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Untreated non-resectable malignant pleural mesothelioma First-line cisplatin + pemetrexed + bevacizumab vs cisplatin + pemetrexed Overall survival Adding bevacizumab improved OS (18.8 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.77; p=0.017); an option for fit patients without contraindications to anti-VEGF therapy, though not universally adopted.

records.title: CheckMate 743
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q6W, to progression, toxicity, or 2 years vs platinum–pemetrexed (cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 + pemetrexed 500 mg/m²) Q3W for up to 6 cycles Overall survival Nivolumab/ipilimumab improved OS (18.1 vs 14.1 months, HR 0.74; p=0.0020), with 5-year OS 14% vs 6%; benefit was greatest in non-epithelioid histology; established dual checkpoint blockade as the preferred first-line option.

records.title: IND.227 / KEYNOTE-483
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line immunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated advanced pleural mesothelioma, ECOG 0-1 Platinum-pemetrexed + pembrolizumab vs platinum-pemetrexed alone Overall survival Adding pembrolizumab to platinum-pemetrexed improved OS (median 17.3 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.64–0.98, p=0.032 against a prespecified boundary of 0.0409; 3-year OS 25% vs 17%), though the authors put the median gain at "only slightly longer than 1 month" and their exploratory 54-month restricted mean difference at 3.4 months. Grade 3/4 treatment-related toxicity 27% vs 15%, on the safety population of 222 and 211. A new frontline option; FDA-approved September 2024.

records.title: MARS
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Surgery in resectable disease · N/A · 2011
records.body: Malignant pleural mesothelioma eligible for surgery after induction chemotherapy Extrapleural pneumonectomy (EPP) vs no EPP Feasibility; overall survival EPP offered no survival benefit and was associated with worse OS (14.4 vs 19.5 months) and greater morbidity; challenged the routine use of EPP and redirected surgical interest toward lung-sparing approaches.

records.title: MARS 2
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Surgery in resectable disease · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable malignant pleural mesothelioma (predominantly epithelioid) Extended pleurectomy/decortication + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone Overall survival Surgery did not improve OS (19.3 vs 24.8 months favouring chemotherapy alone; the trial's primary comparison is a restricted mean survival time difference of -1.9 months at 2 years, 95% CI -3.4 to -0.3, p=0.019, and the hazard ratio 1.28, 95% CI 1.02-1.60, p=0.032, is computed over the first 42 months, the point at which the Kaplan-Meier curves intersect) and was associated with worse QoL, higher adverse events, and higher costs; does not support routine P/D outside of clinical trials.

records.title: MAPS2 (IFCT-1501)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · II · 2019
records.body: Relapsed malignant pleural mesothelioma after platinum-based chemotherapy Second/third-line nivolumab vs nivolumab + ipilimumab 12-week disease control rate 12-week DCR was 40% (nivolumab) and 52% (combination); median OS 15.9 vs 15.9 months; both regimens showed promising activity in the relapsed setting, supporting the dual checkpoint approach later confirmed in CheckMate 743.

records.title: CONFIRM
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Relapsed malignant mesothelioma after ≥1 prior line Nivolumab 240 mg q2w vs placebo Progression-free survival and overall survival (co-primary) Final analysis at a median 37.2 months of follow-up: the co-primary PFS endpoint was met and OS was not. Median PFS 2.89 months (95% CI 2.76-4.11) with nivolumab vs 1.64 (1.38-2.56) with placebo, unadjusted HR 0.65 (0.51-0.82), tested against an alpha of 0.01 under a hierarchical procedure precisely because OS was not significant. Median OS 9.49 months (7.69-11.01) vs 6.77 (5.03-7.92), unadjusted HR 0.81 (0.64-1.04), p=0.093 against a 0.04 threshold; adjusted HR 0.81 (0.64-1.04), p=0.096. Objective response 10.3% vs 0%. The 2021 report was an early interim at 210 of the 291 deaths required and reported OS as met (adjusted HR 0.69, 0.52-0.91, p=0.0090); at the planned threshold, with 298 deaths observed, that survival benefit did not hold. Second line in only 30%, third line 57% and later 13% pooled across arms, with no limit on prior therapies.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1530-1540   Nat Commun 2025;16:6688 final analysis 40691143

records.title: VIM
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · II · 2022
records.body: Relapsed malignant pleural mesothelioma after platinum-based chemotherapy Oral vinorelbine + active symptom control vs active symptom control alone Progression-free survival Vinorelbine improved PFS (4.2 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.60) without significant OS benefit (9.3 vs 9.1 months); provides a chemotherapy option for patients progressing after platinum-pemetrexed in the immunotherapy era.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (Meso cohort)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · II · 2021
records.body: Previously treated advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (single arm) Objective response rate ORR 8% with median DOR 14.3 months; median OS 20.1 months in an unselected pretreated population; limited single-agent activity but durable responses in a minority support biomarker-selected use.

records.title: ITMIG PORT Analysis (Rimner)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Resectable & locally advanced disease — radiotherapy & combined-modality therapy · N/A · 2016
records.body: Completely resected (R0) Masaoka-Koga stage II-III thymoma Surgery + postoperative radiotherapy vs surgery alone Overall survival Postoperative radiotherapy improved 5- and 10-year OS (95%/86% vs 90%/79% with surgery alone; p=0.002), with benefit retained for stage II and III separately and on multivariable analysis; strongest evidence supporting adjuvant radiotherapy in resected stage II-III thymoma.

records.title: Intergroup PAC + RT (Loehrer)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Resectable & locally advanced disease — radiotherapy & combined-modality therapy · II · 1997
records.body: Limited-stage unresectable thymoma/thymic carcinoma, chemo-naive Induction PAC x2-4 cycles then 54 Gy thoracic radiotherapy Response rate Induction PAC produced a 69.6% response (5 CR, 11 PR); with consolidative radiotherapy, median survival reached 93 months and 5-year OS was 52.5%; established combined-modality therapy as standard for unresectable thymoma.

records.title: ADOC (Fornasiero)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · N/A · 1991
records.body: Stage III-IV invasive (advanced) thymoma ADOC (cisplatin, doxorubicin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide) Response rate ORR 91.8% with 43% complete responses and no life-threatening toxicity; one of the most active first-line regimens for advanced thymoma, though never compared randomly against other platinum doublets.

records.title: Intergroup PAC (Loehrer)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · II · 1994
records.body: Metastatic or recurrent thymoma after radiotherapy Cisplatin 50 mg/m² + doxorubicin 50 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² (PAC) IV Q3W, to a maximum of 8 cycles (single-arm) Response rate ORR 50% (3 CR, 12 PR) with median response duration 11.8 months and median OS 37.7 months; established PAC as a standard first-line regimen for advanced thymoma.

records.title: Carboplatin-Paclitaxel (Lemma)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · II · 2011
records.body: Unresectable advanced thymoma (n=21) or thymic carcinoma (n=23) Carboplatin AUC 6 + paclitaxel 225 mg/m² IV Q3W, to a maximum of 6 cycles (single-arm) Response rate ORR 42.9% in thymoma (3 CR, 6 PR) vs 21.7% in thymic carcinoma (all PR); a well-tolerated non-anthracycline platinum doublet that became a widely used first-line option, particularly for thymic carcinoma.

records.title: Cisplatin-Etoposide (Giaccone)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · II · 1996
records.body: Recurrent or metastatic invasive (Masaoka stage III-IV) malignant thymoma, incurable by surgery/radiotherapy, no prior cisplatin or etoposide Cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV day 1 + etoposide 120 mg/m² IV days 1–3, Q3W, to a maximum of 8 cycles (single-arm) Response rate EORTC phase II single-arm study (N=16) in advanced/recurrent malignant thymoma: cisplatin–etoposide produced an objective response rate of 56% (95% CI 30–80%; 5 CR, 4 PR; 60% among the 15 assessable patients) with a median response duration of 3.4 years, median progression-free survival 2.2 years and median overall survival 4.3 years (5-year OS 50%) at 7-year median follow-up. Established cisplatin–etoposide as an active, well-tolerated first-line platinum doublet for advanced thymoma, including as a neoadjuvant backbone.

records.title: RYTHMIC
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · N/A · 2018
records.body: Advanced thymic epithelial tumour (119 thymoma, 117 thymic carcinoma) given systemic therapy, French RYTHMIC national tumour board 2012-2015 PAC commonest first-intent, carboplatin-paclitaxel at first recurrence, across up to 4 lines (observational cohort) Objective response and progression-free survival Real-world benchmark across six treatment settings. Objective response was 79% when chemotherapy was induction before planned surgery or radiotherapy (n=91) but 35% where no focal treatment was feasible (n=54), the latter with median PFS 6.2 mo. In the first-intent setting PAC was associated with better time to progression (adjusted HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.74) and thymoma histology carried a similar effect (HR 0.36); carboplatin-paclitaxel was favoured at first recurrence, and no regimen difference was shown in later lines. Treatment was physician-chosen, not randomised. Response was 39% vs 18% for thymoma against thymic carcinoma at first recurrence and fell to 29% vs 4% by the third. At first recurrence (n=114) median PFS was 7.7 mo and overall survival 44.0 mo. The registry captures no adverse-event data.

records.title: RELEVENT
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced thymic carcinoma — first-line chemo-immunotherapy & antiangiogenic combinations · II · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced thymic carcinoma / B3 thymoma with carcinoma Ramucirumab + carboplatin + paclitaxel, then ramucirumab maintenance Objective response rate Investigator-assessed ORR 80% (centralized review 57.6%) with median PFS 18.1 months and median OS 43.8 months; the highest first-line activity reported in thymic carcinoma versus historical controls.

records.title: MARBLE
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced thymic carcinoma — first-line chemo-immunotherapy & antiangiogenic combinations · II · 2025
records.body: Untreated advanced or recurrent thymic carcinoma Atezolizumab + carboplatin + paclitaxel, then atezolizumab maintenance Objective response rate ORR 56% (27/48, all partial responses; p<0.0001) with no treatment-related deaths; supports adding atezolizumab to first-line carboplatin-paclitaxel for thymic carcinoma.

records.title: Octreotide ± Prednisone (Loehrer)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · II · 2004
records.body: Advanced octreotide-scan-positive thymoma/thymic carcinoma Octreotide, with later addition of prednisone for non-responders Response rate ORR 32% (2 CR, 10 PR; responses confined to pure thymoma) with 2-year OS 75.7%; octreotide with or without prednisone is an option for somatostatin-receptor-positive thymoma.

records.title: Everolimus (Zucali)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · II · 2018
records.body: Advanced thymoma/thymic carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy Everolimus 10 mg once daily to progression or toxicity (single-arm) Disease control rate DCR 88% with median PFS 10.1 months (thymoma 16.6 vs thymic carcinoma 5.6) and median OS 25.7 months; durable disease control but ~6% fatal pneumonitis warrants caution.

records.title: Sunitinib (Thomas)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · II · 2015
records.body: Chemotherapy-refractory thymic carcinoma or thymoma Sunitinib 50 mg/day (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off) Objective response ORR 26% in thymic carcinoma (6/23 PR) versus 6% in thymoma, with stable disease in the majority of both; established sunitinib as an active second-line option for thymic carcinoma.

records.title: REMORA
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · II · 2020
records.body: Advanced/metastatic thymic carcinoma after >=1 platinum regimen Lenvatinib 24 mg/day Objective response rate ORR 38% with disease control rate 95% and median PFS 9.3 months; among the most active second-line agents in thymic carcinoma and a standard salvage option.

records.title: PECATI
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · II · 2025
records.body: Pretreated metastatic B3 thymoma / thymic carcinoma Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab 5-month progression-free survival Met its primary endpoint with 5-month PFS 88.4% and no treatment-related deaths; a chemo-free TKI plus checkpoint-inhibitor combination is a promising platinum-refractory option.

records.title: Pembrolizumab (Giaccone)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — immune checkpoint inhibition · II · 2018
records.body: Recurrent thymic carcinoma after >=1 line of chemotherapy Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w Objective response rate ORR 22.5% (1 CR, 8 PR) with stable disease in 53%; severe autoimmune toxicity occurred in 15% (including myocarditis), so checkpoint blockade requires close monitoring even in thymic carcinoma.

records.title: Pembrolizumab (Cho)
records.subtitle: Thymic Neoplasms · Advanced / recurrent disease — immune checkpoint inhibition · II · 2019
records.body: Refractory/relapsed thymic epithelial tumor (26 carcinoma, 7 thymoma) Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w Response rate Partial responses in 19.2% of thymic carcinoma and 28.6% of thymoma (median PFS 6.1 months), but grade >=3 immune-related events in 71% of thymoma versus 15% of carcinoma; checkpoint blockade is generally avoided in thymoma.

records.title: German Rectal (CAO/ARO/AIO-94)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · III · 2004
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma with inferior margin within 16 cm of the anal verge, clinically cT3-4 or node-positive on mandatory endorectal ultrasound and CT; stage I and distant metastases excluded; age 75 or younger; no previous chemotherapy, pelvic radiotherapy, cancer apart from nonmelanoma skin cancer, or contraindication to chemoradiotherapy Preoperative vs postoperative chemoradiotherapy (TME both) — 50.4 Gy (28 × 1.8 Gy) + concurrent 5-FU 1000 mg/m²/day 120-h infusion (weeks 1 & 5) → adjuvant 5-FU 500 mg/m²/day ×5 days Q4W ×4; postoperative arm adds a 5.4-Gy boost Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, local recurrence, distant recurrence, postoperative complications, acute toxicity, late toxicity, sphincter preservation Preoperative chemoradiotherapy became the standard by halving 5-year local recurrence (6% vs 13%), reducing toxicity and increasing sphincter preservation in tumours planned for APR (39% vs 19%); 5-year OS showed no improvement (76% vs 74%)

records.title: Polish Colorectal (Bujko)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · III · 2006
records.body: Resectable rectal cancer, clinical stage T3 or T4, with no sphincter involvement and the lower tumour margin accessible on digital rectal examination; staging largely clinical - all circular or tethered lesions were classed cT3/cT4 on digital examination, with imaging used only in freely movable non-circumferential tumours to exclude T1/T2 Preoperative short-course radiotherapy 25 Gy in 5 fractions of 5 Gy → TME within 7 days vs Preoperative chemoradiation 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy with bolus 5-FU/leucovorin → TME 4–6 weeks later Primary: sphincter preservation. Secondary: long-term survival, local recurrence, distant metastases, late toxicity, permanent stoma Chemoradiation improved downstaging but not the sphincter-preservation primary endpoint (58.0% vs 61.2% with short-course RT), permanent stoma (51.6% vs 56.9%), 4-year OS (66.2% vs 67.2%), DFS (55.6% vs 58.4%) or local recurrence (14.2% vs 9.0%); it increased severe early toxicity (18.2% vs 3.2%) and reduced compliance (69.2% vs 97.9%), arguing against downstaging as a surrogate
records.keywords: Br J Surg 2006;93:1215-1223   Radiother Oncol 2004;72:15-24 primary report, endpoint definitions 15236870

records.title: TROG 01.04 (Ngan)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · III · 2012
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma with lower border within 12 cm of the anal verge; cT3 by endorectal ultrasound or pelvic MRI, with CT accepted when either failed; nodal status unrestricted and no distant or recurrent disease; prior radiotherapy and another cancer within 5 years excluded Short-course RT 25 Gy (5 × 5 Gy) → surgery at 3-7 days → adjuvant 5-FU/folinic acid ×6 courses vs long-course CRT 50.4 Gy (28 fractions) + infusional 5-FU → surgery at 4-6 weeks → adjuvant 5-FU/folinic acid ×4 courses Primary: local recurrence at 3 years. Secondary: time to local recurrence, time to distant recurrence, relapse-free survival, OS, late toxicity Short-course RT did not differ clearly from long-course chemoradiotherapy in 3-year local recurrence (7.5% vs 4.4%), distant recurrence, 5-year OS (74% vs 70%) or late toxicity; this null superiority result did not establish equivalence

records.title: STAR-01 (Aschele)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation — adding oxaliplatin · III · 2011
records.body: Mid-low rectal adenocarcinoma within 12 cm of the anal verge; cT3-4 and/or cN1-2, clinically resectable without pelvic-wall, prostate or bladder-base infiltration or distant metastases; age ≤75; prior treatment, pelvic RT or another malignancy apart from specified skin/cervical cancers excluded RT 50.4 Gy (28 fractions) + continuous-infusion 5-FU 225 mg/m²/day vs the same RT + 5-FU + oxaliplatin 60 mg/m² weekly ×6 → surgery at 6-8 weeks Primary: overall survival. Secondary: pathological complete response, acute toxicity, treatment compliance Adding concurrent oxaliplatin did not improve pathological complete response (16% in each arm; OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.66-1.44) and increased grade 3-4 preoperative toxicity from 8% to 24%; overall survival, the trial primary endpoint, was not reported

records.title: ACCORD 12/0405 (Gérard)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation — adding oxaliplatin · III · 2010
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma accessible to digital examination; cT3 or resectable cT4, with anterior low-rectal cT2 also eligible; staged by endorectal ultrasound and/or MRI without distant metastases; age ≤80 Cap 45: RT 45 Gy (25 fractions) + capecitabine 800 mg/m² twice daily, 5 days/week ×5 weeks vs Capox 50: RT 50 Gy (25 fractions) + the same capecitabine + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² weekly ×5 → TME at 6 weeks Primary: complete pathological response. Secondary: circumferential resection margin, sphincter preservation, local control, progression-free survival Escalating RT from 45 to 50 Gy while adding oxaliplatin did not meet the pathological complete-response primary endpoint (19.2% vs 13.9%) and increased grade 3-4 preoperative toxicity (25.4% vs 10.9%); the 2 treatment changes cannot be separated, and local control and PFS were not reported

records.title: NSABP R-04 (Allegra)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation — adding oxaliplatin · III · 2015
records.body: Clinical stage II (T3-4N0) or III (T1-4N1-2) rectal adenocarcinoma within 12 cm of the anal verge and amenable to curative resection, treated with preoperative chemoradiation; ECOG 0-1; preexisting peripheral neuropathy, previous pelvic radiation, active inflammatory bowel disease and myocardial infarction within 6 months excluded RT 4500 cGy/25 fractions + boost 540-1080 cGy with CVI 5-FU 225 mg/m2/day throughout RT vs RT + capecitabine 825 mg/m2 po bid throughout RT vs RT + CVI 5-FU 225 mg/m2/day + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m2 IV weekly x5 vs RT + capecitabine 825 mg/m2 po bid + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m2 IV weekly x5 (2x2 factorial; the 2 oxaliplatin arms opened only at the October 2005 amendment, which also cut fluoropyrimidine dosing from 7 to 5 days/week on all arms) Primary: local-regional tumour control at 3 years. Secondary: OS, disease-free survival, time to locoregional recurrence, toxicity, treatment compliance Capecitabine was equivalent to infusional 5-FU as radiosensitisation, with 3-year local-regional failure of 11.8% vs 11.2%, supporting oral capecitabine as standard. Adding oxaliplatin provided no local-regional, DFS or OS benefit but raised grade 3-5 toxicity from about 27% to 41% and grade 3-5 diarrhoea from 6.9% to 16.5%; fewer than 70% completed planned oxaliplatin. On-treatment deaths were 10 with capecitabine vs 3 with 5-FU, a signal the authors considered unresolved despite identical OS

records.title: CAO/ARO/AIO-04 (Rödel)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation — adding oxaliplatin · III · 2015
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma ≤12 cm above the anal verge; cT3-4 or cN1-2 on ultrasound, CT or MRI without metastases; prior chemotherapy or pelvic RT excluded; peripheral neuropathy >grade 2 or chronic diarrhoea >grade 1 excluded Preoperative CRT 50.4 Gy + infusional 5-FU 250 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² → TME → postoperative oxaliplatin/leucovorin/5-FU ×8 cycles vs CRT 50.4 Gy + infusional 5-FU 1000 mg/m² → TME → bolus 5-FU ×4 cycles Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: OS, pathological complete response, R0 resection, sphincter-sparing surgery, acute and late toxicity, locoregional and distant recurrence Integrating oxaliplatin into both preoperative chemoradiotherapy and postoperative chemotherapy improved 3-year DFS (75.9% vs 71.2%; HR 0.79); because both treatment phases changed, the trial does not isolate the contribution of concurrent oxaliplatin

records.title: CAO/ARO/AIO-12 (Fokas)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · II · 2019
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma ≤12 cm from the anal verge with mandatory MRI showing low cT3 <6 cm, middle-third cT3 with >5 mm mesorectal extension, cT4, or nodal involvement including cT1-2/cN+ and high-risk cT3-4/cN0; no distant metastases Induction FOLFOX ×3 → 5-FU/oxaliplatin CRT 50.4 Gy → TME vs 5-FU/oxaliplatin CRT 50.4 Gy → consolidation FOLFOX ×3 → TME (both sequences scheduled surgery on day 123; no adjuvant chemotherapy recommended) Primary: pathological complete response. Secondary: acute toxicity, treatment compliance, surgical complications, tumour regression grading, neoadjuvant rectal score, R0 resection, sphincter-sparing surgery Consolidation FOLFOX after chemoradiotherapy produced 25% pCR vs 17% with induction-first and improved full-dose chemoradiotherapy/oxaliplatin compliance; surgery remained required regardless of response, so the sequence trial did not test organ preservation

records.title: RAPIDO (Bahadoer)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · III · 2021
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma <16 cm from the anal verge with ≥1 MRI high-risk feature: cT4a/b, extramural vascular invasion, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia with tumour or node ≤1 mm, or metastatic lateral nodes; metastatic or recurrent disease excluded Short-course RT 5 × 5 Gy → consolidation CAPOX (6 cycles) or FOLFOX4 (9 cycles) → TME (TNT) vs long-course chemoradiation 50.4 Gy (28 × 1.8) or 50 Gy (25 × 2.0) + concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily → TME → optional adjuvant CAPOX ×8 or FOLFOX4 ×12 Primary: disease-related treatment failure at 3 years. Secondary: neoadjuvant treatment completion, toxicity, R0 resection, pathological complete response, surgical complications, quality of life, functional outcome, OS, local recurrence Short-course RT followed by chemotherapy before surgery reduced 3-year disease-related treatment failure (23.7% vs 30.4%), sustained at 5 years (27.8% vs 34.0%), and doubled pCR (28% vs 14%). The gain was distant control (5-year metastases 23.0% vs 30.4%), while locoregional failure was higher at 3 years (8.3% vs 6.0%) and 5 years (11.7% vs 8.1%); 5-year OS was similar (81.7% vs 80.2%)
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:29-42   Ann Surg 2023;278:e766-e772 5-yr locoregional-failure analysis 36661037

records.title: PRODIGE 23 (Conroy)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · III · 2021
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma within 15 cm of the anal verge; MRI-staged cT4 or cT3 for which a tumour board recommended chemoradiotherapy, without metastases; age <76; prior pelvic RT or chemotherapy, unresectable disease, ischaemic coronary disease, grade >1 neuropathy or active inflammatory bowel disease excluded Induction FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h, Q2W) ×6 → chemoradiotherapy (50.4 Gy + capecitabine) → TME → adjuvant chemotherapy 3 months vs chemoradiotherapy (50.4 Gy + capecitabine) → TME → adjuvant chemotherapy 6 months Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: OS, metastasis-free survival, cancer-specific survival, locoregional and metastatic recurrence, pathological complete response, R0 resection, surgical morbidity, safety, quality of life Induction mFOLFIRINOX before chemoradiotherapy improved DFS, sustained from 3 years (75.7% vs 68.5%) to 7 years (67.6% vs 62.5%), and increased 7-year OS (81.9% vs 76.1%) and metastasis-free survival (79.2% vs 72.3%); pCR was 27.8% vs 12.1%
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:702-715   Ann Oncol 2024;35:873-881 7-yr long-term results 38986769

records.title: STELLAR (Jin)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated distal or middle-third rectal adenocarcinoma; MRI-staged cT3-4 and/or regional node-positive without distant metastases; age ≤70; recurrent disease, contraindication to treatment or MRI, and a second primary malignancy excluded Short-course RT 25 Gy (5 × 5 Gy) → 4 cycles CAPOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14) → TME → 2 cycles CAPOX (TNT) vs long-course chemoradiation 50 Gy (25 fractions) + concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily → TME → 6 cycles CAPOX Primary: disease-free survival at 3 years. Secondary: OS, metastasis-free survival, locoregional recurrence, surgical complications, acute toxicity, treatment completion Short-course RT followed by CAPOX remained an alternative to long-course chemoradiotherapy: 5-year DFS was 62.0% vs 58.7% and 5-year OS 78.1% vs 69.7%; the earlier 3-year analysis established non-inferiority and showed a higher complete-response rate
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1681-1692   J Clin Oncol 2026 5-yr update 42507974

records.title: Habr-Gama
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Organ preservation & watch-and-wait · N/A · 2004
records.body: Distal rectal adenocarcinoma 0-7 cm from the anal verge, selected for primary APR and treated with neoadjuvant CRT; synchronous metastases excluded; results limited to stage-0 patients with cCR sustained ≥12 months or pT0N0M0 after TME; response was assessed without MRI (observational cohorts) 5-FU/leucovorin CRT 50.4 Gy over 6 weeks → observation after complete clinical response sustained ≥12 months (n=71) vs the same CRT → TME after incomplete response, analysed here only for pT0N0M0 (n=22); no adjuvant chemotherapy Primary: N/A. Secondary: OS, disease-free survival, recurrence, stoma rate, surgical morbidity This observational series established watch-and-wait feasibility, not a surgery comparison: 71 of 265 patients had a complete clinical response sustained ≥12 months and were observed, while 22 incomplete clinical responders had pT0N0M0 after TME. At 5 years, reported OS was 100% vs 88% and DFS 92% vs 83%, with no cancer-related deaths among observed patients. Among 71 observed, 5 recurred: 2 bowel-wall regrowths at 56 and 64 months were salvaged and 3 were systemic; no pelvic recurrence occurred. TME produced a stoma in 16 of 22, including 9 permanent colostomies

records.title: IWWD (van der Valk)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Organ preservation & watch-and-wait · N/A · 2018
records.body: Rectal cancer managed by watch-and-wait after a locally defined complete response to neoadjuvant therapy; no central response definition or mandatory assessment modality, and local excision was allowed; near-complete responders, non-cCR or inoperable patients, and baseline metastases excluded (single-arm) Watch-and-wait after locally defined clinical complete response; neoadjuvant regimen, restaging and surveillance followed each centre's local protocol (international registry) Primary: cumulative incidence of local regrowth. Secondary: distant metastasis, OS, disease-specific survival Watch-and-wait after clinical complete response carried 25.2% local regrowth at 2 years; 97% arose in the bowel wall and 88% within 2 years. Of 115 regrowths with documented treatment, 101 salvage resections were R0, and unsalvageable local disease was estimated at ≤1% of the cohort. Distant metastases occurred in 8%; 5-year OS was 84.7% and disease-specific survival 93.8%

records.title: OPRA (Garcia-Aguilar)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Organ preservation & watch-and-wait · II · 2022
records.body: Untreated rectal adenocarcinoma, MRI-staged stage II (cT3-4N0) or III (any T, cN1-2), without distant metastases; recurrent disease and prior pelvic irradiation excluded; after TNT, watch-and-wait was offered only to complete or near-complete responders willing to undergo intensive surveillance Total neoadjuvant therapy, sequencing comparison — induction chemo → CRT (INCT-CRT) vs CRT → consolidation chemo (CRT-CNCT); chemo = FOLFOX ×8 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-h, Q2W) or CAPEOX ×5 (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily), CRT = 50–56 Gy + concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily or 5-FU 225 mg/m²/day → watch-and-wait if cCR/near-cCR, else TME Primary: disease-free survival at 3 years. Secondary: TME-free survival, adverse events, local recurrence, distant recurrence, OS TNT with selective watch-and-wait preserved the rectum in 53% after chemoradiotherapy-first vs 41% after induction chemotherapy, but did not improve the 3-year DFS primary endpoint over the 75% historical benchmark (76% in both sequence groups). Regrowth occurred in 27% vs 40% of observed patients, and 21 of 154 patients advised to undergo TME did not receive it. Grade ≥3 toxicity was 34% vs 41%, with 5 treatment-related deaths

records.title: PROSPECT (Alliance N1048)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Selective omission of radiation · III · 2023
records.body: Previously untreated cT2 node-positive or cT3 rectal adenocarcinoma judged by the patient's own surgeon suitable for sphincter-sparing surgery; T4, four or more pelvic nodes with a short axis over 10 mm, and tumour within 3 mm of the radial margin excluded Neoadjuvant mFOLFOX6 ×6 (Q2W) → selective chemoradiotherapy only if tumour shrinkage <20% → TME vs chemoradiotherapy 50.4 Gy + concurrent fluoropyrimidine → TME (both ± adjuvant FOLFOX) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: OS, local recurrence, R0 resection, pathological complete response, toxicity Neoadjuvant mFOLFOX6 with selective chemoradiotherapy spared pelvic RT in 90.9% without reducing disease control: 5-year DFS was 80.8% vs 78.6%, meeting non-inferiority, with local recurrence about 2% in both arms; 5-year OS was 89.5% vs 90.2%

records.title: Dostarlimab (Cercek)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Immunotherapy for mismatch-repair-deficient disease · II · 2022
records.body: Previously untreated stage II-III dMMR rectal adenocarcinoma without distant metastases; entry by mismatch-repair protein loss on immunohistochemistry; active autoimmune or infectious disease and recent immunosuppression excluded (single-arm) Dostarlimab 500 mg IV Q3W ×9 cycles over 6 months → nonoperative follow-up after clinical complete response; otherwise CRT 50.4 Gy/28 fractions + capecitabine → TME Primary: overall response to dostarlimab with or without chemoradiotherapy; sustained clinical complete response 12 months after dostarlimab or pathological complete response after surgery. Secondary: safety Dostarlimab produced clinical complete response in all 12 patients who completed 6 months; none received chemoradiotherapy or surgery. The overall-response primary endpoint was met, but this was an interim report: 16 were enrolled, 4 remained on treatment and median follow-up was 12 months from enrolment. The 12-month sustained-response primary endpoint remained immature; only 4 had response beyond 1 year after treatment. No progression or recurrence occurred and all 16 were alive within this short follow-up; adverse events occurred in 12 of 16 (75%), with no grade ≥3 events

records.title: ADORE (Hong)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Adjuvant chemotherapy — after preoperative CRT · II · 2014
records.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma below the peritoneal reflection or ≤12 cm from the anal verge; ypStage II (ypT3-4N0) or III (any ypT, ypN1-2) after fluoropyrimidine-only CRT and R0 TME; oxaliplatin-containing CRT, R1/R2 or non-TME resection, neuropathy and prior systemic therapy apart from CRT excluded Adjuvant FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 h) Q2W ×8 vs bolus 5-FU 380 mg/m² + leucovorin 20 mg/m² days 1-5 Q4W ×4 Primary: disease-free survival at 3 years. Secondary: OS, safety, patterns of recurrence, quality of life Adjuvant FOLFOX after preoperative CRT and TME improved DFS vs fluorouracil/leucovorin, sustained from 3 years (71.6% vs 62.9%) to 6 years (68.2% vs 56.8%; HR 0.63); 6-year OS was similar (78.1% vs 76.4%)
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2014;15:1245-1253  25201358 J Clin Oncol 2019;37:3111-3123 long-term results 31593484

records.title: RTOG 87-04/ECOG 1289
records.subtitle: Anal Cancer · Definitive chemoradiation · III · 1996
records.body: Measurable epidermoid carcinoma of the anal canal without distant metastases, across any primary-tumour or regional-node stage; Karnofsky performance status >=60; keratinizing and nonkeratinizing squamous subtypes eligible Pelvic RT 45 Gy in 25 daily 1.8-Gy fractions over 5 weeks (additional 5.4 Gy in 3 fractions if primary remained palpable) + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion for 96 h on days 1 and 29 vs The same RT + 5-FU schedule + mitomycin 10 mg/m2 IV bolus on days 1 and 29 (maximum 20 mg per cycle; protocol-directed reduction of cycle 2 for cytopenias) Negative postinduction biopsy, Positive salvage biopsy, Locoregional control, Time to colostomy, Colostomy-free survival, Disease-free survival, Overall survival, Toxicity Adding mitomycin to 5-FU/RT established the definitive chemoradiation backbone by improving colostomy-free and disease-free outcomes, despite greater severe toxicity. At 4 years, colostomy was 9% vs 22%, colostomy-free survival 71% vs 59%, and DFS 73% vs 51%. The OS difference did not reach statistical significance (76% vs 67%). Grade 4 toxicity was 23% vs 7%; fatal neutropenic sepsis occurred in 4/146 vs 1/145.

records.title: ACT II
records.subtitle: Anal Cancer · Definitive chemoradiation · III · 2013
records.body: Non-metastatic invasive squamous, basaloid or cloacogenic carcinoma of the anal canal or margin, suitable for definitive chemoradiation; previous complete local excision or pelvic radiotherapy, HIV positivity, major cardiac disease and a competing major malignancy were excluded 50.4 Gy/28 fractions + fluorouracil 1000 mg/m²/day on days 1–4 and 29–32 + mitomycin 12 mg/m² on day 1 vs 50.4 Gy/28 fractions + fluorouracil 1000 mg/m²/day on days 1–4 and 29–32 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² on days 1 and 29; each ± 2 cycles fluorouracil/cisplatin maintenance at weeks 11 and 14 Primary: Complete response rate at 26 weeks, Acute grade 3–4 toxicity, Progression-free survival. Secondary: Colostomy-free survival, In-field recurrence rate, Cause-specific survival, Overall survival, Progression-free survival by concurrent chemotherapy ACT II supports mitomycin-based chemoradiation without maintenance chemotherapy as the standard definitive regimen. Cisplatin did not improve complete response at 26 weeks (89.6% vs 90.5% with mitomycin), and maintenance did not improve 3-year PFS (74% vs 73%). Overall grade 3-4 toxicity was similar (71% vs 72%), although haematological toxicity was higher with mitomycin (26% vs 16%); 8/940 patients died from treatment-related causes. In the post-hoc complete-case timing analysis, 72% (151/209) without complete response at 11 weeks from chemoradiotherapy start achieved complete response by week 26, supporting careful observation of resolving disease rather than premature salvage, with prompt evaluation of progression.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2013;14:516-524  23578724 Glynne-Jones et al. - 2017 - Best time to assess complete clinical response after chemoradiotherapy in squamous cell [89aa43b4]

records.title: RTOG 98-11
records.subtitle: Anal Cancer · Definitive chemoradiation · III · 2008
