records.body: Nonmetastatic T2-T4 squamous, basaloid or cloacogenic carcinoma of the anal canal with any pelvic/inguinal nodal status and Karnofsky performance score >=60; T1, M1, AIDS/severe comorbidity and active or recent major malignancy were excluded 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion on days 1-4 and 29-32 + mitomycin 10 mg/m2 IV bolus on days 1 and 29 (maximum 20 mg/course), concurrent with RT 45 Gy in 25 daily 1.8-Gy fractions over 5 weeks; boost to 55-59 Gy in 30-32 fractions over 5.5-6.5 weeks for T3/T4, node-positive or residual T2 disease vs Induction 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion on days 1-4 and 29-32 + cisplatin 75 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 29, then the same drugs on days 57-60/85-88 and days 57/85 concurrent with RT starting day 57; RT 45 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, boosted to 55-59 Gy over 5.5-6.5 weeks for T3/T4, node-positive or residual T2 disease Primary: 5-year disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Local-regional treatment failure, Distant metastasis, Colostomy, Toxicity Immediate 5-FU/mitomycin chemoradiation remains preferred; the tested cisplatin strategy produced worse long-term disease control and survival and cannot be read as a simple radiosensitiser substitution. At 5 years, DFS was 67.8% vs 57.8% and OS 78.3% vs 70.7%. The earlier colostomy advantage attenuated and did not reach statistical significance (11.9% vs 17.3%; HR 1.48, 95% CI 0.98-2.23). Acute grade 3-4 haematological toxicity was higher with mitomycin (61.8% vs 42.0%), while late grade 3-4 toxicity was similar (13.1% vs 10.7%). The cisplatin arm also included induction chemotherapy and delayed radiotherapy.

records.title: Moertel (INT-0035)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 1990
records.body: Resected stage III (Dukes C) colon cancer Levamisole + 5-FU for 1 year vs levamisole alone for 1 year vs observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Time to recurrence; safety; second primary cancers Levamisole + 5-FU reduced recurrence by 41% (95% CI 23–54) and mortality by 33% (10–50) vs observation; levamisole alone had no detectable recurrence or survival benefit.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 1990;322:352-358   Ann Intern Med 1995;122:321-326 final report (stage III) 7847642

records.title: IMPACT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 1995
records.body: Resected stage II-III colon cancer (3 trials) Fluorouracil + folinic acid on days 1–5 every 28 days ×6 cycles (~6 months) vs observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Event-free survival; recurrence; safety Fluorouracil/folinic acid improved 3-year OS to 83% vs 78% (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62–0.97; P=.029) and event-free survival to 71% vs 62% (HR 0.65, 0.54–0.78; nominal P<.0001).

records.title: MOSAIC
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 2004
records.body: Resected stage II-III colon cancer Adjuvant FOLFOX4 — oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² (day 1) added to LV5FU2 (leucovorin + bolus/infusional 5-FU), Q2W, 6 months vs LV5FU2 alone Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; safety 2004 primary analysis: FOLFOX4 improved 3-year DFS to 78.2% vs 72.9% (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.65–0.91; P=.002). 2009 update: 5-year DFS was 73.3% vs 67.4% (HR 0.80, 0.68–0.93; P=.003); in stage III, 6-year OS was 72.9% vs 68.7% (HR 0.80, 0.65–0.97; nominal P=.023), without a significant treatment-by-stage interaction.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2004;350:2343-2351   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:3109-3116 6-yr updated OS (stage III OS HR 0.80) 19451431

records.title: X-ACT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 2005
records.body: Resected stage III (Dukes C) colon cancer Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 every 21 days ×8 cycles (24 weeks) vs bolus 5-FU/leucovorin (Mayo Clinic regimen — leucovorin 20 mg/m² + 5-FU 425 mg/m², days 1–5 every 28 days ×6) Primary: Disease-free survival noninferiority; incidence and onset of predefined grade 3/4 fluoropyrimidine toxicities Secondary: Relapse-free survival; overall survival 2012 final analysis: capecitabine met DFS noninferiority to 5-FU/FA (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77–1.01). RFS superiority was not reached (HR 0.89, 0.78–1.02; nominal P=.104), while OS met noninferiority (HR 0.86, 0.74–1.01). 2005 primary report: onset of the predefined key grade 3/4 fluoropyrimidine toxicities was reduced and delayed with capecitabine (P<.001).
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2005;352:2696-2704   Ann Oncol 2012;23:1190-1197 final results, median 6.9 yr (OS HR 0.86) 21896539

records.title: NSABP C-07
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 2007
records.body: Resected stage II-III colon cancer Adjuvant FLOX — FULV (5-FU 500 mg/m² + leucovorin 500 mg/m² IV bolus weekly ×6 of each 8-week cycle, ×3 cycles) + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² on weeks 1, 3, 5 vs FULV alone Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Relapse-free interval; overall survival; safety; neurotoxicity 2007 primary analysis: FLOX improved DFS (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.69–0.93; P=.0034); 3-year DFS was 76.1% vs 71.8%. Grade 3/4 diarrhoea was 38% vs 32%, and enteropathy-attributed deaths were 5 vs 1. 2011 update: DFS benefit persisted (HR 0.82, 0.72–0.93; nominal P=.002), while the prespecified secondary OS comparison did not reach nominal significance (HR 0.88, 0.75–1.02; P=.08).
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2007;25:2198-2204   J Clin Oncol 2011;29:3768-3774 updated survival & subset analyses, 8-yr 21859995

records.title: QUASAR
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 2007
records.body: Resected colorectal cancer, mostly stage II 5-FU 370 mg/m² IV + folinic acid (high-dose 175 mg or low-dose) — six 5-day courses Q4W or 30 once-weekly courses vs observation Primary: All-cause mortality Secondary: Colorectal cancer mortality; recurrence; toxicity; quality of life; cost-effectiveness Fluorouracil/folinic acid reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70–0.95; P=.008) and recurrence (RR 0.78, 0.67–0.91; nominal P=.001) vs observation. For stage II disease, the 3.6-point 5-year survival benefit is modelled from an assumed 20% baseline mortality, not an observed arm difference.

records.title: XELOXA (NO16968)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · III · 2011
records.body: Resected stage III colon cancer XELOX/CAPOX — oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14, Q3W ×8 cycles (24 weeks) vs bolus FU/FA for 24–32 weeks Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; relapse-free survival; safety 2011 primary analysis, performed after 648/682 planned DFS events: XELOX improved DFS (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.69–0.93; P=.0045); 3-year DFS was 70.9% vs 66.5%. 2015 final update: 7-year OS was 73% vs 67% (HR 0.83, 0.70–0.99; nominal P=.04); no final-analysis alpha was prespecified.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2011;29:1465-1471   J Clin Oncol 2015;33:3733-3740 final OS analysis, median ~7 yr (OS HR 0.83) 26324362

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Baxter et al.)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · N/A · 2022
records.body: Resected stage II colon cancer N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A ASCO guideline update: adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) is not routinely recommended for stage II colon cancer overall. ACT should be offered for stage IIB/IIC (T4) tumors (OS HR 0.64). ACT may be offered for stage IIA with high-risk features (fewer than 12 nodes sampled, LVI/PNI, poor differentiation, obstruction, perforation, or grade BD3 tumor budding). dMMR/MSI tumors should not routinely receive fluoropyrimidine-only ACT. Addition of oxaliplatin is not routinely recommended (insufficient OS/DFS benefit, only a TTR benefit in MOSAIC exploratory analysis) but may be offered via shared decision-making; if used, 3 or 6 months of CAPOX/FOLFOX are both reasonable per IDEA collaboration data, weighing similar 5-year DFS against substantially higher grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy with 6 months (36% vs 13%).

records.title: NSABP C-08
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · III · 2011
records.body: Resected stage II-III colon cancer mFOLFOX6 ×6 months + bevacizumab ×1 year vs mFOLFOX6 ×6 months Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; toxicity Adding 1 year of bevacizumab to mFOLFOX6 did not improve DFS (3-year 77.4% vs 75.5%; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.76–1.04; P=.15). Grade ≥3 hypertension, wound complications, pain and proteinuria were more frequent with bevacizumab; bevacizumab was not associated with increased mortality.

records.title: AVANT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · III · 2012
records.body: Completely resected stage III or high-risk stage II colon carcinoma; adults randomized 4–8 weeks after surgery FOLFOX4 ×24 weeks vs FOLFOX4 ×24 weeks + bevacizumab ×48 weeks vs XELOX ×24 weeks + bevacizumab ×48 weeks Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; safety The global DFS gate failed (P=.2024), so pairwise efficacy was exploratory: bevacizumab-FOLFOX4 vs FOLFOX4 HR 1.17 (95% CI 0.98–1.39) and bevacizumab-XELOX vs FOLFOX4 HR 1.07 (0.90–1.28). Five-year OS was 85% with FOLFOX4, 81% with bevacizumab-FOLFOX4 and 82% with bevacizumab-XELOX; the exploratory bevacizumab-FOLFOX4 vs FOLFOX4 OS HR was 1.27 (1.03–1.57; nominal P=.02). Grade 3–5 adverse events occurred in 73%, 76% and 65% in those same arms.

records.title: N0147 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · III · 2012
records.body: Resected stage III, KRAS wild-type colon cancer mFOLFOX6 + cetuximab vs mFOLFOX6 alone, each for 12 Q2W courses Primary: Disease-free survival in wild-type KRAS Secondary: Time to recurrence; overall survival; toxicity Cetuximab did not improve DFS in wild-type KRAS disease: 3-year DFS 71.5% vs 74.6% with mFOLFOX6 alone (adjusted HR 1.21, 95% CI 0.98–1.49; nominal P=.08). Grade ≥3 adverse events were 73.3% vs 51.1%, including diarrhoea 15.9% vs 9.3% and acne/rash 20.0% vs 0.3%.

records.title: PETACC-8
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · III · 2014
records.body: Resected stage III, KRAS wild-type colon cancer FOLFOX4 + cetuximab for 12 cycles vs FOLFOX4 alone for 12 cycles Primary: Disease-free survival in KRAS exon 2 wild-type disease Secondary: Overall survival; treatment compliance; biomarkers; safety At the planned interim analysis, cetuximab did not improve DFS in KRAS exon 2 wild-type disease: 3-year DFS 75.1% vs 78.0% with FOLFOX4 alone (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.85–1.29; P=.66). Grade 3/4 acne-like rash was 27% vs <1%, diarrhoea 15% vs 9%, mucositis 8% vs 1%, and infusion reactions 7% vs 4%.

records.title: IDEA Collaboration
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Resected stage III colon cancer (6 trials) 3 vs 6 months of FOLFOX or CAPOX Primary: Disease-free survival noninferiority Secondary: Overall survival; treatment adherence; safety, including neurotoxicity 2018 primary analysis: 3 months did not meet DFS noninferiority overall (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.00–1.15; margin 1.12); regimen choice was not randomized, although the adjusted duration-by-regimen interaction was P=.02. 2020 final update: noninferiority remained unestablished for DFS (HR 1.08, 1.02–1.15) and OS (HR 1.02, 0.95–1.11); grade ≥2 neurotoxicity was ~14–17% with 3 months vs ~44–45% with 6 months.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2018;378:1177-1188   Lancet Oncol 2020;21:1620-1629 final OS analysis 33271092

records.title: ACHIEVE-2
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Resected high-risk stage II colon cancer with ≥1 of T4 disease, poor differentiation, <12 nodes, lymphovascular invasion, bowel obstruction, or perforation 3 vs 6 months of adjuvant mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; time to treatment failure; safety; treatment delivery; neuropathy Three-year DFS was 88.2% with 3 months vs 87.9% with 6 months (adjusted HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.67–1.87). The stand-alone trial did not define a noninferiority margin or alpha, so this is not proof of noninferiority. Grade ≥2 neuropathy was 16% vs 43%.

records.title: IDEA Collaboration (Stage II)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Resected high-risk stage II colon or rectal cancer with ≥1 of T4 disease, poor differentiation, vascular/perilymphatic/perineural invasion, inadequate nodal harvest (<10 in SCOT; <12 otherwise), bowel obstruction, or perforation 3 vs 6 months of adjuvant FOLFOX or CAPOX (regimen chosen by clinician/patient, not randomized) Primary: Disease-free survival noninferiority Secondary: Overall survival; safety Three months did not meet DFS noninferiority vs 6 months (5-year 80.7% vs 83.9%; HR 1.17, 80% CI 1.05–1.31; margin 1.20). Regimen choice was not randomized and the multiplicity-adjusted regimen interaction was not significant; descriptive HRs were 1.02 for CAPOX and 1.41 for FOLFOX. Grade ≥2 neuropathy was 13% vs 36%.

records.title: FOxTROT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Neoadjuvant chemotherapy · II/III · 2023
records.body: Resectable M0 colon cancer; biopsy-confirmed cT3–4 with CT extramural extension ≥5 mm (≥1 mm after pilot); fit for surgery/chemotherapy; obstruction allowed after defunctioning stoma OxFU/OxCap for 6 weeks → surgery 4–6 weeks later → postoperative chemotherapy to 24 weeks total vs surgery → 24 weeks postoperative OxFU/OxCap; from 2014, a 12-week total option was permitted for lower-risk or older patients; separate RAS-wild-type panitumumab substudy Primary: 2-year residual or recurrent disease Secondary: Perioperative outcomes; pathological response; depth of extramural spread in the panitumumab substudy Neoadjuvant chemotherapy reduced 2-year residual/recurrent disease to 16.9% vs 21.5% (rate ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.54–0.98; P=.037). R0 resection was 94% vs 89%, with T4 disease 21% vs 31% after treatment.

records.title: NeoCol
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Neoadjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2026
records.body: Histologically confirmed, nonmetastatic colon cancer; CT-defined cT3 with extramural invasion ≥5 mm or cT4; ECOG 0–2 Neoadjuvant CAPOX — capecitabine 2000 mg/m²/day orally days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, Q3W ×3 cycles, then surgery + up to 5 further cycles of CAPOX/capecitabine if adjuvant indicated vs upfront surgery + up to 8 cycles of adjuvant CAPOX or capecitabine monotherapy as indicated (standard) Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; surgical and pathological outcomes; adjuvant chemotherapy; toxicity; quality of life At only 38/56 planned events, neoadjuvant CAPOX did not improve 3-year DFS vs upfront surgery (83% vs 87%; P=.36); the event deficit makes the result nonconfirmatory. Neoadjuvant treatment reduced the proportion meeting postoperative adjuvant-chemotherapy criteria to 59% vs 73% (nominal P=.02).

records.title: DYNAMIC
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · II · 2022
records.body: Resected stage II (T3–4 N0 M0) colon or rectal adenocarcinoma; ECOG 0–2; medically fit for adjuvant oxaliplatin-based or single-agent fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy ctDNA-guided management (adjuvant chemotherapy only for week-4 or week-7 ctDNA positivity) vs standard clinicopathological management Primary: 2-year recurrence-free survival noninferiority Secondary: Adjuvant chemotherapy use; recurrence-free survival by ctDNA status; time to recurrence; overall survival ctDNA-guided management reduced adjuvant-chemotherapy use to 15% vs 28% (nominal RR for standard vs guided management 1.82, 95% CI 1.25–2.65) while meeting 2-year RFS noninferiority: 93.5% vs 92.4%, difference 1.1 points (95% CI −4.1 to 6.2; margin −8.5).

records.title: DYNAMIC-III (AGITG/CCTG)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · II/III · 2025
records.body: Resected R0 stage III colon or rectal adenocarcinoma; medically fit for at least fluoropyrimidine monotherapy; enrolled within 6 weeks after surgery; postoperative ctDNA sampled at weeks 5–6 ctDNA-guided therapy (de-escalate if ctDNA-neg, escalate if ctDNA-pos) vs standard management Primary: 3-year recurrence-free survival in ctDNA-negative disease; 2-year recurrence-free survival in ctDNA-positive disease Secondary: Treatment adherence; ctDNA clearance; overall survival; toxicity Postoperative ctDNA was strongly prognostic (3-year RFS 87% if negative vs 49% if positive; nominal P<.001). In ctDNA-negative disease, guided de-escalation did not confirm noninferiority (85.3% vs 88.1%; difference −2.8 points, 95% CI −8.0 to 2.3; margin −7.5). In ctDNA-positive disease, guided escalation did not meet the phase 2 superiority threshold (2-year RFS 51.1% vs 60.8%; HR 1.16, 0.87–1.53).

records.title: GALAXY (CIRCULATE-Japan)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · N/A · 2023
records.body: Any-stage colon or stage IV/recurrent rectal cancer after curative-intent R0 resection; age ≥20; ECOG 0–1; ≥1 ctDNA result in the MRD or surveillance window; stage I–III rectal cancer excluded Prospective tumor-informed ctDNA surveillance cohort; ACT at clinician discretion; outcomes by MRD status, surveillance status, and ctDNA clearance Primary: Disease-free survival; overall survival Secondary: ctDNA clearance; molecular recurrence In the 2024 enlarged observational cohort, MRD-positive vs negative 24-month DFS was 20.57% vs 85.10% (HR 11.99, 95% CI 10.02–14.35) and OS HR was 9.68 (6.33–14.82); surveillance ctDNA positivity preceded radiological recurrence by median 5.91 months.
records.keywords: Nat Med 2023;29:127-134  36646802 Nat Med 2024;30:3272-3283 23-mo update: DFS/OS + ctDNA clearance 39284954

records.title: ALTAIR (EPOC1905, CIRCULATE-Japan)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · III · 2026
records.body: ctDNA-positive molecular residual disease after curative resection of stage 0–IV CRC (including resected oligometastatic stage IV) — Signatera ctDNA-positive after completion of standard-of-care therapy, with no radiological evidence of disease (post-adjuvant MRD; Japan/Taiwan) Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 Q28D for up to 6 cycles vs matched placebo on the same schedule Primary: Investigator-assessed disease-free survival Secondary: ctDNA clearance; second disease-free survival; overall survival; safety; treatment completion; quality of life Post-adjuvant trifluridine/tipiracil did not improve DFS in ctDNA-positive, radiologically disease-free CRC: median 9.30 vs 5.55 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.60–1.05; P=.107). Grade ≥3 adverse events were 73.0% vs 3.3%, with no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: ALASCCA
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant aspirin — PI3K pathway-altered disease · III · 2025
records.body: Stage I-III rectal or stage II-III colon cancer with somatic PI3K-pathway alterations (PIK3CA hotspot [group A] or other PIK3CA/PIK3R1/PTEN variants [group B]) Aspirin 160 mg once daily for 3 years vs matched placebo Primary: Colorectal cancer recurrence in group A alterations Secondary: Disease-free survival; overall survival; group B recurrence; safety In group A, aspirin reduced 3-year recurrence to 7.7% vs 14.1% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.24–0.98; P=.04). In group B, the descriptive secondary result was 7.7% vs 16.8% (HR 0.42, 0.21–0.83); no multiplicity adjustment was performed. Severe adverse events occurred in 16.8% vs 11.6%.

records.title: NICHE-2
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Immunotherapy for dMMR / MSI-H disease · II · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated, resectable, nonmetastatic dMMR colon cancer; adults with clinical stage I–III in the original cohort, amended to require cT3+, N+, or both; WHO performance status 0–1 (single-arm) Nivolumab 3 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg on day 1 → surgery within 6 weeks of enrolment Primary: Timely surgery; 3-year disease-free survival Secondary: Pathological response; translational genomic analyses The primary timely-surgery endpoint was met: 113/115 patients (98%; 97.5% CI 93–100) underwent timely surgery; 2 treatment-related myositis events caused delay. Among 111 eligible patients, pathological response was 98%, major pathological response 95%, and complete response 68%. No recurrence was observed at median 26.2 months, but the 3-year DFS co-primary endpoint remained immature.

records.title: ATOMIC (A021502)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Immunotherapy for dMMR / MSI-H disease · III · 2026
records.body: Resected stage III dMMR colon cancer Adjuvant atezolizumab 840 mg IV Q2W + mFOLFOX6 ×6 months → atezolizumab monotherapy to 12 months total vs mFOLFOX6 alone ×6 months Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; adverse events; patient-reported outcomes; quality of life At the second prespecified interim analysis, atezolizumab + mFOLFOX6 improved 3-year DFS to 86.3% vs 76.2% (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.35–0.73; P<.001). At the first interim OS analysis, statistical significance was not reached (5-year 89.7% vs 87.9%; HR 0.90, 0.55–1.47; P=.68). Grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 84.1% vs 71.9%.

records.title: CHALLENGE
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant lifestyle intervention — structured exercise · III · 2025
records.body: Resected stage III or high-risk stage II colon adenocarcinoma (T4, <12 nodes resected, or poor differentiation); completed adjuvant chemotherapy 2–6 months earlier; ECOG 0–1; <150 min/week moderate-to-vigorous exercise Structured exercise + health-education materials vs health-education materials alone, each for 3 years Primary: Disease-free survival Secondary: Overall survival; physical activity; fitness; physical functioning; safety Structured exercise improved 5-year DFS to 80.3% vs 73.9% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.94; P=.02). The unadjusted secondary OS result supported longer survival (8-year 90.3% vs 83.2%; HR 0.63, 0.43–0.94). Musculoskeletal adverse events occurred in 18.5% vs 11.5%.

records.title: de Gramont (FOLFOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2000
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colon or rectal adenocarcinoma; age 18–75 years; prior adjuvant chemotherapy permitted if completed ≥6 months earlier; CNS metastases, second malignancy and disease confined to prior radiation fields excluded FOLFOX4 Q2W vs LV5FU2 Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity or discontinuation Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, overall survival, tolerability, quality of life FOLFOX4 improved PFS vs LV5FU2 by investigator assessment (9.0 vs 6.2 mo) and blinded external review (8.2 vs 6.0 mo), and increased external-review ITT response (50.0% vs 21.9%). OS did not reach statistical significance (16.2 vs 14.7 mo). Grade 3–4 neutropenia, diarrhoea and neurologic toxicity increased; 1 therapy-related death occurred

records.title: Saltz (IFL)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2000
records.body: Previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer; prior adjuvant fluorouracil permitted only after ≥1 year disease-free; prior pelvic irradiation excluded, although 9 enrolled patients had received it IFL weekly for 4 weeks Q6W vs fluorouracil/leucovorin daily for 5 days Q4W vs irinotecan alone weekly for 4 weeks Q6W until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, confirmed objective response, safety, quality of life IFL improved the primary comparison with fluorouracil/leucovorin: median PFS 7.0 vs 4.3 months (p=.004), median OS 14.8 vs 12.6 months (p=.04), confirmed response 39% vs 21% and objective response 50% vs 28%. Grade 3–4 diarrhoea was 22.7%, 13.2% and 31.0% with IFL, fluorouracil/leucovorin and irinotecan alone; severe neutropenia was 53.8%, 66.2% and 31.4%. Drug-related mortality was approximately 1% in each arm

records.title: Douillard
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2000
records.body: Previously untreated metastatic or otherwise advanced colorectal adenocarcinoma; age 18–75 years; prior adjuvant chemotherapy permitted if completed >6 months earlier; CNS metastases, unresolved bowel obstruction or diarrhoea, and fluorouracil contraindications excluded Irinotecan + infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin vs infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin; weekly or Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Objective response rate. Secondary: Time to progression, duration of response, overall survival, quality of life, treatment-related adverse events Irinotecan + infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin improved confirmed ITT response (34.8% vs 21.9%; p=.005), median time to progression (6.7 vs 4.4 months; p<.001) and median OS (17.4 vs 14.1 months; p=.031). Grade 3–4 diarrhoea and neutropenia were more frequent with irinotecan and schedule-dependent; one probable treatment-related septic death occurred

records.title: N9741
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2004
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; adjuvant fluorouracil within 12 months, prior advanced-disease therapy, symptomatic neuropathy and CNS metastases excluded FOLFOX Q2W vs IFL on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 Q6W vs IROX Q3W; continue until progression, unmanageable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Time to progression. Secondary: Overall survival, confirmed tumour response rate, time to treatment discontinuation, toxicity FOLFOX improved median time to progression vs IFL (8.7 vs 6.9 mo; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.61–0.89), median OS (19.5 vs 15.0 mo; HR 0.66, 0.54–0.82) and confirmed response (45% vs 31%). IROX did not improve the primary endpoint vs IFL (6.5 vs 6.9 mo; HR 1.02, 0.85–1.23). FOLFOX caused less severe gastrointestinal toxicity and febrile neutropenia but more severe paraesthesia

records.title: GERCOR (Tournigand)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2004
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; age 18–75 years; prior adjuvant chemotherapy permitted if completed ≥6 months earlier; CNS metastases, second malignancy, bowel obstruction, grade ≥2 diarrhoea, symptomatic angina and disease confined to prior radiation fields excluded FOLFIRI until progression or unacceptable toxicity → FOLFOX6 vs FOLFOX6 until progression or unacceptable toxicity → FOLFIRI Primary: Second progression-free survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, overall survival, response rate, safety The sequences did not differ in second PFS (14.2 vs 10.9 mo), measured from randomisation through progression after second-line therapy, or OS (21.5 vs 20.6 mo). First-line FOLFIRI and FOLFOX6 gave similar response (56% vs 54%) and PFS (8.5 vs 8.0 mo); second-line FOLFOX6 after FOLFIRI gave longer PFS than FOLFIRI after FOLFOX6 (4.2 vs 2.5 mo). Grade 3–4 toxicity was 53% with first-line FOLFIRI vs 74% with first-line FOLFOX6

records.title: TRIBE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2014
records.body: Previously untreated, first-occurrence metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma deemed unresectable; age 18–75 years, with ECOG 0 required above 70; adjuvant oxaliplatin within 12 months, grade ≥1 neuropathy, major cardiovascular or bleeding risk and full-dose anticoagulation excluded FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab vs FOLFIRI + bevacizumab for up to 12 cycles → fluorouracil/leucovorin + bevacizumab maintenance until progression Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, objective response rate, R0 resection rate, safety FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab improved PFS (12.1 vs 9.7 mo; HR 0.75) and response (65% vs 53%) over FOLFIRI + bevacizumab. At mature 48.1-mo follow-up, OS was 29.8 vs 25.8 mo (HR 0.80); benefit did not differ across RAS/BRAF subgroups, while BRAF mutation remained strongly prognostic. Grade 3–4 neutropenia (50.0% vs 20.5%), diarrhoea (18.8% vs 10.6%) and neuropathy (5.2% vs 0) increased; adverse-event deaths were 6 vs 4
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2014;371:1609-1618   Lancet Oncol 2015;16:1306-1315 updated OS and RAS/BRAF molecular subgroup analyses 26338525

records.title: TRIPLETE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2022
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable RAS and BRAF V600 wild-type metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; age 18–75 years, with ECOG 0 required at 71–75; prior adjuvant oxaliplatin, relapse <6 months after adjuvant fluoropyrimidine alone, and grade ≥2 neuropathy excluded mFOLFOXIRI + panitumumab vs mFOLFOX + panitumumab Q2W for up to 12 cycles → panitumumab maintenance until progression Primary: Objective response rate. Secondary: Progression-free survival, R0 resection rate, safety ORR 73% vs 76% (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.56-1.34, p=0.526); median PFS 12.7 vs 12.3 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.70-1.11, p=0.277); R0 resection 25% vs 29%. Negative: intensifying the backbone to FOLFOXIRI adds GI toxicity without benefit when combined with panitumumab in RAS/BRAF-wt mCRC.

records.title: NO16966 (XELOX vs FOLFOX-4)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2008
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer; no prior metastatic-disease systemic therapy, oxaliplatin or bevacizumab; clinically significant cardiovascular disease, full-dose anticoagulation, CNS metastases and major bleeding or wound risk excluded XELOX Q3W vs FOLFOX-4 Q2W, pooled across bevacizumab/placebo assignment; continue until progression or 48 weeks, then poststudy treatment permitted until progression Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, overall survival, duration of response, time to treatment failure, safety XELOX was noninferior to FOLFOX4 for PFS: in the regulator-requested eligible population (n=1,904), median PFS was 7.9 vs 8.5 mo (HR 1.05, 97.5% CI 0.94–1.18); ITT results in all 2,034 randomised were concordant (8.0 vs 8.5 mo; HR 1.04, 0.93–1.16). OS was similar (19.8 vs 19.6 mo; HR 0.99, 0.88–1.12). Established XELOX as an oral fluoropyrimidine alternative to FOLFOX4

records.title: TRIBE2
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · III · 2020
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; age 18–75 years, with ECOG 0 required at 71–75; prior palliative therapy, adjuvant oxaliplatin, relapse <6 months after adjuvant fluoropyrimidine alone, and grade ≥2 neuropathy excluded FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab until progression → reintroduce FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab after progression vs mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab until progression → FOLFIRI + bevacizumab after progression Primary: Progression-free survival 2. Secondary: Progression-free survival 1, Second progression-free survival, Overall survival, Objective response rate, Early objective response rate, R0 resection rate, Time to failure of strategy, Safety The primary endpoint was met: median PFS2 19.2 vs 16.4 months with FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab (reintroduced after progression) versus mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab followed by FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88, p=0.0005). Median PFS1 12.0 vs 9.8 months (HR 0.74, 0.63-0.86); ORR 62% vs 50%; R0 resection 17% vs 12%. Median OS 27.4 vs 22.5 months (HR 0.82, 0.68-0.98). Grade 3-4 AEs 68% vs 46% (neutropenia 50% vs 21%, diarrhoea 17% vs 5%). Treatment-related deaths 11 vs 8; more early deaths within 6 months of randomisation with intensification (22 vs 13).

records.title: Cremolini FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab IPD meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · N/A · 2020
records.body: Adults with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer starting first-line therapy; individual-patient-data meta-analysis of five randomised trials comparing FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab with an oxaliplatin- or irinotecan-based doublet + bevacizumab FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab vs Doublet + bevacizumab (FOLFOX or FOLFIRI) Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, R0 resection rate, grade 3–4 adverse events FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab improved pooled OS over chemotherapy doublet + bevacizumab (28.9 vs 24.5 mo; HR 0.81) across 5 first-line randomised trials, with low between-trial heterogeneity; PFS was 12.2 vs 9.9 mo (HR 0.74), response 65% vs 54%, and R0 resection 16% vs 12%. No treatment interaction was detected by BRAF status or prior adjuvant therapy. Grade 3–4 neutropenia (46% vs 22%) and diarrhoea (18% vs 8%) increased

records.title: AVF2107g (Hurwitz)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Previously untreated metastatic colorectal carcinoma; prior adjuvant or radiosensitising fluoropyrimidine permitted if completed >12 months earlier; clinically significant cardiovascular disease, bleeding risk, full-dose anticoagulation and CNS metastases excluded IFL Q6W + bevacizumab Q2W vs IFL Q6W + placebo Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity or 96 weeks Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life Adding bevacizumab to IFL improved median OS 20.3 vs 15.6 months (HR 0.66; p<.001), median PFS 10.6 vs 6.2 months (HR 0.54; p<.001), response 44.8% vs 34.8% and response duration 10.4 vs 7.1 months. Grade 3–4 adverse events were more frequent with bevacizumab (84.9% vs 74.0%), including leukopenia and diarrhoea; exposure was longer with bevacizumab

records.title: NO16966 (bevacizumab)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer; no prior metastatic-disease systemic therapy, oxaliplatin or bevacizumab; clinically significant cardiovascular disease, full-dose anticoagulation, CNS metastases and major bleeding or wound risk excluded XELOX Q3W or FOLFOX-4 Q2W + bevacizumab vs the same chemotherapy + placebo; continue until progression or 48 weeks, then poststudy treatment permitted until progression Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: On-treatment progression-free survival, overall survival, response rate, duration of response, time to treatment failure, safety Median PFS 9.4 vs 8.0 months when bevacizumab was added to oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy (HR 0.83, 97.5% CI 0.72-0.95, p=0.0023), the trial's reported coprimary objective; overall survival was not significantly different at 21.3 vs 19.9 months (HR 0.89, 97.5% CI 0.76-1.03, p=0.077), and response rates were similar. Only 29% of bevacizumab and 47% of placebo recipients were treated until progression despite protocol allowance. The XELOX versus FOLFOX-4 noninferiority coprimary objective is reported in a separate publication and is not established by this one

records.title: CRYSTAL
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · III · 2009
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma with tumour EGFR expression; no prior metastatic-disease chemotherapy, irinotecan-based chemotherapy or anti-EGFR therapy; adjuvant treatment had to end >6 months earlier FOLFIRI Q2W + cetuximab weekly vs FOLFIRI Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, best overall response, safety, curative-intent surgery Cetuximab + FOLFIRI improved primary independent-review PFS in the 1,198 treated ITT population (8.9 vs 8.0 mo; HR 0.85), and updated OS at 46-mo follow-up (19.9 vs 18.6 mo; HR 0.88). In the retrospective KRAS wild-type subgroup (n=666), PFS was 9.9 vs 8.4 mo (HR 0.70), OS 23.5 vs 20.0 mo (HR 0.80), and response 57.3% vs 39.7%; formal interactions supported KRAS as predictive, while BRAF V600E was prognostic without evidence of interaction. Grade 3–4 events increased (79.3% vs 61.0%), notably diarrhoea and skin reactions; no cetuximab-related death was reported
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2009;360:1408-1417   J Clin Oncol 2011;29:2011-2019 updated KRAS/BRAF analysis (ascertainment 45% to 89%), supersedes the 2009 biomarker result 21502544

records.title: PRIME
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · III · 2010
records.body: Previously untreated metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; prior fluorouracil-based adjuvant therapy permitted if recurrence occurred ≥6 months later; prior oxaliplatin excluded Panitumumab + FOLFOX4 Q2W vs FOLFOX4 Q2W until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, objective response rate, safety, metastasectomy rate In wild-type KRAS disease, panitumumab + FOLFOX4 improved central-review PFS (9.6 vs 8.0 mo; HR 0.80), while interim OS did not reach statistical significance (23.9 vs 19.7 mo; HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.67–1.02). In mutant KRAS disease, PFS was worse (7.3 vs 8.8 mo; HR 1.29), supporting biomarker restriction. Wild-type KRAS response was 55% vs 48%

records.title: FIRE-3
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · III · 2014
records.body: Stage IV colorectal adenocarcinoma; after October 2008, KRAS exon 2 wild-type was required; no prior metastatic-disease chemotherapy, anti-EGFR therapy or bevacizumab; adjuvant therapy permitted if completed ≥6 months earlier FOLFIRI Q2W + cetuximab weekly vs FOLFIRI Q2W + bevacizumab Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity, complete response, curative resection or withdrawal Primary: Objective response rate. Secondary: Progression-free survival, overall survival, depth of remission, curative-intent liver resection, safety The primary ITT response comparison was negative: 62.0% with cetuximab vs 58.0% with bevacizumab (OR 1.18, 95% CI 0.85–1.64; p=.18). PFS was also similar (10.0 vs 10.3 months; HR 1.06, 0.88–1.26), while exploratory OS favoured cetuximab (28.7 vs 25.0 months; HR 0.77, 0.62–0.96; p=.017). Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 71% vs 64%; the extended-RAS analyses were retrospective and reported no interaction test

records.title: CALGB/SWOG 80405
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer with centrally confirmed KRAS codon 12/13 wild-type tumour; eligible for mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI; CNS metastases, grade ≥2 neuropathy and major recent bleeding, perforation or surgery excluded mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI selected before randomisation + cetuximab weekly vs the same chemotherapy + bevacizumab Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity, a treatment gap >28 days or discontinuation decision Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, 60-day mortality, arterial thrombotic events, safety Cetuximab did not improve OS over bevacizumab when added to first-line chemotherapy in KRAS wild-type disease (30.0 vs 29.0 mo; HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77–1.01); statistical significance was not reached. PFS (10.5 vs 10.6 mo; HR 0.95) and response (59.6% vs 55.2%) were also similar. This publication reports no primary-tumour sidedness analysis

records.title: PARADIGM
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · III · 2023
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable RAS wild-type colorectal adenocarcinoma; age 20–79 years and enrolled regardless of primary-tumour side; prior oxaliplatin excluded and fluoropyrimidine-only adjuvant therapy permitted if completed ≥24 weeks earlier Panitumumab + mFOLFOX6 Q2W vs bevacizumab + mFOLFOX6 Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, physician decision or curative-intent surgery Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, response rate, duration of response, R0 resection rate, safety Panitumumab improved OS over bevacizumab with mFOLFOX6 in left-sided RAS wild-type disease (37.9 vs 34.3 mo; HR 0.82), and in the overall full-analysis population (36.2 vs 31.3 mo; HR 0.84). Left-sided PFS was similar (13.1 vs 11.9 mo; HR 1.00), while response was higher (80.2% vs 68.6%). Crossing OS curves around 28 mo limit the proportional-hazards summary

records.title: VELOUR
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Second-line & antiangiogenic continuation · III · 2012
records.body: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma not amenable to curative treatment after progression on or after 1 oxaliplatin-containing regimen; prior bevacizumab permitted and prior irinotecan excluded FOLFIRI + aflibercept Q2W vs FOLFIRI + placebo Q2W until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, treatment-emergent adverse events Aflibercept + FOLFIRI improved median OS 13.50 vs 12.06 months (HR 0.817, 95.34% CI 0.713–0.937; p=.0032), independent-review PFS 6.90 vs 4.67 months (HR 0.758, 95% CI 0.661–0.869) and objective response 19.8% vs 11.1%. Grade 3–4 events increased (83.5% vs 62.5%), including hypertension, diarrhoea, neutropenia and proteinuria; adverse-event discontinuation was 26.6% vs 12.1%

records.title: TML (ML18147)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Second-line & antiangiogenic continuation · III · 2013
records.body: Metastatic colorectal cancer progressing within 3 months after first-line bevacizumab-containing chemotherapy; required ≥3 consecutive months of bevacizumab and first-line PFS ≥3 months Switch fluoropyrimidine-based irinotecan- or oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy + bevacizumab matched to Q2W or Q3W vs switched chemotherapy alone until progression, unacceptable toxicity or refusal Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, overall survival from first-line start, confirmed best overall response, safety Continuing bevacizumab with switched second-line chemotherapy improved median OS 11.2 vs 9.8 months (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69–0.94; p=.0062) and PFS 5.7 vs 4.1 months (HR 0.68, 0.59–0.78; p<.0001). Grade 3–5 neutropenia, diarrhoea, thrombosis, bleeding and gastrointestinal perforation were numerically higher; adverse-event discontinuation was 16% vs 9%, with 4 vs 3 treatment-related deaths

records.title: RAISE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Second-line & antiangiogenic continuation · III · 2015
records.body: Metastatic colorectal carcinoma progressing during or within 6 months after first-line bevacizumab, oxaliplatin and fluoropyrimidine; known KRAS exon 2 status; brain metastases, poorly controlled hypertension and major thrombotic or bleeding events excluded FOLFIRI + ramucirumab Q2W vs FOLFIRI + placebo Q2W until progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or decision to stop Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, treatment-emergent adverse events, patient-reported outcomes Ramucirumab + FOLFIRI improved median OS 13.3 vs 11.7 months (HR 0.844, 95% CI 0.730–0.976; p=.0219) and PFS 5.7 vs 4.5 months (HR 0.793, 0.697–0.903; p=.0005). Grade 3 or worse events increased (79% vs 62%), especially neutropenia and hypertension; adverse-event discontinuation was 11% vs 4%

records.title: CORRECT
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · III · 2013
records.body: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma progressing during or within 3 months after locally available standard fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and biologic therapy, or unable to continue because of toxicity; regorafenib-naive Regorafenib 160 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care until progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or physician decision Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, quality of life, safety At a planned interim analysis, regorafenib improved median OS 6.4 vs 5.0 months (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.64–0.94; p=.0052) and PFS 1.9 vs 1.7 months (HR 0.49, 0.42–0.58). Grade 3–4 treatment-related events occurred in 54% vs 14%, notably hand-foot skin reaction, fatigue, diarrhoea and hypertension; one fatal liver injury was compatible with regorafenib causation

records.title: CONCUR
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · III · 2015
records.body: Asian adults with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma after ≥2 prior lines including fluoropyrimidine plus oxaliplatin or irinotecan; progression during or within 3 months after the last standard treatment or within 6 months after adjuvant oxaliplatin Regorafenib 160 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care until progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or physician decision Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, quality of life, safety Regorafenib improved median OS 8.8 vs 6.3 months (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.40–0.77; p=.00016) and PFS 3.2 vs 1.7 months (HR 0.31, 0.22–0.44) in this Asian population; disease control was 51% vs 7%. Grade 3 or worse hand-foot skin reaction occurred in 16% vs 0 and hypertension in 11% vs 3%; treatment interruption or reduction was required in 71% vs 16%, with 2 investigator-attributed drug-related deaths on regorafenib

records.title: RECOURSE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · III · 2015
records.body: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma refractory to ≥2 prior standard regimens including fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and bevacizumab, plus anti-EGFR therapy for KRAS wild-type disease Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 of each 28-day cycle + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care until progression, severe toxicity, withdrawal, death or physician decision Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, safety Trifluridine/tipiracil improved median OS 7.1 vs 5.3 months (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.58–0.81; p<.001), 1-year OS 27% vs 18% and PFS 2.0 vs 1.7 months (HR 0.48, 0.41–0.57). Grade 3 or worse events occurred in 69% vs 52%, driven by neutropenia (38% vs 0), anaemia and thrombocytopenia; febrile neutropenia occurred in 4% and one treatment-related septic death occurred

records.title: SUNLIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · III · 2023
records.body: Unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma after ≤2 prior advanced-disease regimens including fluoropyrimidine, irinotecan, oxaliplatin and anti-VEGF therapy, plus anti-EGFR therapy for RAS wild-type disease Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 of each 28-day cycle + bevacizumab 5 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 vs trifluridine/tipiracil alone until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, quality of life, safety Adding bevacizumab to trifluridine/tipiracil improved median OS 10.8 vs 7.5 months (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.49–0.77; p<.001) and PFS 5.6 vs 2.4 months (HR 0.44, 0.36–0.54; p<.001); objective response remained low at 6.1% vs 1.2%. Grade 3 or worse events were similar (72.4% vs 69.5%), serious events were 24.8% vs 31.3%, and no treatment-related deaths occurred

records.title: FRESCO-2
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · III · 2023
records.body: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and anti-VEGF therapy, plus anti-EGFR therapy if RAS wild-type; progression on or intolerance to trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib; biomarker-appropriate immunotherapy or BRAF inhibition required where available Fruquintinib 5 mg once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care until progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or discontinuation Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life Fruquintinib improved median OS 7.4 vs 4.8 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.55–0.80; p<.0001) and PFS 3.7 vs 1.8 months (HR 0.32, 0.27–0.39; p<.0001); objective response was 2% vs 0. Grade 3 or worse events occurred in 63% vs 50%, notably hypertension, asthenia and hand-foot syndrome; one treatment-related death occurred in each arm

records.title: ReDOS
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · II · 2019
records.body: Advanced or metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma with no curative option after irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluoropyrimidine and VEGF inhibition, plus anti-EGFR therapy where eligible; regorafenib-naive; major cardiac disease, uncontrolled hypertension, thromboembolism and hepatitis B/C excluded Regorafenib dose escalation — 80 mg/day week 1, 120 mg week 2, 160 mg week 3 if no significant drug-related adverse events, then highest tolerated dose vs Regorafenib 160 mg/day from day 1; both arms days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle until progression, and both further randomised 1:1 to pre-emptive or reactive topical clobetasol Primary: Proportion completing 2 cycles and initiating cycle 3. Secondary: Progression-free survival, overall survival, time to progression, dose intensity, grade 3 hand-foot skin reaction or fatigue, quality of life, safety Regorafenib dose escalation enabled more evaluable patients to complete 2 cycles and start cycle 3 than starting at 160 mg (43% [23/54] vs 26% [16/62]). OS (9.8 vs 6.0 mo; HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.47–1.10) and PFS (2.8 vs 2.0 mo; HR 0.84, 0.57–1.24) did not reach statistical significance. Week-2 quality of life favoured escalation, with no difference from week 4. Grade 3–4 fatigue was 13% vs 18%, hand-foot skin reaction 15% vs 16%, abdominal pain 17% vs 6% and hypertension 7% vs 15%; 1 probable treatment-related death occurred with standard dose

records.title: BEACON CRC
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · BRAF V600E-mutated disease · III · 2019
records.body: BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer after 1-2 prior regimens Encorafenib + binimetinib + cetuximab vs encorafenib + cetuximab vs cetuximab + irinotecan or FOLFIRI in 28-day cycles until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, new anticancer therapy or death Primary: Overall survival, objective response rate. Secondary: Overall survival with doublet therapy, progression-free survival, duration of response, safety Triplet encorafenib + binimetinib + cetuximab improved OS vs control in all 665 randomised (9.0 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.52); confirmed central-review response in the first 331 randomised was 26% vs 2%. Encorafenib + cetuximab also improved OS (8.4 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.60) with 20% response. Grade ≥3 events were 58%, 50% and 61% with triplet, doublet and control; investigators attributed 1, 0 and 2 deaths to treatment. Established chemotherapy-free targeted therapy after 1–2 prior regimens

records.title: BREAKWATER
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · BRAF V600E-mutated disease · III · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated stage IV BRAF V600E-mutant, RAS wild-type colorectal adenocarcinoma; age ≥16 years where permitted; prior metastatic-disease therapy, BRAF or EGFR inhibition excluded; MSI-H/dMMR disease required ineligibility for checkpoint inhibition Encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 Q2W vs investigator-choice mFOLFOX6, FOLFOXIRI or CAPOX ± bevacizumab until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, death or loss to follow-up Primary: Objective response rate, progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, time to response, duration of response, second progression-free survival, safety Encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 improved confirmed central-review response in the initial 220-patient primary set (60.9% vs 40.0%), final PFS in all randomised patients (12.8 vs 7.1 mo; HR 0.53), and interim OS (30.3 vs 15.1 mo; HR 0.49). Grade 3–4 events occurred in 81.5% vs 66.8% and serious events in 46.1% vs 38.9%

records.title: MOUNTAINEER
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Other actionable drivers (HER2, KRAS G12C) · II · 2023
records.body: Chemotherapy-refractory HER2-positive, RAS wild-type unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and anti-VEGF therapy, plus checkpoint inhibition for dMMR/MSI-H disease; prior HER2-directed therapy and LVEF <50% excluded Tucatinib + trastuzumab Q3W in cohorts A+B vs tucatinib in cohort C, with trastuzumab add-on permitted; continue until progression, death or intolerable toxicity Primary: Confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: Duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety In the 84-patient A+B primary efficacy set, tucatinib + trastuzumab produced blinded-central-review confirmed response in 38.1% (95% CI 27.7–49.3), including 3 complete responses; median response duration was 12.4 months, PFS 8.2 months and OS 24.1 months. Serious treatment-emergent events occurred in 22% and tucatinib discontinuation for toxicity in 6%; no death was attributed to an adverse event. The single-arm primary analysis does not establish a comparative treatment effect

records.title: CodeBreaK 300
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Other actionable drivers (HER2, KRAS G12C) · III · 2023
records.body: KRAS G12C-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer after ≥1 metastatic-disease line containing fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin and irinotecan unless intolerance made standard refractory therapy appropriate; centrally confirmed mutation; prior KRAS G12C inhibitor excluded Sotorasib 960 mg once daily + panitumumab 6 mg/kg Q2W vs sotorasib 240 mg once daily + panitumumab Q2W vs trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib; continue until central-review progression, unacceptable toxicity, new therapy, withdrawal or death Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, safety, quality of life Sotorasib 960 mg + panitumumab improved central-review PFS vs standard care (5.6 vs 2.0 mo; HR 0.48). The 240-mg comparison did not meet its prespecified criterion (3.9 vs 2.0 mo; HR 0.59). OS was immature. Grade 3 or worse acneiform dermatitis occurred in 11.3% with 960 mg; standard care caused grade 3 or worse neutropenia in 23.5%

records.title: KEYNOTE-177
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · MSI-H / dMMR disease — immunotherapy · III · 2020
records.body: Previously untreated stage IV MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer; prior adjuvant chemotherapy permitted if completed ≥6 months earlier; active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment and immunodeficiency excluded Pembrolizumab Q3W for up to 35 treatments vs mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI Q2W ± bevacizumab or cetuximab; crossover to pembrolizumab for up to 35 treatments permitted after central-review progression Primary: Progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, duration of response, safety Pembrolizumab improved final PFS (16.5 vs 8.2 mo; HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.45–0.80), with crossed curves and a violated proportional-hazards assumption; 24-mo restricted mean PFS was 13.7 vs 10.8 mo. At final follow-up, OS superiority was not established (HR 0.74, 0.53–1.03) amid substantial crossover. Response was 45.1% vs 33.1%; grade 3 or worse treatment-related events were 22% vs 66%
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;383:2207-2218   Lancet Oncol 2022;23:659-670 final OS analysis 35427471

records.title: CheckMate 8HW (first-line vs chemotherapy)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · MSI-H / dMMR disease — immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: First-line unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer with MSI-H/dMMR by local testing and no prior metastatic-disease systemic therapy; immunotherapy-naive; primary efficacy population required central MSI-H/dMMR confirmation (255/303 randomised) Nivolumab 240 mg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 480 mg Q4W for up to 2 years vs investigator-choice mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI ± bevacizumab or cetuximab until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, overall survival, safety First-line nivolumab + ipilimumab improved central-review PFS vs chemotherapy in centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR disease (n=255): 24-mo PFS 72% vs 14%; median not reached vs 5.9 mo. In all 303 randomised on local testing, 24-mo PFS was 63% vs 15%. Grade 3–4 treatment-related events were fewer (23% vs 48%), with 2 vs 0 treatment-related deaths. This interim analysis establishes dual immunotherapy as a first-line standard; OS remains unreported
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;391:2014-2026  39602630 Lancet 2025;405:383-395 dual primary endpoint 2 (nivolumab + ipilimumab vs nivolumab, all lines) and longer-follow-up first-line update 39874977

records.title: COMMIT (NRG-GI004/SWOG-S1610)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · MSI-H / dMMR disease — immunotherapy · III · 2026
records.body: First-line dMMR/MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab + atezolizumab vs atezolizumab monotherapy Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, overall survival, safety Adding mFOLFOX6/bevacizumab to atezolizumab markedly prolonged PFS vs atezolizumab monotherapy (median 30.0 vs 4.3 months, HR 0.439, 95% CI 0.23-0.84, p=0.0103) with higher response (ORR 80.6% vs 46%) and 12-month DCR (62.9% vs 32.4%); interim analysis of the two-arm comparison (atezo n=41 vs FFX/bev+atezo n=41 after the FFX/bev-alone arm was closed). Supports first-line chemo-immunotherapy over single-agent PD-L1 blockade in dMMR/MSI-H mCRC.

records.title: CheckMate 8HW (nivolumab + ipilimumab vs nivolumab)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · MSI-H / dMMR disease — immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: Immunotherapy-naive unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer with MSI-H/dMMR by local testing; any prior metastatic-treatment line permitted; primary efficacy population required central confirmation (582/707 randomised) Nivolumab 240 mg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 480 mg Q4W vs nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W ×6 → nivolumab 480 mg Q4W; maximum 2 years in both arms Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, overall survival, safety Nivolumab + ipilimumab improved central-review PFS vs nivolumab in 582 centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR patients across treatment lines (median not reached vs 39.3 mo; HR 0.62); response was 71% vs 58%. In all 707 randomised on local testing, median PFS was 54.1 vs 18.4 mo (HR 0.64). Grade 3–4 treatment-related events were 22% vs 14%, discontinuation for treatment-related toxicity 14% vs 6%, and treatment-related deaths 2 vs 1. First-line-only efficacy remains masked; OS is also masked

records.title: ORCHESTRA
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Local therapy in metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Adults with multiorgan metastatic colorectal cancer before first-line palliative therapy, with metastases in at least two organs and substantial extrahepatic, hepatic, nodal, adrenal or serosal burden; at least 80% debulking judged feasible; randomised only after response or stable disease on induction CAPOX or FOLFOX with or without bevacizumab Continue CAPOX or FOLFOX with or without bevacizumab vs debulk at least 80% of metastases by surgery, radiotherapy or ablation then resume chemotherapy; complete at least 8 CAPOX or 12 FOLFOX cycles from inclusion Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, safety, treatment burden Tumour debulking added to chemotherapy did not improve OS (30.0 vs 27.5 months; adjusted HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.70–1.10; p=.26) or PFS (10.5 vs 10.4 months; adjusted HR 0.83, 0.67–1.02; p=.08). Grade 2–5 serious adverse events increased to 53% vs 39% (risk difference 14.62 percentage points, 95% CI 4.21–25.03), including 8 vs 0 grade 5 events; 4 deaths were attributed to local treatment. Debulking should not be routine in multiorgan metastatic disease

records.title: MAGIC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2006
records.body: Resectable gastric, GEJ, or lower-esophageal adenocarcinoma (stage II+) Perioperative ECF (3 pre + 3 post) + surgery vs surgery alone Overall survival Perioperative ECF improved OS (5-yr 36% vs 23%, HR 0.75) and PFS; established perioperative chemotherapy as a Western standard for resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma.

records.title: FNCLCC/FFCD 9703 (ACCORD-07)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2011
records.body: Resectable adenocarcinoma of stomach, GEJ, or lower esophagus (~75% GEJ/esophageal) Perioperative cisplatin + fluorouracil + surgery vs surgery alone Overall survival Perioperative CF improved OS (5-yr 38% vs 24%, HR 0.69) and curative-resection rate; corroborated MAGIC, with benefit concentrated in GEJ/distal-esophageal tumors.

records.title: CRITICS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2018
records.body: Resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after neoadjuvant chemo + D1+ resection Postop chemotherapy (ECC) vs postop chemoradiotherapy (45 Gy + cisplatin/capecitabine) Overall survival After adequate preoperative chemo and surgery, adding postoperative radiotherapy did not improve OS (median 43 vs 37 months, HR 1.01); postop chemoradiation is not superior to chemotherapy.

records.title: FLOT4-AIO
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2019
records.body: Resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2+ or node-positive, ECOG 0-1 Perioperative FLOT — docetaxel 50 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² + 5-FU 2600 mg/m² (24-h infusion) day 1, Q2W, 4 pre + 4 post-op cycles vs ECF/ECX — epirubicin 50 mg/m² + cisplatin 60 mg/m² + 5-FU 200 mg/m²/day infusion (or capecitabine 1250 mg/m² orally, days 1–21), Q3W, 3 pre + 3 post Overall survival FLOT improved median OS (50 vs 35 months, HR 0.77) with higher R0 and pCR rates; established FLOT as the preferred perioperative regimen for fit patients.

records.title: PRODIGY
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Resectable locally advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2-3N+ or cT4Nany (Korea) Neoadjuvant DOS — docetaxel 50 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² IV day 1 + S-1 40 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14, Q3W ×3 → D2 surgery → adjuvant S-1 (40–60 mg twice daily days 1–28, Q6W ×8) vs D2 surgery → adjuvant S-1 alone Progression-free survival Neoadjuvant DOS improved 3-yr PFS (66.3% vs 60.2%, HR 0.70) with downstaging; first positive Asian RCT supporting a neoadjuvant approach in D2-resected gastric cancer.

records.title: RESOLVE
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Locally advanced cT4aN+ or cT4b gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, D2 gastrectomy (China) Perioperative SOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + S-1 40–60 mg twice daily days 1–14, Q3W; 3 pre + 5 post-op → 3 cycles S-1 monotherapy) vs adjuvant SOX (8 post-op cycles) vs adjuvant CapOx (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14, Q3W ×8) Disease-free survival Perioperative SOX improved 3-yr DFS over adjuvant CapOx (59.4% vs 51.1%, HR 0.77); adjuvant SOX was non-inferior to CapOx. Supported perioperative/S-1-based chemo in Asian D2 disease.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1081-1092   Lancet Oncol 2025;26:312-319 5-yr overall survival 39952264

records.title: RESONANCE
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Stage II/III resectable gastric cancer (China; 19 centres; mITT 756) Perioperative SOX (S-1 + oxaliplatin) vs adjuvant SOX (1:1) Disease-free survival 3-year DFS 61.7% (perioperative) vs 53.8% (adjuvant) (log-rank p=0.019); R0 resection 94.9% vs 83.7% (p<0.0001) without increased surgical morbidity. Supports perioperative SOX over adjuvant-only SOX in resectable gastric cancer.

records.title: TOPGEAR (AGITG)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma (cT3-4 and/or node-positive) Preop chemoradiotherapy (45 Gy + FU) + perioperative chemo (ECF/FLOT) vs perioperative chemo alone Overall survival Adding preoperative chemoradiotherapy raised pCR (16.8% vs 8.0%) but did not improve OS (median 46 vs 49 months, HR 1.05); perioperative chemotherapy alone remains standard.

records.title: INT-0116 (SWOG 9008)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2001
records.body: Resected (mostly <D2) stage IB-IV(M0) gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Postop chemoradiotherapy (45 Gy + bolus FU/leucovorin) vs surgery alone Overall survival Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved median OS (36 vs 27 months; 3-yr 50% vs 41%; HR for death 1.35 favoring treatment); defined the 'Macdonald regimen' after limited lymphadenectomy.

records.title: ACTS-GC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2007
records.body: Stage II-III gastric adenocarcinoma after D2 gastrectomy (Japan) Adjuvant S-1 80 mg/m²/day orally (4 weeks on / 2 weeks off, 6-week cycles) for 1 year vs surgery alone Overall survival Adjuvant S-1 improved OS (3-yr 80.1% vs 70.1%, HR 0.68); established 1 year of S-1 as a standard after D2 resection in Asian patients.

records.title: CLASSIC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2012
records.body: Stage II-IIIB gastric adenocarcinoma after curative D2 gastrectomy (Asia) Adjuvant CAPOX — capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, Q3W ×8 (6 months) vs surgery alone Disease-free survival Adjuvant CAPOX improved 3-yr DFS (74% vs 59%, HR 0.56); 5-yr follow-up confirmed an OS benefit (78% vs 69%, HR 0.66), establishing CAPOX after D2 resection.

records.title: JACCRO GC-07 (START-2)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2019
records.body: pStage III gastric adenocarcinoma after R0 D2 gastrectomy (Japan) Adjuvant S-1 + docetaxel — S-1 40–60 mg twice daily days 1–14 (Q3W) + docetaxel 40 mg/m² day 1 in courses 2–7, then S-1 days 1–28 (Q6W) to 1 year vs S-1 alone (days 1–28, Q6W, to 1 year) Relapse-free survival Adding docetaxel improved 3-yr RFS (66% vs 50%, HR 0.63), with the final report confirming a 5-yr OS benefit; established S-1 + docetaxel as adjuvant standard for stage III in Asia.

records.title: ARTIST 2
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Node-positive stage II-III gastric adenocarcinoma after curative D2 gastrectomy (Korea) Adjuvant S-1 (40–60 mg twice daily, 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off, ×1 year) vs SOX (S-1 40–60 mg twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, Q3W ×8) vs SOX + chemoradiotherapy 45 Gy (SOXRT) Disease-free survival SOX and SOXRT improved DFS over S-1 monotherapy (S-1 vs SOX HR 0.69), but adding radiotherapy gave no benefit over SOX; doublet adjuvant chemotherapy, not chemoradiation, is preferred after D2.

records.title: KEYNOTE-585
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable, untreated locally advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Perioperative pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (cisplatin-FU or FLOT) vs placebo + chemotherapy Event-free survival, overall survival, pathological complete response Pembrolizumab raised pCR (12.9% vs 2.0%) but did not significantly improve EFS (median 45.8 vs 25.7 months, HR 0.81; threshold not met) or OS; perioperative anti-PD-1 not established by this trial.

records.title: MATTERHORN
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable stage II-IVA gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Perioperative durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W + FLOT (4 cycles: 2 neoadjuvant + 2 adjuvant) → durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W ×10 cycles vs placebo + FLOT Event-free survival Durvalumab + FLOT improved EFS (2-yr 67.4% vs 58.5%; HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.86; P<0.001 against a 2.39% boundary) and pCR (19.2% vs 7.2%; relative risk 2.69, 95% CI 1.86-3.90). At this interim analysis overall survival did not meet its allocated 0.01% alpha (2-yr 75.7% vs 70.4%; P=0.03 against a P<0.0001 threshold), and proportional hazards did not hold: the piecewise hazard ratio for death was 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.39) over months 0-12 and 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.90) from month 12 onward, a late separation. First positive perioperative immunotherapy trial on EFS; now FDA-approved for resectable gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, with no PD-L1 selection requirement and no stage restriction in the indication. The final overall survival analysis is pending.

records.title: DRAGON IV (CAP 05)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Locally advanced resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma (cT3-4 and/or N+) Perioperative camrelizumab + low-dose rivoceranib + SOX (SOXRC) vs SOX Pathologic complete response and event-free survival Adding camrelizumab + rivoceranib to perioperative SOX raised pCR (18.3% vs 5.0%, OR 4.5); first phase 3 showing a PD-1/VEGFR combination improves pathologic response in resectable gastric cancer (survival data pending).

records.title: ASTRUM-006
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: PD-L1 CPS ≥5, resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma (China/Thailand) Neoadjuvant serplulimab + SOX → adjuvant serplulimab vs neoadjuvant placebo + SOX → adjuvant SOX Event-free survival (investigator-assessed; tested in CPS ≥10 then ITT CPS ≥5) Perioperative serplulimab + SOX improved EFS in PD-L1-positive resectable gastric/GEJ cancer: ITT (CPS ≥5) median EFS not reached vs 35.9 months (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56–0.94; p=0.015), and CPS ≥10 not reached vs 42.0 months (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47–0.90; p=0.0082), with a chemo-sparing adjuvant phase and fewer grade ≥3 TRAEs (47% vs 59%). OS still immature.

records.title: CROSS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2012
records.body: Resectable esophageal/GEJ cancer (75% adenocarcinoma, 23% SCC), cT1N1 or cT2-3N0-1 Neoadjuvant carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 50 mg/m² weekly ×5 with concurrent radiotherapy 41.4 Gy (23 fractions) → surgery vs surgery alone Overall survival Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved median OS (49 vs 24 months, HR 0.66) with pCR in 29% (49% SCC, 23% adeno); established trimodality therapy as a standard.

records.title: Neo-AEGIS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2023
records.body: Locally advanced esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma (cT2-3 N0-3) Perioperative chemotherapy — modified MAGIC (epirubicin 50 mg/m² + cisplatin 60 or oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² + 5-FU 200 mg/m²/day infusion or capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily, 3 pre + 3 post) or FLOT vs CROSS trimodality (carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 50 mg/m² weekly ×5 + 41.4 Gy → surgery) Overall survival Despite greater local response with CROSS, 3-yr OS was similar (55% chemo vs 57% CROSS, HR 1.03); perioperative chemotherapy and trimodality therapy yielded comparable survival.

records.title: ESOPEC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable esophageal adenocarcinoma, cT1N+ or cT2-4a Nany M0 Perioperative FLOT — 5-FU 2600 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + docetaxel 50 mg/m² day 1, Q2W (4 pre + 4 post) vs preoperative CROSS chemoradiotherapy — carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 50 mg/m² weekly ×5 + 41.4 Gy (23 fractions) Overall survival Perioperative FLOT improved median OS over CROSS (66.0 vs 37.0 months, HR 0.70); positions FLOT as preferred for resectable esophageal adenocarcinoma.

records.title: CheckMate 577
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Adjuvant immunotherapy — resected esophageal & GEJ cancer · III · 2021
records.body: Resected (R0) stage II-III esophageal/GEJ cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemoRT Adjuvant nivolumab (1 year) vs placebo Disease-free survival Adjuvant nivolumab doubled median DFS (22.4 vs 11.0 months, HR 0.69) across adeno and SCC; established adjuvant immunotherapy for non-pCR patients after trimodality therapy.

records.title: JCOG9907
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Resectable clinical stage II-III thoracic esophageal SCC (non-T4) (Japan) Neoadjuvant cisplatin + fluorouracil (2 cycles) + surgery vs surgery + adjuvant CF Overall survival Neoadjuvant CF improved 5-yr OS over postoperative CF (55% vs 43%, HR 0.73); established preoperative CF as the Japanese standard for resectable esophageal SCC.

records.title: NEOCRTEC5010
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Resectable locally advanced thoracic esophageal SCC, cT1-4N1 or cT4N0 (China) Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (vinorelbine/cisplatin + 40 Gy) + surgery vs surgery alone Overall survival Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved median OS (100.1 vs 66.5 months, HR 0.71) with pCR 43.2% and higher R0 rate; key Asian evidence for trimodality therapy in esophageal SCC.

records.title: JCOG1109 (NExT)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable locally advanced thoracic esophageal SCC, cStage IB-III (Japan) Neoadjuvant then esophagectomy — NeoCF (5-FU 800 mg/m²/day days 1–5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1, Q3W ×2) vs DCF (docetaxel 70 mg/m² + cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 1 + 5-FU 750 mg/m²/day days 1–5, Q3W ×3) vs CF-chemoradiotherapy (5-FU 1000 mg/m²/day days 1–4 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1, Q4W ×2 + concurrent 41.4 Gy, 23 fractions) Overall survival Neoadjuvant DCF improved OS over CF (3-yr 72.1% vs 62.6%, HR 0.68); CF-RT did not (HR 0.84). Established triplet DCF as a neoadjuvant standard for esophageal SCC.

records.title: ESCORT-NEO/NCCES01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable locally advanced thoracic esophageal SCC (T1b-3N1-3 or T3N0) Neoadjuvant camrelizumab + nab-paclitaxel/cisplatin or + paclitaxel/cisplatin vs chemotherapy alone Pathological complete response Adding camrelizumab to chemotherapy raised pCR (28.0% with nab-paclitaxel/cisplatin vs 4.7% chemo alone); early evidence for neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in esophageal SCC.

records.title: RTOG 85-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · III · 1999
records.body: Localized esophageal cancer (T1-3 N0-1 M0), ~85% SCC, non-surgical Chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy + cisplatin/FU) vs radiotherapy alone (64 Gy) Overall survival Concurrent chemoradiotherapy markedly improved survival (5-yr 26% vs 0%; median ~14 vs 9 months); established definitive chemoradiotherapy as standard for non-surgical esophageal cancer.

records.title: INT 0123 (RTOG 94-05)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · III · 2002
records.body: Localized esophageal cancer (85% SCC) treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy High-dose RT (64.8 Gy) vs standard-dose RT (50.4 Gy), both + cisplatin/FU Overall survival Dose escalation did not improve median OS (13.0 vs 18.1 months) or local control and increased treatment-related deaths; established 50.4 Gy as the standard radiotherapy dose.

records.title: PRODIGE5/ACCORD17
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · II/III · 2014
records.body: Localised stage I–IVA esophageal carcinoma (adenocarcinoma, squamous-cell, or adenosquamous), ECOG 0–2, selected for definitive (non-surgical) chemoradiotherapy; 24 centres in France; NCT00861094 Definitive chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks) + either FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² + bolus FU 400 mg/m² + infusional FU 1600 mg/m² over 46 h; 6 cycles, 3 concomitant with RT) or fluorouracil + cisplatin (FU 1000 mg/m²/day days 1–4 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1; 4 cycles, 2 concomitant with RT), 1:1 Progression-free survival (intention-to-treat) FOLFOX-CRT was not superior to FU/cisplatin-CRT for median PFS (9.7 vs 9.4 months, HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.70–1.24, p=0.64) at median 25.3 months' follow-up. Fewer toxic deaths with FOLFOX (1 vs 6, p=0.066); different toxicity profile (more neuropathy/transaminitis with FOLFOX; more mucositis, alopecia, creatinine rises with FU/cisplatin). FOLFOX may be a more convenient definitive-CRT backbone.

records.title: Hulscher (Dutch THTC)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2002
records.body: Resectable mid/distal esophageal or cardia adenocarcinoma Transhiatal esophagectomy vs transthoracic resection with extended en-bloc lymphadenectomy Overall survival No significant OS difference (deaths 70% vs 60% at median 4.7 yr, p=0.12); transthoracic en-bloc resection caused more pulmonary morbidity, with a nonsignificant survival trend favoring it.

records.title: JCOG9501
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · III · 2008
records.body: Curable T2b-T4 (M0) gastric adenocarcinoma at D2-capable centers (Japan) D2 lymphadenectomy alone vs D2 + prophylactic para-aortic nodal dissection (PAND) Overall survival Adding para-aortic nodal dissection to D2 did not improve survival, the trial's primary endpoint: five-year overall survival was 70.3% with D2 plus PAND and 69.2% with D2 alone (hazard ratio for death 1.03, 95% CI 0.77-1.37; two-sided P=0.85). Overall surgery-related complications were 28.1% with PAND versus 20.9% (P=0.07), which the paper does not call an increase; the excess fell in minor complications, 20.0% versus 9.1% (P<0.001, nominal).
