Hospital mortality was 0.8% in both arms. Established D2 without PAND as the standard extent of dissection.

records.title: Dutch D1D2 (Songun)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2010
records.body: Resectable gastric adenocarcinoma treated with curative intent (Netherlands) D1 vs D2 lymphadenectomy (15-year follow-up) Overall survival D2 lowered locoregional recurrence and gastric-cancer-related death (37% vs 48%) with a nonsignificant 15-yr OS gain (29% vs 21%, p=0.34); higher operative mortality made spleen/pancreas-preserving D2 the standard.

records.title: TIME
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2012
records.body: Resectable intrathoracic esophageal/GEJ cancer eligible for esophagectomy Minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) vs open esophagectomy Pulmonary infection within 2 weeks MIE markedly reduced in-hospital pulmonary infection (9% vs 29%) and 2-week infection, with shorter stay and equivalent oncologic adequacy; validated minimally invasive esophagectomy.

records.title: CLASS-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2019
records.body: Clinical T2-4a (N0-3, M0) locally advanced gastric cancer, distal gastrectomy (China) Laparoscopic vs open distal gastrectomy with D2 dissection 3-year disease-free survival Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy was non-inferior for 3-yr DFS (76.5% vs 77.8%); 5-yr OS similar (73% vs 76%), supporting laparoscopy for advanced disease at expert centers.

records.title: KLASS-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2019
records.body: Clinical stage I gastric cancer suitable for distal gastrectomy (Korea) Laparoscopic vs open distal gastrectomy Overall survival (long-term) Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy was non-inferior for 5-yr OS (94.2% vs 93.3%) with lower wound complications; established laparoscopy as standard for early gastric cancer.

records.title: KLASS-02
records.subtitle: Localized Gastric & Esoph · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2020
records.body: Clinical stage II-III locally advanced gastric cancer, distal gastrectomy (Korea) Laparoscopic vs open distal gastrectomy with D2 dissection 3-year relapse-free survival Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy was non-inferior for 3-yr RFS (80.3% vs 81.3%, HR 1.04) with fewer early complications; corroborated CLASS-01 for advanced disease.

records.title: V325
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2006
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Docetaxel + cisplatin + fluorouracil (DCF) vs cisplatin + fluorouracil (CF) Time to progression DCF prolonged time to progression, the primary endpoint: median 5.6 months (95% CI 4.9-5.9) versus 3.7 months (3.4-4.5) with CF, hazard ratio 1.47 (95% CI 1.19-1.82), log-rank P<.001 - this trial expresses hazard ratios as CF relative to DCF, so a value above 1 favours DCF. Median overall survival was 9.2 versus 8.6 months (HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.0-1.6, P=.02) with 2-year survival 18% versus 9%; OS was powered separately with no testing hierarchy, so that p-value is nominal. The added toxicity was specifically neutropenic - grade 3/4 neutropenia 82% versus 57% and complicated neutropenia 29% versus 12% - while grade 3/4 anaemia (18% versus 26%) and thrombocytopenia (8% versus 13%) were lower with DCF; death within 30 days occurred in 10% versus 8%, mainly from infection. Established a docetaxel triplet as an active first-line option.

records.title: REAL-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2008
records.body: Untreated advanced oesophagogastric adenocarcinoma (stomach, GEJ, or oesophagus) Capecitabine vs fluorouracil and oxaliplatin vs cisplatin within epirubicin triplets (2x2) Overall survival (non-inferiority) Capecitabine and oxaliplatin were each non-inferior to fluorouracil and cisplatin; EOX gave the longest OS (11.2 vs 9.9 months with ECF, HR 0.80), validating capecitabine/oxaliplatin backbones.

records.title: GASTFOX (PRODIGE 51)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated advanced HER2-negative gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Docetaxel 50 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + folinic acid 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² (46-h infusion) Q2W (TFOX, a modified FLOT) vs FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + folinic acid 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion) Q2W Progression-free survival Adding docetaxel (TFOX) improved PFS (7.6 vs 6.0 months, HR 0.74) and OS (15.1 vs 12.7 months, HR 0.82) over FOLFOX, with more neuropathy and neutropenia; supports a docetaxel triplet for fit patients.

records.title: GO2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic gastro-oesophageal cancer (oesophagus, GOJ or stomach; adenocarcinoma or squamous) judged by the treating oncologist unsuitable for full-dose combination chemotherapy on grounds of advanced age and/or frailty; no chronological age, performance-status or frailty threshold specified, but patients had to be judged fit for every arm of their randomisation Level A: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily days 1–21 (21-day cycle) vs Level B (80% of Level A doses) vs Level C (60% of Level A doses) vs best supportive care alone (randomised against Level C only) Primary: progression-free survival (CHEMO-INTENSITY randomisation), overall survival (CHEMO-BSC randomisation). Secondary: Overall Treatment Utility, overall survival, response rate, quality of life, fatigue, symptoms, quality-adjusted survival, safety In older or frail patients unsuitable for full-dose chemotherapy, oxaliplatin-capecitabine at 60% dose did not compromise disease control: progression-free survival was non-inferior for both reduced levels (B vs A HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.89-1.32; C vs A HR 1.10, 0.90-1.33) against a permissive boundary of HR 1.34, a 34-day loss from a predicted 134-day median. The lowest dose was gentler - grade 3 or worse non-haematological toxicity 23% against 38% at full dose, 58% against 32% completing 3 cycles unmodified - and Overall Treatment Utility differences were not statistically significant. Geriatric assessment found no group benefiting from higher dose; the nominal interaction (p=.01) ran opposite to expectation, fitter patients gaining more from reduction. In the exploratory 45-patient randomisation, survival with chemotherapy versus best supportive care was 6.1 against 3.0 months (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.35-1.48, p=.34). No treatment-related deaths or serious-adverse-event rates are reported.

records.title: ToGA
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · HER2-positive disease · III · 2010
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W (to progression) + cisplatin–fluoropyrimidine (capecitabine or 5-FU), 6 cycles vs cisplatin–fluoropyrimidine alone, 6 cycles Overall survival Trastuzumab improved median OS (13.8 vs 11.1 months, HR 0.74); established HER2 testing and first-line trastuzumab as standard for HER2-positive disease.

records.title: KEYNOTE-811
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · HER2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) + trastuzumab + fluoropyrimidine–platinum vs placebo + trastuzumab + fluoropyrimidine–platinum Progression-free and overall survival Adding pembrolizumab improved PFS at the prespecified second interim analysis (10.0 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.60-0.87; P=0.0002), meeting the superiority boundary. At the third interim analysis, OS was not significantly improved (20.0 vs 16.8 months, HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.70-1.01), and follow-up continued to the prespecified final OS analysis.

records.title: DESTINY-Gastric01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · HER2-positive disease · II · 2020
records.body: HER2-positive advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, ≥2 prior lines incl trastuzumab (Japan/South Korea) Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV Q3W (to progression) vs physician's-choice chemotherapy — irinotecan 150 mg/m² Q2W or paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 Q4W Objective response rate T-DXd improved ORR (51% vs 14%) and OS (12.5 vs 8.4 months, HR 0.59); first antibody-drug conjugate to show benefit in HER2-positive gastric cancer.

records.title: DESTINY-Gastric04
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · HER2-positive disease · III · 2025
records.body: HER2-positive advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma progressing after a trastuzumab-containing regimen Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV days 1 & 15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 (28-day cycle) Overall survival T-DXd improved median OS (14.7 vs 11.4 months, HR 0.70) over ramucirumab/paclitaxel; established T-DXd as the second-line standard for HER2-positive disease.

records.title: HERIZON-GEA-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · HER2-positive disease · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated HER2-positive locally advanced/metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma Zanidatamab (1800 mg if <70 kg, 2400 mg if ≥70 kg) IV Q3W + tislelizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + fluoropyrimidine–platinum (CAPOX or FP), or zanidatamab + fluoropyrimidine–platinum vs trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W + fluoropyrimidine–platinum Progression-free and overall survival Zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemotherapy improved OS (26.4 vs 19.2 months, HR 0.72) and PFS (HR 0.64) over trastuzumab + chemotherapy; first regimen to beat trastuzumab first-line in HER2-positive disease.

records.title: CSCO HER2 Guideline (2025 Ed.)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · HER2-positive disease · N/A · 2026
records.body: Gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma being assessed for HER2-targeted therapy Guideline framework, not a trial arm comparison — see Key Findings n/a (classification/detection standard, not an efficacy endpoint) CSCO (China) expert-panel guideline redefines HER2 stratification for gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma into four tiers (high/intermediate/low/absent), replacing the binary IHC3+/2+(FISH+) positive/negative scheme used to enrol ToGA/KEYNOTE-811/DESTINY-Gastric04/HERIZON-GEA-01; integrates IHC, ISH, and liquid-biopsy detection standards to guide selection among HER2 antibodies, ADCs, TKIs, and bispecifics.

records.title: CheckMate 649
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated HER2-negative advanced gastric, GEJ, or oesophageal adenocarcinoma (PD-L1 CPS ≥5 primary) Nivolumab 360 mg IV Q3W (or 240 mg Q2W) + CAPOX (Q3W) or FOLFOX (Q2W); nivolumab to a maximum of 2 years vs CAPOX or FOLFOX alone Overall and progression-free survival (CPS ≥5) Nivolumab + chemotherapy improved OS in CPS ≥5 (14.4 vs 11.1 months, HR 0.71) and across all randomized patients (13.8 vs 11.6 months, HR 0.80); established first-line chemo-immunotherapy.

records.title: KEYNOTE-859
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated HER2-negative advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) + fluoropyrimidine–platinum (FP or CAPOX) vs placebo + fluoropyrimidine–platinum Overall survival Pembrolizumab improved OS (12.9 vs 11.5 months, HR 0.78), with larger benefit at higher PD-L1 CPS; broadened first-line chemo-immunotherapy regardless of CPS.

records.title: RATIONALE-305
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2024
records.body: HER2-negative advanced/metastatic gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, first-line, regardless of PD-L1 (Asia, Europe, North America) Tislelizumab + chemotherapy (oxaliplatin/capecitabine or cisplatin/5-FU) vs placebo + chemotherapy (1:1) Overall survival (PD-L1 TAP >=5% and all-randomised) PD-L1 TAP >=5%: median OS 17.2 vs 12.6 months (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.94, p=0.006). All randomised: 15.0 vs 12.9 months (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.70-0.92, p=0.001). Grade >=3 TRAEs 54% vs 50%.

records.title: SPOTLIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Zolbetuximab + mFOLFOX6 vs placebo + mFOLFOX6 Progression-free survival Zolbetuximab prolonged PFS (10.6 vs 8.7 months, HR 0.75) and OS (18.2 vs 15.5 months, HR 0.75); first CLDN18.2-targeted therapy to benefit first-line.

records.title: GLOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Zolbetuximab + CAPOX vs placebo + CAPOX Progression-free survival Zolbetuximab prolonged PFS (8.2 vs 6.8 months, HR 0.69) and OS (14.4 vs 12.2 months, HR 0.77); confirmed SPOTLIGHT with a CAPOX backbone.

records.title: REGARD
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2014
records.body: Previously treated advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV Q2W (to progression) + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care Overall survival Ramucirumab monotherapy improved OS (5.2 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.78); first anti-angiogenic to show single-agent benefit in gastric cancer.

records.title: RAINBOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2014
records.body: Previously treated advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV days 1 & 15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 (28-day cycle) vs placebo + paclitaxel (same schedule) Overall survival Ramucirumab + paclitaxel improved OS (9.6 vs 7.4 months, HR 0.81) and PFS; established the second-line standard of care.

records.title: TAGS
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2018
records.body: Heavily pretreated metastatic gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma (≥2 prior lines) Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 of each 28-day cycle + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care Overall survival Trifluridine/tipiracil improved OS (5.7 vs 3.6 months, HR 0.69); established an oral option in the third-line and beyond.

records.title: ATTRACTION-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced gastric/GEJ cancer refractory to ≥2 prior regimens (Asian) Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W (to progression or toxicity) vs placebo Overall survival Nivolumab improved OS (5.3 vs 4.1 months, HR 0.63; 12-month OS 26.2% vs 10.9%); first checkpoint inhibitor benefit in late-line gastric cancer.

records.title: KEYNOTE-590
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic oesophageal (squamous or adeno) or GEJ carcinoma Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (cisplatin/fluorouracil) vs chemotherapy Overall and progression-free survival Pembrolizumab improved OS (12.4 vs 9.8 months, HR 0.73) and PFS, with greatest benefit in squamous CPS ≥10; established first-line chemo-immunotherapy for oesophageal cancer.

records.title: CheckMate 648
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma Nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W + cisplatin–fluorouracil (4-week cycle), or nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q6W; immunotherapy to a maximum of 2 years vs cisplatin–fluorouracil Overall and progression-free survival Both nivolumab + chemo (OS 13.2 vs 10.7 months, HR 0.74) and nivolumab + ipilimumab (12.7 vs 10.7 months, HR 0.78) improved OS over chemotherapy; two new first-line options, including a chemo-free regimen.

records.title: ESCORT-1st
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (China) Camrelizumab + paclitaxel/cisplatin vs placebo + chemotherapy Overall and progression-free survival Camrelizumab improved OS (15.3 vs 12.0 months, HR 0.70) and PFS; demonstrated first-line chemo-immunotherapy benefit in ESCC.

records.title: ORIENT-15
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma Sintilimab + chemotherapy (cisplatin + paclitaxel or fluorouracil) vs placebo + chemotherapy Overall survival Sintilimab improved OS (16.7 vs 12.5 months, HR 0.63) across PD-L1 subgroups; reinforced first-line chemo-immunotherapy in ESCC.

records.title: RATIONALE-306
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma Tislelizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + investigator's-choice platinum doublet (with fluoropyrimidine or paclitaxel) vs placebo + platinum doublet Overall survival Tislelizumab improved OS (17.2 vs 10.6 months, HR 0.66); among the largest OS gains for first-line ESCC chemo-immunotherapy.

records.title: ATTRACTION-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal squamous — second-line immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma refractory/intolerant to fluoropyrimidine + platinum Nivolumab vs chemotherapy (docetaxel or paclitaxel) Overall survival Nivolumab improved OS (10.9 vs 8.4 months, HR 0.77) regardless of PD-L1 expression; established second-line immunotherapy for ESCC.

records.title: DRAGON-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Peritoneal metastasis — intraperitoneal (bidirectional) therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma with laparoscopically confirmed peritoneal metastasis (China) Intraperitoneal + IV paclitaxel + S-1 (NIPS, bidirectional) vs IV paclitaxel + S-1 Overall survival Adding intraperitoneal paclitaxel (bidirectional therapy) improved median OS (19.4 vs 13.9 months, HR 0.66) and conversion-surgery eligibility; first RCT showing intraperitoneal chemotherapy prolongs survival in gastric peritoneal metastasis.

records.title: RENAISSANCE (AIO-FLOT5)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oligometastatic disease — role of surgery · III · 2024
records.body: Synchronous de-novo oligometastatic (limited-metastatic) gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma responding to induction FLOT Induction FLOT then radical resection of primary + metastases vs continued FLOT alone Overall survival Adding radical surgery to chemotherapy did not improve OS (survival curves crossed — excess early postoperative mortality offset by longer late survival); a negative trial, so surgery is not standard in oligometastatic disease, with possible benefit confined to retroperitoneal-lymph-node-only disease (mOS 30 vs 17 months).

records.title: TROG 03.01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastric & Esoph · Oesophageal — palliative radiotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: Advanced or metastatic (incurable) oesophageal cancer unsuitable for curative treatment with symptomatic dysphagia (Mellow 1-4); ECOG 0-2; biopsy-proven (excludes Seifert 2-3 lesions); no prior chemo or chest radiotherapy, fistula or stent in situ Palliative chemoradiotherapy: RT 35 Gy/15 fractions over 3 wk (Australia, NZ) or 30 Gy/10 fractions over 2 wk (Canada, UK) + cisplatin 80 mg/m2 d1 or 20 mg/m2/d d1-4 + 5-FU 800 mg/m2/d infusion d1-4 vs radiotherapy alone (same RT schedule) Primary: dysphagia relief (>=1-point Mellow improvement at 9 wk sustained to 13 wk). Secondary: dysphagia progression-free survival, overall survival, time to dysphagia response, toxicity Adding chemotherapy to palliative radiotherapy did not meaningfully improve dysphagia relief and increased toxicity. Dysphagia relief (primary): 45% vs 35% (difference 10.6 percentage points); statistical significance not reached. Median dysphagia-PFS 4.1 vs 3.4 mo (HR 0.93, 0.71-1.21); median OS 6.9 vs 6.7 mo (HR 0.98, 0.75-1.29). Severe acute toxicity was higher with chemoradiotherapy (36% vs 16%). Short-course radiotherapy alone is a safe, well-tolerated option for malignant dysphagia.

records.title: ESPAC-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2004
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant 5-FU/folinic acid vs chemoradiotherapy (2x2 factorial) vs observation Overall survival Adjuvant chemotherapy improved median OS (19.7 vs 14.0 months) with 5-year OS 21% vs 8% (HR 0.71), whereas chemoradiotherapy was deleterious (5-year OS 10% vs 20%); established adjuvant chemotherapy, not chemoradiation, as the standard.

records.title: ESPAC-3
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant gemcitabine vs 5-FU/folinic acid Overall survival Gemcitabine and 5-FU/folinic acid gave equivalent median OS (23.6 vs 23.0 months, HR 0.94) but gemcitabine caused fewer serious adverse events; established gemcitabine as the preferred, better-tolerated backbone.

records.title: CONKO-001
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (R0/R1) Adjuvant gemcitabine vs observation Disease-free survival Adjuvant gemcitabine prolonged disease-free survival. The 2007 primary analysis (median follow-up 53 months) reported median DFS 13.4 months (95% CI 11.4-15.3) vs 6.9 months (6.1-7.8), P<.001, among the 354 eligible randomised patients, and reports no hazard ratio for any endpoint; its overall-survival comparison was not significant (22.1 vs 20.2 months, P=.06, with 27% of patients still alive). The 2013 long-term analysis (median follow-up 136 months) reported DFS HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.69, P<.001; 13.4 vs 6.7 months) and OS HR 0.76 (0.61-0.95, P=.01), with 5-year OS 20.7% vs 10.4%. Established adjuvant gemcitabine as a standard of care.

records.title: ESPAC-4
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2017
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly (3 of 4 weeks) + capecitabine 1660 mg/m²/day, days 1–21 (28-day cycle), 6 cycles vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² alone (same schedule) Overall survival Adding capecitabine to gemcitabine improved median OS (28.0 vs 25.5 months, HR 0.82, p=0.032); established gemcitabine-capecitabine as an adjuvant standard for fit patients.

records.title: PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1 Adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX — oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² (reduced to 150 after a safety analysis) + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W ×12 (6 months) vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 every 28 days ×6 Disease-free survival mFOLFIRINOX markedly improved DFS (21.6 vs 12.8 months, HR 0.58) and OS (54.4 vs 35.0 months, HR 0.64); established mFOLFIRINOX as the adjuvant standard for fit patients.

records.title: APACT
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Adjuvant nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 of each 28-day cycle ×6 vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² alone (same schedule) Independently-assessed disease-free survival Adding nab-paclitaxel did not improve independently-reviewed DFS (19.4 vs 18.8 months, HR 0.88, p=0.18) though OS trended better (41.8 vs 37.7 months, HR 0.82); failed to establish the doublet as an adjuvant standard.

records.title: GITSG
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · N/A · 1985
records.body: Resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma Postop 5-FU chemoradiation + maintenance 5-FU vs observation Overall survival Adjuvant 5-FU chemoradiation doubled median OS (20 vs 11 months, p=0.035) and 2-year OS (42% vs 15%); first trial to suggest an adjuvant benefit, though small and slow-accruing.

records.title: EORTC 40891
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · III · 1999
records.body: Resected pancreatic head or periampullary cancer (T1-2 N0-1) Postop 40 Gy + 5-FU chemoradiation vs observation Overall survival Adjuvant 5-FU chemoradiation did not improve OS (death-rate ratio 0.91, p=0.54); failed to confirm a chemoradiation benefit and tempered enthusiasm for the GITSG result.

records.title: RTOG 9704
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · III · 2008
records.body: Resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma 5-FU vs gemcitabine before and after 5-FU-based chemoradiation Overall survival For pancreatic-head tumors, gemcitabine numerically improved median OS (20.5 vs 16.9 months, HR 0.82, p=0.09) but without statistical significance; supported gemcitabine sequencing without proving superiority.

records.title: Prep-02/JSAP-05
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2026
records.body: Resectable (or borderline by portal vein) pancreatic adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant gemcitabine + S-1 then surgery vs upfront surgery (both → adjuvant S-1) Overall survival Neoadjuvant gemcitabine + S-1 improved median OS over upfront surgery (37.0 vs 26.6 months, HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.95, p=0.018); mature full-text results confirm and supersede the earlier ASCO-GI 2019 abstract (which reported 36.7 vs 26.6 months, HR 0.72, p=0.015). First RCT to show a neoadjuvant survival benefit in resectable disease.

records.title: SWOG S1505
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2021
records.body: Resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma Perioperative (12 weeks pre-op + 12 weeks post-op) modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² + leucovorin + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W) vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² (days 1, 8, 15) 2-year overall survival Neither perioperative regimen cleared the prespecified 40% benchmark for 2-year overall survival: 47% (95% CI 31-61) with mFOLFIRINOX and 48% (95% CI 31-63) with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, with median overall survival of 23.2 and 23.6 months. Because that threshold was not met in either arm, the pick-the-winner design never ran a head-to-head survival comparison, so the two regimens were not shown to be equivalent and neither was selected. Central radiology review found 43 of the 146 patients it reviewed (29%) ineligible; with one further ineligibility and one withdrawal, 102 of the 147 enrolled were eligible and evaluable.

records.title: NORPACT-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2024
records.body: Resectable pancreatic head ductal adenocarcinoma per NCCN resectable criteria (no arterial contact, venous contact ≤180° without contour irregularity, no metastasis); fit for pancreatoduodenectomy; WHO PS 0-1; radiologically strongly suspected adenocarcinoma, excludes grade ≥2 neuropathy Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX x4 cycles (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 h, q14d) → surgery → adjuvant chemo vs upfront surgery → adjuvant chemo (gemcitabine+capecitabine or modified FOLFIRINOX per amendment) Primary: overall survival at 18 months. Secondary: median overall survival, progression-free survival, R0 resection, ypN0, resection rate, surgical complications, safety Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve survival in resectable pancreatic head cancer and may have worsened it: 18-month OS 60% vs 73% and median OS 25.1 vs 38.5 months (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.00-2.33) favouring upfront surgery. Resection rate unchanged (82% vs 89%). R0 (56% vs 39%) and node-negative (29% vs 14%) status improved with neoadjuvant therapy, but severe toxicity rose (58% vs 40%, including 2 deaths after the first neoadjuvant cycle). Argues against routine neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX for clearly resectable disease.

records.title: PREOPANC
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2020
records.body: Resectable & borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy then surgery vs upfront surgery Overall survival At long-term follow-up, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus upfront surgery showed 5-year overall survival of 20.5% versus 6.5% and HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.96), nominal P=0.025. The R0 resection rate by intention to treat was 41% (49/119) versus 28% (35/127), nominal P=0.025. The resectability interaction P was 0.56.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2020;38:1763-1773   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1220-1230 long-term results 35084987

records.title: Alliance A021501
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · II · 2022
records.body: Borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma (head) Neoadjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX vs mFOLFIRINOX + hypofractionated radiotherapy 18-month overall survival Adding hypofractionated/SBRT radiotherapy did not help; the mFOLFIRINOX-alone arm reached 18-month OS 66.4% and median OS 29.8 months and was favored, arguing against routine radiotherapy after FOLFIRINOX.

records.title: ESPAC-5 (ESPAC-5F)
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma Immediate surgery vs neoadjuvant gem-cap, FOLFIRINOX, or capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy Recruitment & resection rate (1-year OS secondary) Short-course neoadjuvant therapy improved 1-year overall survival over immediate surgery (76% vs 39%; HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.14-0.60, p=0.0052), and did so despite a lower crude resection rate (55% vs 68%, p=0.33). By arm, 1-year survival was 84% with FOLFIRINOX, 78% with gemcitabine plus capecitabine, 60% with chemoradiotherapy and 39% with immediate surgery (p=0.0028 across all four groups). Survival was a secondary outcome of a feasibility trial powered only for resection rate, with 90 randomised and 86 analysed, at 12.2 months median follow-up and with no multiplicity control.

records.title: PREOPANC-2
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable & borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX vs neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (+ adjuvant gemcitabine) Overall survival Total neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve OS over neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (median 21.9 vs 21.3 months, HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.69-1.13, p=0.32); both neoadjuvant strategies are acceptable options.

records.title: CASSANDRA (PACT-21)
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Stage I-III resectable & borderline resectable PDAC, age ≤75, KPS ≥70 Preoperative PAXG (cisplatin 30 mg/m² + nab-paclitaxel 150 mg/m² + gemcitabine 800 mg/m² + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily [1250 mg/m²/day], every 14 days) vs modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 150 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m², every 14 days) Event-free survival Preoperative PAXG (cisplatin, nab-paclitaxel, gemcitabine, capecitabine) improved EFS over modified FOLFIRINOX (median 16.0 vs 10.2 months, HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47-0.84, p=0.0018; corrected from a prior HR 0.64/p=0.003 transcription); positions PAXG as a more active neoadjuvant regimen pending mature OS from the first-randomisation analysis. The previously-listed "3-year EFS 31% vs 13%" figure has been removed: it is not stated in the PMID 41275879 Lancet abstract (which reports only median EFS in months), could not be verified against this citation, and is likely from an unconfirmed conference slide.

records.title: Burris (gemcitabine)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 1997
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, symptomatic Gemcitabine vs bolus 5-fluorouracil Clinical benefit response Clinical benefit response 23.8% vs 4.8% (p=0.0022) and median OS 5.65 vs 4.41 months (p=0.0025); established gemcitabine as the first-line standard.

records.title: NCIC PA.3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2007
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma Gemcitabine + erlotinib vs gemcitabine + placebo Overall survival Median OS 6.24 vs 5.91 months (HR 0.82, p=0.038) and 1-year OS 23% vs 17%; first targeted agent to improve survival, though benefit was marginal.

records.title: GEM-CAP (Cunningham)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2009
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma Gemcitabine + capecitabine vs gemcitabine Overall survival Median OS 7.1 vs 6.2 months (HR 0.86, p=0.077), not significant, though a meta-analysis supported benefit; a modest combination option.

records.title: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (FOLFIRINOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2011
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1 FOLFIRINOX — oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 180 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly (7 of 8 weeks, then 3 of 4 weeks) Overall survival Median OS 11.1 vs 6.8 months (HR 0.57, p<0.001) and PFS 6.4 vs 3.3 months; established FOLFIRINOX as a standard for fit patients.

records.title: MPACT
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2013
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 every 4 weeks vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly (7 of 8 weeks, then days 1, 8, 15 every 4 weeks) Overall survival Median OS 8.5 vs 6.7 months (HR 0.72, p<0.001) and PFS 5.5 vs 3.7 months; established gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel as an alternative first-line standard.

records.title: NAPOLI-3 (NALIRIFOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1 NALIRIFOX — liposomal irinotecan 50 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 60 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, days 1 & 15 of a 28-day cycle vs nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² (days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle) Overall survival Median OS 11.1 vs 9.2 months (HR 0.83, p=0.036) and PFS 7.4 vs 5.6 months; a liposomal-irinotecan triplet alternative to FOLFIRINOX.

records.title: PANOPTIMOX (PRODIGE 35)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · II · 2021
records.body: Untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma controlled on FOLFIRINOX induction 6 mo FOLFIRINOX vs 4 mo FOLFIRINOX then 5-FU/LV maintenance vs alternating gemcitabine/FOLFIRI.3 Progression-free survival at 6 months Median OS 10.1 vs 11.2 vs 7.3 months across arms; 5-FU/LV maintenance after FOLFIRINOX induction is feasible and effective, supporting an induction-maintenance strategy.

records.title: POLO
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, germline BRCA1/2 mutation, no progression on platinum Maintenance olaparib vs placebo Progression-free survival Median PFS 7.4 vs 3.8 months (HR 0.53, p=0.004); OS not improved; first biomarker-driven maintenance, establishing olaparib for germline BRCA-mutated disease.

records.title: CONKO-003
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · III · 2014
records.body: Advanced gemcitabine-refractory pancreatic adenocarcinoma Oxaliplatin/folinic acid/5-FU (OFF) vs folinic acid/5-FU (FF) Overall survival Median OS 5.9 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.66, p=0.01); established a fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin option after gemcitabine failure.

records.title: NAPOLI-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · III · 2016
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after gemcitabine-based therapy Liposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) 80 mg/m² (70 mg/m² irinotecan base) + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W vs 5-FU/leucovorin; a nal-IRI monotherapy arm (120 mg/m² Q3W) was also included Overall survival Median OS 6.1 vs 4.2 months (HR 0.67, p=0.012) and PFS 3.1 vs 1.5 months; established nal-IRI/5-FU/LV as a second-line standard after gemcitabine.

records.title: CodeBreaK 100 (sotorasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma Sotorasib 960 mg once daily (single-arm; KRAS G12C) Objective response rate ORR 21% with median PFS 4.0 months and OS 6.9 months; first KRAS G12C inhibitor with activity in pancreatic cancer, an option for the rare G12C subset.

records.title: RASolute 302 (daraxonrasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Previously treated metastatic PDAC, RAS-mutant (91.8% RAS G12) Daraxonrasib (oral RAS(ON) inhibitor) 300 mg once daily vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel) Overall survival & progression-free survival (RAS G12) Daraxonrasib roughly doubled OS vs chemotherapy (13.2 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.40) and improved PFS (7.2 vs 3.6 months, HR 0.49), with fewer treatment discontinuations; first targeted therapy to show a major survival benefit in RAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: FOLFIRINOX in LAPC (Suker meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · N/A · 2016
records.body: Locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma FOLFIRINOX (patient-level pooled analysis) Overall survival Pooled median OS 24.2 months, far exceeding historical gemcitabine (6-13 months); supports FOLFIRINOX induction for locally advanced disease.

records.title: LAP07
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · III · 2016
records.body: Locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma controlled after 4 months of gemcitabine-based induction Chemoradiotherapy vs continued chemotherapy (after induction) Overall survival Median OS 15.2 vs 16.5 months (HR 1.03, p=0.83), no survival benefit, though chemoradiotherapy reduced local progression (32% vs 46%); chemotherapy alone remained standard.

records.title: PANOVA-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · III · 2025
records.body: Adults aged 18 years and older with unresectable, locally advanced, biopsy-confirmed, previously untreated pancreatic adenocarcinoma (LA-PAC), life expectancy >=3 months, ECOG PS 0-2. Excluded: implantable electronic medical devices in the torso, and severe hypersensitivity to medical adhesives, hydrogel or the study chemotherapies. 196 sites in 20 countries; enrolled May 2018 to March 2023. TTFields 150 kHz (NovoTTF-200T) worn continuously, recommended average usage >=75% (>=18 h/d), arrays replaced 2-3x/wk + nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 IV followed immediately by gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle; to local progression (RECIST v1.1), intolerable toxicity, noncompliance, pregnancy or withdrawal of consent vs Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 IV followed immediately by gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle; to local progression (RECIST v1.1), intolerable toxicity, noncompliance, pregnancy or withdrawal of consent Overall survival (OS) — time from random assignment to date of death or censoring Adding Tumor Treating Fields (150 kHz, worn continuously) to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel met its primary endpoint: median OS 16.2 vs 14.2 months (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99; stratified log-rank P=.039 against a prespecified boundary of .04794). PFS, the only other endpoint inside the testing hierarchy, was not improved (10.6 vs 9.3 months; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.68-1.05; P=.137), so the hierarchy stopped there and every remaining endpoint carries a nominal, alpha-unprotected p-value: pain-free survival 15.2 vs 9.1 months (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.56-0.97; P=.027), 1-year survival 68.1% vs 60.2% (P=.029), ORR 36.1% vs 30.0% (P=.094, not significant), and resectability numerically lower with TTFields (7.0% vs 10.1%, no p-value reported). Device-related adverse events affected 209 of 274 treated patients (76.3%) and were mainly mild-to-moderate skin reactions, most frequently dermatitis (27.7%); no death was attributed to TTFields. Open-label with no sham device and investigator-assessed response, so the 2.0-month difference in median OS must be weighed against continuous device wear.

records.title: SURF Trial
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Curative-intent locoregional therapy — ablation · N/A · 2022
records.body: Small HCC, Child-Pugh ≤7, ≤3 nodules each ≤3 cm Surgical resection vs radiofrequency ablation (RFA) Recurrence-free and overall survival Co-primary RFS and OS in the randomised component (SURF-RCT), final analysis at a median 6.4 and 6.6 years of follow-up: neither differed significantly. 5-year OS 74.6% (95% CI 66.5-81.0) with resection vs 70.4% (62.2-77.3) with RFA, HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.64-1.43); 5-year RFS 42.9% (34.3-51.2) vs 42.7% (34.4-50.7), HR 0.90 (0.67-1.22). Local recurrence was lower after resection on a nominal test (8.0% vs 15.8%, p=0.03), and serious adverse effects occurred only in the resection arm (3.3% vs none). Accrual was stopped early at 308 randomised against a target of 600, leaving the trial with 67.2% power to detect a 10% difference, so this is a failure to show superiority of resection rather than a demonstration of equivalence: the OS confidence interval remains wide enough to admit a clinically important difference in either direction. The authors themselves treat resection and RFA as effectively equivalent in practice and advise tailoring the choice to the patient's condition and tumour characteristics in a multidisciplinary setting.
records.keywords: Liver Cancer 2022;11:209-218   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2628-2638 final OS and updated RFS analysis 40554738

records.title: Llovet (BCLC)
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) · N/A · 2002
records.body: Unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A/B, Okuda I/II, not for curative therapy Arterial embolisation or chemoembolisation (doxorubicin) vs symptomatic care Overall survival Chemoembolisation improved survival (1- and 2-year 82% and 63% vs 63% and 27% for control; HR of death 0.47); established TACE as standard of care for unresectable intermediate-stage HCC.

records.title: SARAH
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · III · 2017
records.body: Locally advanced or inoperable HCC, including portal vein invasion Y-90 resin microsphere radioembolisation (SIRT) vs sorafenib Overall survival SIRT did not improve OS over sorafenib (median 8.0 vs 9.9 months, HR 1.15) despite higher tumour response (19% vs 12%) and better tolerability/quality of life; Y-90 is not a substitute for systemic therapy in advanced HCC.

records.title: DOSISPHERE-01
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · II · 2021
records.body: Locally advanced HCC ≥7 cm, eligible for Y-90 glass microspheres Personalised dosimetry (≥205 Gy to index lesion) vs standard dosimetry (120 Gy) Objective response rate (EASL) Personalised dosimetry doubled response (71% vs 36%) and markedly improved OS (median 26.6 vs 10.7 months); established tumour-dose–guided Y-90 radioembolisation.

records.title: TACTICS
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · II · 2020
records.body: Unresectable HCC amenable to TACE, Child-Pugh ≤7 TACE plus sorafenib vs TACE alone Progression-free survival and overall survival Co-primary endpoints of progression-free and overall survival under a gatekeeping strategy with a ONE-SIDED alpha of 0.15; the overall-survival gate required PFS significance at p<0.15. PFS here is TACE-specific: time to unTACEable progression or death assessed by RECICL, with new intrahepatic lesions explicitly not counted as progression, so it is not comparable with PFS or time-to-progression in trials using RECIST 1.1 or mRECIST. The 2020 primary analysis reported median PFS 25.2 vs 13.5 months (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.41-0.87, p=0.006) and did not analyse overall survival, only 92 of 125 OS events (73.6%) being mature; the trial under-enrolled, 156 randomised against 168 anticipated. The 2022 final analysis reported PFS significantly improved at 22.8 vs 13.5 months (HR 0.661, 95% CI 0.466-0.938, p=0.02) and overall survival not significantly improved at 36.2 vs 30.8 months (HR 0.861, 95% CI 0.607-1.223, p=0.40). Signalled benefit of combining systemic therapy with TACE.

records.title: EMERALD-1
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Unresectable HCC amenable to embolisation TACE + durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W → durvalumab 1120 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W (maintenance) vs TACE + durvalumab (same, without bevacizumab) vs TACE + placebo Progression-free survival Adding durvalumab plus bevacizumab to TACE improved PFS (15.0 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.77); durvalumab plus TACE alone did not (HR 0.94); first positive phase 3 of TACE plus systemic immunotherapy.

records.title: LEAP-012
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Unresectable, non-metastatic intermediate-stage HCC not amenable to curative therapy TACE + lenvatinib + pembrolizumab vs TACE + dual placebo Progression-free survival and overall survival Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab added to TACE improved PFS (14.6 vs 10.0 months, HR 0.66); OS was not significantly improved at the first analysis; reinforces TACE–systemic combinations for intermediate HCC.

records.title: EMERALD-3
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Unresectable embolization-eligible HCC (eeHCC) TACE + STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg IV ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W) + lenvatinib 12 mg/day (≥60 kg) or 8 mg/day (<60 kg), to progression, toxicity, or 36 months vs TACE + STRIDE (same, without lenvatinib) vs TACE alone Progression-free survival (STRIDE + lenvatinib + TACE vs TACE) Adding STRIDE (tremelimumab + durvalumab) plus lenvatinib to TACE improved PFS (13.0 vs 9.8 months, HR 0.70) with a positive but not yet statistically significant OS trend at interim analysis (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.65-1.09, ~40% maturity); STRIDE plus TACE alone (without lenvatinib) also improved PFS (HR 0.71) and OS (HR 0.70) vs TACE. Grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs were more frequent with the triplet (62.7%) than STRIDE+TACE (48.6%) or TACE alone (18.6%). Interim analysis of an ongoing trial — OS immature; abstract only, no peer-reviewed full publication yet.

records.title: STORM
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · III · 2015
records.body: HCC at high recurrence risk after curative resection or ablation Adjuvant sorafenib vs placebo Recurrence-free survival Sorafenib did not improve RFS (median 33.4 vs 33.8 months, HR 0.94) or OS; showed adjuvant TKI therapy has no role after curative HCC treatment.

records.title: IMbrave050
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · III · 2023
records.body: Resected or ablated HCC at high risk of recurrence Adjuvant atezolizumab + bevacizumab (1 year) vs active surveillance Recurrence-free survival Improved RFS at the interim analysis (HR 0.72), but the benefit was not maintained on updated analysis; adjuvant atezolizumab/bevacizumab is not established as standard.

records.title: SHARP
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, no prior systemic therapy (Western) Sorafenib vs placebo Overall survival Sorafenib improved median OS (10.7 vs 7.9 months, HR 0.69) and time to progression (5.5 vs 2.8 months); established the first systemic standard for advanced HCC.

records.title: Asia-Pacific (Cheng)
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2009
records.body: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, Asia-Pacific (largely HBV-related) Sorafenib vs placebo Overall survival Sorafenib improved OS (6.5 vs 4.2 months, HR 0.68) and TTP (2.8 vs 1.4 months); confirmed sorafenib benefit in a predominantly hepatitis B Asian population.

records.title: REFLECT
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A First-line lenvatinib 12 mg/day (≥60 kg) or 8 mg/day (<60 kg) vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily Overall survival (non-inferiority) Lenvatinib was non-inferior for OS (13.6 vs 12.3 months, HR 0.92) with better PFS (7.4 vs 3.7 months) and ORR (41% vs 12%); established lenvatinib as a first-line alternative to sorafenib.

records.title: IMbrave150
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Untreated unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A Atezolizumab 1200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily Overall survival and progression-free survival Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab improved OS (median 19.2 vs 13.4 months, HR 0.66) and PFS (6.8 vs 4.3 months, HR 0.59); became the first-line standard of care for advanced HCC.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;382:1894-1905   J Hepatol 2022;76:862-873 updated OS analysis 34902530

records.title: HIMALAYA
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A, no main portal vein thrombosis STRIDE — tremelimumab 300 mg IV ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W vs durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily Overall survival STRIDE improved OS vs sorafenib (median 16.4 vs 13.8 months, HR 0.78; 36-month OS 30.7% vs 19.8%) and durvalumab was non-inferior; established a dual-immunotherapy first-line option.
records.keywords: NEJM Evid 2022;1:EVIDoa2100070   Ann Oncol 2024;35:448-457 4-yr OS update 38382875

records.title: CheckMate 9DW
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W vs investigator's choice — lenvatinib 8 or 12 mg/day (by bodyweight) or sorafenib 400 mg twice daily Overall survival Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improved OS (median 23.7 vs 20.6 months, HR 0.79) with higher ORR (36% vs 13%); added a dual-checkpoint first-line option and gained regulatory approval.

records.title: CARES-310
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated unresectable/metastatic HCC, Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0-1 (83% Asian, HBV-predominant) Camrelizumab + rivoceranib vs sorafenib Progression-free survival and overall survival Camrelizumab (anti-PD-1) + rivoceranib (oral VEGFR2 TKI) improved both co-primary endpoints over sorafenib in untreated unresectable HCC. At the protocol-specified final analysis (351 deaths, 98% of 359 planned events): OS 23.8 vs 15.2 months, stratified HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.52-0.79); PFS 5.6 vs 3.7 months, stratified HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.44-0.67), identical to the earlier cutoff. Significance was established at the earlier PFS primary and OS interim analyses, and the final report states only nominal p values. Tolerability is the trade-off: grade >=3 treatment-related events 81% vs 54% of the 272 and 269 treated, hypertension 38% vs 15%, rivoceranib dose reduction in 48%; more sorafenib patients received subsequent immunotherapy (36% vs 17%). A first-line option in which toxicity burden rather than efficacy drives selection.
records.keywords: Lancet 2023;402:1133-1146   Lancet Oncol 2025;26:1598-1611 final OS analysis 41308676

records.title: RESORCE
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2017
records.body: HCC progressing on sorafenib, Child-Pugh A, sorafenib-tolerant Regorafenib + best supportive care vs placebo + BSC Overall survival Regorafenib improved OS (median 10.6 vs 7.8 months, HR 0.63); first agent to show benefit after sorafenib progression.

records.title: CELESTIAL
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Advanced HCC after sorafenib, up to 2 prior systemic regimens Cabozantinib vs placebo Overall survival Cabozantinib improved overall survival at the second interim analysis (median 10.2 vs 8.0 months, stratified HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63-0.92, P=0.005) and progression-free survival (5.2 vs 1.9 months, stratified HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.36-0.52), establishing a later-line standard after sorafenib; objective response was 4% vs under 1% (P=0.009), all three endpoints alpha-protected. Delivery is governed by tolerability: grade 3/4 events in 68% vs 36% of the 467 and 237 treated, hand-foot skin reaction 17% vs 0% and hypertension 16% vs 2%, and 62% required dose reduction to a median average daily dose of 35.8 mg against a 60 mg start, so most patients did not sustain the starting dose.

records.title: REACH-2
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Advanced HCC after sorafenib with AFP ≥400 ng/mL Ramucirumab + best supportive care vs placebo + BSC Overall survival Ramucirumab improved OS (median 8.5 vs 7.3 months, HR 0.71) in AFP-high patients; first biomarker-selected systemic therapy in HCC.

records.title: CheckMate 040 / 459
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · I/II–III · 2022
records.body: Advanced HCC. CheckMate 040: post-sorafenib 2nd-line, including 154 sorafenib-experienced patients given nivolumab monotherapy (145 from dose expansion, 9 from dose escalation, all at 3 mg/kg) and the nivolumab + ipilimumab cohort of 148 randomised. CheckMate 459: no previous systemic therapy, 1st-line. N=743 is CheckMate 459's randomised total alone (371 nivolumab, 372 sorafenib); CheckMate 040 is not counted in it. Nivolumab monotherapy (vs sorafenib in 459); nivolumab + ipilimumab (040 cohort 4) ORR (040, phase 1/2); overall survival (459, phase 3) In CheckMate 040's 154 sorafenib-experienced patients given nivolumab monotherapy, ORR was 14% (22 of 154; 95% CI 9%-21%) on blinded independent central review and 20% (31 of 154; 95% CI 14%-27%) by investigator assessment, both per RECIST v1.1 at 5-year follow-up, in groups pooled across both study phases so neither is a primary-endpoint result. Confirmatory first-line CheckMate 459 then missed its primary endpoint: OS 16.4 vs 14.7 months, stratified HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.72-1.02), p=0.075 against a prespecified significance boundary of 0.0419, leaving monotherapy without confirmed benefit. Nivolumab was nonetheless better tolerated than sorafenib (grade >=3 palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia under 1% vs 14%, hypertension 0 vs 7% of the 367 and 363 treated). The nivolumab + ipilimumab cohort randomised 148 patients 1:1:1 across three regimens, and the arm that was approved - nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, then nivolumab - gave ORR 32% (16 of 50; 95% CI 20%-47%) and median OS 22.8 months (95% CI 9.4 to not reached), against 27% and 12.5 months in arm B and 29% and 12.7 months in arm C; the study was not powered to detect differences between the three arms and made no statistical comparison of them. That arm earned 2nd-line accelerated approval, and CheckMate 9DW then showed a significant overall survival benefit for the same regimen first-line against lenvatinib or sorafenib; contrasting fates of two arms hinging on confirmatory data.
