records.title: KEYNOTE-394
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Advanced HCC after sorafenib/chemotherapy, Asian patients Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (≤35 cycles) + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care Overall survival Pembrolizumab improved OS (median 14.6 vs 13.0 months, HR 0.79) with better PFS and ORR; confirmed single-agent anti-PD-1 benefit second-line in Asian patients.

records.title: IMbrave251
records.subtitle: Advanced & Locoregional HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2026
records.body: LA/mHCC that progressed after atezolizumab + bevacizumab (2L) Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W + lenvatinib (8 mg/day <60 kg or 12 mg/day ≥60 kg) or sorafenib vs lenvatinib or sorafenib alone (second-line, post-IO) Overall survival Did not meet its primary OS endpoint: median OS 14.6 vs 12.5 months with atezolizumab + TKI vs TKI alone (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72-1.08, p=0.21); PFS was similar (4.3 vs 4.8 months, HR 1.05). First global phase 3 trial to address 2L therapy sequencing after atezolizumab+bevacizumab progression; establishes a benchmark OS of ~12-15 months for TKI-based 2L therapy in this setting despite the negative result.

records.title: NEO-GAP
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Resectable high-risk intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (>5 cm, multifocal, vascular invasion, or node+) Single-arm neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin + nab-paclitaxel (GAP) x4 Feasibility (completion of therapy and resection) Neoadjuvant GAP was feasible: 77% completed chemotherapy and underwent resection (PR 23%, DCR 90%) without excess surgical morbidity; supported further perioperative study.

records.title: GAIN (AIO/CALGP/ACO)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable biliary tract cancer / incidental gallbladder carcinoma Neoadjuvant gem-cis then resection vs immediate resection (± adjuvant) Overall survival Neoadjuvant gem-cis improved median OS (27.8 vs 14.6 months) and R0 resection (62.5% vs 33.3%) vs upfront surgery; closed early at N=68, so signal-generating rather than definitive.

records.title: GOLP (ZSAB-neoGOLP)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2026
records.body: Resectable high-risk intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma Neoadjuvant GEMOX + lenvatinib + toripalimab then surgery vs immediate surgery Event-free survival Neoadjuvant GOLP prolonged EFS (18.0 vs 8.7 months, HR 0.43) without compromising resection at the interim analysis (not yet crossing the significance boundary); first randomized support for neoadjuvant therapy in high-risk iCCA.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: PRODIGE 12/ACCORD 18
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · III · 2019
records.body: Resected (R0/R1) biliary tract cancer, all sites Adjuvant gemcitabine + oxaliplatin (GEMOX) x12 vs surveillance Relapse-free survival GEMOX did not improve RFS (median 30.4 vs 18.5 months, HR 0.88) or OS; a negative trial that did not support adjuvant GEMOX.

records.title: BILCAP
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · III · 2019
records.body: Resected (R0/R1) cholangiocarcinoma or muscle-invasive gallbladder cancer Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle ×8 vs observation Overall survival Missed the ITT OS endpoint (51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81, p=0.097) but improved OS in the prespecified per-protocol analysis (53 vs 36 months, HR 0.75); adopted as the adjuvant standard of care.

records.title: ASCOT (JCOG1202)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · III · 2023
records.body: Resected biliary tract cancer (all sites), Asian patients Adjuvant S-1 (40/50/60 mg by body-surface area, twice daily) 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off ×4 cycles vs observation Overall survival S-1 improved 3-year OS (77.1% vs 67.6%, HR 0.69); established adjuvant S-1 as a standard for resected BTC in Asian patients.

records.title: ABC-02
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer Cisplatin + gemcitabine vs gemcitabine alone Overall survival Cisplatin-gemcitabine improved OS (11.7 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.64) and PFS (8.0 vs 5.0 months); established gem-cis as the first-line standard for over a decade.

records.title: TOPAZ-1
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic biliary tract cancer Durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1 of each 21-day cycle + gemcitabine–cisplatin (up to 8 cycles) → durvalumab 1500 mg monotherapy Q4W to progression vs placebo + gemcitabine–cisplatin → placebo Overall survival Adding durvalumab improved OS (12.8 vs 11.5 months, HR 0.80) with higher 24-month survival (24.9% vs 10.4%); first chemo-immunotherapy standard in advanced BTC.
records.keywords: NEJM Evid 2022;1:EVIDoa2200015   JAMA Oncol 2026 4-year OS post hoc analysis 42424063

records.title: KEYNOTE-966
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated metastatic or unresectable biliary tract cancer Pembrolizumab + gem-cis vs placebo + gem-cis Overall survival Adding pembrolizumab improved OS (12.7 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.83); a second first-line chemo-immunotherapy option.

records.title: SWOG S1815
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated advanced biliary tract cancer GAP — gemcitabine 800 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² + nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV on days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs GC — gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² on days 1 & 8 (21-day cycle) Overall survival N=441 eligible and analysable of 452 randomised (ten ineligible; one withdrew consent immediately after random assignment; the overall-survival figures below are modified-intention-to-treat figures computed on that analysed set). The nab-paclitaxel triplet did not improve OS (14.0 vs 13.6 months, HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.72-1.14, p=0.41) and added toxicity; GAP not adopted as a standard.

records.title: ABC-06
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Second-line chemotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Advanced BTC progressing after first-line gem-cis Active symptom control (ASC) + FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + L-folinic acid 175 mg + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W, ≤12 cycles) vs ASC alone Overall survival FOLFOX modestly improved OS (6.2 vs 5.3 months, HR 0.69; 12-month OS 25.9% vs 11.4%); established FOLFOX as a second-line standard.

records.title: NIFTY
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Second-line chemotherapy · N/A · 2021
records.body: Metastatic BTC progressing after first-line gem-cis, Korea Liposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) + 5-FU/LV vs 5-FU/LV Progression-free survival nal-IRI plus 5-FU/LV improved central-review PFS (7.1 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.56) and OS (8.6 vs 5.5 months); a second-line option, though a later independent re-review tempered the PFS magnitude.

records.title: FIGHT-202
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (intrahepatic CCA) · II · 2020
records.body: Previously treated advanced cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements Single-arm pemigatinib (FGFR1-3 inhibitor) Objective response rate ORR 35.5% with median DOR 7.5 months in FGFR2-fusion patients (none in other/no FGFR alterations); led to first FGFR-targeted approval in cholangiocarcinoma.

records.title: FOENIX-CCA2
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (intrahepatic CCA) · II · 2023
records.body: Previously treated FGFR2-rearranged intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma Single-arm futibatinib (covalent FGFR1-4 inhibitor) Objective response rate ORR 42% with median DOR 9.7 months, PFS 9.0 and OS 21.7 months; supported approval of futibatinib, active including after prior FGFR inhibitors.

records.title: FIGHT-302
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (intrahepatic CCA) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 rearrangement First-line pemigatinib vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (crossover to pemigatinib allowed) Progression-free survival In a trial that closed early when first-line standard of care changed and did not meet its accrual target, first-line pemigatinib improved progression-free survival (8.3 versus 6.8 months; HR 0.584, 95% CI 0.393-0.868), objective response (47.0% versus 15.5%) and duration of response (14.2 versus 6.3 months), while overall survival was not improved (24.4 versus 25.0 months; HR 1.095, 95% CI 0.733-1.637) - roughly 80% of the chemotherapy group went on to an FGFR inhibitor, so the survival comparison is confounded by crossover. The publication states no testing hierarchy, and the authors label the primary progression-free survival p-value nominal, cautioning that it 'should be interpreted with caution in the context of the reduced sample size and event count'. In the 83 and 73 patients treated, hyperphosphatemia - the FGFR class effect - affected 81.9% versus 2.7% but was almost always mild, with one grade >=3 case; dry eye (36.1% versus 4.1%) was the other characteristic toxicity. Grade >=3 events were 78.3% versus 67.1%, and three fatal events versus none were judged unrelated to pemigatinib. Pemigatinib needed more dose interruption (84.3% versus 64.4%) yet caused fewer discontinuations for toxicity (6.0% versus 11.0%). The gemcitabine-cisplatin comparator predates TOPAZ-1 and KEYNOTE-966 and first-line pemigatinib is not FDA-approved, so this informs sequencing more than it changes first-line practice.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: ClarIDHy
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — IDH1 mutation · III · 2020
records.body: Previously treated IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma Ivosidenib 500 mg once daily (continuous 28-day cycles) vs placebo (IDH1-mutant) Progression-free survival Ivosidenib improved PFS (2.7 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.37); OS favored ivosidenib after crossover adjustment (10.3 vs 5.1 months); established IDH1-targeted therapy.

records.title: MyPathway
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — HER2 amplification / overexpression · II · 2021
records.body: Previously treated HER2-amplified/overexpressed metastatic BTC Single-arm pertuzumab + trastuzumab Objective response rate ORR 23% with median PFS 4.0 and OS 10.9 months; early proof-of-concept for dual HER2 blockade in BTC.

records.title: HERIZON-BTC-01
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — HER2 amplification / overexpression · II · 2023
records.body: Previously treated HER2-amplified advanced BTC (IHC 2+/3+) Zanidatamab 20 mg/kg IV Q2W (single-arm; HER2-amplified) Objective response rate Confirmed ORR 41.3% (cohort 1) with median DOR 12.9 months; supported FDA accelerated approval of zanidatamab (2024) for HER2 IHC 3+ BTC.

records.title: ROAR
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — BRAF V600E & mismatch-repair deficiency · II · 2020
records.body: Previously treated BRAF V600E-mutated biliary tract cancer Single-arm dabrafenib + trametinib Objective response rate In the 2020 interim BTC cohort (n=43; 91% intrahepatic), investigator-assessed ORR was 51% (95% CI 36-67), versus 47% (31-62) by independent review; all responses were partial. Median PFS was 9 months (95% CI 5-10) and OS 14 months (10-33) at 10-month median follow-up. Single-arm study; no comparative efficacy inference.

records.title: PROMID
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Somatostatin analogues — antiproliferative control · III · 2009
records.body: Treatment-naive metastatic well-diff midgut NET (functioning & nonfunctioning) Octreotide LAR 30 mg vs placebo Time to tumor progression Octreotide LAR prolonged time to progression (14.3 vs 6.0 months, HR 0.34) in mostly low-burden midgut NET; established somatostatin analogues as first-line antiproliferative therapy.

records.title: CLARINET
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Somatostatin analogues — antiproliferative control · III · 2014
records.body: Advanced grade 1-2 nonfunctioning enteropancreatic NET (Ki-67 <10%) Lanreotide autogel 120 mg vs placebo Progression-free survival Lanreotide prolonged PFS (median not reached vs 18.0 months, HR 0.47) in grade 1-2 nonfunctioning GEP-NET; confirmed somatostatin analogues control tumor growth irrespective of symptoms.

records.title: NETTER-1
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced progressive SSTR+ midgut NET, after somatostatin analogue 177Lu-DOTATATE 7.4 GBq IV every 8 weeks (×4 infusions) + octreotide LAR 30 mg IM vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg IM every 4 weeks Progression-free survival In NETTER-1, PRRT markedly improved progression-free survival: the primary hazard ratio is 0.18 (95% CI 0.11-0.29, p<0.0001) on the regulatory reassessment using prerandomisation baseline scans, correcting the 0.21 the 2017 primary published on the same July 2015 data cutoff - a re-read of the imaging, not longer follow-up. At the prespecified final analysis, done 5 years after the last randomisation because that preceded the alternative 158-death trigger, overall survival did not differ significantly, the comparison falling short of its prespecified threshold of 0.049915: median 48.0 vs 36.3 months, HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.60-1.17), two-sided p=0.30. That is a licensed negative result rather than a nominal one: both preceding steps of the testing hierarchy - progression-free survival and objective response - succeeded, so the overall survival test was inferential. The paper attributes the null partly to crossover, while stating that other confounding factors clearly existed: 41 (36%) of 114 control patients received subsequent PRRT, 26 (23%) within 24 months. The proportional-hazards assumption was not fulfilled (Schoenfeld p=0.03), which is why the paper adds a restricted mean survival time analysis. Myelodysplastic syndrome occurred in 2 (2%) of 111 treated patients with no new cases on long-term follow-up; one died of it, the only reported PRRT-related death - serious adverse events were not collected in the control group during long-term follow-up. Established PRRT for progressive SSTR+ midgut NET.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2017;376:125-135   Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1752-1763 final overall survival and long-term safety; PFS hazard ratio corrected to 0.18 on regulatory reassessment 34793718

records.title: NETTER-2
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · III · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced grade 2-3 well-diff SSTR+ GEP-NET First-line 177Lu-DOTATATE 7.4 GBq IV every 8 weeks (×4 infusions) + octreotide LAR 30 mg IM vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg IM every 4 weeks (grade 2/3) Progression-free survival First-line 177Lu-DOTATATE nearly tripled PFS (22.8 vs 8.5 months, HR 0.28) and ORR (43% vs 9%) vs high-dose octreotide; extended PRRT to newly diagnosed higher-grade GEP-NET.

records.title: COMPETE
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · III · 2026
records.body: Inoperable progressive grade 1/2 SSTR+ GEP-NET (Ki-67 <=20%) 177Lu-edotreotide (ITM-11) vs everolimus Progression-free survival 177Lu-edotreotide improved PFS over everolimus (median 23.9 vs 14.1 months, stratified HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48–0.95, p=0.022 against a final-analysis boundary of 0.044) and ORR (22% vs 4%; 44 of 201 and 4 of 95). Treatment-related discontinuation was 2% vs 15% on the safety set of 217 and 99 (Fisher's exact p<0.0001, nominal). OS remains immature at 115 events — 63.4 vs 58.7 months, HR 0.78 (0.53–1.15), p=0.21 — and may be confounded by 52% of the everolimus arm crossing to subsequent PRRT. The authors claim the first phase 3 to show superior efficacy for PRRT against a targeted agent, and explicitly decline indirect comparison with the NETTER trials.

records.title: RADIANT-3
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · III · 2011
records.body: Advanced progressive low/intermediate-grade pancreatic NET Everolimus 10 mg once daily vs placebo (advanced pancreatic NET) Progression-free survival Everolimus prolonged PFS (11.0 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.35) in advanced progressive panNET; established mTOR inhibition as a standard option.

records.title: Sunitinib (Raymond)
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · III · 2011
records.body: Advanced progressive well-diff pancreatic NET Sunitinib 37.5 mg vs placebo Progression-free survival Sunitinib improved PFS (11.4 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.42) in advanced progressive panNET; trial stopped early, establishing VEGFR-directed TKI therapy.

records.title: RADIANT-4
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · III · 2016
records.body: Advanced progressive nonfunctional well-diff lung or GI NET Everolimus 10 mg once daily vs placebo (advanced non-functional lung/GI NET) Progression-free survival Everolimus prolonged PFS (11.0 vs 3.9 months, HR 0.48) in nonfunctional lung/GI NET; extended mTOR inhibition beyond the pancreas.

records.title: SANET-ep
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · III · 2020
records.body: Advanced progressive well-diff extrapancreatic NET (China) Surufatinib 300 mg vs placebo Progression-free survival Surufatinib prolonged PFS (9.2 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.33) in extrapancreatic NET; stopped early for efficacy, adding a multitargeted (VEGFR/FGFR/CSF1R) option.

records.title: SANET-p
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · III · 2020
records.body: Advanced progressive well-diff pancreatic NET (China) Surufatinib 300 mg vs placebo Progression-free survival Surufatinib prolonged PFS (10.9 vs 3.7 months, HR 0.49) in advanced panNET; stopped early for efficacy, confirming activity across NET subtypes.

records.title: CABINET (Alliance A021602)
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · III · 2025
records.body: Previously treated advanced pancreatic or extrapancreatic NET Cabozantinib 60 mg once daily vs placebo Progression-free survival Cabozantinib improved PFS in both pancreatic (13.8 vs 4.4 months, HR 0.23) and extrapancreatic (8.4 vs 3.9 months, HR 0.38) cohorts after prior therapy; stopped early for efficacy, establishing cabozantinib in previously treated NET.

records.title: ECOG-ACRIN E2211
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Cytotoxic chemotherapy — pancreatic NET · II · 2023
records.body: Advanced progressive low/intermediate-grade pancreatic NET CAPTEM — capecitabine 750 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² once daily days 10–14, every 28 days vs temozolomide 200 mg/m² days 1–5 every 28 days Progression-free survival Adding capecitabine to temozolomide (CAPTEM) prolonged PFS (22.7 vs 14.4 months, HR 0.58) with a nonsignificant OS trend (58.7 vs 53.8 months, HR 0.82); established CAPTEM as a preferred chemotherapy for panNET.

records.title: TELESTAR
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Carcinoid syndrome — symptom control · III · 2017
records.body: Carcinoid syndrome with >=4 bowel movements/day despite somatostatin analogue Telotristat ethyl 250 or 500 mg TID vs placebo (added to SSA) Change in bowel movement frequency Telotristat ethyl (250 mg TID) increased the proportion with durable >=30% reduction in bowel movements (44% vs 20%) and lowered urinary 5-HIAA; first oral agent for refractory carcinoid syndrome diarrhea.

records.title: TOPIC-NEC (JCOG1213)
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated advanced/recurrent poorly-diff digestive-system NEC Etoposide + cisplatin vs irinotecan + cisplatin Overall survival Etoposide-cisplatin and irinotecan-cisplatin gave similar OS (12.5 vs 10.9 months, HR 1.04); confirmed platinum-etoposide as a standard first-line backbone for digestive NEC.

records.title: NET-02
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) · II · 2023
records.body: Progressive poorly-diff extrapulmonary NEC, second-line Liposomal irinotecan/5-FU/folinic acid vs docetaxel 6-month progression-free survival rate nal-IRI/5-FU met its 6-month PFS endpoint (29.6%) while docetaxel did not (13.8%), with no OS difference; supports nal-IRI/5-FU as a second-line option in extrapulmonary NEC.

records.title: ACOSOG Z9001 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · III · 2009
records.body: Resected KIT+ primary GIST ≥3 cm 1 year adjuvant imatinib vs placebo Recurrence-free survival Imatinib improved 1-year RFS (98% vs 83%, HR 0.35) with no early overall-survival difference; established 1 year of adjuvant imatinib after resection of primary GIST.

records.title: SSG XVIII / AIO
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Resected high-risk KIT+ GIST 3 years vs 1 year adjuvant imatinib Recurrence-free survival Three years of imatinib improved recurrence-free survival, the primary endpoint: 5-year RFS 71.1% vs 52.3% (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.44-0.81, P<.001), ITT at a median 90 months' follow-up. Overall survival, a secondary endpoint, was 91.9% vs 85.3% (HR 0.60, 0.37-0.97, P=.036); the trial adjusted no p-value for multiple testing, so everything below the primary is nominal. Established 3 years as the adjuvant standard for high-risk GIST. Grade 3-4 adverse events 32.8% (65/198) vs 20.1% (39/194), P=.006, on top of a chronic low-grade burden — periorbital oedema 74.2% vs 59.3% (P=.002), muscle cramps 49.0% vs 30.9%, anaemia 80.3% vs 72.2%. By the 2016 analysis 26.8% vs 12.6% had stopped imatinib for a reason other than recurrence, and 13.6% vs 7.7% for an adverse event; the 2012 report gave 25.8% for the 36-month group. Cardiac events over the 2016 follow-up were similar (3.0% vs 5.2%, no formal test).
records.keywords: JAMA 2012;307:1265-1272   J Clin Oncol 2016;34:244-250 updated analysis 26527782

records.title: EORTC 62024
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Resected intermediate/high-risk KIT+ GIST 2 years adjuvant imatinib vs observation Imatinib failure-free survival 5-year imatinib failure-free survival was similar (87% vs 84%, p=0.44), but relapse-free survival was improved (3-year 84% vs 66%); supported adjuvant imatinib while suggesting longer duration is needed.

records.title: PERSIST-5
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · II · 2018
records.body: Resected intermediate/high-risk primary GIST 5 years adjuvant imatinib (single arm) Recurrence-free survival 5-year RFS was 90% and OS 95%, with no recurrences among patients with imatinib-sensitive genotypes who stayed on drug; supports extended adjuvant duration in high-risk disease.

records.title: IMADGIST (FSG)
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Resected localized GIST, ≥35% relapse risk, on imatinib 3 years 6 years vs 3 years adjuvant imatinib Disease-free survival Extending imatinib to 6 years improved 3-year DFS from randomization (87% vs 55%, HR 0.40); OS was not yet different, supporting longer adjuvant duration for the highest-risk GIST.

records.title: B2222
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · II · 2002
records.body: Advanced unresectable/metastatic KIT+ GIST Imatinib 400 vs 600 mg/day Objective response rate Imatinib produced a partial response in 53.7% with durable disease control and a later median OS of ~57 months; first trial to establish imatinib as standard first-line therapy for advanced GIST.

records.title: EORTC 62005
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · III · 2004
records.body: Advanced/metastatic KIT+ GIST Imatinib 800 vs 400 mg/day Progression-free survival 800 mg/day modestly prolonged PFS (HR 0.82, p=0.026) without an OS benefit; the advantage was concentrated in KIT exon 9 tumors, supporting 400 mg as standard except for exon 9.

records.title: MetaGIST
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · N/A · 2010
records.body: Advanced GIST (pooled EORTC 62005 + S0033) Imatinib 800 vs 400 mg/day Progression-free survival Pooled analysis showed a small PFS advantage for 800 mg/day confined to KIT exon 9-mutant GIST, with no OS difference; defined 400 mg as standard and 800 mg for exon 9 tumors.

records.title: BFR14 (FSG)
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · III · 2010
records.body: Advanced GIST, non-progressing after 3 years of imatinib Interrupt vs continue imatinib Progression-free survival Interruption led to rapid progression (most within months) versus continuation, and rechallenge seldom restored prior depth of response; established continuous imatinib until progression.

records.title: A6181004 (Sunitinib)
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · III · 2006
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib failure/intolerance Sunitinib vs placebo Time to tumor progression Sunitinib quadrupled time to progression (27.3 vs 6.4 weeks, HR 0.33) and improved OS (HR 0.49); established sunitinib as second-line therapy for imatinib-resistant GIST.

records.title: GRID
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · III · 2013
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib and sunitinib Regorafenib vs placebo Progression-free survival Regorafenib improved PFS (4.8 vs 0.9 months, HR 0.27); OS was not significant due to 85% crossover; established regorafenib as third-line standard.

records.title: INVICTUS
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · III · 2020
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib Ripretinib vs placebo Progression-free survival Ripretinib improved PFS (6.3 vs 1.0 months, HR 0.15) and median OS (15.1 vs 6.6 months); established ripretinib as fourth-line standard.

records.title: INTRIGUE
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · III · 2022
records.body: Advanced GIST progressing on first-line imatinib Ripretinib 150 mg once daily (continuous) vs sunitinib 50 mg once daily (4 weeks on / 2 weeks off) — second-line Progression-free survival Ripretinib was not superior to sunitinib (PFS 8.0 vs 8.3 months ITT; KIT exon 11 8.3 vs 7.0 months, HR 0.88) but was better tolerated; sunitinib remained the second-line standard.

records.title: PEAK
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · III · 2026
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib failure/intolerance (second-line) Bezuclastinib + sunitinib vs sunitinib Progression-free survival The combination improved PFS (16.5 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.50) and ORR (46% vs 26%); poised to redefine second-line therapy (FDA priority review, PDUFA Nov 2026).

records.title: NAVIGATOR
records.subtitle: GIST · Mutation-specific therapy — PDGFRA D842V · I · 2020
records.body: Advanced PDGFRA D842V-mutant GIST (imatinib-insensitive) Avapritinib (single arm) Objective response rate Avapritinib produced an ORR of 88% (9% complete responses) with durable benefit (12-month DOR 70%); established avapritinib as standard for PDGFRA D842V-mutant GIST.

records.title: VOYAGER
records.subtitle: GIST · Mutation-specific therapy — PDGFRA D842V · III · 2021
records.body: Advanced molecularly unselected GIST, third/fourth line Avapritinib 300 mg once daily (continuous) vs regorafenib 160 mg once daily (3 weeks on / 1 week off) Progression-free survival Avapritinib did not improve PFS over regorafenib (4.2 vs 5.6 months, HR 1.25, p=0.055), missing its primary endpoint; confirmed avapritinib's role is restricted to PDGFRA D842V disease.

records.title: POTOMAC
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) — BCG ± immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: BCG-naive, high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (high-grade Ta/T1 and/or CIS) Durvalumab + BCG (induction + maintenance) vs BCG (induction + maintenance); third arm durvalumab + BCG induction only Disease-free survival Adding 1 year of durvalumab to BCG (induction + maintenance) improved DFS (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.50–0.93, p=0.0154) in BCG-naive high-risk NMIBC; first phase 3 to show systemic PD-(L)1 benefit added to BCG.

records.title: SWOG 8710 (INT-0080)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Neoadjuvant & perioperative chemotherapy — muscle-invasive bladder cancer · III · 2003
records.body: Resectable muscle-invasive bladder cancer (cT2-T4a N0M0) Neoadjuvant MVAC ×3 then cystectomy vs cystectomy alone Overall survival Neoadjuvant MVAC improved median OS (77 vs 46 months) and raised the pT0 rate (38% vs 15%); established neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy as a standard before cystectomy.

records.title: ABC Meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Neoadjuvant & perioperative chemotherapy — muscle-invasive bladder cancer · N/A · 2003
records.body: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (11 neoadjuvant trials, individual-patient data) Neoadjuvant platinum-based combination chemotherapy + local therapy vs local therapy alone Overall survival Neoadjuvant platinum-based combination chemotherapy improved OS (HR 0.86), a 5% absolute gain in 5-year survival; provided the evidentiary basis for neoadjuvant chemotherapy in MIBC.

records.title: VESPER (GETUG-AFU V05)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Neoadjuvant & perioperative chemotherapy — muscle-invasive bladder cancer · III · 2022
records.body: Resectable MIBC (88% treated in the neoadjuvant setting) Perioperative dose-dense MVAC (methotrexate/vinblastine/doxorubicin/cisplatin, Q2W ×6) vs gemcitabine–cisplatin (Q3W ×4); neoadjuvant (majority) or adjuvant Progression-free survival at 3 years dd-MVAC did not significantly improve 3-yr PFS in the whole population (64% vs 56%, HR 0.77) but did in the neoadjuvant subgroup (66% vs 56%, HR 0.70), where 5-yr OS was also higher (66% vs 57%, HR 0.71); supports six cycles of dd-MVAC as preferred neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

records.title: IMvigor010
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after radical surgery Adjuvant atezolizumab vs observation Disease-free survival Atezolizumab did not improve DFS (median 19.4 vs 16.6 months, HR 0.89); a negative adjuvant trial, though a later ctDNA-positive subset analysis suggested benefit and seeded ctDNA-guided trials.

records.title: CheckMate 274
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after radical surgery Adjuvant nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W for up to 1 year vs placebo Disease-free survival Nivolumab improved median DFS (ITT 20.8 vs 10.8 months, HR 0.70; PD-L1≥1% HR 0.55); established adjuvant nivolumab for high-risk resected urothelial carcinoma.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:2102-2114  34077643 J Clin Oncol 2025;43:15-21 expanded efficacy 39393026

records.title: NIAGARA
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Cisplatin-eligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer (cT2-T4a N0/1 M0) Neoadjuvant durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q3W + gemcitabine–cisplatin ×4 → radical cystectomy → adjuvant durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W ×8 vs neoadjuvant gemcitabine–cisplatin ×4 → radical cystectomy alone Event-free survival Perioperative durvalumab improved EFS (24-mo 67.8% vs 59.8%, HR 0.68) and OS (24-mo 82.2% vs 75.2%, HR 0.75) with higher pCR (37.3% vs 27.5%); established perioperative chemoimmunotherapy in MIBC.

records.title: AMBASSADOR (Alliance A031501)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after radical surgery Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W for up to 1 year (18 cycles) vs observation Disease-free survival Pembrolizumab improved median DFS (29.6 vs 14.2 months, HR 0.73) regardless of PD-L1 status; OS was not significantly different. Corroborated adjuvant PD-1 blockade after surgery.

records.title: KEYNOTE-905 / EV-303
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: Cisplatin-ineligible (or cisplatin-declining) muscle-invasive bladder cancer (cT2-T4aN0M0) Perioperative enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV (days 1 & 8) + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W — 3 neoadjuvant cycles → radical cystectomy → 6 adjuvant EV + 14 adjuvant pembrolizumab cycles (9 EV / 17 pembrolizumab total) vs radical cystectomy alone Event-free survival (and overall survival) Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab improved EFS (2-yr 74.7% vs 39.4%, HR 0.40) and OS (2-yr 79.7% vs 63.1%, HR 0.50), with pCR 57.1% vs 8.6%; established a perioperative chemo-free standard for cisplatin-ineligible MIBC, a group with no prior effective perioperative systemic option.

records.title: KEYNOTE-B15 / EV-304
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: Cisplatin-eligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer (cT2-T4aN0M0 or T1-T4aN1M0), radical cystectomy candidates Perioperative enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab vs neoadjuvant gemcitabine-cisplatin (both with radical cystectomy) Event-free survival Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab improved EFS vs neoadjuvant cisplatin–gemcitabine (24-mo 79.4% vs 66.2%, HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.41–0.70) and overall survival (24-mo 86.9% vs 81.3%, HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48–0.89, P=0.006), with higher pCR (55.8% vs 32.5%, ITT-denominated; difference 23.4 points, 95% CI 16.7–29.8, P<0.001); OS and pCR were both alpha-controlled key secondary endpoints. Only 64.7% of the EV arm started the adjuvant phase. In the control arm 6.9% received adjuvant anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy (a protocol amendment permitted adjuvant nivolumab), so the comparator was largely without adjuvant immunotherapy. Grade ≥3 any-cause AEs were higher (75.7% vs 67.2%; as-treated, 403/396), which the authors say probably owes in part to longer exposure (median therapy 10.2 vs 3.5 months); drug-related grade ≥3 was similar (46.4% vs 46.5%), with toxicity differing in kind and more discontinuation for drug-related AEs (35.2% vs 11.1%). Cisplatin-eligible counterpart to EV-303.

records.title: IMvigor011
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer, ctDNA-positive on serial post-cystectomy surveillance (no radiographic evidence of disease) ctDNA-positive: adjuvant atezolizumab 1680 mg IV Q4W for 12 cycles (up to 1 year) vs placebo; ctDNA-negative patients received no treatment and were followed observationally Investigator-assessed disease-free survival In ctDNA-positive patients, adjuvant atezolizumab significantly improved disease-free survival (9.9 vs 4.8 months; HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.47-0.87, p=0.005) and overall survival (32.8 vs 21.1 months; HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.39-0.90, p=0.01) versus placebo. Among 357 patients with persistent ctDNA-negative status who received no treatment, disease-free survival was 95% at 1 year and 88% at 2 years, supporting treatment de-escalation in this group. Grade 3/4 adverse events were more frequent with atezolizumab (28% vs 22%) but without new safety signals. First prospective randomized validation of ctDNA-guided patient selection for adjuvant immunotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2025 (published online Oct 20, 2025)

records.title: BC2001
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Bladder-preservation — trimodality therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer managed with bladder preservation Radiotherapy + concurrent 5-FU/mitomycin C vs radiotherapy alone Locoregional disease-free survival Adding concurrent chemotherapy improved 2-yr locoregional DFS (67% vs 54%, HR 0.68) without excess serious toxicity; established chemoradiotherapy as the standard for bladder preservation.

records.title: von der Maase (GC vs MVAC)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2000
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma Gemcitabine-cisplatin vs MVAC Overall survival GC produced similar OS to MVAC (median 13.8 vs 14.8 months, HR 1.04) with a better safety profile; established gemcitabine-cisplatin as a standard first-line regimen.

records.title: CheckMate 901
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated unresectable/metastatic urothelial carcinoma, cisplatin-eligible First-line nivolumab 360 mg IV Q3W + gemcitabine–cisplatin ×6 → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W maintenance (to progression or max 2 years) vs gemcitabine–cisplatin ×6 Overall survival and progression-free survival Nivolumab + gem-cis improved OS (median 21.7 vs 18.9 months, HR 0.78) and PFS (7.9 vs 7.6 months, HR 0.72), with a higher CR rate (21.7% vs 11.8%); a first-line chemoimmunotherapy option.

records.title: EV-302 (KEYNOTE-A39)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (platinum-eligible or -ineligible) First-line enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV (days 1 & 8) + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (EV to progression; pembrolizumab to 35 cycles) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin or carboplatin (6 cycles) Overall survival and progression-free survival EV + pembrolizumab nearly doubled median OS (31.5 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.47) and PFS (12.5 vs 6.3 months, HR 0.45); established EV-pembrolizumab as the first-line standard of care.

records.title: RC48-C016 (Sheng et al.)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated HER2-expressing (IHC 1+, 2+, or 3+) locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer First-line disitamab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV + toripalimab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W (to progression) vs gemcitabine–cisplatin (or carboplatin AUC 4.5) Q3W, up to 6 cycles Progression-free survival (blinded independent review) and overall survival (dual primary) Disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab significantly improved both primary endpoints versus chemotherapy: PFS 13.1 vs 6.5 months (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.28-0.46, p<0.001) and OS 31.5 vs 16.9 months (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.73, p<0.001). ORR was 76.1% vs 50.2%. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were less frequent with the ADC-immunotherapy combination (55.1% vs 86.9%), driven mainly by lower hematologic toxicity, though peripheral neurotoxicity and aminotransferase elevation were more common. Establishes a HER2-informed, biomarker-selected first-line regimen as an alternative to EV-302 and CheckMate 901.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2025 (published online Oct 19, 2025)

records.title: JAVELIN Bladder 100
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Switch-maintenance therapy — advanced urothelial carcinoma · III · 2020
records.body: Advanced urothelial carcinoma without progression after 1st-line platinum chemotherapy Switch-maintenance avelumab 10 mg/kg IV Q2W + best supportive care vs best supportive care alone (after 4–6 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy without progression) Overall survival Maintenance avelumab improved median OS in all randomized patients (21.4 vs 14.3 months, HR 0.69) and in the PD-L1-positive group (HR 0.56); established first-line switch-maintenance immunotherapy.

records.title: KEYNOTE-045
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Second-line & later therapy — metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2017
records.body: Platinum-refractory advanced urothelial carcinoma Pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel, or vinflunine) Overall survival Pembrolizumab improved median OS (10.3 vs 7.4 months, HR 0.73) with durable responses; first agent to beat chemotherapy in the second line and established checkpoint blockade after platinum.

records.title: EV-301
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Second-line & later therapy — metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Advanced urothelial carcinoma after platinum and PD-1/L1 therapy Enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV (days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle) vs investigator-choice chemotherapy — docetaxel, paclitaxel, or vinflunine (day 1, Q3W); to progression Overall survival Enfortumab vedotin improved median OS (12.9 vs 8.9 months, HR 0.70) and PFS (5.6 vs 3.7 months); established the first antibody-drug conjugate for previously treated urothelial carcinoma.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2021;384:1125-1135   Ann Oncol 2023;34:1047-1054 24-mo long-term outcomes 37678672

records.title: THOR (Cohort 1)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Second-line & later therapy — metastatic urothelial carcinoma · III · 2023
records.body: Advanced urothelial carcinoma with FGFR2/3 alterations after PD-1/L1 therapy Erdafitinib 8 mg orally once daily (pharmacodynamically-guided uptitration to 9 mg on day 14) vs investigator-choice chemotherapy — docetaxel 75 mg/m² or vinflunine 320 mg/m² IV Q3W; to progression Overall survival Erdafitinib improved median OS (12.1 vs 7.8 months, HR 0.64) and PFS; validated FGFR-targeted therapy in FGFR-altered urothelial carcinoma.

records.title: POUT
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) — adjuvant therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Resected pT2-T4 N0-3 M0 upper tract urothelial carcinoma after nephroureterectomy Adjuvant gemcitabine–cisplatin (or carboplatin AUC 4.5–5 if GFR <50) ×4 cycles, started within 90 days of surgery vs surveillance Disease-free survival Adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy improved 3-yr DFS (71% vs 46%, HR 0.45); established adjuvant chemotherapy as the standard after nephroureterectomy for UTUC.

records.title: SPCG-4
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Active surveillance & definitive local therapy — clinically localized disease · III · 2014
records.body: Clinically localized prostate cancer (largely palpable, pre-PSA era) Radical prostatectomy vs watchful waiting Death from any cause, prostate-cancer death, metastasis Radical prostatectomy reduced prostate-cancer mortality (RR 0.56) and all-cause mortality vs watchful waiting over 23 years (NNT 8 to avoid one death); confirmed a survival benefit of surgery in clinically detected disease.

records.title: ProtecT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Active surveillance & definitive local therapy — clinically localized disease · III · 2016
records.body: PSA-detected clinically localized prostate cancer Active monitoring vs radical prostatectomy vs radiotherapy Prostate-cancer-specific mortality At a median 15 years prostate-cancer mortality was low and did not differ across monitoring, surgery and radiotherapy (45/1643, 2.7% overall; 3.1% vs 2.2% vs 2.9%; P=0.53, the trial's only alpha-protected comparison); monitoring roughly doubled metastases (9.4% vs 4.7% vs 5.0%) with all-cause deaths similar (356/1643, 21.7%; adjusted HR 0.89 [95% CI 0.69-1.15] and 0.88 [0.68-1.13] vs monitoring, no p reported and intervals unadjusted for multiplicity). Active monitoring was protocol-driven deferral of radical treatment, not sustained surveillance - over half that arm had been treated radically by 10 years - and up to 34% of the cohort was intermediate- or high-risk, so the trial supports a shared trade-off discussion rather than surveillance in a named risk band.

records.title: EORTC 22863
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 1997
records.body: Locally advanced / high-metastatic-risk prostate cancer External-beam RT + 3-yr androgen suppression vs RT alone Clinical disease-free survival Adding 3 years of goserelin to radiotherapy improved the primary endpoint, 10-yr clinical disease-free survival (47.7% vs 22.7%, HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.33-0.55), and also 10-yr OS (58.1% vs 39.8%, HR 0.60) and prostate-cancer mortality (10.3% vs 30.4%, HR 0.38) - the latter two prespecified but carrying no allocated alpha, so nominal (Bolla 2010; the 10-yr landmark exceeds the 9.1-yr median follow-up). Earlier reports give 5-yr OS 79% vs 62% (1997, HR 0.50) and 78% vs 62% (2002, HR 0.51). The control arm received deferred androgen suppression on progression (72% of progressors), so this is early vs deferred ADT; 65% completed the assigned 3 years.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 1997;337:295-300   Lancet 2002;360:103-108 5-yr DFS/OS, median 66 mo (OS HR 0.51) 12126818 Lancet Oncol 2010;11:1066-1073 10-yr results 20933466

records.title: RTOG 9408
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 2011
records.body: Localized prostate cancer, PSA ≤20 (mostly intermediate-risk) RT + 4-month ADT vs RT alone Overall survival Adding 4 months of ADT to RT improved 10-yr OS (62% vs 57%) and reduced prostate-cancer death (4% vs 8%), with benefit concentrated in intermediate-risk men; defined short-course ADT with RT.

records.title: RTOG 9202
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 2003
records.body: Locally advanced (T2c-T4) prostate cancer RT + long-term (28-mo) vs short-term (4-mo) ADT Disease-free survival Long-term ADT improved disease-free and disease-specific survival vs 4 months, with an overall-survival benefit in Gleason 8-10 disease; supported prolonged ADT for high-risk disease.

records.title: EORTC 22961
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 2009
records.body: Locally advanced prostate cancer treated with RT 6 months vs 3 years of androgen suppression Overall survival (non-inferiority) Six months of ADT was not non-inferior to 3 years (5-yr mortality 19.0% vs 15.2%, HR 1.42); confirmed long-course ADT as standard with RT for locally advanced disease.

records.title: CAN-2409 (aglatimagene besadenovec)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy combination — novel agents · III · 2026
records.body: Intermediate- or high-risk localised prostate cancer planned for EBRT, ECOG 0–2 (USA/Puerto Rico); ADT optional Intraprostatic aglatimagene besadenovec + valacyclovir + EBRT vs placebo + valacyclovir + EBRT (2:1) Disease-free survival (intention-to-treat) Adding intratumoral aglatimagene besadenovec (gene-mediated immunotherapy) + valacyclovir to standard EBRT improved the primary endpoint, disease-free survival, in intermediate/high-risk localised prostate cancer (median not reached vs 86.1 months, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.94; p=0.016, ITT, alpha-protected). Grade >=3 TEAEs were 8% (40/479) vs 7% (17/232) in the safety population; no safety comparison is tested, so tolerability is similar on descriptive counts rather than demonstrated equivalent. Overall survival was immature and numerically favoured placebo (HR 1.18, 95% CI 0.64-2.15, nominal p=0.59, 51 deaths). ADT use was optional and stratified, not mandated - so this is an RT-combination, not an RT+ADT, trial.

records.title: CHHiP
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2016
records.body: Localized T1b-T3a prostate cancer Moderate hypofractionation (60 Gy/20) vs conventional (74 Gy/37) Biochemical/clinical failure (non-inferiority) 60 Gy in 20 fractions was non-inferior to 74 Gy in 37 (5-yr biochemical/clinical control 90.6% vs 88.3%, HR 0.84) with similar toxicity; established moderate hypofractionation as standard.

records.title: HYPO-RT-PC
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2019
records.body: Intermediate-to-high-risk localized prostate cancer Ultra-hypofractionation (42.7 Gy/7) vs conventional (78 Gy/39) Failure-free survival (non-inferiority) Ultra-hypofractionation was non-inferior to conventional RT for failure-free survival (per-protocol; prespecified margin 4% absolute at 5 years, critical HR 1.338): 5-yr FFS 84% in both arms (Widmark 2019; restated as 85% in the 10-yr report), and at 10 years 72% vs 65% with adjusted HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69-1.03 (Nilsson 2026). Late grade >=2 cumulative incidence was similar - genitourinary 28% vs 30%, gastrointestinal 14% vs 14% (1 minus Kaplan-Meier from start of RT). Non-inferiority licenses no superiority claim, and the two post-hoc analyses point differently: a log-rank test gave p=0.12 (superiority not reached) while a separate fixed-timepoint analysis at 10 years was significant (p=0.025), favouring ultra-hypofractionation; both are post hoc with nominal p, so neither establishes superiority. Only 11% of patients were high-risk and no ADT was permitted, so both reports draw their conclusion for intermediate-risk disease.

records.title: PACE-B
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2024
records.body: Low/favorable-intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer (no ADT) 5-fraction SBRT (36.25 Gy) vs conventional/moderate hypofractionated RT Freedom from biochemical/clinical failure (non-inferiority) Five-fraction SBRT was non-inferior to conventional RT (5-yr freedom from failure 95.8% vs 94.6%) with similar late toxicity; established SBRT as a standard option for lower-risk disease.

records.title: ASCENDE-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2017
records.body: Intermediate- and high-risk localized prostate cancer LDR brachytherapy boost vs dose-escalated EBRT boost (both + 12-mo ADT + pelvic RT) Biochemical progression-free survival An LDR brachytherapy boost roughly halved biochemical failure vs dose-escalated EBRT (b-PFS HR 2.04 favoring brachytherapy; 9-yr ~83% vs 62%) at the cost of more genitourinary toxicity; established brachytherapy boost for higher-risk disease.
records.keywords: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2017;98:275-285

records.title: STAMPEDE (abiraterone, M0)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Intensification in high-risk non-metastatic disease · III · 2022
records.body: High-risk non-metastatic (M0) prostate cancer starting ADT + RT ADT + abiraterone (± enzalutamide) vs ADT alone Metastasis-free survival Adding abiraterone to ADT improved 6-yr metastasis-free survival (82% vs 69%, HR 0.53) and overall survival (HR 0.60); enzalutamide added no benefit over abiraterone. A new option for high-risk M0 disease.

records.title: PROTEUS
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Intensification in high-risk non-metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Newly diagnosed, nonmetastatic high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate adenocarcinoma in candidates for radical prostatectomy; conventional imaging centrally negative (clinical N1 allowed), ECOG 0-1, and fit for at least 13 months of ADT; full PROTEUS biopsy-core risk criteria are in an unfiled supplement. Perioperative ADT + apalutamide (6 cycles before and 6 cycles after radical prostatectomy) vs Perioperative ADT + placebo (6 cycles before and 6 cycles after radical prostatectomy) Pathological complete response/minimal residual disease and metastasis-free survival (dual) After 6 neoadjuvant cycles, ITT pCR/MRD at surgery was 94/1057 (8.9%) with perioperative ADT plus apalutamide vs 10/1052 (1.0%) with ADT plus placebo (OR 10.17, 95% CI 5.27-19.64; P<0.001). At 61.7 months' median follow-up, final ITT central-review MFS analysis after 472 of 477 planned events showed 5-year MFS of 78.2% vs 73.5% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.67-0.96; P=0.02). Hierarchical EFS, time to subsequent treatment, distant metastasis and 4-year freedom from disease also favoured apalutamide. The hierarchy stopped at conventional-imaging-only MFS (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.67-1.07; no protected P), so the final PSA-free-survival endpoint was not formally tested. Treatment-period grade 3/4 AEs in the safety population were 416/1050 (39.6%) vs 325/1050 (31.0%); the between-group difference was driven primarily by rash. Control was perioperative ADT plus placebo with radical prostatectomy, not radical prostatectomy alone.

records.title: RTOG 9601
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2017
records.body: Biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy (pT2-3 N0) Salvage RT + 24-mo bicalutamide 150 mg vs salvage RT + placebo Overall survival Adding 2 years of bicalutamide to salvage RT improved 12-yr OS (76.3% vs 71.3%, HR 0.77) and halved prostate-cancer death, with benefit greatest at higher PSA; supported hormone-intensified salvage.

records.title: GETUG-AFU 16
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2016
records.body: Rising PSA after prostatectomy (0.2-2.0 ng/mL) Salvage RT + 6-mo goserelin vs salvage RT alone Progression-free survival Adding 6 months of goserelin to salvage RT improved 5-yr biochemical/clinical PFS (80% vs 62%, HR 0.50), sustained at 10 years (64% vs 49%); validated short-course ADT with salvage RT.

records.title: RADICALS-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2020
records.body: Post-prostatectomy with ≥1 risk factor (pT3-4, Gleason 7-10, margin+, PSA≥10) Adjuvant RT vs observation with early salvage RT Freedom from distant metastasis (biochemical PFS reported) Adjuvant RT did not improve 5-yr biochemical PFS vs early salvage (85% vs 88%, HR 1.10) but doubled urinary/bowel toxicity; established observation with early salvage RT as standard.

records.title: SPPORT (RTOG 0534)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2022
records.body: Biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy Prostate-bed RT alone vs +short-term ADT vs +ADT + pelvic-node RT Freedom from progression Escalating salvage RT improved 5-yr freedom from progression stepwise (70.9% prostate-bed RT, 81.3% +ADT, 87.4% +ADT + pelvic-node RT); supported adding ADT and pelvic-node coverage in salvage.

records.title: RADICALS-HD
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2024
records.body: Postoperative radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy (PSA <5, M0) 24 months vs 6 months of ADT added to postoperative RT (companion randomisation: 6 months vs none) Metastasis-free survival Adding 24 months of ADT improved MFS over 6 months (10-yr MFS 78.1% vs 71.9%, HR 0.77, p=0.029) at the cost of more toxicity; in the companion randomisation, adding 6 months versus no ADT did not significantly improve MFS. Defines ADT duration with postoperative RT - long-course for those who can tolerate it.

records.title: CHAARTED (E3805)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — docetaxel intensification · III · 2015
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer ADT + docetaxel ×6 vs ADT alone Overall survival At the 2015 interim analysis docetaxel added to ADT improved median OS 57.6 vs 44.0 months (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.47-0.80), with high-volume disease HR 0.60. At the 2018 mature analysis the effect attenuated to HR 0.72 (0.59-0.89) and the volume conclusion changed: high-volume sustained the benefit (51.2 vs 34.4 months, HR 0.63, 0.50-0.79) while low-volume showed none (HR 1.04, 0.70-1.55); heterogeneity between strata P=.033. First regimen to extend survival in mHSPC.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2015;373:737-746   J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1080-1087 long-term survival analysis at 53.7-mo median follow-up (overall OS HR 0.72; high-volume sustained HR 0.63; low-volume OS benefit not sustained HR 1.04) 29384722

records.title: STAMPEDE (docetaxel)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — docetaxel intensification · III · 2016
records.body: Metastatic & high-risk non-metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer ADT + docetaxel ×6 vs ADT alone (± zoledronic acid) Overall survival Docetaxel improved OS in metastatic patients (median ~60 vs 45 months, HR 0.76); zoledronic acid added nothing to OS. Long-term HES-linked secondary analysis (Jones 2025, n=2042, ~10-yr f/u): ZA reduced fracture-related hospitalisations in M1 disease (SDHR 0.73, p=0.015, 5-yr ARR ~5.6%) but not M0; docetaxel fracture-neutral. Confirmed upfront docetaxel for mHSPC; supports bone-protective agents in mHSPC.
records.keywords: Lancet 2016;387:1163-1177   Ann Oncol 2025;36:1331-1341 10-yr fracture secondary analysis (ZA reduces FRH in M1) 40680994

records.title: LATITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2017
records.body: High-risk de novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer ADT + abiraterone–prednisone vs ADT + placebo Overall survival & radiographic PFS (co-primary) At the 2017 first interim analysis abiraterone added to ADT improved OS (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51-0.76) and rPFS 33.0 vs 14.8 months (HR 0.47, 0.39-0.55). The 2019 final OS analysis gives 53.3 vs 36.5 months (HR 0.66, 0.56-0.78); the ITT rPFS was not re-analysed then, so the 2017 figures remain the trial's only ITT rPFS result. Established abiraterone for high-risk mCSPC.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2017;377:352-360   Lancet Oncol 2019;20:686-700 final overall survival analysis (median 53.3 vs 36.5 months, HR 0.66) 30987939

records.title: STAMPEDE (abiraterone)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2017
records.body: Metastatic & high-risk locally advanced hormone-sensitive prostate cancer ADT + abiraterone–prednisolone vs ADT alone Overall survival Abiraterone added to ADT improved 3-yr OS (83% vs 76%, HR 0.63) and failure-free survival (HR 0.29); confirmed abiraterone intensification across mHSPC and high-risk M0.

records.title: TITAN
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (all-comers) ADT + apalutamide vs ADT + placebo Overall survival & radiographic PFS (co-primary) Apalutamide improved OS (HR 0.67; final HR 0.65) and 24-mo rPFS (68.2% vs 47.5%, HR 0.48) across disease volumes; established apalutamide for mCSPC.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2019;381:13-24   J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2294-2303 final survival analysis (OS HR 0.65; crossover-adjusted HR 0.52) 33914595

records.title: ENZAMET
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer Enzalutamide 160 mg once daily + ADT to progression vs standard non-steroidal antiandrogen (bicalutamide, nilutamide, or flutamide) + ADT (concurrent docetaxel permitted in both arms) Overall survival At the 2019 interim analysis enzalutamide improved OS (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.52-0.86); at the 2023 planned primary analysis HR 0.70 (0.58-0.84), 5-year OS 67% vs 57%. Whether the benefit depends on concurrent docetaxel is unresolved rather than settled either way: the randomised planned-docetaxel strata gave HR 0.82 (0.63-1.06) with docetaxel versus 0.60 (0.47-0.78) without, with no statistical evidence of a differential effect (adjusted p for interaction 0.47), and the trial was neither designed nor powered for that comparison. Established enzalutamide for mHSPC.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2019;381:121-131   Lancet Oncol 2023;24:323-334 mature overall survival analysis (HR 0.70; 5-yr OS 67% vs 57%; benefit consistent across concurrent docetaxel) 36990608

records.title: ARCHES
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer Enzalutamide 160 mg once daily + ADT vs placebo + ADT; to progression (prior docetaxel permitted) Radiographic progression-free survival Enzalutamide reduced radiographic progression or death by 61% (rPFS HR 0.39; median not reached vs 19.0 months) and later improved OS (HR 0.66); confirmed enzalutamide for mCSPC.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2019;37:2974-2986   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1616-1622 final overall survival analysis (HR 0.66) 35420921

records.title: ARANOTE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2024
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (71% high-volume; 31% Asian) Darolutamide 600 mg twice daily + ADT vs placebo + ADT; to progression Radiographic progression-free survival Darolutamide added to ADT reduced radiographic progression or death by 46% (rPFS HR 0.54; 24-month rPFS 70.3% vs 52.1%), with a tolerability profile near-identical to placebo; established the darolutamide doublet for mHSPC (previously validated only as a triplet with docetaxel in ARASENS).

records.title: ARASENS
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) · III · 2022
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (~87% de novo) Darolutamide 600 mg twice daily + ADT + 6 cycles docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV Q3W vs placebo + ADT + 6 cycles docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV Q3W; darolutamide to progression Overall survival Adding darolutamide to ADT + docetaxel reduced death by 32.5% (HR 0.68; 4-yr OS 62.7% vs 50.4%); established the darolutamide triplet for fit mHSPC.

records.title: PEACE-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) · III · 2022
records.body: De novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer 2×2 factorial — ± abiraterone 1000 mg once daily + prednisone 5 mg twice daily and ± prostate radiotherapy, added to standard of care (ADT alone or with docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV Q3W); abiraterone to progression Radiographic PFS & overall survival (co-primary) In the ADT + docetaxel population, adding abiraterone improved rPFS (4.5 vs 2.0 years, HR 0.50) and OS (HR 0.75); supported the abiraterone triplet, especially in high-volume disease.

records.title: AMPLITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · III · 2025
records.body: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer with HRR gene alteration (56% BRCA1/2; 78% high-volume) Niraparib + abiraterone-prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone-prednisone Radiographic progression-free survival Adding niraparib to abiraterone in HRR-altered mCSPC improved rPFS in BRCA disease (not reached vs 26 months, HR 0.52) and in the overall HRR population (HR 0.63, P=0.0001); OS immature but trending favourable (HRR HR 0.79). First trial to extend PARP+ARPI into the hormone-sensitive setting; grade >=3 AEs 75% (anaemia 29%).

records.title: CAPItello-281
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · III · 2026
records.body: PTEN-deficient de novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer Capivasertib + abiraterone-prednisone/prednisolone + ADT vs placebo + abiraterone-prednisone/prednisolone + ADT Radiographic progression-free survival In PTEN-deficient mCSPC (25.3% of tested patients), adding the AKT inhibitor capivasertib to abiraterone improved rPFS (33.2 vs 25.7 months, HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66-0.98, P=0.034); OS immature and not yet significant (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.71-1.15). Common AEs with capivasertib were diarrhea (51.9%), hyperglycemia (38.0%) and rash (35.4%). First trial to extend PI3K/AKT-pathway inhibition into the hormone-sensitive setting for a PTEN-deficient biomarker subgroup.

records.title: TALAPRO-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · III · 2026
records.body: HRR gene-altered metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (metastatic APMS), ECOG 0–1 Talazoparib 0.5 mg orally once daily + enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily + ongoing ADT vs placebo + enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily + ongoing ADT; until radiographic progression (continuation permitted if clinically benefiting), unacceptable toxicity, patient decision, or death Investigator-assessed imaging-based progression-free survival Talazoparib added to enzalutamide and ADT improved 3-year imaging-based PFS (77% vs 56%; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.36–0.65; P<0.001). Interim 3-year OS was 78% vs 72% (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.56–1.04). Serious adverse events were more frequent (42% vs 32%); grade ≥3 anemia occurred in 51%, with two treatment-related deaths in the talazoparib group.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026; published online May 30

records.title: PSMAddition
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — radioligand therapy (PSMA) · III · 2025
records.body: PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer 177Lu-PSMA-617 + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI Radiographic progression-free survival Adding 177Lu-PSMA-617 to ADT + ARPI improved rPFS (HR 0.72; medians not yet reached) with an early non-significant OS trend (HR 0.84); first phase 3 to extend PSMA radioligand therapy into the hormone-sensitive setting. ESMO 2025 abstract (LBA6) - not yet a full publication.

records.title: STAMPEDE (prostate RT)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · MCSPC — radiotherapy to the primary tumour · III · 2018
records.body: Newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer ADT + prostate radiotherapy vs ADT alone Overall survival Prostate RT did not improve OS overall but improved 3-yr OS in low-metastatic-burden disease (81% vs 73%, HR 0.68); established prostate RT for low-volume mHSPC.

records.title: EMBARK
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · Non-metastatic castration-sensitive — high-risk biochemical recurrence · III · 2023
records.body: High-risk biochemical recurrence (PSA-DT ≤9 mo), non-metastatic Enzalutamide + leuprolide vs leuprolide vs enzalutamide monotherapy Metastasis-free survival Enzalutamide plus leuprolide improved metastasis-free survival versus leuprolide alone: 5-year 87.3% (95% CI 83.0-90.6) versus 71.4% (65.7-76.3), HR 0.42 (0.30-0.61), P<0.001 (primary, alpha-protected). Enzalutamide monotherapy also improved metastasis-free survival as a prespecified secondary: 5-year 80.0% (75.0-84.1), HR 0.63 (0.46-0.87), P=0.005. At the final analysis, enzalutamide plus leuprolide improved overall survival: 8-year 78.9% versus 69.5%, HR 0.60 (0.44-0.80), P<0.001; enzalutamide monotherapy did not improve overall survival: 8-year 73.1% versus 69.5%, HR 0.83 (0.63-1.10), P=0.19. The combination comparison was tested at two-sided alpha 0.0499 and succeeded, licensing the conditional monotherapy test at the same alpha; its negative result is alpha-protected. The enzalutamide arms were not formally compared. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 52.4%, 49.4%, and 57.3%; fractures were 22.4%, 15.0%, and 14.1% in the combination, leuprolide-alone, and monotherapy groups. Established enzalutamide intensification for high-risk biochemical recurrence.

records.title: KEYNOTE-564
records.subtitle: Adjuvant & Metastatic RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2021
records.body: Resected intermediate-high/high-risk or M1 NED clear-cell RCC Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W for up to 17 cycles (~1 year) vs placebo Disease-free survival Adjuvant pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival at the first interim analysis (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.87, P=0.002). Alpha then passed to overall survival, which met its boundary at the third interim analysis: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.44-0.87), P=0.005 against a prespecified two-sided boundary of 0.0144, on 55 of 496 vs 86 of 498 deaths, with 48-month OS 91.2% vs 86.0%. Because the null was rejected there, the analysis plan specifies no further formal OS testing, so this is the trial's definitive alpha-protected survival result. Disease-free survival was not formally tested again, so the more mature HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.59-0.87) reported alongside it carries no alpha and does not supersede the 0.68. The survival gain was achieved despite subsequent anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy in 69.7% of placebo patients who received any systemic therapy vs 41.0% on pembrolizumab. Treatment-related grade 3-4 events 18.6% vs 1.2%, with no death attributed to pembrolizumab. The authors note that no adjuvant VEGFR-TKI has prolonged overall survival and that the adjuvant atezolizumab and nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab trials have not shown a lower risk of death, and conclude that these results support adjuvant pembrolizumab as a standard intervention after surgery in this disease context.

records.title: LITESPARK-005
records.subtitle: Adjuvant & Metastatic RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2024
records.body: Advanced clear-cell RCC after PD-(L)1 and VEGFR-TKI (1-3 prior regimens) Belzutifan 120 mg once daily vs everolimus 10 mg once daily; to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival and overall survival (co-primary) Belzutifan improved centrally reviewed PFS at the first interim analysis despite equal medians of 5.6 months: 18-month PFS was 24.0% vs 8.3% (P=0.002), meeting the prespecified significance criterion; confirmed ORR was 21.9% vs 3.5% (P<0.001). At the second interim analysis, OS did not meet its prespecified significance criterion (21.4 vs 18.1 months, HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.73-1.07; P=0.20).

records.title: TiNivo-2
records.subtitle: Adjuvant & Metastatic RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2024
records.body: Advanced RCC, progression during/after 1–2 prior lines including one ICI Tivozanib 0.89 mg once daily + nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W; to progression vs tivozanib 1.34 mg once daily; to progression PFS by independent radiology review (RECIST 1.1) Median PFS 5.7 vs 7.4 mo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.84–1.43; p=0.49) — NEGATIVE; adding nivolumab (ICI rechallenge) to tivozanib post-ICI provided no PFS benefit. In ICI-immediate-prior subgroup (n=244): PFS 7.4 vs 9.2 mo. SAEs 32% vs 37%; 1 treatment-related death (tivozanib arm). Supports discouraging ICI rechallenge post-progression.

records.title: LenCabo
records.subtitle: Adjuvant & Metastatic RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · II · 2026
records.body: Metastatic ccRCC progressed on prior PD-(L)1 ICI (1–2 prior lines) Lenvatinib 18 mg once daily + everolimus 5 mg once daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg once daily; all to progression PFS (Bayesian optimal phase II design) Median PFS 15.7 vs 10.2 mo (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29–0.89; p=0.02). ORR 52.6% vs 38.6%. OS immature (n=24/86 events; 1-yr OS 87.0% vs 84.6%). Tox-driven discontinuation 20% vs 10.9%. First head-to-head comparison of post-ICI targeted therapies in ccRCC; informs sequencing.

records.title: ESE Guideline (Fassnacht et al.)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · N/A · 2018
records.body: Adrenocortical carcinoma, adults N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A European Society of Endocrinology guideline (with ENSAT) covering diagnosis, staging, and management of adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC). Diagnosis requires histopathology using the Weiss score (>=3 criteria indicates malignancy) plus Ki67 index; SF-1 immunohistochemistry distinguishes adrenocortical from non-adrenocortical tumors. ENSAT staging (I-IV) is recommended, with tumor stage, resection status, Ki67 index, and cortisol excess as key prognostic factors. Surgery: complete en bloc resection by experienced adrenal/oncological surgeons is curative-intent standard; open surgery preferred for tumors with radiological invasion, laparoscopic reasonable for tumors <6cm without invasion. Adjuvant mitotane is suggested for high-risk patients (stage III, R1 resection, or Ki67 >10%); no consensus for low/moderate-risk patients (ongoing ADIUVO trial). Adjuvant radiotherapy considered on individualized basis for R1/Rx resection or stage III. For advanced/metastatic disease: mitotane monotherapy or mitotane plus EDP (etoposide-doxorubicin-cisplatin) per FIRM-ACT trial, based on prognostic parameters — EDP-M significantly improved PFS (5.0 vs 2.1 months, HR 0.55) over mitotane-streptozotocin, though OS difference was not significant (14.8 vs 12.0 months, HR 0.79, p=0.07). Genetic counseling recommended given ~5% germline TP53 (Li-Fraumeni) and ~3% Lynch syndrome association.

records.title: Adjuvant Mitotane (Terzolo)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · N/A · 2007
records.body: Completely resected (R0) adrenocortical carcinoma, adults (Italian + German cohorts) Adjuvant mitotane (titrated to 14–20 mg/L) vs observation (two concurrent control cohorts) Recurrence-free survival (retrospective comparison) Adjuvant mitotane after complete resection prolonged recurrence-free survival vs the two control cohorts (median RFS 42 vs 10 vs 25 months; HR for recurrence 2.91, 95% CI 1.77–4.78, P<0.001, and 1.97, 95% CI 1.21–3.20, P=0.005), confirmed on multivariate analysis. Toxicity mainly grade 1–2; 13% needed temporary dose reduction. Foundation for adjuvant mitotane in resected ACC (caveat: retrospective, non-randomized).

records.title: FIRM-ACT (Fassnacht)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · III · 2012
records.body: Advanced (locally advanced or metastatic) adrenocortical carcinoma, adults EDP — etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 2–4 + doxorubicin 40 mg/m² IV day 1 + cisplatin 40 mg/m² IV days 3–4, Q4W — plus mitotane (titrated to 14–20 mg/L blood level) vs streptozocin 1 g IV days 1–5 in cycle 1 then 2 g IV day 1 Q3W plus mitotane (titrated to 14–20 mg/L); first-line, to progression Progression-free survival (key secondary: overall survival) First-line EDP + mitotane improved response rate (23.2% vs 9.2%, P<0.001) and median PFS (5.0 vs 2.1 months; HR 0.55; 95% CI 0.43–0.69; P<0.001) over streptozocin + mitotane. Overall survival was not significantly different (14.8 vs 12.0 months; HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.61–1.02; P=0.07). Serious adverse-event rates similar between arms. Established EDP + mitotane as the standard first-line regimen for advanced ACC.

records.title: IGCCCG
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · N/A · 1997
records.body: Metastatic germ-cell tumours (5,202 NSGCT + 660 seminoma), first-line cisplatin era Prognostic-factor analysis (primary site, marker levels, non-pulmonary visceral mets) Progression-free & overall survival Defined good / intermediate / poor prognosis groups; 5-yr OS 91% / 79% / 48% (poor risk all NSGCT, including mediastinal primaries). Became the universal risk-stratification framework guiding first-line therapy.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 1997;15:594-603   J Clin Oncol 2001;19:2534-2541 HCG-AFP decline analysis 11331333

records.title: IGCCCG Update
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · N/A · 2021
records.body: Metastatic NSGCT treated 1990-2013 with cisplatin/etoposide first-line chemo Contemporary re-analysis & refined prognostic model Progression-free & overall survival 5-yr OS improved to 96% (good), 89% (intermediate) and 67% (poor, from 48%); PFS 89% / 75% / 54%. Added age, lung metastases and an LDH 2.5x ULN cut-off for finer prognostication.

records.title: MRC TE19 / EORTC 30982
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · III · 2005
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma after orchidectomy Single-dose carboplatin (AUC 7) vs adjuvant radiotherapy Relapse-free rate (non-inferiority) Noninferiority trial in 1477 patients randomised 3:5 (carboplatin 573, radiotherapy 904), powered to exclude an absolute difference greater than 3% in the 2-year relapse-free rate. The 2005 primary analysis (median follow-up 4 years) reported relapse-free rates for radiotherapy vs carboplatin of 96.7% (95% CI 95.3-97.7) vs 97.7% (96.0-98.6) at 2 years and 95.9% (94.4-97.1) vs 94.8% (92.5-96.4) at 3 years, HR 1.28 (90% CI 0.85-1.93, p=0.32; a hazard ratio above 1 favours radiotherapy), with second contralateral germ-cell tumours in 10 radiotherapy vs 2 carboplatin patients. The 2011 mature analysis (median follow-up 6.5 years) confirmed noninferiority - 5-year relapse-free rate 94.7% carboplatin vs 96.0% radiotherapy, HR 1.25 (90% CI 0.83-1.89), the 90% CI for the absolute difference excluding rates above 3% at 2 years and above 3.5% at 5 years - and established a significant reduction in second germ-cell tumours, 2 carboplatin vs 15 radiotherapy (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.05-0.95, P=.03). Established one cycle of carboplatin as an adjuvant alternative to radiotherapy.
records.keywords: Lancet 2005;366:293-300   J Clin Oncol 2011;29:957-962 mature results 21282539 J Natl Cancer Inst 2011;103:241-249 pooled relapse-pattern analysis (TE10/TE18/TE19) 21212385

records.title: MRC TE18 / EORTC 30942
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · III · 2005
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma, adjuvant radiotherapy Para-aortic RT 20 Gy/10 fractions vs 30 Gy/15 fractions Relapse rate (non-inferiority) 20 Gy non-inferior to 30 Gy: 11 vs 10 relapses (HR 1.11), 2-yr relapse-rate difference 0.7%, with less acute lethargy and faster return to work. Established 20 Gy as the standard adjuvant RT dose when RT is used.

records.title: Carboplatin de-escalation (van de Wetering)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · N/A · 2018
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma after orchidectomy N/A — opinion (surveillance vs adjuvant carboplatin / radiotherapy) N/A Argues surveillance should be the default for most compliant CS I seminoma patients, and that adjuvant carboplatin and radiotherapy — validated only in unselected populations — are now overused. Notes ~15% relapse on surveillance with near-100% salvage success, questioning routine adjuvant treatment. Influential de-escalation viewpoint from Erasmus MC / MSKCC germ-cell authorities.

records.title: SGCCG nomogram (Aparicio)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · N/A · 2014
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma after orchidectomy, risk-adapted (surveillance for low-risk, adjuvant carboplatin for high-risk) N/A — pooled analysis of three prospective risk-adapted CS I seminoma studies (surveillance vs two cycles adjuvant carboplatin); relapse-nomogram derivation Disease-free (relapse-free) survival; derivation of a relapse-prediction nomogram Pooled analysis of 744 clinical stage I seminoma patients (median follow-up 80 months): 63 relapses (11.1%) — 14.8% on surveillance vs 3.2% after adjuvant carboplatin (P=0.0001); 5-year disease-free survival 92.3% (88.3% surveillance vs 96.8% carboplatin) with 100% cause-specific survival. A surveillance-derived nomogram identified rete testis invasion and tumour size (continuous) as the independent predictors of relapse, supporting individualised rather than universal adjuvant carboplatin. A prognostic tool requiring prospective validation, not a treatment comparison.

records.title: SWENOTECA seminoma (Tandstad)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · N/A · 2011
