records.body: Testicular seminoma of any clinical stage after orchidectomy; binational population-based SWENOTECA V cohort 2000-2006, 86% clinical stage I CS1 by protocol choice: surveillance, adjuvant RT 25.2 Gy, or one course carboplatin AUC 7; CS2A RT 27 Gy; CS2B and above EP or BEP x4 (non-randomised) Relapse-free interval (none declared primary) Population-based confirmation that clinical stage I seminoma is curable by any of three strategies: relapse-free interval 85.7% on surveillance, 96.1% after one course of carboplatin and 99.2% after adjuvant radiotherapy, with 5-yr cause-specific survival 99.6% across all 1384 men at a median 5.2 yr. Carboplatin follow-up was the shortest at a median 3.4 yr, against a latest relapse anywhere in the study at 7.0 yr. The Cox estimate favouring radiotherapy over carboplatin (HR 4.7, 95% CI 1.1-14.4) is adjusted for the imbalanced vascular invasion and tumour size but not for rete testis invasion, which was not recorded, so it compares chosen treatments rather than randomised ones. No stage IIA/B patient given chemotherapy relapsed (0/73) against 3 of 29 after stage IIA radiotherapy. SWENOTECA has since abandoned adjuvant radiotherapy as a recommended option over late second-cancer risk.

records.title: AUO AH 01/94 (GTCSG)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I non-seminoma · III · 2008
records.body: Clinical stage I non-seminoma after orchidectomy One course of adjuvant BEP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + bleomycin 30,000 IU (30 mg) IV days 1, 8, 15 (single cycle) vs nerve-sparing retroperitoneal lymph-node dissection (RPLND) Recurrence rate One cycle of BEP markedly reduced recurrence vs RPLND (2 vs 15 events; 2-yr recurrence-free survival 99.5% vs 91.9%, HR 7.9 favouring BEP). Established single-cycle adjuvant BEP as superior to community-standard RPLND.

records.title: SWENOTECA
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I non-seminoma · N/A · 2014
records.body: Clinical stage I non-seminoma, risk-adapted by lymphovascular invasion (LVI) One course of adjuvant BEP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV daily days 1–5 + bleomycin 30 mg IV days 1, 5, 15 (single cycle) vs surveillance (offered to LVI-negative patients) Relapse rate After one course of adjuvant BEP, 5-yr relapse was only 3.2% (LVI+) and 1.6% (LVI-) with 100% cause-specific survival. Confirmed one BEP cycle as standard for CS I non-seminoma, especially with LVI.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2014;25:2167-2172   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:2122-2128 SWENOTECA NSGCT management program 19307506

records.title: Spanish GCCG (Garcia-del-Muro)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage II seminoma · N/A · 2008
records.body: Stage IIA (nodes <2 cm) or IIB (2-5 cm) pure testicular seminoma after orchidectomy, at diagnosis (82%) or relapsing on stage I surveillance (18%) Cisplatin-based chemotherapy: E400P (etoposide-cisplatin) x4 in 83% or BE500P x3 in 17% (single-arm) Progression-free and overall survival Chemotherapy alone controlled most stage IIA/IIB seminoma without irradiating the retroperitoneum: 5-yr progression-free survival 90% (95% CI 82-98) and overall survival 95% (89-100) at a median 71.5 mo, with complete response in 60 of 72 and no failure of first-line treatment. All 6 relapses followed E400P, the reduced-etoposide schedule 83% received and which the authors recommend against, advising 3 cycles of BE500P or 4 of E500P instead. All 6 were stage IIB and no stage IIA patient relapsed. Two men who had never received radiotherapy developed oesophageal carcinoma at 2 and 4 yr and died of it, and 3 of the 4 deaths were not from seminoma. Observational and single-arm - no comparison against radiotherapy was made despite the title, and no late toxicity was reported at this follow-up with no systematic late-effects assessment performed.

records.title: Williams (Intergroup)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 1987
records.body: Disseminated germ-cell tumours, first-line Cisplatin/bleomycin + etoposide (BEP) vs + vinblastine (PVB) Disease-free response & survival Substituting etoposide for vinblastine gave equal-to-higher disease-free rates (83% vs 74% in advanced disease) with markedly less neuromuscular toxicity. Established BEP as the standard first-line regimen.

records.title: Loehrer (ECOG)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 1995
records.body: Good-risk (minimal/moderate) disseminated germ-cell tumours 3 cycles EP vs 3 cycles BEP (testing bleomycin) Failure-free survival Omitting bleomycin worsened outcomes: failure-free survival 69% vs 86% and OS 86% vs 95% (both P=.01). Confirmed bleomycin is essential when only three cycles are given for good-risk disease.

records.title: EORTC/MRC (de Wit)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 2001
records.body: Good-prognosis metastatic germ-cell cancer (IGCCCG) 2×2 factorial: 3 vs 4 cycles of BEP, and 5-day vs 3-day schedule. Per cycle — etoposide 500 mg/m² (100 mg/m² days 1–5 [5-day] or 165 mg/m² days 1–3 [3-day]) + cisplatin 100 mg/m² (20 mg/m² days 1–5 or 50 mg/m² days 1–2) + bleomycin 30 mg weekly (days 1, 8, 15, cycles 1–3) Progression-free survival (equivalence) Three cycles of BEP equivalent to four (2-yr PFS 90.4% vs 89.4%) and a 3-day schedule equalled 5-day. Established 3xBEP as the good-risk standard, reducing cumulative toxicity.

records.title: Horwich (MRC/EORTC)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 1997
records.body: Good-prognosis metastatic nonseminomatous germ-cell cancer (MRC/EORTC criteria), testicular primary Bleomycin 30 U IV day 2 + etoposide 120 mg/m² IV days 1–3 + cisplatin 100 mg/m² IV (divided over 2 or 5 days), Q3W ×4 cycles (BEP) vs the same schedule with carboplatin AUC 5 IV replacing cisplatin (CEB) Failure-free survival (equivalence design) Randomised MRC/EORTC trial (N=598) in good-prognosis metastatic NSGCT: substituting carboplatin (CEB) for cisplatin (BEP) was inferior — 1-year failure-free rate 77% vs 91% (HR 2.75, 95% CI 1.88–4.03; P<0.001) and 3-year survival 90% vs 97% (HR 2.65, 95% CI 1.39–5.05; P=0.003), with complete response 87.3% vs 94.4% (P=0.009). Established that carboplatin should not replace cisplatin in curative first-line germ-cell chemotherapy.

records.title: GETUG T93BP (Culine)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 2007
records.body: Good-risk metastatic nonseminomatous germ-cell tumour (Institut Gustave Roussy model; IGCCCG good-risk), testicular/retroperitoneal primary Bleomycin 30 IU IV days 1, 8, 15 + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cisplatin 20 mg/m² IV days 1–5, Q3W ×3 cycles (BEP) vs etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cisplatin 20 mg/m² IV days 1–5, Q3W ×4 cycles (EP, bleomycin omitted) Favorable response rate (equivalence design) Randomised GETUG trial (N=270) in good-risk metastatic NSGCT: 3×BEP and 4×EP produced similar favorable-response rates (94.7% vs 96.8%; P=0.34). Non-significant trends favoured 3×BEP for 4-year event-free survival (91% vs 86%; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.29–1.19; P=0.135) and overall survival (96% vs 92%; HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.15–1.20; P=0.096), but the trial was underpowered for survival. 3×BEP is the treatment of choice, with 4×EP reserved for a bleomycin contraindication.

records.title: Nichols (Intergroup)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — intermediate & poor prognosis · III · 1998
records.body: Advanced intermediate/poor-risk disseminated germ-cell tumours 4 courses of BEP vs VIP at 3-week intervals. BEP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + bleomycin 30 U IV weekly ×12 weeks. VIP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 75 mg/m² + ifosfamide 1.2 g/m² IV days 1–5 (mesna uroprotection) Failure-free survival VIP and BEP gave equivalent efficacy (2-yr FFS 64% vs 60%, OS 74% vs 71%) but VIP was more myelotoxic. Kept 4xBEP as standard; VIP reserved for patients in whom bleomycin is contraindicated.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 1998;16:1287-1293   Cancer 2003;97:1869-1875 final analysis 12673712

records.title: GETUG-13
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — intermediate & poor prognosis · III · 2014
records.body: Poor-prognosis NSGCT with unfavourable tumour-marker decline after 1 cycle BEP Dose-dense intensified regimen vs continued standard BEP (marker-guided) Progression-free survival Switching unfavourable-decline patients to a dose-dense regimen improved 3-yr PFS (59% vs 48%, HR 0.66) and cut the need for salvage high-dose chemo (6% vs 16%). Established marker-decline-guided intensification for poor-prognosis disease.

records.title: Kondagunta (MSKCC) TIP
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · II · 2005
records.body: First relapse, favourable-risk (testis primary + prior CR to first-line) Paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin (TIP) x4 cycles Complete response & PFS Four cycles of TIP achieved 70% complete response, 63% durable CR and 65% 2-yr PFS. Established TIP as a standard conventional-dose first-salvage regimen for favourable-risk relapse.

records.title: Einhorn (Indiana) HDCT
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · N/A · 2007
records.body: Relapsed/refractory metastatic germ-cell tumours (mostly second-line) Two sequential cycles high-dose carboplatin + etoposide with PBSC rescue Durable complete remission Tandem high-dose carboplatin/etoposide gave durable disease-free status in 116/184 (63%), including 18/40 platinum-refractory patients. Established high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue as a curative salvage option.

records.title: TI-CE (Feldman, MSKCC)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · II · 2010
records.body: Relapsed germ-cell tumours with unfavourable salvage-risk features TI-CE: paclitaxel/ifosfamide then high-dose carboplatin/etoposide x3 + PBSC Disease-free survival TI-CE produced 5-yr DFS 47% and OS 52% in poor-risk relapse; mediastinal primary and >=2 prior lines predicted worse outcome. Validated TI-CE high-dose chemotherapy for unfavourable-risk salvage.

records.title: CLIMATE (ANZUP 1906)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Post-chemotherapy management & biomarkers · N/A · 2026
records.body: Clinical stage I testicular germ-cell tumour, post-orchidectomy MRD assessment Plasma miR-371a-3p detectable vs undetectable (observational cohort) Recurrence-free survival Detectable post-orchidectomy plasma miR-371a-3p strongly predicted relapse (HR 10.3, 95% CI 5.3-19.8; 20% of the cohort relapsed), outperforming conventional markers. Positions miR-371 as an MRD tool to refine adjuvant decisions (not yet standard of care).

records.title: RTOG 90-01 (Morris)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1999
records.body: High-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO IIB-IVA, or IB-IIA ≥5 cm/node+) Pelvic RT + concurrent cisplatin/5-FU vs extended-field (pelvic + para-aortic) RT Overall survival Concurrent chemoradiation improved 5-year OS (73% vs 58%, HR for death 0.52) and reduced local failure and distant metastases; helped establish cisplatin-based chemoradiation as standard.

records.title: GOG 120 (Rose)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1999
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer, FIGO IIB-IVA Cisplatin-based chemoradiation (cisplatin or cisplatin/5-FU/hydroxyurea) vs hydroxyurea + RT Progression-free survival Cisplatin-containing chemoradiation improved PFS and OS vs hydroxyurea (relative risk of progression 0.57 and 0.55 for the cisplatin arms); weekly cisplatin became the standard radiosensitizer.

records.title: GOG 123 (Keys)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1999
records.body: Bulky stage IB2 cervical carcinoma (tumor ≥4 cm), pre-hysterectomy Weekly cisplatin + RT vs RT alone, both followed by adjuvant hysterectomy Progression-free survival Adding weekly cisplatin to RT reduced risk of progression (RR 0.51) and death (RR 0.54), with significantly higher 4-year PFS and OS; cemented concurrent cisplatin for bulky early-stage disease.

records.title: CCCMAC (IPD meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · N/A · 2008
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer across 18 randomized chemoradiation trials (individual patient data) Concurrent chemoradiation vs radiotherapy alone Overall survival Chemoradiation improved 5-year OS by 6% (66% vs 60%, HR 0.81) and DFS by 8%, with benefit greatest for platinum-based regimens; confirmed chemoradiation as the standard of care.

records.title: OUTBACK (GOG-0274)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · III · 2023
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer after primary cisplatin-based chemoradiation Adjuvant carboplatin + paclitaxel after chemoradiation vs chemoradiation alone Overall survival Adjuvant chemotherapy did not improve 5-year OS (72% vs 71%, HR 0.90) and added toxicity; sequential adjuvant chemotherapy should not be given after chemoradiation.

records.title: INTERLACE (GCIG)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · III · 2024
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2008 IB1 node+ to IVA) Induction weekly IV carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² for 6 weeks, then standard cisplatin-based chemoradiation (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² for 5 weeks concurrent with external-beam RT plus brachytherapy) vs the same chemoradiation alone Progression-free survival Short induction chemotherapy improved 5-year PFS (72% vs 64%, HR 0.65) and OS (80% vs 72%, HR 0.60); a feasible intensification using existing drugs.

records.title: KEYNOTE-A18 (ENGOT-cx11/GOG-3047)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · III · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2014 III-IVA, or IB2-IIB node+) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×5 cycles concurrent with cisplatin-based chemoradiation (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² + external-beam RT plus brachytherapy), then pembrolizumab 400 mg IV Q6W ×15 cycles vs placebo plus the same chemoradiation Progression-free survival Pembrolizumab added to chemoradiation met both dual primary endpoints, at two different interim analyses. At the first interim analysis progression-free survival improved (2-year PFS 68% vs 57%, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.89, p=0.0020). All alpha then passed to overall survival, tested at the second interim analysis: HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.90; one-sided p=0.0040) against a prespecified boundary of 0.01026, on 75 deaths (14%) vs 109 (21%) at a 76.7% information fraction, median overall survival not reached in either group, 36-month OS 82.6% vs 74.8%; the paper calls this the final, formally tested overall survival result. Progression-free survival was not formally tested again there, so the more mature HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.56-0.84) reported alongside it carries no alpha and does not supersede the 0.70. Potentially immune-mediated adverse events 39% vs 17% (grade >=3 5% vs 1%); grade >=3 treatment-emergent events 78% vs 70%; two treatment-related deaths in each group. The authors conclude that the two analyses together support pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy as a new standard of care.
records.keywords: Lancet 2024;403:1341-1350   Lancet 2024;404:1321-1332 overall survival results, second interim analysis 39288779

records.title: GOG 204 (Monk)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · III · 2009
records.body: Stage IVB, recurrent, or persistent cervical carcinoma, first-line Cisplatin + paclitaxel vs cisplatin + vinorelbine, gemcitabine, or topotecan Overall survival No doublet was superior to cisplatin/paclitaxel (median OS ~12.9 months), with trends favoring it; established cisplatin/paclitaxel as the chemotherapy backbone.

records.title: GOG 240 (Tewari)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · III · 2014
records.body: Recurrent, persistent, or metastatic cervical cancer, first-line Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone (2×2 factorial), chemo being cisplatin 50 mg/m² + paclitaxel 135–175 mg/m² or topotecan 0.75 mg/m² days 1–3 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m²; 21-day cycles to progression Overall survival Adding bevacizumab improved OS (17.0 vs 13.3 months, HR 0.71) and PFS (8.2 vs 5.9 months); the first antiangiogenic and first survival gain in this setting.

records.title: JCOG0505 (Kitagawa)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · III · 2015
records.body: Metastatic or recurrent cervical cancer, first-line (Japan; JCOG) Paclitaxel + carboplatin (TC) vs paclitaxel + cisplatin (TP) Overall survival (non-inferiority) Non-inferiority met: median OS 17.5 (TC) vs 18.3 (TP) months (HR 0.994, 90% CI 0.789-1.253). In cisplatin-naive patients OS favoured TP (23.2 vs 13.0 months). Established carboplatin-paclitaxel as a convenient standard except in cisplatin-naive disease.

records.title: KEYNOTE-826 (Colombo)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer, first-line Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to 35 cycles + platinum doublet (paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5, capped at 6 cycles) ± bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W (investigator's discretion) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy ± bevacizumab Progression-free and overall survival Pembrolizumab improved PFS (10.4 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.65) and OS (HR 0.67; final median 26.4 vs 16.8 months); established first-line chemo-immunotherapy.

records.title: BEATcc (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Metastatic, persistent, or recurrent cervical cancer, first-line Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W added to bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + platinum–paclitaxel (cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m², day 1 Q3W) vs the same bevacizumab + platinum–paclitaxel alone; treatment to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Atezolizumab improved PFS (13.7 vs 10.4 months, HR 0.62) and OS (32.1 vs 22.8 months, HR 0.68); a bevacizumab-containing chemo-immunotherapy option regardless of PD-L1.

records.title: COMPASSION-16
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer (China; regardless of PD-L1) Cadonilimab (PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) + platinum chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab vs placebo + chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab Progression-free and overall survival (dual) At prespecified interim analyses, cadonilimab improved PFS (12.7 vs 8.1 months, stratified HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49–0.80, p<0.0001 against a boundary of 0.0005) and OS (not reached vs 22.8 months, HR 0.64, 0.48–0.86, p=0.0011 against 0.006), the OS interim firing at 193 of the 290 deaths required for the final analysis. Bevacizumab was optional and used by 60%; the trial reports both strata with no interaction test — without bevacizumab PFS HR 0.46 (0.32–0.66) and OS 0.50 (0.33–0.75), with bevacizumab 0.81 (0.58–1.13) and 0.84 (0.56–1.26) — and the authors conclude benefit “regardless of the use of bevacizumab”, speculating only that it might suit those not eligible for it. No treatment-by-PD-L1 interaction test is reported either, so PD-L1 consistency is directional only. Conducted wholly in China; adverse events led to discontinuation in 28% vs 11%. At publication the NMPA approval covered cadonilimab monotherapy at second line or later, not this first-line combination.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (Chung)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · II · 2019
records.body: Previously treated advanced cervical cancer (cervical cohort) Single-arm pembrolizumab monotherapy Objective response rate ORR 14.3% overall and 14.6% in PD-L1+ (CPS ≥1) tumors with durable responses; led to accelerated approval for PD-L1+ pretreated disease.

records.title: EMPOWER-Cervical 1 (GOG-3016)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · III · 2022
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after first-line platinum Cemiplimab vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy Overall survival Cemiplimab improved OS (12.0 vs 8.5 months, HR 0.69) regardless of PD-L1 or histology; validated checkpoint blockade as a second-line standard.

records.title: innovaTV 204 (GOG-3023/ENGOT-cx6)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · II · 2021
records.body: Previously treated recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer Single-arm tisotumab vedotin (tissue factor-directed ADC) Objective response rate Confirmed ORR 24% (7% complete) with median DOR 8.3 months; supported accelerated approval of the first ADC in cervical cancer.

records.title: innovaTV 301 (ENGOT-cx12)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · III · 2024
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after 1-2 prior lines Tisotumab vedotin (tissue factor-directed ADC) 2.0 mg/kg IV Q3W vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy (topotecan, vinorelbine, gemcitabine, irinotecan, or pemetrexed); to progression Overall survival Tisotumab vedotin improved OS (11.5 vs 9.5 months, HR 0.70) and PFS (4.2 vs 2.9 months); confirmatory phase 3 converting accelerated to full approval.

records.title: CheckMate 358 (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · I-II · 2024
records.body: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell cervical carcinoma, ≤2 prior systemic therapies (first- and later-line) Nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W (monotherapy); or nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q6W; or nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W; treatment to progression, toxicity, or 24 months Investigator-assessed objective response rate Multicohort phase 1–2 trial (176 treated of 193 enrolled; 90 randomised between the two combination regimens): objective response rate 26% (5/19) with nivolumab monotherapy, 31% (14/45) with NIVO3+IPI1, and 38% (43/112) with pooled NIVO1+IPI3 (40% in the randomised NIVO1+IPI3 group), with durable responses seen regardless of PD-L1 status. Serious treatment-related AEs were 16%, 27%, and 42% respectively, with one treatment-related death (immune-mediated colitis). Signal-generating support for chemotherapy-free dual immunotherapy; no randomised comparator arm, so hypothesis-generating rather than practice-defining.

records.title: EORTC 55971 (Vergote)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2010
records.body: Bulky stage IIIC-IV epithelial ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer Neoadjuvant chemotherapy + interval debulking surgery vs primary debulking surgery + chemotherapy Overall survival NACT + interval debulking was non-inferior to primary debulking (median OS 30 vs 29 months, HR for death 0.98; PFS ~12 months in both) with less perioperative morbidity; validated NACT for bulky disease.

records.title: CHORUS (Kehoe)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2015
records.body: Newly diagnosed FIGO stage III-IV ovarian cancer Primary chemotherapy (NACT) + interval surgery vs primary surgery + chemotherapy Overall survival Primary chemotherapy was non-inferior to primary surgery (median OS 24.1 vs 22.6 months, HR 0.87) with fewer postoperative adverse events and deaths; confirmed NACT as an alternative standard.

records.title: SCORPION (Fagotti)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2020
records.body: Stage IIIC-IV ovarian cancer with high tumor load Primary debulking surgery vs neoadjuvant chemotherapy + interval debulking Progression-free survival & perioperative complications Similar PFS (15 vs 14 months) and OS (41 vs 43 months) between arms, but NACT gave higher complete resection (77% vs 48%) and fewer major complications (8% vs 26%); supports NACT for high tumor burden.

records.title: LION (Harter)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2019
records.body: Advanced ovarian cancer, macroscopically complete resection, clinically normal nodes Systematic pelvic/para-aortic lymphadenectomy vs no lymphadenectomy at primary surgery Overall survival Lymphadenectomy did not improve OS (65.5 vs 69.2 months, HR 1.06) or PFS and increased complications and mortality; abandoned routine nodal dissection in this setting.

records.title: JCOG0602 (Onda)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2016
records.body: Stage III/IV ovarian, tubal, and peritoneal cancer Upfront primary debulking surgery (PDS) + 8 cycles TC vs neoadjuvant chemo (4 cycles TC) then interval debulking surgery then 4 more cycles TC Treatment invasiveness (surgical morbidity); non-inferiority for OS reported separately Neoadjuvant-chemo arm required fewer surgeries, shorter operating time, less blood loss, and fewer grade 3-4 postoperative complications than upfront debulking; this invasiveness report preceded the planned survival non-inferiority analysis.

records.title: GOG-0213 (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · III · 2019
records.body: First platinum-sensitive recurrence, investigator-judged resectable Secondary surgical cytoreduction + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone Overall survival Secondary cytoreduction did not prolong OS (50.6 vs 64.7 months, HR 1.29) despite 67% complete resection; questioned routine secondary surgery in unselected relapse.

records.title: DESKTOP III (Harter/Du Bois)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · III · 2021
records.body: First platinum-sensitive relapse, positive AGO score (predicting complete resection) Secondary cytoreductive surgery + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone Overall survival Surgery improved OS (53.7 vs 46.0 months, HR 0.75) and PFS (18.4 vs 14.0 months); complete resection reached 61.9-month OS, supporting surgery in AGO-score-selected patients.

records.title: SOC-1 (Shi)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · III · 2021
records.body: First platinum-sensitive relapse, iModel/PET-selected resectable disease Secondary cytoreduction + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone Progression-free and overall survival Surgery prolonged PFS (17.4 vs 11.9 months, HR 0.58); interim OS numerically higher (58.1 vs 53.9 months, HR 0.82), reinforcing benefit with careful selection.

records.title: GOG 111 (McGuire)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 1996
records.body: Suboptimally debulked stage III-IV ovarian cancer, first-line Cisplatin + paclitaxel vs cisplatin + cyclophosphamide Overall survival Paclitaxel improved OS (38 vs 24 months, HR 0.61) and PFS (18 vs 13 months); established paclitaxel-platinum as the first-line standard.

records.title: GOG 158 (Ozols)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2003
records.body: Optimally debulked stage III ovarian cancer, first-line Carboplatin + paclitaxel vs cisplatin + paclitaxel Progression-free survival Carboplatin/paclitaxel was equivalent (median PFS 20.7 vs 19.4 months, HR 0.88; comparable OS) with markedly less toxicity; became the universal chemotherapy backbone.

records.title: GOG 172 (Armstrong)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2006
records.body: Optimally debulked stage III ovarian cancer, first-line IV paclitaxel 135 mg/m² (24-h infusion) day 1 + IP cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 2 + IP paclitaxel 60 mg/m² day 8, Q3W × 6 vs IV paclitaxel 135 mg/m² (24-h infusion) day 1 + IV cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 2, Q3W × 6 Overall survival Intraperitoneal therapy improved OS (65.6 vs 49.7 months, HR 0.75) and PFS (23.8 vs 18.3 months) at the cost of toxicity; prompted an NCI clinical alert favoring IP chemotherapy.

records.title: JGOG 3016 (Katsumata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2009
records.body: Stage II-IV ovarian cancer (Japanese), first-line Dose-dense paclitaxel 80 mg/m² (1-h infusion) on days 1, 8, 15 + carboplatin AUC 6 day 1, Q3W × 6 vs conventional paclitaxel 180 mg/m² (3-h infusion) day 1 + carboplatin AUC 6 day 1, Q3W × 6 Progression-free survival Dose-dense paclitaxel improved PFS (28.0 vs 17.2 months, HR 0.71) and OS; benefit was not reproduced in later Western trials (GOG-262, ICON8, MITO-7).

records.title: MITO-7 (Pignata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2014
records.body: FIGO stage IC-IV advanced ovarian cancer, chemo-naive Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 60 mg/m² for 18 consecutive weeks vs carboplatin AUC 6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² Q3W × 6 PFS and quality of life (FACT-O/TOI), co-primary No PFS difference (17.3 vs 18.3 months, HR 0.96); weekly schedule had a more stable QoL trajectory and less grade 3-4 neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and neuropathy.

records.title: GOG-262 (Chan)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2016
records.body: Advanced (stage III/IV) epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer; bevacizumab optional (84% opted in) Weekly (dose-dense) paclitaxel + carboplatin vs every-3-week paclitaxel + carboplatin Progression-free survival ITT PFS 14.7 (weekly) vs 14.0 months (q3wk) (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74-1.06, p=0.18) - not significant. In patients not receiving bevacizumab, weekly paclitaxel improved PFS (14.2 vs 10.3 months, HR 0.62); no benefit among bevacizumab users (interaction p=0.047).

records.title: ICON8 (Clamp)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed stage IC-IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer (immediate or delayed primary surgery) 3-weekly carboplatin-paclitaxel (group 1) vs weekly dose-dense paclitaxel (groups 2 and 3) Progression-free survival No PFS benefit from weekly dose-dense paclitaxel: median PFS 17.7 (group 1) vs 20.8 (group 2) vs 21.0 months (group 3) (log-rank p=0.35 and 0.51). Confirms lack of dose-dense benefit in a predominantly non-Asian population.

records.title: GOG 218 (Burger)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · III · 2011
records.body: Newly diagnosed stage III (incompletely resected)-IV ovarian cancer Carboplatin–paclitaxel Q3W × 6 in all arms; bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W from cycle 2 — through cycle 6 only (bevacizumab-initiation) or continued to cycle 22 / ~15 months (bevacizumab-throughout) vs chemotherapy + placebo Progression-free survival Bevacizumab throughout improved PFS (14.1 vs 10.3 months, HR 0.72) but not OS; introduced antiangiogenic maintenance to front-line therapy.

records.title: ICON7 (Perren)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · III · 2011
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk early or advanced ovarian cancer Carboplatin–paclitaxel Q3W × 6 + bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV Q3W concurrently, then continued for 12 further cycles (~12 months) or to progression vs chemotherapy alone Progression-free survival Bevacizumab improved PFS (19.0 vs 17.3 months, HR 0.81); final analysis showed an OS benefit confined to the high-risk-of-progression subgroup.

records.title: SOLO-1 (Moore)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2018
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer with BRCA1/2 mutation, in response to platinum Maintenance olaparib 300 mg twice daily (tablets), continued to progression or a maximum of 2 years vs placebo Progression-free survival Olaparib dramatically prolonged PFS (median not reached vs 13.8 months, HR 0.30); established first-line PARP maintenance for BRCA-mutated disease.

records.title: PRIMA (González-Martín)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer responding to platinum (all-comers) Maintenance niraparib vs placebo Progression-free survival Niraparib improved PFS overall (13.8 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.62) with greatest benefit in HRD-positive disease (21.9 vs 10.4 months, HR 0.43); extended PARP maintenance regardless of biomarker.

records.title: PAOLA-1 (Ray-Coquard)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer receiving first-line bevacizumab Maintenance olaparib 300 mg twice daily (tablets) for up to 24 months + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W for up to 15 months total vs placebo + bevacizumab Progression-free survival Adding olaparib improved PFS (22.1 vs 16.6 months, HR 0.59), with marked benefit in HRD-positive tumors (37.2 vs 17.7 months, HR 0.33); established the olaparib-bevacizumab combination.

records.title: ATHENA-MONO (Monk)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2022
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer responding to platinum (all-comers) Maintenance rucaparib 600 mg twice daily, continued to progression, toxicity, or a maximum of 24 months vs placebo Progression-free survival Rucaparib improved PFS in the ITT population (20.2 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.52) and HRD subgroup (28.7 vs 11.3 months, HR 0.47); confirmed broad first-line PARP maintenance benefit.

records.title: DUO-O
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2026
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer without a tumour BRCA mutation (non-tBRCAm) Chemo + durvalumab + bevacizumab → durvalumab + bevacizumab + olaparib maintenance vs chemo + bevacizumab → bevacizumab Progression-free survival The durvalumab + bevacizumab + olaparib regimen improved PFS in non-tBRCAm disease - HRD-positive 37.3 vs 23.0 months (HR 0.49) and non-tBRCAm ITT 24.2 vs 19.3 months (HR 0.63); the durvalumab-only arm was not significant (HR 0.87) and interim OS showed no benefit (HR 0.95). An intensive IO-containing first-line option; OS immature/negative to date.

records.title: Study 19 (Ledermann)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · II · 2012
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed high-grade serous ovarian cancer in response to platinum Maintenance olaparib vs placebo Progression-free survival Olaparib prolonged PFS (8.4 vs 4.8 months, HR 0.35), with the greatest benefit in BRCA-mutated patients; first proof of concept for PARP maintenance in relapse.

records.title: SOLO-2 (Pujade-Lauraine)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer with BRCA1/2 mutation Maintenance olaparib (tablets) vs placebo Progression-free survival Olaparib prolonged investigator-assessed progression-free survival, the alpha-protected primary endpoint (19.1 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.22-0.41, p<0.0001). The 2021 final analysis reported a 12.9-month median overall-survival gain (51.7 vs 38.8 months, HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.54-1.00, p=0.054) that did not meet its predefined significance threshold, and which is unadjusted for the 38% of placebo-group patients who received subsequent PARP-inhibitor therapy. Confirmed PARP maintenance for BRCA-mutated relapse.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1274-1284   Lancet Oncol 2021;22:620-631 final OS analysis 33743851

records.title: NOVA (ENGOT-OV16, Mirza)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2016
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer in response to platinum Maintenance niraparib vs placebo Progression-free survival Niraparib prolonged PFS in the germline-BRCA cohort (21.0 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.27) and the non-germline cohort (9.3 vs 3.9 months, HR 0.45); extended PARP maintenance beyond BRCA.

records.title: ARIEL3 (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer in response to platinum Maintenance rucaparib vs placebo Progression-free survival Rucaparib prolonged PFS in the ITT population (10.8 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.36), the BRCA-mutant (16.6 vs 5.4 months) and HRD/LOH-high subgroups; broadened PARP maintenance options.

records.title: OReO/ENGOT-ov38
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2023
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer, previously treated with one prior PARP inhibitor (analyzed separately in BRCA-mutated and non-BRCA-mutated cohorts) Maintenance olaparib rechallenge 300 mg twice daily (tablets; 250 mg twice daily if prior intolerance), to progression vs placebo Progression-free survival First randomized trial of PARP inhibitor maintenance rechallenge. Olaparib significantly improved PFS vs placebo in both the BRCA-mutated cohort (4.3 vs 2.8 months; HR 0.57, p=0.022) and non-BRCA-mutated cohort (5.3 vs 2.8 months; HR 0.43, p=0.0023). No overall survival benefit was seen in the BRCA-mutated cohort (HR 0.88); OS was immature in the non-BRCA-mutated cohort. No new safety signals. Established a statistically significant, albeit modest, benefit of PARP inhibitor rechallenge regardless of BRCA status.

records.title: OCEANS (Aghajanian)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2012
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian, peritoneal, or tubal cancer Gemcitabine–carboplatin (6, up to 10 cycles) + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W, bevacizumab then continued to progression vs gemcitabine–carboplatin + placebo Progression-free survival Bevacizumab prolonged PFS (12.4 vs 8.4 months, HR 0.48) without an OS benefit; an option for platinum-sensitive relapse.

records.title: GOG-0213 bevacizumab (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer (chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab randomisation) Paclitaxel-carboplatin + bevacizumab then bevacizumab maintenance vs paclitaxel-carboplatin alone Overall survival Median OS 42.2 vs 37.3 months (HR 0.829, 95% CI 0.683-1.005, p=0.056; sensitivity analysis on audited stratification HR 0.823, 95% CI 0.680-0.996, p=0.0447). Bevacizumab with second-line platinum doublet improved outcomes in platinum-sensitive relapse.

records.title: MITO-16b/MaNGO-OV2b (Pignata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2021
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer previously treated with first-line bevacizumab (>=6 months since last platinum) Carboplatin-based doublet + bevacizumab (beyond-progression rechallenge) vs carboplatin-based doublet alone Progression-free survival Median PFS 11.8 vs 8.8 months (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.41-0.65, p<0.0001). Re-introducing bevacizumab beyond progression after first-line bevacizumab improves PFS in platinum-sensitive relapse.

records.title: AURELIA (Pujade-Lauraine)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2014
records.body: Platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer Single-agent chemotherapy (investigator's choice: weekly paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or topotecan) ± bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV Q2W (or 15 mg/kg Q3W with 3-weekly topotecan), to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Bevacizumab prolonged PFS (6.7 vs 3.4 months, HR 0.48) and raised ORR (27% vs 12%); first agent to improve outcomes in platinum-resistant disease.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2014;32:1302-1308   Ann Oncol 2017;28:1842-1848 OS exploratory analysis 28481967 J Clin Oncol 2015;33:3836-3838 chemotherapy-cohort analysis 26282651

records.title: MIRASOL (Moore)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2023
records.body: Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer with high folate receptor-α (FRα) expression Mirvetuximab soravtansine 6 mg/kg (adjusted ideal body weight) IV Q3W, to progression or toxicity vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy (weekly paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or topotecan) Progression-free survival Mirvetuximab improved PFS (5.6 vs 4.0 months, P<0.001; restricted mean PFS at 12 months 6.13 vs 4.72 months - the paper reports no intention-to-treat hazard ratio for progression-free survival), OS (16.46 vs 12.75 months, HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.50-0.89, P=0.005) and ORR (42% vs 16%); first ADC to improve survival in platinum-resistant disease.

records.title: ROSELLA (GOG-3073/ENGOT-ov72)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2025
records.body: Platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian/peritoneal/tubal cancer, <=3 prior lines, prior bevacizumab Relacorilant 150 mg orally the day before, of, and after each nab-paclitaxel dose + nab-paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle vs nab-paclitaxel monotherapy 100 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8, 15 Q4W Progression-free and overall survival (dual) Adding relacorilant to nab-paclitaxel improved PFS (6.5 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.70) and, at interim analysis, OS (16.0 vs 11.5 months, HR 0.69); first-in-class glucocorticoid-receptor antagonist and a new option for platinum-resistant disease.

records.title: Gordon (PLD vs topotecan)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — chemotherapy (platinum-resistant) · III · 2001
records.body: Recurrent epithelial ovarian carcinoma, recurred after or refractory to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² IV Q4W vs topotecan 1.5 mg/m²/day IV on days 1–5 Q3W Response rate, PFS, OS Overall response and PFS similar between arms; in the platinum-sensitive subgroup PLD significantly improved PFS and OS (108 vs 71.1 weeks median OS); topotecan caused more severe hematologic toxicity.

records.title: Mutch (gemcitabine vs PLD)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — chemotherapy (platinum-resistant) · III · 2007
records.body: Platinum-resistant, taxane-pretreated ovarian cancer Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV on days 1 and 8 Q3W vs pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² IV day 1 Q4W PFS No significant difference in PFS (3.6 vs 3.1 months), OS, or response rate; PLD caused more hand-foot syndrome and mucositis, gemcitabine more cytopenias — comparable therapeutic index, gemcitabine an acceptable alternative to PLD.

records.title: ENGOT-ov65/KEYNOTE-B96
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — chemotherapy (platinum-resistant) · III · 2026
records.body: Platinum-resistant recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer, 1-2 prior lines Pembrolizumab 400 mg IV Q6W for up to 18 cycles + weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on days 1, 8, 15 of each 21-day cycle (± bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV Q2W per investigator) vs placebo Q6W + weekly paclitaxel (± bevacizumab) Progression-free survival (key secondary: overall survival) Significantly improved PFS (8.3 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.70, p<0.0001) and overall survival (17.7 vs 14.0 months, HR 0.82, p=0.011) versus paclitaxel alone; greater benefit in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 tumours (OS 18.2 vs 14.0 months, HR 0.76). First phase 3 trial to show an overall survival benefit with immune checkpoint inhibition in ovarian cancer, establishing this regimen as a new standard of care.

records.title: MILO/ENGOT-ov11
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · III · 2020
records.body: Recurrent or persistent low-grade serous ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal carcinoma, 1-3 prior chemotherapy lines (>=1 platinum) Binimetinib 45 mg orally twice daily vs physician's choice chemotherapy (pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, paclitaxel, or topotecan) Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review Stopped early for futility: median PFS by blinded central review 9.1 months with binimetinib vs 10.6 months with physician's choice chemotherapy (HR 1.21, 95% CI 0.79-1.86); grade >=3 adverse events 76% vs 44% and discontinuation for toxicity 31% vs 17%. Post hoc, KRAS mutation was associated with response to binimetinib (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.53-7.66), but the point estimate also favoured KRAS-mutant patients in the chemotherapy arm and no binimetinib-versus-chemotherapy comparison was made in any mutation subgroup.

records.title: GOG-281/LOGS
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · II/III · 2022
records.body: Recurrent low-grade serous ovarian or peritoneal carcinoma, >=1 prior platinum-based regimen Trametinib 2 mg orally once daily vs Physician's choice standard of care (paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, topotecan, letrozole, or tamoxifen); crossover to trametinib permitted at progression Investigator-assessed progression-free survival Trametinib improved investigator-assessed PFS over physician's choice standard of care (median 13.0 vs 7.2 months; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.36-0.64) and response rate (26% vs 6%), establishing MEK inhibition as an active option in recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma. Median overall survival was 37.6 vs 29.2 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.51-1.12), with 68% of the standard-of-care group crossing over to trametinib and no crossover-adjusted analysis reported. Grade >=3 events on trametinib were mainly rash, anaemia and hypertension (13%, 13% and 12%).

records.title: RAMP 201 (ENGOT-OV60/GOG-3052)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · II · 2025
records.body: Recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, >=1 prior platinum line (N = go-forward combination group) Avutometinib 3.2 mg orally twice weekly + defactinib 200 mg orally twice daily, 3 weeks on/1 week off vs Avutometinib 4.0 mg orally twice weekly monotherapy, 3 weeks on/1 week off Objective response rate (confirmed, by BICR) Avutometinib plus defactinib gave a confirmed ORR by blinded independent central review of 31% (95% CI 23-41) in efficacy-evaluable patients, 44% in the KRAS-mutant and 17% in the KRAS wild-type cohort, with median PFS 12.9 months overall and 22.0 versus 12.8 months by KRAS status; the paper reports no interaction test and no formal comparison between cohorts. Median duration of response was 31.1 months among confirmed responders. Grade >=3 treatment-related events were mainly raised creatine phosphokinase (24%), and 10% discontinued for adverse events.

records.title: GOG 3026
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · II · 2026
records.body: Recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma of the ovary, fallopian tube, or peritoneum; centrally confirmed, measurable, no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor Ribociclib 600 mg orally once daily on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle + letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily, to progression or unacceptable toxicity (single-arm) Confirmed objective response rate (investigator-assessed, RECIST 1.1) Ribociclib plus letrozole met its primary endpoint in this single-arm trial: confirmed ORR 30.6% (90% CI 19.9-43.2; 15 of 49) against a prespecified bar of 8 responses, clinical benefit rate 84% and median PFS 14.5 months (90% CI 10.1-28.8) at 37.7 months' median follow-up. Every interval is 90%, following the two-stage design's 10% type I error. Treatment-related grade >=3 neutropenia occurred in 47% and 98% needed at least one dose adjustment, though only 4% discontinued for toxicity. Estrogen receptor status was neither required for entry nor measured.

records.title: PORTEC-1 (Creutzberg)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · III · 2000
records.body: Stage I endometrioid endometrial cancer (intermediate-risk by grade/invasion) Postoperative pelvic EBRT vs observation Locoregional recurrence Pelvic radiotherapy halved 5-year locoregional recurrence (4% vs 14%) but did not improve overall survival (81% vs 85%); shifted many stage I patients to observation and defined the role of RT as local control only.

records.title: GOG 99 (Keys)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Intermediate-risk stage IB-IIB (occult) endometrial cancer Adjuvant pelvic radiotherapy vs observation Cumulative recurrence Pelvic RT reduced 2-year cumulative recurrence (3% vs 12%, HR 0.58) without a significant survival benefit; defined a high-intermediate-risk subgroup (age, grade, LVSI, outer-third invasion) that derives most of the benefit.

records.title: PORTEC-2 (Nout)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · III · 2010
records.body: High-intermediate-risk stage I-IIA endometrial cancer Vaginal brachytherapy vs pelvic EBRT Vaginal recurrence Vaginal brachytherapy was non-inferior for vaginal control (5-year vaginal recurrence 1.8% vs 1.6%) with equal OS and far less gastrointestinal toxicity; established VBT as the adjuvant standard for high-intermediate-risk disease.

records.title: GOG 249 (Randall)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · III · 2019
records.body: High-intermediate / high-risk early-stage endometrial cancer Pelvic RT vs vaginal brachytherapy + carboplatin/paclitaxel Recurrence-free survival Vaginal brachytherapy plus chemotherapy was not superior to pelvic RT for recurrence-free survival (HR 0.92) and produced more pelvic/nodal relapses; pelvic radiotherapy remained a standard for early-stage high-risk disease.

records.title: TCGA (Cancer Genome Atlas)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Molecular classification · N/A · 2013
records.body: Endometrial carcinomas (endometrioid and serous) — integrated genomic analysis Genomic, transcriptomic and proteomic characterization Molecular classification Defined four molecular subgroups — POLE-ultramutated, MSI-hypermutated, copy-number-low, and copy-number-high (serous-like) — with distinct prognoses; the foundation for molecular classification now guiding risk stratification and adjuvant therapy.

records.title: PORTEC-3 molecular (Léon-Castillo)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Molecular classification · III · 2020
records.body: High-risk endometrial cancer with molecular classification (post-hoc) Chemoradiotherapy vs radiotherapy alone, by molecular subgroup Recurrence-free survival p53-abnormal tumors derived significant benefit from adjuvant chemoradiation (5-year RFS 59% vs 36%) while POLE-mutant tumors had excellent outcomes regardless of treatment (RFS ~98%); validated molecular classification for tailoring adjuvant therapy.

records.title: ESGO-ESTRO-ESP Guideline (Concin et al.)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Molecular classification · N/A · 2025
records.body: Endometrial carcinoma, all stages and molecular subtypes N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A Updated ESGO-ESTRO-ESP guideline incorporating the 2023 FIGO staging system, which integrates molecular classification (POLEmut, MMRd, NSMP, p53abn) with anatomic/histologic factors into prognostic risk groups (low, intermediate, high-intermediate, high, uncertain). POLEmut tumors of any stage I-II require no adjuvant therapy (excellent prognosis); p53abn and NSMP high-grade/ER-negative tumors are high-risk regardless of stage. Adjuvant therapy is risk-stratified: no therapy for low risk; vaginal brachytherapy for intermediate risk; external beam RT for high-intermediate risk; concurrent/sequential chemoradiation or chemotherapy alone for high risk, with immune checkpoint inhibitor added to chemotherapy for stage III-IVA MMRd disease. Sentinel lymph node biopsy with ultrastaging is now standard for surgical staging of uterus-confined disease. First-line systemic therapy for unresectable/recurrent disease: immune checkpoint inhibitor (dostarlimab/durvalumab/pembrolizumab) plus carboplatin-paclitaxel for MMRd tumors; carboplatin-paclitaxel alone (with ICI plus PARP inhibitor maintenance as an option) for non-MMRd tumors. Second-line: pembrolizumab-lenvatinib for non-MMRd, ICI monotherapy for MMRd if ICI-naive. Represents the current consensus framework underlying molecular-classification-driven management of PORTEC-3, TCGA, NRG-GY018, RUBY, DUO-E, and AtTEnd already filed on this sheet. Supplementary appendix (filed separately) contains full treatment algorithms, evidence summary tables, and radiotherapy/pathology technical principles.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2025;26:e423-e435   Concin et al. - 2025 - ESGO-ESTRO-ESP Guidelines for Endometrial Carcinoma (Supplementary Appendix)

records.title: GOG 122 (Randall)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Locally advanced — adjuvant chemotherapy ± radiation · III · 2006
records.body: Stage III-IV endometrial cancer, ≤2 cm residual after surgery Doxorubicin/cisplatin (AP) chemotherapy vs whole-abdominal irradiation Overall survival AP chemotherapy improved stage-adjusted 5-year OS (55% vs 42%, HR 0.68) and PFS over whole-abdominal radiation; established systemic chemotherapy as the backbone for advanced disease.

records.title: PORTEC-3 (de Boer)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Locally advanced — adjuvant chemotherapy ± radiation · III · 2018
records.body: High-risk endometrial cancer (stage I grade 3 with risk factors, stage II-III, serous/clear-cell) Radiotherapy 48.6 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions + concurrent cisplatin 50 mg/m² ×2 cycles, then carboplatin (AUC5)–paclitaxel 175 mg/m² Q3W ×4 cycles vs radiotherapy alone (48.6 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions) Overall and failure-free survival At the non-prespecified post-hoc update, chemoradiotherapy versus radiotherapy alone showed 5-year failure-free survival of 76.5% versus 69.1%, adjusted HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.52-0.94), nominal P=0.016, and 5-year overall survival of 81.4% versus 76.1%, adjusted HR 0.70 (0.51-0.97), nominal P=0.034. No alpha was allocated to this update. Stage III and serous analyses were post-hoc exploratory; no formal interaction tests were reported. At 60 months, grade 2 or worse adverse events were 38% (76/201) versus 23% (43/187), driven by sensory neuropathy at 6% (13/201) versus 0/187; grade 3 or worse events were 8% (16/201) versus 5% (10/187), nominal P=0.24.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2018;19:295-309   Lancet Oncol 2019;20:1273-1285 patterns of recurrence and post-hoc survival update 31345626

records.title: GOG 258 (Matei)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Locally advanced — adjuvant chemotherapy ± radiation · III · 2019
records.body: Stage III-IVA endometrial cancer after surgery Cisplatin 50 mg/m² IV days 1 and 29 concurrent with pelvic EBRT (45 Gy / 25 fractions), then carboplatin (AUC5–6)–paclitaxel 175 mg/m² Q3W ×4 cycles vs carboplatin (AUC6)–paclitaxel 175 mg/m² Q3W ×6 cycles alone Relapse-free survival Adding radiation to chemotherapy did not improve relapse-free survival (5-year 59% vs 58%, HR 0.90) despite fewer local/nodal relapses; chemotherapy alone remained the standard backbone for advanced disease.

records.title: KEYNOTE-B21 (Van Gorp)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Locally advanced — adjuvant chemotherapy ± radiation · III · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk endometrial cancer, no residual disease after curative surgery (FIGO I/II non-endometrioid or p53-abnormal; III/IVA any histology) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×6 cycles then 400 mg IV Q6W ×6 cycles + adjuvant carboplatin–paclitaxel ± radiotherapy vs placebo + carboplatin–paclitaxel ± radiotherapy Disease-free survival and overall survival Adjuvant pembrolizumab did not improve DFS in the all-comer population (HR 1.02); benefit was confined to the dMMR subgroup (HR 0.31, 2-yr DFS 92.4% vs 80.2%), with no signal in pMMR (HR 1.20).
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2024;35:968-980   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:251-259 dMMR subgroup analysis 39411812

records.title: GOG 177 (Fleming)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — chemotherapy backbone · III · 2004
records.body: Advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma Paclitaxel + doxorubicin + cisplatin (TAP) vs doxorubicin + cisplatin (AP) Overall survival Adding paclitaxel improved response (57% vs 34%), PFS (8.3 vs 5.3 months) and OS (15.3 vs 12.3 months, HR 0.75); established a taxane-containing standard despite substantial neurotoxicity.

records.title: GOG 209 (Miller)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — chemotherapy backbone · III · 2020
records.body: Advanced (stage III-IV) or recurrent endometrial carcinoma Carboplatin AUC6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² (3-h) day 1 Q3W, up to 7 cycles vs TAP — doxorubicin 45 mg/m² + cisplatin 50 mg/m² day 1, paclitaxel 160 mg/m² day 2, with G-CSF — Q3W, up to 7 cycles Overall survival (non-inferiority) Carboplatin/paclitaxel was non-inferior to TAP for OS (37 vs 41 months, HR 1.00) and PFS (13 vs 14 months) with less toxicity; established carboplatin/paclitaxel as the chemotherapy backbone for the disease.

records.title: GOG-86P
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — chemotherapy backbone · II · 2018
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive stage III/IVA (measurable disease) or stage IVB/recurrent endometrial cancer Phase II — three experimental arms (each ×6 cycles then maintenance to progression) vs historical carboplatin–paclitaxel control (GOG 209): (1) carboplatin–paclitaxel + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W → bevacizumab maintenance; (2) carboplatin–paclitaxel + temsirolimus 25 mg IV days 1 and 8 Q3W → temsirolimus maintenance; (3) ixabepilone 30 mg/m² IV + carboplatin + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W → bevacizumab maintenance Progression-free survival vs. historical control Randomized phase II study testing three novel first-line regimens against historical paclitaxel/carboplatin controls. PFS was not significantly improved in any experimental arm. Overall survival was significantly longer with paclitaxel/carboplatin/bevacizumab versus historical controls (HR 0.71, 92% CI 0.55-0.91), but not with the temsirolimus or ixabepilone-containing arms. An exploratory biomarker analysis (Leslie et al., Gynecol Oncol 2021) found that TP53-mutant tumors derived significant benefit from bevacizumab over temsirolimus (PFS HR 0.48; OS HR 0.61), while TP53 wild-type tumors did not — nominating TP53 status as a candidate predictive biomarker for anti-angiogenic therapy in endometrial cancer.
records.keywords: Gynecol Oncol 2018;150:274-281   Gynecol Oncol 2021;161:113-121 exploratory TP53 biomarker analysis 33541735

records.title: MITO END-2
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — chemotherapy backbone · II · 2019
records.body: Advanced (FIGO III-IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer Carboplatin (AUC5)–paclitaxel 175 mg/m² Q3W ×6–8 cycles + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W, continued as maintenance to progression or toxicity vs carboplatin–paclitaxel alone ×6–8 cycles Progression-free survival Randomized phase II trial testing carboplatin-paclitaxel with or without bevacizumab. PFS was numerically but not significantly longer with bevacizumab (13.7 vs 10.5 months, HR 0.84, p=0.43); overall survival also favored bevacizumab without reaching significance (40.0 vs 29.7 months, HR 0.71, p=0.24). Six-month disease control rate was significantly higher with bevacizumab (90.7% vs 70.4%). Cardiovascular toxicity (hypertension, thromboembolism) was increased with bevacizumab. Together with GOG-86P, failed to establish a definitive PFS benefit for bevacizumab in endometrial cancer, in contrast to its established role in ovarian cancer.

records.title: NRG-GY018 / KEYNOTE-868 (Eskander)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Advanced (stage III-IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer, by MMR status Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin–paclitaxel ×6 cycles, then pembrolizumab 400 mg IV Q6W maintenance up to 14 cycles (max 20 cycles of pembrolizumab total) vs placebo + carboplatin–paclitaxel Progression-free survival Pembrolizumab added to chemotherapy improved PFS in both the dMMR cohort (12-month PFS 74% vs 38%, HR 0.30) and the pMMR cohort (13.1 vs 8.7 months, HR 0.54); established first-line chemoimmunotherapy across MMR groups.

records.title: RUBY (Mirza)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Primary advanced (stage III-IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer Dostarlimab 500 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin–paclitaxel ×6 cycles, then dostarlimab 1000 mg IV Q6W maintenance up to 3 years vs placebo + carboplatin–paclitaxel Progression-free survival and overall survival Dostarlimab improved 24-month PFS overall (36.1% vs 18.1%, HR 0.64) with a striking dMMR/MSI-H benefit (HR 0.28) and improved OS (HR 0.64); established dostarlimab chemoimmunotherapy, especially in dMMR disease.

records.title: DUO-E (Westin)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer Carboplatin–paclitaxel + durvalumab 1120 mg IV Q3W ×6 cycles, then maintenance durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W ± olaparib 300 mg twice daily to progression vs carboplatin–paclitaxel + placebo → placebo maintenance Progression-free survival Durvalumab improved PFS (HR 0.71) and adding maintenance olaparib improved it further (15.1 vs 9.6 months, HR 0.55 vs control); the olaparib benefit was concentrated in pMMR tumors.

records.title: AtTEnd (Colombo)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma, by MMR status Atezolizumab + carboplatin/paclitaxel vs chemotherapy Progression-free survival Atezolizumab improved PFS markedly in dMMR disease (NR vs 6.9 months, HR 0.36) and modestly in all-comers (10.1 vs 8.9 months, HR 0.74), with an OS trend favoring atezolizumab (38.7 vs 30.2 months); confirmed checkpoint benefit is driven by dMMR tumors.

records.title: RUBY Part 2 (ENGOT-EN6/GOG-3031)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Advanced / recurrent — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2026
records.body: Primary advanced (stage III-IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer (all-comers by MMR) Dostarlimab + carboplatin/paclitaxel → dostarlimab + niraparib maintenance vs placebo + chemotherapy Progression-free survival Dostarlimab + chemo followed by dostarlimab + niraparib maintenance improved PFS (14.5 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.60) regardless of MMR status, including in pMMR disease; adds a niraparib-containing maintenance strategy. ESMO 2024 abstract - not yet a full publication.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (O'Malley)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · II · 2022
records.body: Previously treated MSI-H/dMMR advanced endometrial cancer Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to 35 cycles (single-arm; MSI-H/dMMR) Objective response rate Pembrolizumab produced durable responses (ORR 50%, 16% complete; median DOR not reached) in pretreated MSI-H/dMMR disease; basis for the tumor-agnostic and dMMR-specific approvals.

records.title: GARNET (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · II · 2023
records.body: Pretreated advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer, dMMR/MSI-H and MMRp/MSS cohorts Dostarlimab 500 mg IV Q3W ×4 cycles, then 1000 mg IV Q6W to progression (single-arm) Objective response rate Dostarlimab produced durable responses in pretreated dMMR/MSI-H (ORR 45.5%) and MMRp/MSS (ORR 15.4%) disease; supported accelerated approval in dMMR endometrial cancer.

records.title: KEYNOTE-775 / Study 309 (Makker)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · III · 2022
records.body: Advanced endometrial cancer after ≥1 prior platinum regimen Lenvatinib 20 mg orally once daily + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs physician's-choice chemotherapy (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV Q3W or paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly) Progression-free survival and overall survival Lenvatinib/pembrolizumab improved PFS (all-comers 7.2 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.56; pMMR 6.6 vs 3.8 months) and OS (18.3 vs 11.4 months, HR 0.62); established the standard second-line regimen for pMMR disease.

records.title: Fader (HER2+ serous)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · II · 2018
records.body: Advanced (stage III-IV) or recurrent HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma Carboplatin–paclitaxel Q3W ×6 cycles ± trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg IV Q3W, continued to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Adding trastuzumab improved PFS (12.6 vs 8.0 months, HR 0.44), with the largest gain in stage III-IV disease; established HER2-directed therapy for HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2044-2051   Clin Cancer Res 2020;26:3928-3935 updated OS analysis 32601075

records.title: DESTINY-PanTumor02 (endometrial cohort)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Recurrent — immunotherapy & targeted therapy (pretreated) · II · 2024
records.body: Previously treated HER2-expressing (IHC 3+/2+) advanced endometrial cancer (basket cohort) Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W to progression or toxicity (single-arm; HER2-expressing endometrial cohort) Objective response rate In the endometrial cohort, T-DXd produced ORR 57.5% (the highest among basket tumour types), with greatest activity in HER2 IHC3+ disease; supported the tumour-agnostic FDA approval of T-DXd for HER2 IHC3+ solid tumours, extending HER2-directed options beyond trastuzumab.

records.title: SIENDO / ENGOT-EN5 (Vergote)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Maintenance — emerging · III · 2023
records.body: Advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer in response after first-line chemotherapy Maintenance oral selinexor vs placebo Progression-free survival Maintenance selinexor modestly improved PFS in the ITT population (5.7 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.70); a pre-specified TP53-wild-type subgroup showed a large benefit (27.4 vs 5.2 months, HR 0.42), now under confirmatory study.

records.title: MACH-NC (Pignon)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation & EGFR inhibition · N/A · 2009
records.body: Non-metastatic HNSCC treated with curative locoregional therapy (IPD meta-analysis, 87 trials) Addition of chemotherapy to locoregional treatment; concomitant vs induction timing Overall survival Individual-patient-data meta-analysis, 87 trials and 16,485 patients with non-metastatic HNSCC, comparing curative locoregional treatment against the same treatment plus chemotherapy (primary endpoint overall survival). Adding chemotherapy improved OS (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92, p<0.0001; absolute 5-yr benefit 4.5%), but a significant chemotherapy-timing interaction (p<0.0001) localised that benefit: concomitant chemoradiation (50 trials, 9,615 patients) HR 0.81 (0.78-0.86), absolute 5-yr benefit 6.5%; induction (31 trials, 5,311 patients) HR 0.96 (0.90-1.02, p=0.18), non-significant; adjuvant HR 1.06 (0.95-1.18), no benefit. The concomitant benefit declined with age (trend p=0.003), and non-platinum single-agent chemotherapy was significantly inferior. Establishes concomitant platinum-based chemoradiation — not chemotherapy as an undifferentiated category — as the nonsurgical curative-intent standard this stream is built on.

records.title: Bonner
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation & EGFR inhibition · III · 2006
records.body: Locoregionally advanced HNSCC (oropharynx, larynx, hypopharynx) for definitive RT Radiotherapy + cetuximab vs radiotherapy alone Locoregional control Phase 3, N=424, locoregionally advanced HNSCC of the oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx; definitive radiotherapy plus cetuximab vs radiotherapy alone (primary endpoint locoregional control). Cetuximab improved locoregional control (HR 0.68, p=0.005) and median overall survival (49.0 vs 29.3 months, HR 0.74, p=0.03 at the 2006 primary; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.95, p=0.018, 5-yr OS 45.6% vs 36.4% at the 2010 update), adding acneiform rash and infusion reactions but no excess mucositis or myelosuppression; among cetuximab-treated patients a prominent grade 2 or higher rash was associated with better survival (HR 0.49, 0.34-0.72), a hypothesis-generating signal. The comparator was radiotherapy alone, not cisplatin-chemoradiation — Bonner establishes cetuximab-radiotherapy as superior to radiotherapy alone but never tests it against MACH-NC's concomitant-cisplatin standard, and HPV/p16 status was not assessed.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2006;354:567-578   Lancet Oncol 2010;11:21-28 5-year update 19897418

records.title: Pan-Asian ESMO Guideline (Keam et al.)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation & EGFR inhibition · N/A · 2021
records.body: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, larynx, oropharynx, and hypopharynx (excluding nasopharyngeal carcinoma) N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A Pan-Asian adaptation (KSMO/ESMO/CSCO/ISMPO/JSMO/MOS/SSO/TOS) of the EHNS-ESMO-ESTRO 2020 guideline for SCCHN. Standard options for locally advanced disease are surgery plus adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy or primary concomitant chemoradiotherapy (CRT); IMRT/VMAT is mandatory. Concomitant cisplatin 100mg/m2 triweekly is standard, with weekly 40mg/m2 an accepted alternative (including post-operatively) given comparable efficacy with better tolerability in Asian patients. Induction chemotherapy is reserved mainly for larynx preservation (TPF, up to 3 cycles per response) and is not otherwise routine. For recurrent/metastatic disease, pembrolizumab monotherapy (PD-L1 CPS≥20) or pembrolizumab plus platinum/5-FU (CPS≥1) are standard first-line per KEYNOTE-048; platinum/5-FU/cetuximab (EXTREME) remains standard for PD-L1-negative disease. Nivolumab is standard second-line post-platinum. Notably diverges from Western guidelines only on DPD testing (not routine in Asia given low prevalence of DPD deficiency) and weekly-cisplatin acceptance reflecting regional toxicity/reimbursement patterns.

records.title: VA Larynx (Wolf)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Larynx preservation · III · 1991
records.body: Resectable stage III/IV laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma Induction cisplatin/5-FU then RT vs total laryngectomy + postoperative RT Overall survival Induction chemotherapy then RT preserved the larynx in 64% with equivalent 2-yr OS (68% in both arms); established nonsurgical larynx preservation as an option.

records.title: RTOG 91-11 (Forastiere)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Larynx preservation · III · 2003
records.body: Stage III/IV glottic or supraglottic larynx cancer, larynx-preservation candidates Induction cisplatin/5-FU→RT vs concurrent cisplatin/RT vs RT alone Laryngeal preservation Three-arm phase 3, N=547 randomised (518 analysed in 2003; 520 in the 2013 long-term report), stage III/IV glottic or supraglottic larynx cancer eligible for preservation; induction cisplatin/fluorouracil then radiotherapy vs concurrent cisplatin-radiotherapy vs radiotherapy alone. The reports name different primary endpoints: 2003 laryngeal preservation, 2013 the composite laryngectomy-free survival (LFS). At 3.8 years (2003) concurrent chemoradiotherapy gave the highest 2-yr larynx preservation (88% vs 75% induction, p=0.005; vs 70% radiotherapy alone, p<0.001) at roughly double the grade 3/4 mucosal toxicity, while induction was no better than radiotherapy alone (p=0.27). At 10.8 years (2013) preservation holds - 10-yr 81.7% concurrent vs 67.5% induction vs 63.8% radiotherapy alone (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.37-0.89 vs induction) - but on LFS the chemotherapy arms are indistinguishable (10-yr 23.5% vs 28.9%; HR 1.05, 0.83-1.34) while both beat radiotherapy alone (HR 0.78, 0.61-0.98). Overall survival never separates and by 10 years trends against concurrent (27.5% vs 38.8%; HR 1.25, 0.98-1.61), with deaths unrelated to cancer or treatment highest in that arm. No multiplicity adjustment or subgroup analysis: all p-values nominal. Against VA Larynx's own induction regimen, it establishes concurrent sequencing as superior for organ preservation without a survival gain.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2003;349:2091-2098   J Clin Oncol 2013;31:845-852 10-year long-term results 23182993

records.title: TAX 323 (Vermorken)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Induction (sequential) chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Unresectable locally advanced HNSCC (induction setting) Induction TPF (docetaxel/cisplatin/5-FU) vs PF, then radiotherapy Progression-free survival Phase 3, N=358, previously untreated unresectable locally advanced HNSCC; induction docetaxel-cisplatin-fluorouracil (TPF) vs cisplatin-fluorouracil (PF), then radiotherapy alone (primary endpoint progression-free survival). TPF improved PFS (11.0 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.72, p=0.007) and overall survival (18.8 vs 14.5 months, HR 0.73, p=0.02), with a significantly higher response rate and fewer toxic deaths (2.3% vs 5.5%) despite more grade 3/4 neutropenia — PF instead caused more thrombocytopenia, stomatitis, and hearing loss. To accommodate docetaxel the TPF arm reduced both cisplatin (75 mg/m²) and fluorouracil (750 mg/m²/day) below the PF arm's full doses (100 and 1000). With TAX 324 it establishes that adding docetaxel to induction PF improves the induction step, but the two trials dose TPF differently and disagree on whether TPF's response-rate advantage is significant — concordant in direction, not identical.

records.title: TAX 324 (Posner)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Induction (sequential) chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Locally advanced HNSCC (unresectable or organ-preservation candidates) Induction TPF vs PF, then carboplatin chemoradiation Overall survival Phase 3, N=501, locally advanced HNSCC spanning technical unresectability, low surgical curability, and organ-preservation candidacy; induction TPF vs PF followed by carboplatin-based chemoradiation (primary endpoint overall survival). TPF improved OS (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.54-0.90; median 71 vs 30 months; 3-yr 62% vs 48%, p=0.006) and PFS (HR 0.71, 0.56-0.90, p=0.004; median 36 vs 13 months), but — unlike TAX 323 — the post-induction response rate did not differ significantly (72% vs 64%, p=0.07). Grade 3/4 neutropenia was higher with TPF (83% vs 56%), yet TPF caused far fewer treatment delays (29% vs 65%, p<0.001) and toxic-death rates were similar between arms. Its TPF used full-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m²) matched to its own PF arm rather than TAX 323's reduced doses, so the two induction-composition trials agree on TPF's survival benefit while differing in regimen and in whether the response advantage reaches significance.

records.title: EORTC 22931 (Bernier)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Resected high-risk HNSCC (positive margins, extracapsular spread, or stage III/IV) Postoperative cisplatin chemoradiation vs RT alone Progression-free survival Phase 3, N=334, resected high-risk HNSCC (positive margins, extracapsular extension, or stage III/IV disease); postoperative concurrent cisplatin (100 mg/m² on days 1, 22, 43) chemoradiation vs radiotherapy alone (primary endpoint progression-free survival). Concurrent cisplatin significantly improved progression-free survival (HR 0.75, p=0.04; 5-yr 47% vs 36%), overall survival (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95, p=0.02; 5-yr 53% vs 40%), and locoregional control (5-yr cumulative relapse 18% vs 31%) — positive on all three endpoints, in direct contrast to MACH-NC's negative sequential post-treatment adjuvant subgroup, because it tests concurrent postoperative chemoradiation rather than adjuvant chemotherapy given after locoregional treatment ends. The pooled Bernier 2005 analysis with RTOG 9501 localises the chemotherapy benefit to patients with extracapsular extension and/or positive margins.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2004;350:1945-1952   Head Neck 2005;27:843-850 comparative EORTC/RTOG risk-stratification analysis 16161069

records.title: RTOG 9501 (Cooper)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · III · 2004
records.body: Resected high-risk HNSCC (≥2 nodes, extracapsular spread, or positive margins) Postoperative cisplatin chemoradiation vs RT alone Locoregional control Phase 3, N=416 eligible of 459 randomised (the trial's planned analysis population; all three hazard ratios below are eligible-set figures), resected high-risk HNSCC defined by two or more positive nodes, extracapsular extension, and/or positive margins; postoperative concurrent cisplatin-chemoradiation vs radiotherapy alone (primary endpoint locoregional control). Chemoradiation significantly improved locoregional control (HR for local/regional recurrence 0.61, 95% CI 0.41-0.91, p=0.01) and disease-free survival (HR 0.78, 0.61-0.99, p=0.04), but overall survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.84, 0.65-1.09, p=0.19). Unlike EORTC 22931, RTOG 9501 added a two-or-more-node criterion and enrolled a predominantly node-count-defined population (94% N2-3 vs 57% in EORTC 22931); the pooled Bernier 2005 analysis localises the benefit to extracapsular extension and/or positive margins and finds no benefit in node-count-only patients, so population composition — not a genuine treatment-effect conflict — is the leading explanation for why its overall-survival result diverged from EORTC 22931's.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2004;350:1937-1944   Head Neck 2005;27:843-850 comparative EORTC/RTOG risk-stratification analysis 16161069

records.title: JCOG1008 (Kiyota)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · II/III · 2022
records.body: Resected high-risk LA-SCCHN (positive margins and/or extranodal/extracapsular extension) Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² IV for 7 cycles vs 3-weekly cisplatin 100 mg/m² IV for 3 cycles, each concurrent with postoperative radiotherapy Overall survival (phase III), noninferiority (HR margin 1.32) Phase II/III, N=261, resected high-risk LA-SCCHN (positive margins and/or extranodal extension); weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² for 7 cycles vs 3-weekly cisplatin 100 mg/m² for 3 cycles, each concurrent with postoperative radiotherapy, testing noninferiority for overall survival (margin HR 1.32). Weekly cisplatin was noninferior at the interim analysis (HR 0.69, 99.1% CI 0.37-1.27) and at the 5.6-yr final analysis (5-yr OS 71.2% vs 58.7%, HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.52-1.12; adjusted HR 0.88), with less grade ≥3 neutropenia (35% vs 49%), infection, and renal and hearing toxicity — but two treatment-related deaths occurred in the weekly arm versus none with 3-weekly.
