This is a cisplatin schedule and dose-intensity question layered on the concurrent postoperative backbone EORTC 22931 and RTOG 9501 established, not a re-test of whether concurrent chemotherapy works; it makes weekly cisplatin a standard postoperative option.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1980-1990; long-term follow-up J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print, doi:10.1200/JCO-25-01708)   Tahara et al. - 2026 - Long-Term Follow-Up of JCOG1008, a Randomized Phase II - III Trial of Chemoradiotherapy Comparing [7bbd14df]

records.title: NIVOPOSTOP (Bourhis)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Postoperative (adjuvant) therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Resected advanced-stage high-risk HNSCC (extracapsular extension, positive margins, ≥4 nodes, or multiple perineural invasion) Adjuvant nivolumab + cisplatin chemoradiation then nivolumab vs chemoradiation alone Disease-free survival Phase 3, N=680, resected uniformly high-risk locally advanced HNSCC (advanced stage plus a named high-risk feature: extracapsular extension, positive margins, ≥4 nodes, or multiple perineural invasion); adjuvant-only nivolumab added to concurrent cisplatin-radiotherapy vs cisplatin-radiotherapy alone (primary endpoint investigator-assessed disease-free survival). Nivolumab improved DFS irrespective of PD-L1 expression: HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.60-0.98), stratified log-rank p=0.034; 3-yr DFS 63.1% vs 52.5%. The benefit was driven by reduced locoregional relapse (subdistribution HR 0.63, 0.42-0.94) rather than distant relapse (0.95, 0.61-1.48). DFS by masked independent central review was weaker and not significant (HR 0.89, 0.69-1.14) — attributed to imaging-only review in resected, irradiated anatomy — with a 32-event-correction sensitivity analysis at HR 0.81 (0.63-1.03). Overall survival is immature (158 of 242 planned deaths). Grade 4 treatment-related adverse events (10% vs 5%) and serious treatment-related events (33% vs 19%) were more frequent with nivolumab; treatment-related deaths unchanged (two per arm). Sibling to KEYNOTE-689's perioperative sandwich, and the first phase 3 to improve on the >20-year-old adjuvant cisplatin-chemoradiation standard in high-risk resected disease.

records.title: RTOG 1016 (Gillison)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · HPV-positive oropharynx — de-escalation · III · 2019
records.body: HPV(p16)-positive oropharyngeal SCC suitable for chemoradiation Radiotherapy + cetuximab vs radiotherapy + cisplatin Overall survival (non-inferiority) Phase 3 non-inferiority trial, N=849, HPV (p16)-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma; radiotherapy plus cetuximab vs radiotherapy plus cisplatin, powered for overall-survival non-inferiority (margin HR 1.45). Cetuximab failed the prespecified non-inferiority test: OS HR 1.45 (one-sided 95% upper CI 1.94; p=0.51 for non-inferiority), 5-yr OS 77.9% vs 84.6%, with significantly worse progression-free survival (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.29-2.29, p=0.0002; 5-yr 67.3% vs 78.4%) and locoregional failure (HR 2.05). Together with De-ESCALaTE it reaches the same practice conclusion — cisplatin-chemoradiation remains standard and cetuximab is not a de-escalation substitute — but by a different evidentiary route, as a formal overall-survival non-inferiority failure on its own primary endpoint, powered and prespecified for exactly this comparison.

records.title: De-ESCALaTE (Mehanna)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · HPV-positive oropharynx — de-escalation · III · 2019
records.body: Low-risk HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCC (minimal smoking) Radiotherapy + cisplatin vs radiotherapy + cetuximab Severe (grade 3-5) toxicity Phase 3, N=334, low-risk HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (p16-positive with minimal smoking); radiotherapy plus cisplatin vs radiotherapy plus cetuximab (primary endpoint overall severe grade 3-5 toxicity at 24 months). The primary toxicity endpoint was neutral — cetuximab did not reduce severe toxicity (mean 4.8 vs 4.8 events per patient, p=0.98) or all-grade toxicity (p=0.49) — so the de-escalation rationale failed on the endpoint it was built to test. Its practice-defining result rests instead on prespecified secondary endpoints the trial was not powered for: 2-yr overall survival 97.5% vs 89.4% (HR 5.0, 95% CI 1.7-14.7, p=0.001) and 2-yr recurrence 6.0% vs 16.1% (HR 3.4, 1.6-7.2, p=0.0007). It reaches RTOG 1016's conclusion that cisplatin-radiotherapy remains standard, but via a neutral primary toxicity endpoint and a not-formally-powered secondary survival signal rather than a formal non-inferiority test.

records.title: KEYNOTE-412 (Machiels)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Definitive chemoradiation + immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Unresected locally advanced HNSCC receiving definitive chemoradiation Pembrolizumab + chemoradiation then pembrolizumab vs placebo + chemoradiation Event-free survival Phase 3, N=804, newly diagnosed unresected locally advanced HNSCC (PD-L1-unselected, p16-mixed); pembrolizumab added before, during, and after concurrent chemoradiation vs placebo plus chemoradiation (primary endpoint event-free survival). Pembrolizumab did not significantly improve EFS: HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.68-1.03), log-rank p=0.043 against a prespecified boundary of p≤0.024 — a favourable trend that missed its own bar, making this a negative trial by design. Overall survival was correspondingly not different (HR 0.90, 0.71-1.15) and immature. A prespecified PD-L1 CPS ≥1 subgroup trended larger (HR 0.80, 0.64-1.00) and a post-hoc CPS ≥20 subgroup larger still, but this is an unresolved candidate predictive signal, not a validated selection gate. Serious adverse events (62% vs 49%) and discontinuation from adverse events (41% vs 33%) were both higher with pembrolizumab, so immunotherapy is not added to definitive chemoradiation outside trials.

records.title: KEYNOTE-689 (Uppaluri)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Resectable disease — perioperative immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable locally advanced (stage III-IVA) HNSCC Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab + standard care vs standard care (surgery + adjuvant RT ± cisplatin) Event-free survival Phase 3, N=714, resectable locally advanced (stage III-IVA) HNSCC; neoadjuvant plus adjuvant ('sandwich') pembrolizumab added to standard care (surgery plus risk-adapted adjuvant radiotherapy ± cisplatin) vs standard care alone (primary endpoint event-free survival). EFS was positive hierarchically across all three prespecified populations at the first interim (median follow-up 38.3 months): CPS-10 HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.49-0.88, p=0.004), CPS-1 HR 0.70 (0.55-0.89, p=0.003), and total population HR 0.73 (0.58-0.92, p=0.008; 3-yr EFS 57.6% vs 46.4%). Major pathological response was 9.4% vs 0% (total population, p<0.001) and surgical completion was unaffected (88.4% vs 87.7%). Overall survival trended favourable (CPS-10 HR 0.72, 0.52-0.98) but did not cross its prespecified alpha boundary and was not formally tested — an immature, non-alpha-controlled signal, not a proven survival benefit. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were similar (44.6% vs 42.9%), but immune-mediated events were far more common (43.2% vs 10.2% any grade) and treatment-related death more frequent (1.1% vs 0.3%). The first positive perioperative immunotherapy in HNSCC, sibling to the adjuvant-only NIVOPOSTOP; its benefit skews toward distant over locoregional recurrence by the trial's own first-event counts — a descriptive read, not the formal competing-risk analysis NIVOPOSTOP reports.

records.title: EXTREME (Vermorken)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic HNSCC Platinum/5-FU + cetuximab vs platinum/5-FU Overall survival Cetuximab improved median OS (10.1 vs 7.4 months, HR 0.80), PFS (5.6 vs 3.3 months) and response (36% vs 20%); first regimen to extend OS in R/M HNSCC.

records.title: KEYNOTE-048 (Burtness)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic HNSCC Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to progression, toxicity, or 35 cycles, alone or + platinum–5-FU backbone (6 cycles) vs cetuximab 400 mg/m² IV loading then 250 mg/m² weekly + platinum–5-FU backbone (EXTREME regimen) Overall survival Pembrolizumab+chemo improved OS in CPS≥1 (HR 0.65) and the total population (HR 0.77); pembrolizumab monotherapy improved OS in CPS≥20 (14.7 vs 11.0 months). Established PD-L1-guided first-line immunotherapy.
records.keywords: Lancet 2019;394:1915-1928   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:2321-2332 PD-L1 CPS subgroup analysis 35333599 J Clin Oncol 2023;41:790-802 4-yr updated results 36219809

records.title: TMC-I (Tata Memorial)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2026
records.body: First-line palliative, platinum-sensitive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC (India) Triple oral metronomic chemotherapy (methotrexate + celecoxib + erlotinib) + ultra-low-dose nivolumab (20 mg) vs paclitaxel + carboplatin Overall survival The oral metronomic + ultra-low-dose nivolumab regimen improved median OS (10.3 vs 6.2 months, HR 0.57) with lower grade >=3 toxicity (37% vs 48%) and a fraction of the cost (~US$230/month); a low-cost, accessible option where IO-chemotherapy is unavailable. Comparator was chemotherapy alone (not pembrolizumab-chemotherapy). ASCO 2026 abstract - not yet a full publication.

records.title: METRO PLUS
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Platinum-sensitive, unresectable advanced HNSCC eligible for palliative platinum chemo (single-centre, North India) Paclitaxel-carboplatin + triple oral metronomic chemo (erlotinib + celecoxib + methotrexate) vs paclitaxel-carboplatin alone Overall survival Adding triple oral metronomic chemotherapy to paclitaxel-carboplatin doubled median overall survival (10.0 versus 5 months; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.72, P<.001) and progression-free survival (6 versus 2 months; HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.28-0.5). The proportional-hazards assumption failed for overall survival (P=.01), so the authors also report restricted mean survival of 12 versus 7 months, with a ratio of survival time lost of 1.33 (95% CI 1.17-1.51). Grade 3 or higher toxicity was 8.4% versus 12.6% (P=.400), but all-grade toxicity rose substantially with metronomic therapy - rash 62.2% versus 4.5%, diarrhoea 42.9% versus 10.9%, mucositis 76.5% versus 54.6%. Single-centre North India, 85% oral-cavity primary, comparator chemotherapy alone rather than pembrolizumab-chemotherapy - a low-cost first-line option for resource-limited settings rather than a new global standard.

records.title: KEYNOTE-B10 (Dzienis)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line therapy · IV · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated recurrent/metastatic HNSCC, any PD-L1 status (single-arm) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to 35 cycles + carboplatin–paclitaxel backbone (6 cycles; 5-FU-free) ORR ORR 49% (7% complete response) with a manageable safety profile; supports a fluorouracil-free chemo-immunotherapy alternative to the KEYNOTE-048 platinum/5-FU regimen.

records.title: CheckMate 141 (Ferris)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line & post-platinum · III · 2016
records.body: Platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic HNSCC (progression ≤6 months) Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W to progression or toxicity vs investigator's choice — methotrexate 40–60 mg/m² weekly, docetaxel 30–40 mg/m² weekly, or cetuximab 400 mg/m² IV loading then 250 mg/m² weekly Overall survival Nivolumab improved median OS (7.5 vs 5.1 months, HR 0.70) and 1-yr OS (36.0% vs 16.6%) with less toxicity; first checkpoint inhibitor approved in R/M HNSCC.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2016;375:1856-1867   Oral Oncol 2018;81:45-51 2-yr long-term survival update by PD-L1 expression 29884413

records.title: KEYNOTE-040 (Cohen)
records.subtitle: Head & Neck SCC · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line & post-platinum · III · 2019
records.body: Platinum-pretreated recurrent/metastatic HNSCC Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to progression, toxicity, or 24 months vs investigator's choice — methotrexate 40 mg/m² weekly (up to 60 mg/m²), docetaxel 75 mg/m² Q3W, or cetuximab 400 mg/m² IV loading then 250 mg/m² weekly Overall survival Pembrolizumab improved median OS (8.4 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.80) with greater benefit at higher PD-L1; supported PD-1 blockade after platinum.

records.title: Intergroup 0099 (Al-Sarraf)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1998
records.body: Stage III/IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma (predominantly Western population) Concurrent cisplatin/RT then adjuvant cisplatin/5-FU vs RT alone Progression-free survival Chemoradiation plus adjuvant chemotherapy improved 3-yr OS (78% vs 47%; 1998 primary); the trial's final report (ASCO 2001 abstract, never fully published) gave 5-yr OS 67% vs 37%. Established chemoradiation as the standard for advanced NPC.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 1998;16:1310-1317   Proc Am Soc Clin Oncol 2001;20:227a (abstract 905)

records.title: MAC-NPC (Blanchard)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Non-metastatic NPC treated with radiotherapy (IPD meta-analysis, 19 trials) Addition of chemotherapy to RT; comparison of chemotherapy timing Overall survival MAC-NPC Collaborative Group individual-patient-data analyses. Blanchard 2015 pairwise meta-analysis (19 trials, 4,806 patients, reference radiotherapy alone): adding chemotherapy improved overall survival (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.73-0.86; absolute 5-year benefit 6.3%), with a significant chemotherapy-timing interaction (p=0.01) favouring concomitant plus adjuvant (HR 0.65) and concomitant alone (HR 0.80) but not adjuvant alone (HR 0.87) or induction alone (HR 0.96). The 2023 network reanalysis (Petit; 28 trials, 8,214 patients, reference concomitant chemoradiotherapy) ranked induction with taxanes (HR 0.75) and induction without taxanes (HR 0.81) highest, ahead of chemoradiotherapy-then-adjuvant (HR 0.88, ns) and radiotherapy alone (HR 1.26, worst-ranked); because the reference arms differ, the 2015 and 2023 hazard ratios are not directly comparable.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2015;16:645-655   Lancet Oncol 2023;24:611-623 updated meta-analysis 37269842

records.title: Guangzhou-01 (Wu, oxaliplatin CCRT)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 2005
records.body: WHO type II/III (nonkeratinizing/undifferentiated) locoregionally advanced NPC; stage T3/T4 (any N) and/or N2/N3 (any T), M0 by 1997 AJCC/UICC; endemic (Chinese) single-centre cohort, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center Radiotherapy (70–74 Gy to primary tumour, 60–64 Gy to involved neck; conventional fractionation) + concurrent oxaliplatin 70 mg/m² IV (2-h infusion) weekly ×6 cycles vs radiotherapy alone (same RT) Overall survival (explicitly designated the primary endpoint in the 2005 primary publication; secondary endpoints objective response rate, safety profile, relapse-free survival and metastasis-free survival) Long-term follow-up of the single-centre Guangzhou-01 phase III trial (enrolled Jan 2001–Jan 2003; N=115, CCRT n=59, RT alone n=56) testing addition of concurrent weekly oxaliplatin to radiotherapy. At a median follow-up of 114 months, adding oxaliplatin improved 5-year OS (73.2% vs 60.2%; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.31–0.94, P=0.028; 3/5/7-yr OS 89.6/73.2/71.3% vs 67.6/60.2/56.3%) and 5-year metastasis-free survival (74.7% vs 63.0%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.29–0.94, P=0.027), but did not significantly improve locoregional failure-free survival (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.29–1.29, P=0.190). Primary-site complete response was higher with CCRT (83% vs 66%, P=0.032). In a post hoc subgroup analysis the survival benefit was confined to T3-4N0-1 disease (n=58; 5-yr OS 84.2% vs 55.3%, HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.16–0.96, P=0.034), with no benefit in T3-4N2-3 or T1-2N2-3 and no significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction (P=0.789). Late toxicity was higher with CCRT (total late toxic-effect rate 66.1% vs 48.2%, P=0.040, driven by xerostomia 13.6% vs 1.8%, P=0.002); grade 3 late toxicity 28.8% vs 19.6% (P=0.102, ns), with no fatal or grade 4 events. Compliance was excellent (97% completed all planned doses of oxaliplatin and radiotherapy; the Discussion separately reports 95% completing all planned oxaliplatin). Supports weekly oxaliplatin as an alternative optional concurrent regimen in endemic locoregionally advanced NPC, not as a validated substitute for cisplatin: the comparator was radiotherapy alone, and the authors state that a randomised trial comparing cisplatin-based with oxaliplatin-based CCRT would be necessary; the original 2-year preliminary results were reported by Zhang et al. (J Clin Oncol 2005;23:8461-8468).
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2005;23:8461-8468 Guangzhou-01 primary report; 2-year preliminary results 16230677 Ann Oncol 2013;24:2131-2136 long-term follow-up at median 114 months; source of the col-H figures 23661293

records.title: Sun (TPF induction)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — induction chemotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Stage III-IVB locoregionally advanced NPC Induction TPF (docetaxel/cisplatin/5-FU) + cisplatin chemoradiation vs chemoradiation alone Failure-free survival Phase 3, N=480, previously untreated stage III-IVB (except T3-4N0) locoregionally advanced NPC; three cycles of induction docetaxel, cisplatin and fluorouracil (TPF) added before cisplatin concurrent chemoradiation vs concurrent chemoradiation alone. TPF induction improved 3-year failure-free survival (80% vs 72%, HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.48-0.97, p=0.034), overall survival (HR 0.59, 0.36-0.95, p=0.029) and distant failure-free survival (HR 0.59, 0.37-0.96, p=0.031), while locoregional failure-free survival did not differ (HR 0.64, 0.37-1.13, p=0.12). Grade 3-4 neutropenia was far more common with induction (42% vs 7%). With Zhang's gemcitabine-cisplatin induction, established taxane-based induction added to the concurrent chemoradiation floor as a top-ranked modality in the 2023 MAC-NPC network reanalysis.

records.title: Zhang (GP induction)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — induction chemotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Locoregionally advanced NPC (stage III-IVB, excluding T3-4N0) Induction gemcitabine 1 g/m² IV on days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV on day 1, Q3W ×3 cycles, then concurrent cisplatin 100 mg/m² Q3W ×3 with IMRT vs concurrent cisplatin 100 mg/m² Q3W ×3 with IMRT alone Recurrence-free survival Phase 3, N=480, newly diagnosed stage III-IVB (except T3-4N0) locoregionally advanced NPC; three cycles of induction gemcitabine plus cisplatin added before cisplatin concurrent chemoradiation vs concurrent chemoradiation alone. GP induction improved 3-year recurrence-free survival (85.3% vs 76.5%, stratified HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34-0.77, p=0.001) and 3-year overall survival (94.6% vs 90.3%, HR 0.43, 0.24-0.77), driven chiefly by reduced distant recurrence (3-year distant recurrence-free survival 91.1% vs 84.4%, HR 0.43, 0.25-0.73) with locoregional control unchanged. Grade 3-4 acute toxicity was higher with induction (75.7% vs 55.7%, predominantly haematological) while late grade 3-4 toxicity was comparable (9.2% vs 11.4%). The non-taxane counterpart to Sun's TPF, gemcitabine-cisplatin became a preferred induction regimen and helped move the 2023 MAC-NPC network toward induction.

records.title: Chen (metronomic capecitabine)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adjuvant therapy · III · 2021
records.body: High-risk locoregionally advanced NPC after chemoradiation Adjuvant metronomic capecitabine 650 mg/m² orally twice daily for 1 year vs observation Failure-free survival Phase 3, N=406, high-risk locoregionally advanced NPC (stage III-IVA, excluding T3-4N0 and T3N1) in remission after definitive chemoradiation; one year of adjuvant metronomic capecitabine 650 mg/m2 orally twice daily vs observation. Metronomic capecitabine improved 3-year failure-free survival (85.3% vs 75.7%, stratified HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.32-0.79, p=0.0023) and 3-year overall survival (93.3% vs 88.6%, stratified HR for death 0.44, 95% CI 0.22-0.88, p=0.018), with manageable toxicity (grade 3 adverse events 17% vs 6%; grade 3 hand-foot syndrome 9%; no treatment-related deaths). A positive result establishing a low-dose, low-cost adjuvant schedule against a timing category the MAC-NPC pairwise and network analyses both left non-significant.

records.title: CSCO/ASCO Guideline (Chen et al.)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adjuvant therapy · N/A · 2021
records.body: Stage II-IVA nasopharyngeal carcinoma N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A Joint CSCO/ASCO guideline on definitive-intent chemoradiotherapy for stage II-IVA NPC. IMRT with daily image guidance to 70 Gy/33-35 fractions is standard. Stage II (T2N0) generally does not need chemotherapy; T1-2N1 may receive concurrent chemotherapy. Stage III-IVA (except T3N0) should receive induction chemotherapy plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy (based on Sun/TPF and Zhang/GP induction trials already in this sheet), or concurrent chemoradiotherapy plus adjuvant chemotherapy if induction is not given. Concurrent cisplatin (weekly 40mg/m2 or triweekly 80-100mg/m2, cumulative ≥200mg/m2) is standard; nedaplatin, carboplatin, or oxaliplatin are alternatives if cisplatin is contraindicated. Adjuvant PF (cisplatin/5-FU) for 3 cycles is recommended when adjuvant therapy is used; non-platinum adjuvant regimens remain experimental. Synthesizes the evidentiary basis underlying the induction (Sun, Zhang) and adjuvant (Chen metronomic capecitabine) trials already filed on this sheet.

records.title: CONTINUUM (sintilimab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adding immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: High-risk locoregionally advanced NPC Sintilimab 200 mg IV Q3W ×12 cycles (3 induction + 3 concurrent + 6 adjuvant) added to gemcitabine–cisplatin induction + concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation vs gemcitabine–cisplatin induction + concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation alone Event-free survival Phase 3, N=425, high-risk locoregionally advanced NPC (stage III-IVa, excluding T3-4N0 and T3N1); sintilimab added across the induction, concurrent and adjuvant phases of a gemcitabine-cisplatin induction plus concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation backbone vs the backbone alone. Adding sintilimab improved 36-month event-free survival (86% vs 76%, stratified HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.38-0.92, p=0.019), with significant gains in distant metastasis-free (HR 0.57, p=0.041) and locoregional recurrence-free survival (HR 0.54, p=0.043); 36-month overall survival was identical (92% vs 92%, HR 0.86, p=0.60) and immature. Grade 3-4 adverse events 74% vs 65%, with two immune-related deaths. The first phase 3 trial showing a PD-1 inhibitor benefits definitive treatment of locoregional NPC, so far as an event-free-survival intensification rather than a proven survival gain.

records.title: DIPPER (adjuvant camrelizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Locoregional — adding immunotherapy · III · 2025
records.body: High-risk locoregionally advanced NPC after induction-concurrent chemoradiation Adjuvant camrelizumab for 12 cycles vs observation Event-free survival Adjuvant camrelizumab improved 3-yr event-free survival (86.9% vs 77.3%, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.36-0.89, P=0.01); OS boundary not crossed. Supports adjuvant PD-1 blockade in high-risk NPC.

records.title: Zhang (GP vs FP)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic NPC Gemcitabine 1 g/m² IV on days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV on day 1, Q3W vs fluorouracil 4 g/m² IV continuous infusion over 96 h + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV on day 1, Q3W; both to a maximum of 6 cycles Progression-free survival Phase 3, N=362, previously untreated recurrent/metastatic NPC: gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP) vs fluorouracil-cisplatin, both to a maximum of 6 cycles. GP improved median progression-free survival (7.0 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.44-0.68) and objective response (64% vs 42%, RR 1.5, 95% CI 1.2-1.9, p<0.0001), with more myelosuppression but less mucositis and no treatment-related deaths; the overall-survival difference (29.1 vs 20.9 months) was preliminary and immature. Established GP as the standard first-line chemotherapy backbone that every subsequent first-line chemo-immunotherapy trial (JUPITER-02, CAPTAIN-1st, RATIONALE-309, Penpulimab) holds constant in both arms.

records.title: JUPITER-02 (toripalimab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic NPC Toripalimab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + GP Progression-free survival Phase 3, N=289, multinational (China, Taiwan, Singapore), previously untreated recurrent/metastatic NPC: toripalimab vs placebo added to gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP) and continued as maintenance. Toripalimab improved median progression-free survival (BICR 21.4 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.37-0.73) and, uniquely in this stream, met a prespecified alpha-controlled overall-survival endpoint (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.45-0.89, two-sided p=0.008; median OS not reached vs 33.7 months; 3-year OS 64.5% vs 49.2%), with benefit consistent across PD-L1 and EBV-DNA subgroups. Grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events 9.6% vs 1.4%. The only first-line anti-PD-1 plus GP trial with a formally tested survival benefit, and the survival anchor of the first-line chemo-immunotherapy wave.

records.title: CAPTAIN-1st (camrelizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic NPC Camrelizumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + GP Progression-free survival Camrelizumab improved median PFS (9.7 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.54). At 5 years, median OS was 34.5 vs 26.6 months (stratified HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.55-0.99; nominal P=0.047) and 5-year OS was 37.8% vs 24.2%; OS was a key secondary endpoint without prespecified multiplicity adjustment. Supports PD-1 plus chemotherapy in the first line.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1162-1174   JAMA Oncol 2026;12:295-302 5-year OS analysis 41609753

records.title: RATIONALE-309 (tislelizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic NPC Tislelizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + gemcitabine–cisplatin (4–6 cycles) vs placebo + gemcitabine–cisplatin; tislelizumab continued to progression Progression-free survival Phase 3, N=263, treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC: tislelizumab vs placebo added to gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP). At the primary analysis (March 2021 cutoff) tislelizumab improved median progression-free survival (IRC-assessed 9.2 vs 7.4 months, HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.38-0.73, p<0.0001; consistent investigator-assessed HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.38-0.76). At the updated cutoff (median follow-up 15.5 months) it also improved progression-free survival 2 (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.24-0.63), while overall survival showed only an immature favourable trend (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.35-1.01), diluted by a crossover design in which 49% of the placebo arm received tislelizumab after progression. Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse events 2.3%. Reproduces the class first-line PFS benefit; its crossover and PFS2 endpoint are methodological distinctions rather than pharmacological, leaving its survival case less mature than JUPITER-02's prespecified OS win.

records.title: Penpulimab (AK105-304)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated recurrent/metastatic non-keratinizing NPC Penpulimab 200 mg IV Q3W + gemcitabine + cisplatin/carboplatin (up to 6 cycles), then penpulimab maintenance vs placebo + gemcitabine–platinum, then placebo maintenance; penpulimab to progression Progression-free survival Phase 3, N=291, previously untreated recurrent/metastatic non-keratinizing NPC: penpulimab vs placebo added to gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin, then maintenance. At the prespecified interim analysis penpulimab improved median progression-free survival (BIRC 9.6 vs 7.0 months, HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.33-0.62, p<0.0001), the numerically strongest PFS hazard ratio of the four first-line anti-PD-1 trials, but overall survival was immature and not reached (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.63-1.40). Distinguished by a flexible cisplatin-or-carboplatin backbone and an Fc-silenced IgG1 format advanced as a rationale for low immune toxicity (grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events 4.1%). The newest of the four, with the least mature survival data of the group.

records.title: Liu et al.
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — maintenance therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Newly diagnosed metastatic NPC with disease control after 4-6 cycles TPC induction chemo Capecitabine maintenance 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily on days 1–14, Q3W + best supportive care vs best supportive care alone; capecitabine to progression or a maximum of 2 years Progression-free survival Capecitabine maintenance markedly improved PFS (35.9 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.44) and ORR (25.0% vs 11.5%); OS immature (HR 0.59, NS) with manageable toxicity (grade 3-4 mainly hand-foot syndrome, anemia); first prospective evidence for maintenance therapy after induction chemo in metastatic NPC.

records.title: Yang (izalontamab brengitecan)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — second-line & beyond · III · 2025
records.body: Heavily pretreated recurrent/metastatic NPC, progressed after ≥2 lines of chemo including platinum and anti-PD-(L)1 Izalontamab brengitecan (EGFR×HER3 bispecific antibody–drug conjugate) 2·5 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle vs chemotherapy ORR and OS (dual primary) Phase 3, N=386, heavily pretreated recurrent/metastatic NPC progressing after 2 or more chemotherapy lines including platinum and an anti-PD-(L)1: izalontamab brengitecan (an EGFR and HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate) vs physician's-choice chemotherapy. At the first planned interim (final analysis for response), izalontamab brengitecan improved objective response (BICR 54.6%, 95% CI 45.2-63.8, vs 27.0%, 95% CI 19.1-36.0; difference 27.9%, 95% CI 15.5-39.4, p<0.0001) and progression-free survival (HR 0.44), while the co-primary overall survival was immature. Toxicity was haematologic-dominant, with more grade 3 or higher events on the ADC. The first phase 3 win for a targeted antibody-drug conjugate in NPC: a response and PFS win in the post-immunotherapy refractory population, not yet a survival win.

records.title: Chong (pembrolizumab ± bevacizumab)
records.subtitle: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma · Metastatic — second-line & beyond · II · 2025
records.body: Platinum-resistant recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + bevacizumab 7·5 mg/kg IV (1 week before each pembrolizumab dose) vs pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W alone; to progression, toxicity, or 32 cycles Objective response rate Randomised phase 2, N=48, platinum-resistant, checkpoint-inhibitor-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC: bevacizumab (anti-VEGF priming one week before each dose) plus pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab alone. Adding bevacizumab raised objective response (58.3%, 95% CI 36.6-77.9, vs 12.5%, 95% CI 2.7-32.4; RR 4.67, 95% CI 1.54-14.18, p=0.0010) and median progression-free survival (13.8 vs 1.6 months, HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.13-0.50, p<0.0001). Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events 29% vs 8%, with a bevacizumab-specific tumoral-site vascular risk (thrombosis or bleeding 17%, including carotid blowout and cerebrovascular thrombosis). A small hypothesis-generating signal needing phase 3 confirmation; its checkpoint-naive eligibility dates it as first-line anti-PD-1 becomes standard, leaving most platinum-resistant patients immunotherapy-experienced.

records.title: RTOG-MRC Neutron (Laramore)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Locoregional — radiotherapy (adenoid cystic carcinoma) · N/A · 1993
records.body: Inoperable or recurrent adenoid cystic carcinoma of major/minor salivary glands Fast-neutron radiotherapy vs photon/mixed-beam radiotherapy Locoregional control Neutrons improved 10-yr locoregional control (56% vs 25%) but not survival (dominated by distant metastasis); historical basis for neutron RT in unresectable ACC.
records.keywords: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 1993;27:235-240

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Geiger et al.)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Locoregional — radiotherapy (adenoid cystic carcinoma) · N/A · 2021
records.body: Salivary gland malignancy, all histologies and stages N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A First formal evidence-based ASCO guideline for salivary gland malignancy (SGM), covering preoperative workup, surgery, radiotherapy, systemic therapy, follow-up, and recurrent/metastatic disease. Surgical excision is the mainstay of curative treatment; postoperative RT is recommended for all resected adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) and for high-grade tumors, positive margins, perineural/lymphovascular invasion, nodal metastases, or T3-T4 disease. Concurrent chemoradiation is not routinely recommended outside a clinical trial. In the recurrent/metastatic setting, targeted therapy should be guided by molecular alterations: multitargeted TKIs (lenvatinib, sorafenib) for ACC; NTRK inhibitors for NTRK-fusion secretory carcinoma; HER2-directed therapy for HER2-positive salivary duct carcinoma; and androgen deprivation for AR-positive disease. Checkpoint inhibitors are not routinely recommended except for high-TMB or MSI-H tumors. This guideline provides the evidentiary/decision framework underlying the targeted-therapy trials (lenvatinib, axitinib, trastuzumab, larotrectinib, androgen blockade) already filed on this sheet.

records.title: Lenvatinib (Tchekmedyian)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Adenoid cystic carcinoma — antiangiogenic TKIs · II · 2019
records.body: Progressive recurrent/metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma Single-arm lenvatinib 24 mg daily Objective response rate ORR 15.6% (all partial) with 75% stable disease and median PFS 17.5 months; met its primary endpoint, showing meaningful TKI activity in ACC.

records.title: Axitinib (Kang)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Adenoid cystic carcinoma — antiangiogenic TKIs · II · 2021
records.body: Progressive recurrent/metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma Axitinib 5 mg twice daily vs observation 6-month progression-free survival Axitinib improved 6-mo PFS (73.2% vs 23.2%) and median PFS (10.8 vs 2.8 months); first randomized evidence of TKI benefit in ACC.

records.title: Takahashi (trastuzumab + docetaxel)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Salivary duct / HER2-positive — HER2-directed therapy · II · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive locally advanced/recurrent or metastatic salivary duct carcinoma Single-arm trastuzumab + docetaxel Objective response rate ORR 70.2% with median PFS 8.9 months and OS 39.7 months; established HER2-directed therapy for salivary duct carcinoma.

records.title: MYTHOS (trastuzumab deruxtecan)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Salivary duct / HER2-positive — HER2-directed therapy · II · 2024
records.body: HER2-expressing recurrent/metastatic salivary gland carcinoma Single-arm trastuzumab deruxtecan Objective response rate ORR 68.4% by independent review with median PFS 15.9 months; supports the HER2 antibody-drug conjugate in HER2-positive salivary cancer.

records.title: Limaye (trastuzumab in SDC)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Salivary duct / HER2-positive — HER2-directed therapy · N/A · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive (IHC 1-3+) salivary duct carcinoma, adjuvant or palliative setting Trastuzumab + paclitaxel/carboplatin (TCH), adjuvant (n=8) or palliative (n=5) Retrospective outcome review 62% of adjuvant patients disease-free beyond 2 years; all 5 metastatic patients responded to TCH (1 complete response, ongoing at 52 months); median response duration 18 months — early evidence supporting routine HER2 testing and trastuzumab-based therapy in SDC.

records.title: EORTC 1206 (Locati)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · Androgen receptor-positive — androgen blockade · II · 2024
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic androgen receptor-positive salivary gland cancer (chemo-naive) Androgen deprivation (triptorelin + bicalutamide) vs chemotherapy Progression-free survival ADT was neither superior nor inferior to chemotherapy (median PFS 4.0 vs 6.5 months; ORR 23% vs 35%) but was far less toxic, supporting ADT as a tolerable option in AR-positive disease.

records.title: Larotrectinib (salivary cohort)
records.subtitle: Salivary Gland Cancer · TRK fusion (secretory carcinoma) — TRK inhibition · II · 2024
records.body: TRK fusion-positive (ETV6-NTRK3) salivary gland cancers, mostly secretory carcinoma Single-arm larotrectinib 100 mg twice daily, continuous 28-day cycles, to progression (pooled phase I/II) Objective response rate ORR 92% (13% complete) with durable responses; TRK inhibition is highly active where an NTRK fusion is present.

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Saba et al.)
records.subtitle: Thyroid Cancer · Thyroid carcinoma · N/A · 2026
records.body: Thyroid carcinoma (differentiated, medullary, anaplastic), adults N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A ASCO guideline on systemic therapy across thyroid cancer subtypes (well-differentiated, differentiated high-grade/poorly differentiated, anaplastic, medullary). Primary treatment of well-differentiated disease is surgery ± radioactive iodine (RAI); for RAI-refractory well-differentiated disease, lenvatinib is the preferred first-line multikinase inhibitor (SELECT — PFS benefit; ORR ~65% vs 1.5% placebo), with sorafenib an alternative (DECISION). Biomarker-directed options for BRAF V600E, RET mutation/fusion, and NTRK fusion. Distinct systemic strategies outlined for medullary and anaplastic subtypes.

records.title: Dabrafenib + trametinib (Gao)
records.subtitle: Thyroid Cancer · Thyroid carcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, centrally confirmed BRAF V600E, progressing after one or two previous VEGFR-targeted therapies; ECOG 0-2. Entry allowed any differentiated histology; all 153 enrolled had papillary carcinoma, 86% Asian, 50% from mainland China Dabrafenib 150 mg orally twice daily + trametinib 2 mg orally once daily until progression vs matching placebos (2:1; crossover to open-label dabrafenib + trametinib on centrally confirmed progression) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate, overall survival, duration of response, safety, serous retinopathy In BRAF V600E-mutant papillary thyroid cancer progressing after VEGFR-targeted therapy, dabrafenib plus trametinib markedly prolonged progression-free survival: median 12.8 against 3.7 months with placebo (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.25-0.57, p<0.0001), response 57% against 4% (p<0.0001), disease control 88% against 63%. Overall survival at this interim analysis did not reach statistical significance - median not reached against 25.9 months, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.36-1.19), p=0.083 - with 58% of the placebo arm crossing over after progression. Toxicity was near-universal in both arms (any adverse event 98% against 90%): pyrexia 48%, anaemia 45%, serious adverse events 43% against 25%, pneumonia the commonest grade 3 or worse event at 8%, serous retinopathy 7% against none, and one treatment-related death from cerebrovascular accident.

records.title: EORTC 18071
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2015
records.body: Completely resected high-risk stage III cutaneous melanoma Adjuvant ipilimumab 10 mg/kg vs placebo Recurrence-free survival (OS co-primary) Adjuvant ipilimumab improved RFS and OS (5-yr OS 65.4% vs 54.4%, HR 0.72) but caused grade 3-4 immune toxicity in ~54% and 5 treatment-related deaths; proof-of-concept for adjuvant checkpoint blockade, later supplanted by anti–PD-1.

records.title: COMBI-AD
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2017
records.body: Resected stage III BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma Adjuvant dabrafenib + trametinib (12 mo) vs placebo Relapse-free survival Dabrafenib plus trametinib lowered recurrence (3-yr RFS 58% vs 39%, HR 0.47); established adjuvant BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy as an option for resected BRAF-mutant stage III disease.

records.title: CheckMate 238
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2017
records.body: Resected stage IIIB/C or IV melanoma Adjuvant nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs ipilimumab 10 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses then Q12W; both up to 1 year, to recurrence or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Nivolumab improved RFS over ipilimumab (12-mo RFS 70.5% vs 60.8%, HR 0.65) with far less grade 3-4 toxicity (14% vs 46%); established anti–PD-1 over ipilimumab in the adjuvant setting.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2017;377:1824-1835   N Engl J Med 2026;394:333-342 9-yr final analysis 41124198

records.title: KEYNOTE-054 (EORTC 1325)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2018
records.body: Completely resected high-risk stage III melanoma Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×18 doses (~1 year) vs placebo; to recurrence or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Pembrolizumab improved RFS versus placebo (1-yr RFS 75.4% vs 61.0%, HR 0.57) across subgroups including BRAF wild-type; a standard adjuvant option regardless of BRAF status.

records.title: KEYNOTE-716
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2022
records.body: Resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma, sentinel-node negative Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×17 cycles (~1 year) vs placebo; to recurrence or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Pembrolizumab improved RFS versus placebo (HR 0.65) and distant metastasis-free survival (HR 0.64); extended adjuvant anti–PD-1 to high-risk node-negative stage II disease.

records.title: CheckMate 76K
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2023
records.body: Resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma, sentinel-node negative Adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W vs placebo; to 12 months, recurrence, or toxicity Recurrence-free survival Nivolumab reduced recurrence versus placebo (12-mo RFS 89.0% vs 79.4%, HR 0.42) and improved DMFS (HR 0.47); a second adjuvant anti–PD-1 option for stage II melanoma.

records.title: SWOG S1801
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Resectable stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab vs adjuvant-only pembrolizumab Event-free survival Giving 3 doses of pembrolizumab before surgery improved EFS versus the same drug given only after surgery (2-yr EFS 72% vs 49%, HR 0.58); demonstrated the value of neoadjuvant immunotherapy sequencing.

records.title: NADINA
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable macroscopic stage III melanoma Neoadjuvant ipilimumab 80 mg + nivolumab 240 mg IV Q3W ×2 cycles → therapeutic lymph-node dissection, then response-driven adjuvant (major pathological response → no adjuvant; partial response/non-response → dabrafenib + trametinib if BRAF-mutant or nivolumab 480 mg Q4W if BRAF wild-type) vs upfront lymph-node dissection → adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W ×12 cycles Event-free survival Two cycles of neoadjuvant ipilimumab + nivolumab then response-driven adjuvant therapy beat adjuvant nivolumab (12-mo EFS 83.7% vs 57.2%, HR 0.32); ~59% had a major pathologic response and skipped adjuvant therapy, establishing neoadjuvant dual checkpoint blockade as a standard for macroscopic stage III.

records.title: KEYNOTE-942 (mRNA-4157/V940)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Adjuvant & neoadjuvant — resected / resectable disease · II · 2024
records.body: Resected high-risk stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma Intismeran autogene (individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccine) + pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab Recurrence-free survival Adding the personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccine to adjuvant pembrolizumab prolonged RFS (18-mo RFS 79% vs 62%, HR 0.56), with benefit sustained at 3- and 5-year follow-up (~49% reduction in recurrence or death); first randomized signal for an individualized cancer vaccine, with phase 3 confirmation (V940-001) ongoing.

records.title: BRIM-3
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2011
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600E-mutant unresectable/metastatic melanoma Vemurafenib vs dacarbazine Overall survival and progression-free survival Vemurafenib reduced the risk of death by 63% (HR 0.37) and prolonged PFS (5.3 vs 1.6 months) versus dacarbazine; first targeted therapy to improve survival in melanoma and validated BRAF as a drug target.

records.title: coBRIM
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2014
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant advanced melanoma Vemurafenib + cobimetinib vs vemurafenib Progression-free survival Adding the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib improved PFS (9.9 vs 6.2 months, HR 0.51) and response rate; established combined BRAF + MEK inhibition over BRAF inhibition alone.

records.title: COMBI-v
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Dabrafenib + trametinib vs vemurafenib Overall survival The dabrafenib/trametinib doublet improved OS over vemurafenib (12-mo OS 72% vs 65%, HR 0.69) and PFS (11.4 vs 7.3 months); confirmed BRAF/MEK combination as a first-line targeted standard.

records.title: COLUMBUS
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated/1 prior line BRAF V600-mutant advanced melanoma Encorafenib + binimetinib vs vemurafenib (vs encorafenib) Progression-free survival Encorafenib + binimetinib improved PFS versus vemurafenib (14.9 vs 7.3 months, HR 0.54) with favorable tolerability; a third BRAF/MEK doublet standard.

records.title: DREAMseq (EA6134)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — BRAF / MEK-targeted therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Arm A→C: nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W to 72 weeks, then dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily + trametinib 2 mg once daily at progression vs Arm B→D: dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily + trametinib 2 mg once daily to progression → nivolumab + ipilimumab at progression 2-year overall survival Starting with nivolumab/ipilimumab and switching to dabrafenib/trametinib at progression gave higher 2-year overall survival than the reverse sequence (71.8%, 95% CI 62.5-79.1, vs 51.5%, 95% CI 41.7-60.4; log-rank P=.010 on Kaplan-Meier estimates). The protocol-specified primary comparison - a Mantel-Haenszel test of 2-year landmark rates among the 176 patients followed at least 2 years - did not cross its efficacy boundary (P=.163); the trial was stopped early on the DSMC's recommendation after the Kaplan-Meier analysis crossed the O'Brien-Fleming boundary at 59% information time, with the 95% repeated CI for the difference 2.6% to 37.9%. Established immunotherapy-first sequencing for BRAF V600-mutant disease.

records.title: MDX010-20 (ipilimumab)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Previously treated HLA-A*0201+ metastatic melanoma Ipilimumab ± gp100 vaccine vs gp100 vaccine Overall survival Ipilimumab improved OS versus vaccine alone (median 10.0 vs 6.4 months, HR ~0.66); first agent ever to improve survival in advanced melanoma and validated CTLA-4 blockade.

records.title: KEYNOTE-006
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · III · 2015
records.body: Advanced melanoma, ≤1 prior therapy (ipilimumab-naive) Pembrolizumab (Q2W or Q3W) vs ipilimumab Progression-free and overall survival Pembrolizumab improved OS (HR 0.63-0.69; 1-yr OS ~74% vs 58%) and PFS versus ipilimumab with less high-grade toxicity; established anti–PD-1 monotherapy as first-line over ipilimumab.

records.title: CheckMate 067
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated advanced melanoma Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses; all to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival and ORR Nivolumab + ipilimumab and nivolumab alone improved PFS (11.5 and 6.9 vs 2.9 months) and ORR (58% and 44% vs 19%) over ipilimumab, with durable long-term survival on extended follow-up; established first-line dual checkpoint blockade.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2015;373:23-34   N Engl J Med 2017;377:1345-1356 overall survival 28889792

records.title: RELATIVITY-047
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · II/III · 2022
records.body: Untreated metastatic/unresectable melanoma Nivolumab + relatlimab (anti–LAG-3) fixed-dose vs nivolumab Progression-free survival Adding the LAG-3 inhibitor relatlimab improved PFS over nivolumab alone (median 10.1 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.75); established LAG-3 + PD-1 blockade as a first-line option with lower toxicity than nivolumab/ipilimumab.

records.title: OPTiM (T-VEC)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIB-IV melanoma Intralesional talimogene laherparepvec vs subcutaneous GM-CSF Durable response rate T-VEC improved durable response rate (16% vs 2%) and ORR (26% vs 6%) versus GM-CSF; first oncolytic immunotherapy approved for melanoma, useful for injectable locoregional disease.

records.title: C-144-01 (lifileucel)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · II · 2025
records.body: Advanced melanoma refractory to anti–PD-1 (and BRAF/MEK if indicated) (single-arm) One-time lifileucel autologous TIL infusion (1×10⁹–150×10⁹ cells) after nonmyeloablative lymphodepletion (cyclophosphamide + fludarabine), then high-dose IL-2 (≤6 doses) Objective response rate Lifileucel produced an ORR of 31.4% with median duration of response 36.5 months in checkpoint-refractory melanoma; first FDA-approved cellular (TIL) therapy for a solid tumor.

records.title: Rohaan (TIL vs ipilimumab)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIC/IV melanoma, 86% refractory to anti-PD-1 therapy TIL therapy: nonmyeloablative lymphodepletion (cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg/day IV ×2 days + fludarabine 25 mg/m²/day IV ×5 days) → single adoptive transfer of ≥5×10⁹ TILs → high-dose IL-2 600,000 IU/kg IV Q8H (max 15 doses) vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses PFS Median PFS 7.2 vs 3.1 months (HR 0.50); ORR 49% vs 21%; median OS 25.8 vs 18.9 months; first phase III trial establishing TIL therapy's benefit over standard checkpoint immunotherapy.

records.title: IGNYTE (RP1)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · II · 2025
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma with confirmed progression while on ≥8 weeks of anti–PD-1 as the last prior therapy, given alone or combined with another anticancer agent and including adjuvant anti–PD-1; measurable disease plus an injectable lesion ≥1 cm required; prior oncolytic therapy or serious complications from checkpoint therapy excluded (single-arm) RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) intratumorally 1 × 10⁶ PFU/mL then up to 7 further doses at 1 × 10⁷ PFU/mL Q2W (more allowed; ≤10 mL/dose) + nivolumab 240 mg Q2W from RP1 dose 2 ×8 cycles → 480 mg Q4W ×≤21 cycles (≤2 years) Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety A third of anti-PD-1-failed melanomas responded to intratumoural RP1 with nivolumab (single-arm): the primary objective response rate by modified RECIST was 33.6% (95% CI 25.8-42.0) against a design null of below 15%, though no test result is reported; by conventional RECIST, response was 32.9% (25.2-41.3) with complete response in 15.0%. Responses were deep and durable - median duration 33.7 months (95% CI 14.1-not reached), 69.5% ongoing at 1 year - and noninjected lesions regressed nearly as often as injected. Median progression-free survival was only 3.6 months (2.0-5.0); overall survival 75.3% at 1 year and 63.3% at 2 years, median not reached. Treatment-related adverse events were 90.0% any-grade - commonest fatigue 32.9%, chills 32.1%, pyrexia 30.7%, almost all grade 1-2 - but 12.9% grade 3-4, with five grade 4 events including myocarditis and splenic rupture, and no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: IMCgp100-202 (tebentafusp)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated HLA-A*02:01+ metastatic uveal melanoma Tebentafusp (gp100×CD3 ImmTAC) vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab/ipilimumab/dacarbazine) Overall survival Tebentafusp improved OS versus investigator's choice (median 21.7 vs 16.0 months, HR 0.51) despite low response rates; first therapy to improve survival in metastatic uveal melanoma.

records.title: OptimUM-02
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · II/III · 2026
records.body: First-line HLA-A*02:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma Darovasertib (PKC inhibitor) + crizotinib vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab, ipilimumab+nivolumab, or dacarbazine), 2:1 Progression-free survival Darovasertib plus crizotinib improved progression-free survival over investigator's choice (median 6.9 versus 3.1 months; HR 0.42, p<.0001) with objective response 37.1% versus 5.8% - the first randomised win in HLA-A2-negative metastatic uveal melanoma, the population tebentafusp cannot treat. These are the phase 2 efficacy primary results of a nested phase 2/3 trial; overall survival is the phase 3 primary endpoint and has not been reported. ASCO 2026 LBA9503 - a conference abstract, not yet a full publication.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl 17):LBA9503   Orloff et al. - 2026 - Darovasertib plus crizotinib vs investigator's choice as first-line treatment for HLA-A2 negative [1126b8da]

records.title: Sheng et al (toripalimab + axitinib)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · I · 2019
records.body: Treatment-naive metastatic mucosal melanoma Toripalimab (anti–PD-1) + axitinib Safety and objective response Toripalimab + axitinib achieved an ORR of 48.3% with median PFS 7.5 months in treatment-naive mucosal melanoma, a subtype largely resistant to single-agent checkpoint blockade; key early evidence for IO + VEGF-TKI in mucosal disease.

records.title: SECOMBIT (Ascierto)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — sequencing of targeted therapy & immunotherapy · II · 2023
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Arm A: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily to progression → ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W; Arm B: ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W to progression → encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily; Arm C: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ×8 weeks → ipilimumab + nivolumab to progression → encorafenib + binimetinib 2-year OS 2-year/3-year OS 65%/54% (A), 73%/62% (B), 69%/60% (C); all arms exceeded the prespecified OS threshold; immunotherapy-first and sandwich sequencing trended better than targeted-therapy-first.

records.title: EBIN (Robert)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — sequencing of targeted therapy & immunotherapy · II · 2025
records.body: Untreated, unresectable stage III/IV melanoma with BRAF V600E/K mutations Induction: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ×12 weeks → nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W to progression, toxicity, or 2 years vs no induction: nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W to progression, toxicity, or 2 years PFS No PFS benefit from targeted-therapy induction before checkpoint inhibition (median PFS 9 vs 9 months, HR 0.87); more grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs with induction (42% vs 32%) — does not support induction sequencing.

records.title: Stupp (EORTC-NCIC 26981-22981)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2005
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age ≤70, WHO PS 0-2 RT 60 Gy in 30 fractions + concurrent oral temozolomide 75 mg/m²/day throughout RT (max 49 days), then after a 4-week break six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide 150→200 mg/m² days 1–5 Q4W vs RT alone (60 Gy in 30 fractions) Overall survival Temozolomide added to RT improved median OS (14.6 vs 12.1 months, HR 0.63) and 2-yr OS (26.5% vs 10.4%), with benefit greatest in MGMT-methylated tumors; established the 'Stupp regimen' as standard of care.

records.title: AVAglio (Chinot)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2014
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after surgery RT/temozolomide + bevacizumab vs RT/temozolomide + placebo Progression-free and overall survival (co-primary) Met one co-primary and missed the other: PFS 10.6 vs 6.2 months (stratified HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.55–0.74, p<0.001 against a prespecified alpha of 0.01) but OS 16.8 vs 16.7 months (HR 0.88, 0.76–1.02, p=0.10 against 0.04). Deterioration-free survival was longer on all five prespecified quality-of-life scales and on Karnofsky performance status, and among patients taking glucocorticoids at baseline these were discontinued in 66.3% vs 47.1% — all nominal, since no alpha sits below the two co-primaries. Grade ≥3 adverse events often associated with bevacizumab occurred in 32.5% vs 15.8%. The authors conclude a 4.4-month PFS gain “with quality of life and functional status maintained” at the cost of more adverse events; they do not conclude there is no role. The trial did not establish a survival benefit, and bevacizumab is not standard first-line.

records.title: RTOG 0825 (Gilbert)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2014
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after surgery RT/temozolomide + bevacizumab vs RT/temozolomide + placebo Progression-free and overall survival (co-primary) Upfront bevacizumab did not improve OS (15.7 vs 16.1 months, HR 1.13) and the PFS gain (10.7 vs 7.3 months) missed the prespecified threshold, with more cognitive/QoL decline; reserved for symptomatic recurrence.

records.title: EF-14 (Stupp)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after completing chemoradiation Tumor-treating fields + maintenance temozolomide vs maintenance temozolomide alone Progression-free survival Adding TTFields improved median OS (20.9 vs 16.0 months, HR 0.63) and PFS (6.7 vs 4.0 months); established TTFields as an option added to maintenance temozolomide.

records.title: CeTeG/NOA-09 (Herrlinger)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated glioblastoma, age 18-70 Lomustine + temozolomide vs temozolomide (both with RT) Overall survival Lomustine-temozolomide improved median OS (48.1 vs 31.4 months, HR 0.60) in this small trial; an intensified option for fit MGMT-methylated patients.

records.title: Keime-Guibert
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2007
records.body: Glioblastoma/anaplastic astrocytoma, age ≥70, KPS ≥70 Radiotherapy (50 Gy) + supportive care vs supportive care alone Overall survival RT prolonged median OS (29.1 vs 16.9 weeks, HR 0.47) without worsening QoL or cognition; confirmed a survival benefit of RT in fit elderly patients.

records.title: Roa
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2004
records.body: Glioblastoma, age ≥60, KPS ≥50 Short-course RT (40 Gy/15) vs standard RT (60 Gy/30) Overall survival Abbreviated RT gave equivalent median OS (5.6 vs 5.1 months) with less steroid use; established hypofractionated RT as standard for older patients.

records.title: NOA-08 (Wick)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2012
records.body: Anaplastic astrocytoma/glioblastoma, age >65, KPS ≥60 Dose-dense temozolomide alone vs radiotherapy alone Overall survival (noninferiority) Temozolomide was noninferior to RT (median OS 8.6 vs 9.6 months; EFS 3.3 vs 4.7 months); MGMT methylation predicted benefit from temozolomide, supporting biomarker-guided monotherapy.

records.title: Nordic (Malmström)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2012
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age >60 Temozolomide vs hypofractionated RT (34 Gy/10) vs standard RT (60 Gy/30) Overall survival Temozolomide (median OS 8.3 months) and hypofractionated RT (7.5 months) outperformed standard RT (6.0 months), especially in patients >70; temozolomide benefit confined to MGMT-methylated tumors.

records.title: CCTG CE.6 (Perry)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · III · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age ≥65 Short-course RT (40 Gy/15) + concurrent/adjuvant temozolomide vs short-course RT alone Overall survival Adding temozolomide to short-course RT improved median OS (9.3 vs 7.6 months, HR 0.67), with greatest benefit in MGMT-methylated tumors (13.5 vs 7.7 months); established hypofractionated RT + temozolomide for fit elderly patients.

records.title: EORTC 26101 (Wick)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Recurrent glioblastoma · III · 2017
records.body: Glioblastoma at first progression after chemoradiation Lomustine + bevacizumab vs lomustine alone Overall survival Adding bevacizumab prolonged PFS (4.2 vs 1.5 months) but not OS (9.1 vs 8.6 months, HR 0.95); no survival role for the combination at recurrence.

records.title: REGOMA (Lombardi)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Recurrent glioblastoma · II · 2019
records.body: Glioblastoma at first relapse after surgery and Stupp chemoradiation Regorafenib vs lomustine Overall survival Regorafenib improved median OS (7.4 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.50); a signal supporting regorafenib as a recurrence option pending phase 3 confirmation.

records.title: EORTC 22845 (van den Bent)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · III · 2005
records.body: Adult grade 2 astrocytoma/oligodendroglioma after surgery Early postoperative RT (54 Gy) vs RT deferred until progression Overall and progression-free survival Early RT lengthened PFS (5.3 vs 3.4 years, HR 0.59) but not OS (7.4 vs 7.2 years); supported deferring RT in selected low-risk patients.

records.title: RTOG 9802 (Buckner)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · III · 2016
records.body: High-risk (age ≥40, or <40 with subtotal resection) grade 2 glioma RT + PCV (procarbazine/lomustine/vincristine) vs RT alone Overall survival Adding PCV to RT improved median OS (13.3 vs 7.8 years, HR 0.59) and PFS (10.4 vs 4.0 years), with benefit concentrated in IDH-mutant tumors; established RT+PCV for high-risk low-grade glioma.

records.title: INDIGO (Mellinghoff)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · III · 2023
records.body: Residual/recurrent grade 2 IDH1/2-mutant glioma, surgery only Vorasidenib vs placebo Progression-free survival Vorasidenib, a brain-penetrant IDH inhibitor, prolonged PFS (27.7 vs 11.1 months, HR 0.39) and time to next intervention, with durability confirmed on extended follow-up; established targeted therapy that can delay chemoradiation. FDA-approved August 2024 (Voranigo) - the first systemic therapy for grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma.

records.title: ASCO-SNO Guideline (Mohile et al.)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · N/A · 2022
records.body: Adult diffuse astrocytic and oligodendroglial tumors (IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype, all grades) N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A ASCO-SNO joint guideline organizing glioma management by molecular classification (IDH mutation, 1p19q codeletion) per WHO 2016/2021 CNS criteria. IDH-mutant, 1p19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma (grade 2-3): RT plus PCV (TMZ a reasonable alternative if toxicity a concern); initial therapy may be deferred in favorable-prognosis patients until progression. IDH-mutant, 1p19q-non-codeleted astrocytoma grade 2: RT plus adjuvant TMZ or PCV, with deferral an option in low-risk patients; grade 3: RT plus adjuvant TMZ (per CATNON). IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma may be treated as grade 3 astrocytoma or as IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype: concurrent TMZ/RT followed by 6 months adjuvant TMZ is standard (Stupp regimen); alternating electric field therapy may be added; bevacizumab not recommended for newly diagnosed disease. Hypofractionated RT with TMZ is reasonable when a 6-week course is not appropriate. In older/frail patients: best supportive care, RT alone (MGMT-unmethylated), or TMZ alone (MGMT-methylated). No recommendation possible for recurrent glioblastoma or diffuse midline glioma given insufficient evidence — clinical trial referral is the strong recommendation in both settings. Updated in 2025 (see linked update) to add vorasidenib as an option during the deferral period for IDH-mutant grade 2 tumors, based on the INDIGO trial already filed on this sheet.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2022;40(4):403-426   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2129-2133 rapid recommendation update (vorasidenib) 40300117

records.title: RTOG 9402 (Cairncross)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant grade 3 (anaplastic) glioma & 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma · III · 2006
records.body: Newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors Neoadjuvant PCV → RT vs RT alone Overall survival PCV+RT doubled median OS in 1p/19q-codeleted tumors (14.7 vs 7.3 years, HR 0.59) but not in non-codeleted tumors; established PCV+RT for codeleted anaplastic oligodendroglioma.

records.title: EORTC 26951 (van den Bent)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant grade 3 (anaplastic) glioma & 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma · III · 2006
records.body: Newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors RT (59.4 Gy) → adjuvant PCV vs RT alone Overall survival Adjuvant PCV improved median OS (3.5 vs 2.6 years, HR 0.78), with the largest benefit in 1p/19q-codeleted tumors; confirmed PCV+RT for codeleted disease.

records.title: CATNON (van den Bent)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant grade 3 (anaplastic) glioma & 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma · III · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed 1p/19q non-codeleted anaplastic (grade 3) glioma RT ± concurrent and/or adjuvant temozolomide (2x2 factorial) Overall survival Adjuvant temozolomide improved 5-yr OS (55.9% vs 44.1%, HR 0.65), with benefit confined to IDH-mutant tumors; established adjuvant temozolomide for non-codeleted grade 3 glioma.

records.title: JCOG0504 (Kayama)
records.subtitle: Other CNS Tumors · Brain metastases · III · 2018
records.body: Adults 20-79 yr, ECOG PS 0-2 (or 3 if from neurologic deficit only), with <=4 surgically resected brain metastases and only one lesion >3 cm; primary tumors NSCLC, breast, colon, kidney, ovary, uterine cervix/corpus, stomach, or esophagus; registered and treated within 21 days of resection. Post-resection whole-brain radiotherapy 37.5 Gy in 15 fractions vs post-resection salvage stereotactic radiosurgery (gamma-knife, CyberKnife, or linear accelerator) to residual or new lesions <=3 cm (or >3 cm with GTV <=10 mL), up to 8 lesions, with MRI surveillance every 2 months for year 1 then every 3 months; both initiated within 21 days of surgery; systemic therapy permitted in both arms. Overall survival (noninferiority; one-sided alpha=0.05; noninferiority margin HR <=1.385, ~2.5-month decrease in median OS). Salvage SRS noninferior to WBRT for OS. Median OS 15.6 mo in both arms (WBRT 95% CI 12.3-19.8; SRS 95% CI 11.4-20.8); HR 1.05 (90% CI 0.83-1.33), one-sided P for noninferiority =.027 - margin met. 1-yr OS 61.1% vs 56.7%; 3-yr OS 27.1% vs 27.2%. Intracranial PFS favored WBRT (median 10.4 vs 4.0 mo; HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.46-2.51). In the SRS arm, 37.3% ultimately needed WBRT, 6% needed no postoperative RT and stayed recurrence-free >=12 mo, and median time to protocol-treatment failure was 6.0 mo. MMSE and PS non-worsening were similar at 12 mo (MMSE 45.3% vs 42.5%; PS 46.0% vs 46.3%), but grade 2-4 cognitive dysfunction after day 91 was higher with WBRT (16.4% vs 7.7%, P=.048), as was memory disturbance (16.4% vs 6.8%). Leptomeningeal metastasis as first recurrence 12.9% vs 5.7%. Established surgery + salvage SRS with MRI surveillance as a standard for 1-4 resected brain metastases.

records.title: Aoyama (Intracranial GCT)
records.subtitle: Other CNS Tumors · Intracranial germ cell tumors · II · 2002
records.body: Intracranial germ-cell tumors (pure germinoma, HCG-β-secreting germinoma, mixed / non-germinomatous GCT) (single-arm) EP — etoposide 100 mg/m² + cisplatin 20 mg/m² IV, days 1–5 Q4W, 3 cycles (gross total/subtotal resection) or 4 cycles (partial resection/biopsy) for solitary pure germinoma; ICE — ifosfamide 900 mg/m² + cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 60 mg/m² IV, days 1–5 Q4W, 3–6 cycles (max six) for other GCTs; followed by involved-field RT (24 Gy/12 fx germinoma; 40–54 Gy other GCTs; craniospinal for highly malignant) Disease-related, overall & relapse-free survival; neurocognitive outcome Single-center prospective trial of induction chemo then reduced-dose/volume RT. 5-yr disease-related/overall/relapse-free survival 100%/93%/69% overall (100%/100%/86% for pure germinomas; all 6 non-germinomatous GCTs alive). 8 relapses, all but one salvaged; no full-scale/verbal/performance IQ decline after treatment. Supports chemo (EP/ICE) + reduced-dose involved-field RT, sparing full craniospinal irradiation for germinomas.

records.title: O’Sullivan (NCIC SR2)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · III · 2002
records.body: Extremity soft-tissue sarcoma undergoing limb-conserving surgery + radiotherapy Preoperative RT (50 Gy) vs postoperative RT (66 Gy) Wound complications within 120 days Preoperative RT roughly doubled major wound complications (35% vs 17%, p=0.01) but uses a lower dose and smaller field, trading early morbidity for less late fibrosis; overall survival marginally favoured preoperative RT (p=0.048). Frames RT timing as a deliberate trade-off.

records.title: EORTC 62931 (Woll)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · III · 2012
records.body: Resected grade II–III soft-tissue sarcoma, any site Adjuvant doxorubicin + ifosfamide + lenograstim vs observation Overall survival Did not demonstrate a survival benefit: 5-year OS 66.5% vs 67.8% (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68–1.31, p=0.72); relapse-free survival HR 0.91 (0.67–1.22). Metastases — the mechanism adjuvant chemotherapy should prevent — occurred in 35% of both arms. But the trial fell short of its own design: 141 of the 146 required deaths, with 38 of 351 (11%) ineligible after randomisation, so the interval does not exclude a 32% relative risk reduction. This same report's updated meta-analysis of 2145 patients gives HR 0.86 (p=0.02), and the authors leave the recommendation open pending individual-patient-data analysis. Adjuvant chemotherapy is not standard for resected STS.

records.title: ISG-STS 1001 (Gronchi)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · III · 2017
records.body: Localised high-risk STS of extremity / trunk wall (five histotypes) Neoadjuvant standard epirubicin + ifosfamide (3 cycles) vs histotype-tailored regimen Disease-free survival Standard anthracycline + ifosfamide was superior to histotype-tailored therapy (46-month projected DFS 62% vs 38%; HR 2.00 favouring standard, p=0.006); stopped for futility. Defines 3 cycles of neoadjuvant epirubicin + ifosfamide as standard for high-risk extremity/trunk STS.

records.title: STRASS (EORTC-62092, Bonvalot)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · III · 2020
records.body: Primary, operable retroperitoneal sarcoma Preoperative RT + surgery vs surgery alone Abdominal recurrence-free survival No benefit (median abdominal RFS 4.5 vs 5.0 years; HR 1.01, p=0.95), with substantial radiation toxicity. Preoperative RT should not be standard of care for retroperitoneal sarcoma.

records.title: EORTC 62012 (Judson)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — first-line · III · 2014
records.body: Locally advanced / metastatic high-grade STS, first-line Doxorubicin vs intensified doxorubicin + ifosfamide Overall survival No OS gain: median 12.8 vs 14.3 months, HR 0.83 (95.5% CI 0.67–1.03), p=0.076 against a prespecified boundary of 0.0451. The combination improved PFS (4.6→7.4 months, HR 0.74) and response (14%→26%), but on nominal p-values only — the primary test failed, so no secondary inherits alpha protection — and at a cost: febrile neutropenia 46% with the combination vs 13%, discontinuation for toxicity 18% vs 3%. Single-agent doxorubicin remains the first-line standard; add ifosfamide when tumour shrinkage is the explicit goal.

records.title: GeDDiS (Seddon)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — first-line · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced / metastatic STS, first-line Doxorubicin vs gemcitabine + docetaxel Progression-free at 24 weeks No difference (24-week PFS 46.3% vs 46.4%; median PFS 23.3 vs 23.7 weeks). Confirms doxorubicin as the first-line standard; gemcitabine + docetaxel is not a superior front-line option.

records.title: ANNOUNCE (Tap)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — first-line · III · 2020
records.body: Anthracycline-naive advanced STS Olaratumab 20 mg/kg IV cycle 1 (loading), then 15 mg/kg IV, days 1 and 8 Q3W + doxorubicin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, up to 8 21-day cycles, then olaratumab monotherapy to progression vs doxorubicin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 + placebo, up to 8 cycles Overall survival (total STS and leiomyosarcoma) No OS benefit (total STS HR 1.05, 20.4 vs 19.7 months; LMS HR 0.95). The confirmatory trial refuted the earlier phase II signal and olaratumab was withdrawn. Defining negative.

records.title: PALETTE (van der Graaf)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · III · 2012
records.body: Metastatic non-adipocytic STS after chemotherapy Pazopanib vs placebo Progression-free survival PFS 4.6 vs 1.6 months (HR 0.31, p<0.0001); OS non-significant. Approval; standard later-line option for non-adipocytic STS.

records.title: Trabectedin vs dacarbazine (Demetri)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · III · 2016
records.body: Metastatic liposarcoma / leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline + ≥1 line Trabectedin vs dacarbazine Overall survival PFS 4.2 vs 1.5 months (HR 0.55, p<0.001); OS non-significant (12.4 vs 12.9 months). Approval for L-sarcomas on disease control.

records.title: Eribulin vs dacarbazine (Schöffski)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · III · 2016
records.body: Advanced liposarcoma / leiomyosarcoma after ≥2 regimens Eribulin vs dacarbazine Overall survival OS 13.5 vs 11.5 months (HR 0.77, p=0.017); benefit driven by liposarcoma. Approval (liposarcoma after anthracycline).

records.title: SPEARHEAD-1 (afami-cel, D’Angelo)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · II · 2024
records.body: HLA-A*02, MAGE-A4+ advanced synovial sarcoma / myxoid round-cell liposarcoma, pre-treated Afamitresgene autoleucel — single IV infusion day 1 (transduced dose 1.0–10.0×10⁹ T cells) after lymphodepletion (fludarabine 30 mg/m² IV days −7 to −4 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV days −5 to −3); one infusion only, no re-treatment (single-arm) Overall response rate ORR 37% overall, 39% in synovial sarcoma, durable in heavily pre-treated patients. Basis for the first engineered TCR T-cell therapy approved in a solid tumour (synovial sarcoma). Phase II, single-arm registration study.

records.title: Atezolizumab in ASPS (Chen / Van Tine)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · II · 2023
records.body: Advanced alveolar soft part sarcoma (adult + paediatric) Atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1), single-arm Objective response rate ORR 37% (1 complete, 18 partial responses), responses durable. First and only approved systemic therapy for ASPS — a low-mutation sarcoma that is nonetheless immunotherapy-responsive. Phase II, single-arm registration trial.

records.title: AMPECT (nab-sirolimus, Wagner)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · II · 2021
records.body: Advanced malignant PEComa nab-Sirolimus 100 mg/m² IV over 30 min days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle (once weekly ×2, Q3W), to progression, toxicity, or patient preference (single-arm) Objective response rate ORR 39%, durable; responses enriched in TSC1/TSC2-mutant tumours (89% vs 13%). First approved therapy for malignant PEComa. Phase II, single-arm registration trial.

records.title: SARC041
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · III · 2026
records.body: Recurrent or metastatic dedifferentiated liposarcoma with RECIST progression within 6 months; any number of prior systemic therapies Abemaciclib 200 mg orally twice daily vs matching placebo Progression-free survival Abemaciclib improved median PFS (9.67 vs 1.52 months; HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.25–0.59; P<0.001). ORR was 9.3% vs 0% (P=0.057); median OS was not reached vs 25.45 months (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.28–1.07; P=0.077). Grade ≥3 adverse-event rates were similar and no new safety signals emerged.

records.title: DeFi (nirogacestat, Gounder)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Borderline / locally aggressive · III · 2023
records.body: Progressing desmoid tumours (aggressive fibromatosis) Nirogacestat 150 mg orally twice daily, continuous in 28-day cycles, to progression vs placebo Progression-free survival PFS HR 0.29 (p<0.001); 2-year event-free 76% vs 44%; ORR 41% vs 8%. First approved systemic therapy for desmoid tumours.

records.title: Sorafenib for desmoid (Gounder, Alliance A091105)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Borderline / locally aggressive · III · 2018
