records.body: Desmoid tumour requiring treatment: unresectable or high-morbidity surgery, progressive, or symptomatic; about half newly diagnosed Sorafenib vs placebo (crossover allowed) Progression-free survival 2-year PFS 81% vs 36% (HR 0.13, 95% CI 0.05–0.31, p<0.001) in 84 of 87 randomised, but the trial was halted and unblinded after the DSMB requested an efficacy analysis at the preplanned interim, when 24 of the 52 required events had been observed, leaving the reported result on 29 events, so the effect size is likely overstated. ORR 33% vs 20% is reported descriptively, with no comparative test; the authors read the 20% placebo response as support for an initial period of observation in newly diagnosed disease. Established a systemic option for desmoid (predates nirogacestat).

records.title: ENLIVEN (pexidartinib, Tap)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Borderline / locally aggressive · III · 2019
records.body: Advanced tenosynovial giant cell tumour not amenable to surgery Pexidartinib (CSF1R inhibitor) vs placebo Overall response at week 25 ORR 39% vs 0% (p<0.0001) with functional improvement; mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity is an identified risk. First systemic therapy for TGCT.

records.title: INT-0133 (mifamurtide, Meyers)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Bone sarcoma — osteosarcoma · III · 2008
records.body: Newly diagnosed resectable non-metastatic osteosarcoma ± ifosfamide and ± muramyl tripeptide (MTP-PE) added to cisplatin/doxorubicin/methotrexate (2×2) Event-free and overall survival Adding MTP-PE improved 6-year OS 70%→78% (HR 0.71, p=0.03); adding ifosfamide did not. Basis for mifamurtide (EU-approved); ifosfamide not added to the MAP backbone.

records.title: EURAMOS-1 (Marina)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Bone sarcoma — osteosarcoma · III · 2016
records.body: High-grade osteosarcoma with poor histologic response to preoperative MAP Postoperative MAP vs MAPIE (added ifosfamide + etoposide) Event-free survival No EFS benefit from intensification (HR 0.98) and more toxicity. Defines MAP as standard of care even for poor responders; escalating chemotherapy on poor response does not help.

records.title: INT-0091 (Grier)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Bone sarcoma — Ewing sarcoma · III · 2003
records.body: Newly diagnosed Ewing sarcoma / PNET of bone Standard VDC (+ dactinomycin) vs VDC alternating with ifosfamide + etoposide (VDC/IE) Event-free survival In non-metastatic disease, VDC/IE improved 5-year EFS 54%→69% (p=0.005) and OS 61%→72% (p=0.01); no benefit in metastatic disease. Established VDC/IE as the chemotherapy backbone.

records.title: AEWS0031 (Womer)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Bone sarcoma — Ewing sarcoma · III · 2012
records.body: Localised Ewing sarcoma Interval-compressed VDC/IE every 2 weeks vs every 3 weeks Event-free survival Dose-dense scheduling improved 5-year EFS 65%→73% (p=0.048) with no added toxicity. Established interval compression as the standard for localised Ewing.

records.title: rEECur (McCabe)
records.subtitle: Soft Tissue & Bone Sarcoma · Bone sarcoma — Ewing sarcoma · II/III · 2022
records.body: Recurrent / primary refractory Ewing sarcoma, age 4–50 High-dose ifosfamide vs topotecan + cyclophosphamide (4-arm RCT; also irinotecan/temozolomide, gemcitabine/docetaxel) Event-free survival High-dose ifosfamide outperformed topotecan + cyclophosphamide (median OS 16.8 vs 10.4 months; EFS 5.7 vs 3.7 months). First randomised trial in relapsed/refractory Ewing; positions high-dose ifosfamide as preferred salvage. Conference abstract (ASCO 2022) — full publication pending.

records.title: ESMO Lymphomas Guideline (Eyre et al.)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Guidelines · N/A · 2025
records.body: DLBCL, PCNSL, follicular lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and nodal PTCL (comprehensive multi-entity guideline) N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A Current ESMO clinical practice guideline across the seven commonest lymphoma entities. DLBCL: 6 cycles of R-CHOP remains standard for IPI 0-1; 6 cycles of R-Pola-CHP is a first-line option for IPI >=2; PET-adapted cycle number and involved-site radiotherapy are formalised for limited-stage disease; FISH for MYC rearrangement should be carried out, with BCL2 FISH if MYC is rearranged, to identify double-hit disease. Early relapsed or refractory DLBCL within 12 months: axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel, with bispecific antibodies and glofitamab-GemOx as later options. Hodgkin lymphoma: PET-adapted therapy remains central, and BrECADD and nivolumab-AVD are frontline standards for advanced-stage disease. Also covers follicular, mantle cell and marginal zone lymphoma, primary CNS lymphoma and nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2025 (Journal Pre-proof, ANNONC 1872)   Ann Oncol 2015;26(Suppl 5):v116-v125   Ann Oncol 2018;29(Suppl 4):iv19-iv29

records.title: LNH-98.5 (GELA)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Establishing R-CHOP immunochemotherapy · III · 2002
records.body: Previously untreated DLBCL, age 60-80, stage II-IV Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 of each cycle + CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) ×8 cycles Q3W vs CHOP ×8 cycles Q3W Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, disease-free survival, response rate, toxicity Adding rituximab to CHOP improved survival in elderly DLBCL and established R-CHOP as the frontline standard; the first trial to show that adding an antibody to chemotherapy improves survival in lymphoma. At a median 5 yrs the benefit held: OS 58% vs 45%, EFS 47% vs 29%. The prespecified 2-yr analysis the trial was reported on gave EFS 57% vs 38%, p<0.001, and OS 70% vs 57%, p=0.007; complete or unconfirmed complete response 76% vs 63%, p=0.005, with complete response alone 52% vs 37%. No clinically meaningful increase in toxicity.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2002;346:235-242   J Clin Oncol 2005;23:4117-4126 5-year follow-up 15867204

records.title: MInT
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Establishing R-CHOP immunochemotherapy · III · 2006
records.body: Untreated CD20-positive DLBCL, age 18-60, age-adjusted IPI 0-1 in stage II-IV, or stage I with bulk Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 of each cycle (6 doses) + 6 cycles CHOP-like chemotherapy vs 6 cycles CHOP-like chemotherapy alone; bulky/extranodal sites received consolidation radiotherapy Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: response, progression during therapy, progression-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Adding rituximab to CHOP-like chemotherapy raised 3-yr EFS from 59% to 79% in young good-prognosis DLBCL, an absolute gain of 20 points (95% CI 13-27), and 3-yr OS from 84% to 93%, a gain of 9 points (95% CI 3-13); rituximab became standard in this age group on these data. Read the effect size with care for 3 reasons. The trial stopped early for efficacy at its first interim analysis, so every figure here is post-truncation and likely flatters the benefit. The widely quoted HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.34-0.59) comes from a multivariable model adjusted for bulk and age-adjusted IPI, not from the primary analysis. And the CHOP versus CHOEP comparison often cited from this trial was not randomised - regimen was chosen by country - and the authors state it was not an endpoint. Grade 3-4 toxicity did not differ materially; treatment-related deaths were 6 with rituximab vs 1 without, on small numbers.

records.title: RICOVER-60
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Establishing R-CHOP immunochemotherapy · III · 2008
records.body: Untreated aggressive CD20+ B-cell lymphoma, aged 61-80. 1,242 were enrolled and 1,222 randomly assigned after 20 were excluded for missing or retracted consent 2×2 factorial: 6 vs 8 cycles CHOP-14 (cyclophosphamide–doxorubicin–vincristine–prednisone every 14 days with G-CSF support), each ± rituximab 375 mg/m² IV (8 doses, held constant across both R arms); all patients received a vincristine–prednisone pre-phase Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: response, progression during therapy, progression-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Six cycles of R-CHOP-14 is the preferred regimen: rituximab drives the benefit, and a 7th and 8th cycle on top bought nothing and cost lives. 3-year event-free survival was 47.2% with 6 cycles of CHOP-14, 53.0% with 8, 66.5% with 6 cycles of R-CHOP-14 and 63.1% with 8. Against 6 cycles of CHOP-14 the gain was 19.3 points (95% CI 11.1 to 27.5) for 6 cycles of R-CHOP-14 and 15.9 (7.6 to 24.2) for 8; while 8 cycles of CHOP-14 without rituximab improved event-free survival, by 5.8 points on an interval of -2.8 to 14.4, but not progression-free or overall survival. 3-year overall survival was 67.7%, 66.0%, 78.1% and 72.5% in the same order, so the 8-cycle rituximab arm sat 5.6 points below the 6-cycle one, which the authors attribute to more treatment-associated deaths, 8% against 6%, and more deaths from lymphoma or second cancers. Only 6 cycles of R-CHOP-14 improved survival against the control, by 10.4 points (2.8 to 18.0); complete response was 78% against 68%.

records.title: R-CHOP-14 v 21 (NCRI)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Schedule & elderly / frail adaptations · III · 2013
records.body: Untreated DLBCL, aged 18 or over, bulky stage IA or stage IB-IV, any IPI score. All 1,080 randomised patients were analysed 6 cycles R-CHOP Q2W plus 2 further rituximab doses (R-CHOP-14, with G-CSF) vs 8 cycles R-CHOP Q3W (R-CHOP-21); rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1, CHOP backbone (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisolone) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, response rate, toxicity Dose-dense scheduling did not improve survival: the trial set out to show R-CHOP every 14 days superior to every 21 days and did not. 2-year overall survival was 82.7% with R-CHOP-14 against 80.8% with R-CHOP-21, hazard ratio for death 0.90 (95% CI 0.70 to 1.15), and the primary endpoint was missed. Progression-free survival did not separate either, hazard ratio 0.94 (0.76 to 1.17). R-CHOP-14 did not improve response: complete or unconfirmed complete response was 58% against 63% with the 21-day schedule, while overall response was 91% against 88%; neither difference was established. Treatment-related deaths were 9 with the 14-day schedule against 3 with the 21-day, a threefold numerical excess on 12 events, and the difference did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up 46 months. R-CHOP every 21 days remains the standard schedule.

records.title: LNH03-7B (R-miniCHOP)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Schedule & elderly / frail adaptations · II · 2011
records.body: Untreated CD20-positive DLBCL, age over 80, age-adjusted IPI 1-3 (single-arm) R-miniCHOP x6 cycles Q3W - rituximab 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 400 mg/m2, doxorubicin 25 mg/m2, vincristine 1 mg flat (all IV day 1), prednisone 40 mg/m2 PO days 1-5 Primary: overall survival. Secondary: response, event-free survival, disease-free survival, progression-free survival, safety Attenuated-dose CHOP with full-dose rituximab extended curative-intent immunochemotherapy past 80, and is a standard reference for fit patients of that age. Median OS 29 mo, 2-yr OS 59%, and complete or unconfirmed complete response 62% (complete response alone 40%, 59 of 149). Toxicity was not trivial: 27 patients (18%) died during treatment and 12 deaths were attributed to treatment toxicity. The first prospective trial confined to DLBCL over 80, median age 83, so it carries no comparator and no randomised evidence that attenuation preserves efficacy.

records.title: FLYER
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Schedule & elderly / frail adaptations · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated aggressive CD20-positive B-cell lymphoma, age 18-60, age-adjusted IPI 0 and no bulk (largest mass <7.5 cm) 6 cycles R-CHOP Q3W vs 4 cycles R-CHOP Q3W + 2 further rituximab doses (6 rituximab doses in both arms, median 106 days of antibody in each) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, complete response rate, safety Four cycles of R-CHOP plus 2 further rituximab doses were non-inferior to 6 cycles in young patients with age-adjusted IPI 0 and no bulk, with less toxicity: 3-yr PFS 96% vs 94%, absolute difference 3%, and fewer non-haematological adverse events (1036 vs 1280). The chemotherapy is shortened, not the antibody - both arms received 6 rituximab doses over a median 106 days, and the authors do not recommend fewer. Two caveats limit how far this travels. The primary endpoint was changed from event-free to progression-free survival by protocol amendment after the first interim analysis, which showed event-free survival running below the assumed rate. And only non-inferiority was tested; no superiority test was performed, so 4 cycles is a defensible option in this narrow good-prognosis group but was never shown to be better.

records.title: CALGB/Alliance 50303
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated stage II-IV DLBCL, or stage I primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma; any IPI DA-EPOCH-R ×6 21-day cycles, pharmacodynamically dose-adjusted vs R-CHOP ×6 21-day cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response rate, toxicity Intensifying the backbone with infusional dose-adjusted DA-EPOCH-R did not improve progression-free survival over R-CHOP; the primary endpoint was missed (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.68-1.27, p=0.65) and overall survival was no better (HR 1.09, 0.75-1.59, p=0.64), with 5-yr PFS 68% vs 66%. Toxicity was substantially worse: grade 3-5 treatment-related events 98% vs 78%, grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia 35% vs 18%, neuropathy 19% vs 3%, mucositis 8% vs 2%; 5 treatment-related deaths (2%) in each arm. Efficacy is reported on the 491 of 524 randomised who were eligible. A post-hoc subgroup with IPI 3-5 favoured DA-EPOCH-R for PFS (HR 0.63, 0.41-0.99) with no difference in OS (HR 0.78, 0.47-1.32), so it remains a hypothesis. R-CHOP remains the standard.

records.title: GOYA
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated advanced CD20+ DLBCL Obinutuzumab 1000 mg IV (days 1, 8 and 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of cycles 2-8) + CHOP vs rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 of cycles 1-8 + CHOP; 8 21-day antibody cycles with 6 or 8 cycles of CHOP Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, event-free survival, complete response rate, overall response rate, disease-free survival, time to next antilymphoma treatment, safety Substituting the glycoengineered anti-CD20 obinutuzumab for rituximab did not improve progression-free survival; the primary endpoint was missed, with 3-yr PFS 69.6% vs 66.9%, stratified HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.76-1.11, p=0.39). Overall survival was identical (3-yr 81.2% vs 81.4%, HR 1.00, 0.78-1.28) and independent review agreed with the investigators (HR 0.89, 0.72-1.10). Toxicity rose: grade 3-5 adverse events 73.7% vs 64.7%, serious 42.6% vs 37.6% and fatal 5.8% vs 4.3%, all on the 1,407 treated; any-grade infusion-related reactions 36% vs 24% were the largest gap. A preplanned exploratory investigator-assessed analysis in the 540 germinal-centre patients gave HR 0.72 (0.51-1.03), a hypothesis rather than a result: the interval crosses 1, no interaction test is reported, and among the 933 of 1,418 with a cell-of-origin result the overall HR was already 0.82 (0.64-1.04). Unlike in CLL and follicular lymphoma, a more potent anti-CD20 does not beat rituximab in DLBCL.

records.title: REMoDL-B
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated DLBCL, randomised after one cycle of R-CHOP and stratified by cell of origin from real-time gene-expression profiling; patients whose profiling was unsuccessful were not randomised and continued on R-CHOP R-CHOP cycle 1 in all patients → randomised from cycle 2 to bortezomib 1.3 mg/m² IV or 1.6 mg/m² SC on days 1 and 8 + R-CHOP ×5 vs R-CHOP ×5; 6 cycles in total in both arms Primary: 30-month progression-free survival. Secondary: progression-free survival by cell-of-origin subgroup, overall survival, event-free survival, response, response duration, peripheral neuropathy, quality of life, safety Adding bortezomib to R-CHOP did not meet its primary endpoint. Among the 719 patients classified as ABC or GCB in real time and randomised on that result, 30-mo PFS was 74.3% vs 70.1%: HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.65-1.13, p=0.28), and 0.84 (0.64-1.11) in the prespecified adjusted model. Overall survival did not differ (30-mo 83.6% vs 82.7%, HR 0.89, 0.62-1.28). Neuropathy was the price: any grade more common, grade 3 or worse 3.8% vs 2.2%; haematological toxicity was not increased. A 5-yr update, in 801 patients reclassified retrospectively, again found nothing overall (PFS HR 0.81, p=0.085; OS HR 0.86, p=0.32) but reported a treatment-by-cell-of-origin interaction for PFS (interaction p=0.026, heterogeneity p=0.023, both nominal): PFS HR 0.65 (0.43-0.98) in ABC and 0.46 (0.26-0.84) in molecular high-grade, against 1.05 (0.74-1.5) in GCB. No interaction test is reported for OS, so the survival differences by subtype are descriptive. Hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2019;20:649-662   J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2718-2723 5-year molecular-subgroup follow-up 36972491

records.title: PHOENIX
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated non-germinal-centre B-cell DLBCL by Hans immunohistochemistry, stage II-IV Ibrutinib 560 mg PO once daily + R-CHOP vs placebo + R-CHOP; 6 or 8 21-day cycles Primary: event-free survival in the intent-to-treat non-germinal-centre population; event-free survival in the ABC subset. Secondary: progression-free survival, complete response rate, overall survival, safety Adding ibrutinib to R-CHOP missed both co-primary endpoints: event-free survival in the ITT non-GCB population (HR 0.934, 95% CI 0.726-1.200, p=0.59) and in the gene-expression-defined ABC subset (HR 0.949, 0.704-1.279, p=0.73). Selecting more precisely for ABC recovered nothing, and overall survival was flat (HR 0.991, 0.712-1.380). A prespecified exploratory treatment-by-age interaction test returned nominal p=0.0365 for continuous age and p=0.0087 below 60, but the within-stratum estimates behind it are post hoc: under 60, EFS HR 0.579 (0.380-0.881); 60 or older, EFS HR 1.228 (0.887-1.699) and OS HR 1.440 (0.963-2.152), both numerically worse with ibrutinib. The split tracks how much R-CHOP each group received: in patients 60 or older, serious adverse events were 63.4% vs 38.2%, R-CHOP was stopped for toxicity in 35.1% vs 15.0% and 6 or more cycles were delivered in 73.7% vs 88.8%, against 35.7% vs 28.6%, 12.3% vs 7.6% and 92.9% vs 93.0% under 60. R-CHOP remains standard.

records.title: ROBUST
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated ABC-type DLBCL by prospective central gene-expression profiling, stage II-IV, IPI 2 or higher; germinal-centre and unclassified DLBCL were ineligible Lenalidomide 15 mg PO days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle + R-CHOP ×6 cycles (R²-CHOP) vs placebo + R-CHOP ×6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, overall and complete response rate, duration of response, time to next antilymphoma treatment, safety Adding lenalidomide to R-CHOP in prospectively selected ABC-type disease did not improve progression-free survival; the primary endpoint was missed (IRAC-assessed HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.63-1.14, p=0.29, against a design target of HR 0.625) and the key secondary EFS ran the wrong way (HR 1.04, 0.80-1.34, p=0.73, nominal). The authors call the OS data immature (HR 0.93, 0.65-1.32). Response was the same in both arms: ORR 91%, CR 69% vs 65%. Grade 3/4 toxicity was worse with lenalidomide (neutropenia 60% vs 48%, anaemia 22% vs 14%, thrombocytopenia 17% vs 11%, febrile neutropenia 14% vs 9%); 17% vs 11% discontinued for an adverse event, and 75% vs 84% completed all 6 cycles of both drugs. The cautionary tale is the selection: central pathology screened 2,109 to randomise 570 (27%), and the authors raise the resulting 31-day median from diagnosis to treatment as a possible bias towards less high-risk disease; control patients did better than projected, at 2-yr PFS 64% and OS 80%.

records.title: SWOG 9704
records.subtitle: DLBCL · High-risk consolidation — upfront autologous transplant · III · 2013
records.body: High-intermediate- or high-risk aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma by age-adjusted IPI, randomised only after at least a partial response to five cycles of CHOP or R-CHOP CHOP or R-CHOP ×5 cycles in all patients → responders randomised to 1 further cycle then autologous stem-cell transplant with total-body irradiation or carmustine/etoposide/cyclophosphamide conditioning vs 3 further cycles, 8 in total Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: second malignancy, safety Upfront autologous transplantation in first remission improved progression-free survival but not overall survival, and both were primary endpoints: 2-yr PFS 69% vs 55% (HR 1.72 favouring transplant, 95% CI 1.18-2.51, p=0.005) against 2-yr OS 74% vs 71% (HR 1.26, 0.82-1.94, p=0.30). Effective salvage explains the gap: 18 of the 62 control relapses (29%) survived progression-free, whereas 23 of the 28 relapses (82%) after early transplant were fatal. Applicability to modern DLBCL is the open question — only 150 of 225 randomised B-cell patients received rituximab — but within that subgroup the estimate runs the same way, less precisely (2-yr PFS 73% vs 63%; HR 1.56, 0.92-2.63, p=0.10), with no differential effect by induction (interaction p=0.33). Grade 3/4 infection 50% vs 13%; deaths from toxicity 5% vs 2%. An OS advantage confined to the 88 high-risk patients (82% vs 64%) was unplanned and underpowered, and the high-intermediate majority ran the other way (70% vs 75%).

records.title: POLARIX
records.subtitle: DLBCL · New frontline standards — ADC, immunomodulation & epigenetics · III · 2022
records.body: Previously untreated DLBCL, age 18-80, IPI 2-5 Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV day 1 (replacing vincristine) + R-CHP ×6 cycles Q3W (pola-R-CHP), then rituximab ×2 cycles vs R-CHOP ×6 cycles Q3W, then rituximab ×2 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, complete response rate, overall survival, disease-free survival, safety Replacing vincristine with the CD79b antibody-drug conjugate polatuzumab vedotin holds a progression-free survival advantage out to 5 years, but overall survival has never separated: 5-yr PFS 64.9% vs 59.1% (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.62-0.97) against 5-yr OS 82.3% vs 79.5% (HR 0.85, 0.63-1.15), the survival interval crossing 1 at the 2-yr cut and again at 5 yr. The tangible gain is less relapse to treat: over that time 25.5% vs 35.3% needed any subsequent line. The primary endpoint was met at the 2-yr analysis (PFS HR 0.73, 0.57-0.95, p=0.02; 2-yr PFS 76.7% vs 70.2%), on grade >=3 adverse events of 60.7% vs 59.8% but grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia 13.8% vs 8.0%. In exploratory subgroups carrying no interaction test, benefit sat in ABC-type disease (5-yr PFS HR 0.38, 0.24-0.59) and not GCB (1.07, 0.74-1.56), so no comparison between subtypes is licensed.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2022;386:351-363   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:3698-3705 5-year follow-up 40991874

records.title: frontMIND
records.subtitle: DLBCL · New frontline standards — ADC, immunomodulation & epigenetics · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated DLBCL or high-grade B-cell lymphoma at high-intermediate or high risk (IPI 3-5, or age-adjusted IPI 2-3), starting treatment within 28 days of the diagnostic biopsy Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg IV days 1, 8 and 15 + lenalidomide 25 mg PO days 1-10 + R-CHOP ×6 21-day cycles vs matching placebos + R-CHOP ×6 21-day cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, complete response rate, objective response, progression-free survival by cell-of-origin subtype, time to next treatment, CNS relapse, quality of life, safety Adding tafasitamab and lenalidomide to R-CHOP in high-risk untreated disease cut progression or death by 25%: the primary endpoint was met (PFS HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59-0.96, p=0.0194; 2-yr PFS 71.1% vs 62.9%), with event-free survival also met in the hierarchy (HR 0.79, 0.64-0.97, p=0.026). Overall survival was formally tested at this interim analysis and not met (HR 0.85, 0.63-1.14, p=0.2703); the authors call the data immature and will reassess at the 5-year final analysis. The cost is real: grade >=3 treatment-emergent events 87% vs 76%, serious events 50% vs 39%, fatal events 6% vs 4%, plus tafasitamab infusions on days 1, 8 and 15 of every cycle and lenalidomide on days 1-10. Cell-of-origin subgroups were prespecified but not powered, and no interaction test was reported, so no comparison between them is licensed: ABC-like HR 0.59 (0.36-0.95), GCB-like 0.69 (0.40-1.19). An option in high-risk disease, not an established first-line standard.

records.title: DEB
records.subtitle: DLBCL · New frontline standards — ADC, immunomodulation & epigenetics · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated MYC/BCL2 double-expressor DLBCL, age 18-80, IPI 2-5; double-hit and triple-hit lymphoma excluded by protocol Tucidinostat 20 mg PO days 1, 4, 8 and 11 of each 21-day cycle + R-CHOP ×6 cycles → tucidinostat maintenance up to 24 weeks in complete responders vs matching placebo + R-CHOP ×6 cycles → placebo maintenance Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, progression-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, safety Adding the HDAC inhibitor tucidinostat to R-CHOP in MYC/BCL2 double-expressor disease: the primary endpoint was met on event-free survival, 2-yr EFS 60.3% vs 50.5% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.54-0.96, p=0.02), on a complete-response rate of 73.0% vs 61.8%. The trial was not designed to test the survival endpoints, and each ran the same way on an interval crossing 1: PFS HR 0.78 (0.56-1.09), OS 0.77 (0.53-1.13), disease-free survival 0.79 (0.51-1.20). Toxicity is the practical objection and it sits in the maintenance phase: grade >=3 events 85.8% vs 72.6% during combination therapy but 77.4% vs 39.1% during maintenance, in the 137 and 115 patients who received it. On combination, grade 3-4 neutropenia 60.7% vs 45.3% and infectious pneumonia 15.6% vs 7.1%. Conducted entirely in China. Testing tucidinostat rather than bortezomib, it extends the double-expressor hypothesis without validating REMoDL-B's bortezomib signal.
records.keywords: JAMA 2026;335:1684-1693   Lancet Oncol 2019;20:649-662 REMoDL-B exploratory bortezomib context 30948276

records.title: Lewis (International CNS Prophylaxis Study Group)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · CNS prophylaxis in high-risk disease · N/A · 2023
records.body: DLBCL or high-grade B-cell lymphoma, age 18-80, at high risk of CNS progression — CNS-IPI 4 or more, double- or triple-hit lymphoma, kidney or adrenal involvement, or primary testicular or breast lymphoma — treated outside a trial with CHOP, DA-EPOCH, CHOEP or CEOP plus an anti-CD20 antibody, without first-line autologous transplant High-dose methotrexate, median 2 cycles (range 1-6), >=3 g/m² in 73%, cumulative median 6 g/m², given during frontline chemoimmunotherapy in 35% and after completion in 49% (n=425) vs no high-dose methotrexate (n=1,993) Primary: CNS progression. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival The largest and most rigorous evidence against routine high-dose methotrexate prophylaxis. Analysed from diagnosis it appeared to lower CNS progression (adjusted HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.38-0.90, p=0.014), but that estimate is inflated by immortal-time bias, since a patient must survive induction to receive it — and even at face value the adjusted 5-yr risk difference across the cohort is 1.6% (-1.5 to 4.4), a number needed to treat of 63. Confined to the 1,616 patients in complete response at the end of induction, the clean landmark, the association no longer stands: adjusted HR 0.74 (0.4-1.3, p=0.30) on an adjusted 5-yr CNS-progression risk of 5.0% vs 6.5%. Among those complete responders no subgroup showed a reduction except high-grade B-cell lymphoma and CNS-IPI 4, and neither dose nor timing separated. Exposure was assigned by clinicians, not randomised, and no interaction test was reported.

records.title: Alizadeh et al. (Lymphochip)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Molecular classification — cell of origin · N/A · 2000
records.body: De novo DLBCL, untreated at biopsy, treated with anthracycline-based multi-agent chemotherapy N/A — gene expression profiling study, not a treatment trial N/A — molecular classification and correlation with overall/event-free survival The study that established DLBCL as at least 2 molecularly distinct diseases by cell of origin. Unsupervised clustering of expression data split cases into germinal-centre B-cell-like (BCL-6, CD10, A-myb) and activated B-cell-like (IRF4/MUM1, BCL-2, FLIP), and the split tracked survival after comparable anthracycline-based chemotherapy: 76% vs 16% alive at 5 yr across the 40 patients with survival data (19 GCB, 21 ABC; nominal p=0.01 on the whole curve), and it still separated survival within the 24 patients at IPI 0-2 (nominal p=0.05). The subgroups were derived post hoc from the expression data itself and no hazard ratio, interval or multivariable model appears anywhere, so the classification is shown to add information alongside the IPI rather than to be independent of it; 5 germinal-centre patients died within 2 yr and 3 activated-B patients were alive at 5 yr. Cell of origin was later formalised in immunohistochemical and gene-expression assays and remains standard.

records.title: PARMA
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · N/A · 1995
records.body: Intermediate- or high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma in first or second relapse, age 18-60, after a pre-rituximab doxorubicin-containing regimen and a complete response to initial induction maintained at least 4 weeks; chemosensitive, meaning a complete or partial response to 2 courses of DHAP; CNS or bone marrow involvement at relapse excluded Involved-field radiotherapy 26 Gy if indicated → BEAC + autologous bone marrow transplantation vs 4 further courses of DHAP → involved-field radiotherapy 35 Gy if indicated Event-free survival, overall survival, response, toxicity Established autologous transplantation as the standard for chemosensitive relapsed aggressive NHL, and still the reference point — though it predates rituximab. Transplantation improved 5-yr EFS 46% vs 12% and 5-yr OS 53% vs 32%. Chemosensitivity is the gate the whole strategy rests on: 5-yr OS was 42% in the randomised patients against 11% in the 90 who never responded to DHAP. Delayed transplant, after the control arm had failed, salvaged only 2 of 18. Toxic deaths 3 of the 49 actually transplanted (6%) vs 0 of 54; renal toxicity ran the other way, 5 cases after transplant vs 14 on further DHAP. Read the control arm carefully: 11 of the 20 control-arm survivors were alive with progressive disease, so 32% at 5 yrs is not 32% in remission. Median follow-up 63 mo; stopped early for poor accrual, and the authors say the population was deliberately selected in the control arm's favour.

records.title: HOVON 44
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · III · 2008
records.body: Relapsed or refractory aggressive CD20+ B-cell NHL after anthracycline, age 18-65 Rituximab + DHAP-VIM-DHAP → BEAM + ASCT if CR/PR after 2 cycles vs DHAP-VIM-DHAP → BEAM + ASCT if CR/PR after 2 cycles Response rate, failure-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival Adding rituximab to DHAP-VIM-DHAP reinduction before BEAM and autologous transplant improved every measure of disease control but not survival. Response after 2 cycles 75% vs 54%, more patients reached transplant 63% vs 46%, and 24-mo failure-free survival 50% vs 24% (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.70). Overall survival did not differ: 24-mo 59% vs 52%, HR 0.76 (0.52-1.10). The authors lean on an adjusted model, OS HR 0.60 (0.41-0.89), but its covariates were chosen after the data were seen. Two limits govern how far this travels. Only 4% in either arm had had rituximab before and 85% had a CHOP-like first-line regimen, so this is rituximab-naive relapse, not relapse after R-CHOP. And the publication reports no adverse-event table, no toxicity grades and no treatment-related mortality; its whole safety statement is a Discussion sentence, data not shown, that infection rates and count recovery were unaffected. Median follow-up 31 mo.

records.title: CORAL
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · III · 2010
records.body: Relapsed or refractory CD20+ DLBCL after first-line CHOP-like therapy, age 18-65 R-ICE ×3 q3w → BEAM + ASCT in responders vs R-DHAP ×3 q3w → BEAM + ASCT in responders Primary: mobilisation-adjusted response rate after 3 cycles. Secondary: event-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, overall response rate, stem-cell mobilisation, toxicity R-ICE and R-DHAP are interchangeable as salvage before BEAM and autologous transplant; what decides outcome is not the regimen but what preceded it. Mobilisation-adjusted response after 3 cycles 52.3% vs 54.5%, 3-yr EFS 26% vs 35%, 3-yr OS 47% vs 51% — no difference on any measure. Prior rituximab and early relapse are what separate patients: 3-yr EFS 21% with prior rituximab vs 47% without, and 20% in refractory disease or relapse within 12 mo vs 45% relapsing later. The 2 compound — beyond 12 mo prior rituximab did not affect EFS, but early relapse after rituximab (n=187) gave a 3-yr PFS of only 23%, the group the authors say needs new approaches. Toxicity favoured R-ICE: platelet transfusion 35% vs 57%, serious adverse events in 58 vs 68 patients, grade 4 renal toxicity in 11 on R-DHAP; 3 toxic deaths after transplant. Median follow-up 27 mo.

records.title: NCIC-CTG LY.12
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · N/A · 2014
records.body: Relapsed or refractory aggressive-histology lymphoma after one anthracycline-containing regimen, or transformed indolent lymphoma after no more than 3 regimens including an anthracycline; ECOG 0-3; rituximab was added to both arms for CD20-positive disease only from a November 2005 amendment GDP ×2-3 q3w (+ rituximab if CD20+) → ASCT in responders vs DHAP ×2-3 q3w (+ rituximab if CD20+) → ASCT in responders Primary: response rate after 2 cycles, transplantation rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, stem-cell mobilisation, adverse events, quality of life, resource usage GDP delivers the same salvage result as DHAP with far less inpatient burden, and is the reasonable outpatient default before autologous transplant in relapsed/refractory aggressive lymphoma. The 2 arms were indistinguishable on everything that mattered: ORR after 2 cycles 45% vs 44%, transplantation rate 52% vs 49%, 4-year EFS 26% and OS 39% in both. The difference is tolerability and setting — grade 3-4 toxicity 47% vs 61%, febrile neutropenia 9% vs 23%, platelet transfusion 31% vs 47%, hospitalisation 47% vs 99%, and 2 treatment-attributed deaths vs 6, with better quality of life on GDP. Population was 71% DLBCL, 67% rituximab-exposed, over 70% primary refractory or relapsing within a year; response is lower here than in CORAL, which the authors attribute to CORAL having admitted only DLBCL.

records.title: SCHOLAR-1
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — outcomes after failed salvage · N/A · 2017
records.body: Refractory DLBCL, PMBCL or transformed FL: PD/SD on chemotherapy or relapse <=12 mo after ASCT N/A — no randomised comparison; outcomes of the next line of therapy after refractory status, pooled across MDACC, IA/MC, LY.12 and CORAL Objective response rate, complete response rate, overall survival The historical benchmark single-arm CAR T-cell studies are read against, and the reason they changed practice: before CAR T-cell therapy, refractory DLBCL had ORR 26% to the next line, CR 7%, median OS 6.3 mo and 20% alive at 2 years. Pooled from 2 phase 3 trials and 2 institutional cohorts. Outcome tracked with disease burden rather than with refractory category — ECOG >=2, advanced stage and high IPI each roughly doubled to tripled the hazard of death. The 2-year tail belongs to the minority who responded to salvage or reached transplant — but median OS was 14.9 mo only after a CR, against 6.9 mo after a PR and 14.4 mo after transplant; 73% did neither. Caveats: no central response review, and the analysis was run by Kite Pharma, whose CAR T-cell product it would go on to benchmark. Refractory disease is not trial-eligible relapse — within LY.12 and CORAL their refractory subsets responded at 26% and 31%, against 44-64% overall.

records.title: RE-MIND2
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — outcomes after failed salvage · N/A · 2022
records.body: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL treated at second, third or fourth line, with an anti-CD20-containing regimen among their therapies; of 3,454 enrolled in the observational cohort the matched analysis sets are 76, 75 and 74 pairs of patients not candidates for autologous transplant Tafasitamab + lenalidomide (L-MIND trial cohort) vs matched real-world cohorts: any systemic therapy pooled, bendamustine-rituximab, R-GemOx (76/75/74 pairs) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, event-free survival, progression-free survival, time to next treatment, safety Benchmarks what conventional therapy achieves in transplant-ineligible relapsed DLBCL: median OS 11.6 mo on pooled systemic therapy, 9.9 mo with bendamustine-rituximab and 11.0 mo with R-GemOx; ORR 46-55%; median PFS 5-8 mo. Real-world patients treated at second, third or fourth line, matched 1:1 to 76 of the 81 patients in the single-arm L-MIND study. Tafasitamab-lenalidomide bettered all 3 (HR 0.55, 0.42, 0.47), but this is the sponsor's own comparison of a trial cohort against health records, with response scored differently on each side, and the bendamustine-rituximab result is unstable — rebalancing the covariates raised its ORR to 68% and the survival advantage became, in the authors' words, less pronounced than in the primary analysis. A 2023 extension adds pola-BR, rituximab-lenalidomide and CAR T-cell therapy on 24-37 pairs each; the CAR-T comparison (HR 0.95, 0.48-1.91) is underpowered and poorly stage-matched, and is not evidence of equivalence. MorphoSys-sponsored.
records.keywords: Clin Cancer Res 2022;28:4003-4017  35674661 Ann Hematol 2023;102:1773-1787 prespecified pola-BR, R2 and CAR T-cell comparisons 37171597

records.title: ZUMA-1
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, third line and beyond · II · 2017
records.body: Refractory DLBCL, PMBCL or transformed FL: PD/SD to last chemotherapy or relapse ≤12 mo after ASCT (single-arm) Axicabtagene ciloleucel 2 × 10⁶ CAR T cells/kg as a single IV infusion, after conditioning fludarabine 30 mg/m²/day + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m²/day on days -5, -4 and -3 Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Established axicabtagene ciloleucel as curative-intent therapy in refractory large B-cell lymphoma, producing a durable plateau in a population whose historical median survival is about 6 mo. ORR 82% with CR 54%; independent review gave a lower 71%, so the headline figure is investigator-assessed. At 15.4 mo, 42% remained in response, median PFS 5.8 mo, median OS not reached and 52% alive at 18 mo. Deliverable: 101 of the 111 enrolled were infused (91%), median 17 days from leukapheresis to delivery; 69% had had >=3 prior lines. Late deepening changes management — 23 patients converted to CR after the first assessment without further therapy, so an early partial response should be observed rather than consolidated. Toxicity is near-universal but largely reversible: CRS 93% though only 13% grade >=3, neurologic events 64% with 28% grade >=3, tocilizumab in 43%. 3 patients (3%) died during treatment, 2 of them CRS-related.

records.title: JULIET
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, third line and beyond · II · 2019
records.body: Adults with relapsed/refractory DLBCL after ≥2 lines, ineligible for or relapsed after autologous SCT (single-arm) Tisagenlecleucel single IV infusion, median 3.0 × 10⁸ CAR-positive viable T cells, after fludarabine–cyclophosphamide or bendamustine lymphodepletion Primary: best overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, overall survival, safety Tisagenlecleucel produces durable remissions in relapsed/refractory DLBCL, but only in the 67% of enrolled patients who reach infusion — deliverability, not activity, is what limits it. Only 111 of the 165 enrolled were infused (67%), at a median 54 days from enrolment, with 16 dying before infusion. ORR 52% by independent review with CR 40% among the 93 evaluated for response, but 34% across everyone enrolled, which is what enrolment actually delivers; median OS was 12 mo from infusion against 8.3 mo from enrolment, the gap being attrition rather than drug effect. Responses that did occur held: median duration not reached, 65% relapse-free at 12 mo from first response, and no responder underwent consolidative transplant. Toxicity within 8 weeks: CRS 58% with 22% grade 3-4 on the Penn scale, which grades more severely than the scales used in other CAR T-cell trials; neurologic events 21%; grade 3-4 infection 20%, with a further 18% beyond 8 weeks.

records.title: TRANSCEND NHL 001
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, third line and beyond · I · 2020
records.body: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma after 2 or more previous lines including an anti-CD20 antibody and an anthracycline — DLBCL, transformed indolent lymphoma, high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma or grade 3B follicular lymphoma; previous transplant, secondary CNS involvement and moderate renal or cardiac impairment were allowed; 9 of those infused entered before an amendment required both previous lines to be systemic (single-arm) Lisocabtagene maraleucel at a target dose of 50, 100 or 150 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells, each dose given as sequential infusions of its CD8+ and CD4+ components at equal target doses, 2-7 days after fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² daily ×3; a single administration, with a split 2-dose schedule at 50 × 10⁶ also tested and retreatment permitted after relapse from complete response. 100 × 10⁶ was the recommended dose taken into dose confirmation Primary: adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities, objective response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival Liso-cel gives durable remissions in third-line and later large B-cell lymphoma with low rates of severe cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity, though 15% of those leukapheresed never reach infusion. ORR 73% and CR 53% among the 256 infused and evaluable; counting everyone leukapheresed, ORR 61% and CR 44% — 50 were never infused, 33 because they died. Median leukapheresis to infusion 37 days; bridging in 59% of the 269 infused. From infusion in the 256: median PFS 6.8 mo, 44% progression-free at 12 mo; median OS 21.1 mo, 58% alive at 12 mo. Median DoR not reached, 55% of responders still in response at 12 mo. Safety in the 269: CRS 42%, grade 3+ only 2%; neurological events 30%, 10% grade 3+; grade 3+ infection 12%; grade 3+ cytopenias unresolved at day 29 in 37%; 7 (3%) died of a treatment-emergent event, none from CRS or neurological events. CRS graded by 2014 Lee criteria — the Penn scale used in JULIET yields higher severe rates, so rates are not comparable across trials.

records.title: ZUMA-7
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · III · 2022
records.body: Large B-cell lymphoma by WHO 2016 criteria in the second line, either refractory to first-line therapy — defined as no complete response — or relapsed from complete remission no more than 12 months after completing first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing an anti-CD20 antibody and an anthracycline, with relapse biopsy-proven; all patients had to be intended for high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell transplant Axicabtagene ciloleucel 2 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells/kg as a single infusion after cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² + fludarabine 30 mg/m² daily on days -5, -4 and -3, with bridging therapy limited to glucocorticoids, vs 2-3 cycles of investigator-selected platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy → high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell transplant in those with a complete or partial response (1:1) Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Axi-cel beat salvage chemoimmunotherapy with transplant in responders as second-line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma refractory to or relapsing within 12 mo of first-line therapy: EFS median 8.3 vs 2.0 mo by blinded central review, HR 0.40; 24-mo EFS 41% vs 16%; ORR 83% vs 50%; CR 65% vs 32%. Survival has not followed: at this interim analysis median OS was not reached vs 35.1 mo, HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.53-1.01), statistical significance not reached; 56% of the standard-care arm went on to cellular immunotherapy off protocol. Only 36% of the standard-care arm reached transplant; 94% of those assigned axi-cel were infused, with successful manufacture for every patient leukapheresed. Among those treated, toxicity differs in kind: grade 3+ AEs 91% vs 83%; CRS 92%, 6% grade 3+; neurological events 60% vs 20%, grade 3+ 21% vs 1%, with no deaths from either; febrile neutropenia the mirror image at 2% vs 27%. Fatal AEs 4% vs 1%, 1 of them axi-cel-related.

records.title: TRANSFORM
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · III · 2022
records.body: Transplant-eligible large B-cell lymphoma, age 18-75, refractory to first-line anthracycline plus anti-CD20 chemoimmunotherapy or relapsed within 12 months of a response to it; centrally confirmed histology of DLBCL not otherwise specified, transformed indolent lymphoma, high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma, T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma or grade 3B follicular lymphoma; secondary CNS lymphoma allowed (1:1) Lisocabtagene maraleucel at a total target dose of 100 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells, given as 2 sequential infusions of its CD8+ and CD4+ components, after fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² daily ×3, with 1 cycle of bridging immunochemotherapy permitted during manufacture, vs 3 cycles of salvage immunochemotherapy — R-DHAP, R-ICE or R-GDP by investigator choice → high-dose chemotherapy with autologous transplant in those responding. Standard-care patients meeting protocol criteria could cross over to liso-cel as third-line treatment Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, overall response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, rate of transplant completion, safety Liso-cel beat salvage immunochemotherapy with transplant in responders as second-line treatment of transplant-eligible large B-cell lymphoma refractory to or relapsing within 12 mo of first-line therapy: EFS median 10.1 vs 2.3 mo by independent review, HR 0.35; CR 66% vs 39%; ORR 86% vs 48%; PFS median 14.8 vs 5.7 mo, HR 0.41. OS favoured liso-cel at this interim analysis but the data are immature — median not reached vs 16.4 mo, HR 0.51 (0.26-1.00), an interval reaching 1, median follow-up only 6.2 mo, and 50 of the 92 assigned to standard care approved to cross over to liso-cel. Only 46% of the standard-care arm reached transplant; 89 of the 92 assigned liso-cel received it, and 63% of that arm had bridging therapy. CRS 49% but grade 3 in only 1%, neurological events 12% with 4% grade 3, and no grade 4 or 5 of either; grade 3+ AEs 92% vs 87%; prolonged grade 3+ cytopenia 43% vs 3%; any-grade febrile neutropenia 15% vs 24%; grade 3+ infection 15% vs 21%.

records.title: BELINDA
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · III · 2022
records.body: Histologically confirmed aggressive B-cell lymphoma in the second line, refractory to first-line therapy — defined as no complete response — or relapsed within 12 months of the last dose of a first-line regimen containing an anti-CD20 antibody and an anthracycline; patients had to be judged eligible for autologous transplant by the investigator (1:1) Tisagenlecleucel 0.6-6.0 × 10⁸ CAR+ viable T cells as a single infusion after fludarabine 25 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 250 mg/m² daily ×3, with optional bridging chemotherapy from the same 4 prespecified platinum-containing regimens, vs investigator's choice of those 4 regimens → high-dose chemotherapy with autologous transplant in those responding, with a second regimen permitted for an inadequate week-6 response. Standard-care patients could cross over to tisagenlecleucel at or after week 12 Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response, safety Tisagenlecleucel missed the primary endpoint: EFS median 3.0 mo in both arms, HR 1.07 (0.82-1.40), statistical significance not reached — no gain over salvage chemotherapy with transplant in second-line large B-cell lymphoma. The reason looks like delivery rather than the drug — median leukapheresis to infusion 52 days, 83% of the arm received bridging chemotherapy and 48% 2 or more cycles or regimens, and by the week 6 assessment, before infusion, 26% already had progressive disease against 14% on standard care. Response at or after week 12 was 46% vs 43%, CR 28% vs 28%. Survival was immature and never formally compared: HR for death 1.24 (0.83-1.85), with 51% of the standard-care arm crossing over. 96% of those assigned tisagenlecleucel received it; 33% of the standard-care arm reached transplant. Among those infused, CRS 61% with 5% grade 3+ and neurological events 10% with 2% grade 3+; across the randomised arms, grade 3+ AEs 84% vs 90%.

records.title: PILOT
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · II · 2022
records.body: Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma after exactly 1 previous line, in patients not intended for transplant by the investigator and meeting at least 1 of 6 protocol criteria: age 70 or over, ECOG 2, carbon monoxide diffusing capacity 60% or less, left ventricular ejection fraction under 50%, creatinine clearance under 60 mL/min, or AST or ALT more than twice the upper limit of normal (single-arm) Lisocabtagene maraleucel at a total target dose of 100 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells, given as 2 sequential infusions of its CD8+ and CD4+ components, after fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² daily ×3, with bridging therapy permitted at the investigator's discretion and outpatient administration allowed; a single administration, with retreatment permitted after relapse from complete response, and follow-up for 2 years after infusion Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, event-free survival, overall survival, safety Liso-cel is deliverable and active as second-line treatment in patients not intended for transplant, median age 74 with 26% at ECOG 2: ORR 80% by independent review and CR 54% among the 61 given liso-cel, against the 50.2% response rate of a real-world cohort built on the same eligibility criteria; counting everyone leukapheresed, 68% and 46%. Median PFS 9.0 mo, EFS 7.2 mo, OS not reached; median DoR 12.1 mo among the 49 who responded. 12 of the 74 leukapheresed were never infused, 5 of them because they died. Median leukapheresis to infusion 35.5 days; 52% of those infused had bridging therapy and 20 were treated as outpatients. Severe CRS and neurological events were uncommon, but cytopenias were not: CRS 38% with grade 3 in 2%, neurological events 31% with grade 3 in 5%, no grade 4 or 5 of either; grade 3+ neutropenia 48%, grade 3+ cytopenias unresolved at day 28 in 30%, grade 3+ infection 7%. 2 died of treatment-emergent events, both of COVID-19, 1 considered related to liso-cel.

records.title: ALYCANTE
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · II · 2023
records.body: Large B-cell lymphoma refractory to or relapsing within 12 months of first-line therapy, in patients judged by their physician ineligible for high-dose chemotherapy with autologous transplant and meeting at least 1 of 3 objective criteria: age 65 or over, HCT-CI comorbidity score of 3 or more, or a previous autologous transplant given as first-line consolidation; known CNS disease excluded (single-arm) Axicabtagene ciloleucel 2 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells/kg as a single intravenous infusion, given 2-7 days after cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² + fludarabine 30 mg/m² daily ×3, with bridging therapy permitted at the investigator's discretion — R-GemOx in 51 of the 52 bridged, for 1 to 3 cycles Primary: complete metabolic response at 3 months. Secondary: objective response rate at 3 months, complete metabolic response at 6 months, best objective response rate, best complete metabolic response, duration of response, event-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Axi-cel produces high complete response rates as second-line treatment in transplant-ineligible patients, median age 70, but at a real cost in late infection. Complete metabolic response at 3 mo 71% among the 62 infused, 67% counting all 69 leukapheresed; central review gave a lower 66%, so the headline is investigator-assessed. ORR 76% at 3 mo, best CMR 79%. Median PFS 11.8 mo with 49% progression-free at 12 mo; median OS not reached with 78% alive at 12 mo; median DoR not reached. 84% received bridging therapy, almost always R-GemOx, and 63% of those bridged did not respond to it. Toxicity is substantial: CRS 94% with 8% grade 3-4, ICANS 52% with 15% grade 3-4, 26% transferred to intensive care for CAR T-cell toxicity, and grade 3+ cytopenias unresolved at 30 days in 37%. Non-relapse mortality 10%: every fatal event was an infection and all occurred beyond 2 mo after infusion, 2 of them COVID-19, without which the authors put non-relapse mortality at 6%.

records.title: Glofitamab pivotal (NP30179)
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · I/II · 2022
records.body: Histologically confirmed DLBCL not otherwise specified, transformed follicular lymphoma, high-grade B-cell lymphoma or primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma, relapsed after or refractory to at least 2 previous lines including at least 1 anti-CD20 antibody-containing and 1 anthracycline-containing regimen; previous CAR T-cell therapy was permitted (single-arm) Obinutuzumab 1000 mg IV 7 days before the first glofitamab dose, to mitigate cytokine release syndrome → glofitamab IV as step-up doses of 2.5 mg on day 8 and 10 mg on day 15 of cycle 1, then 30 mg on day 1 of cycles 2-12, on 21-day cycles. Fixed duration: 12 cycles then stop, or earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity. Hospitalisation was required for the first glofitamab dose, and for later doses only after grade 2 or higher cytokine release syndrome Primary: complete response rate. Secondary: objective response, duration of response, duration of complete response, time to first complete response, time to first objective response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Glofitamab is a fixed-duration bispecific — 12 cycles then stop — producing durable complete remissions in heavily pretreated DLBCL, including after CAR T-cell therapy. CR 39% and ORR 52% by independent review among all 155 enrolled, at 12.6 mo median follow-up; the registrational analysis was an earlier cut at 9.0 mo in the 108-patient pivotal cohort, CR 35% against a 20% historical control. 33% had already received CAR T cells and their CR rate was the same 35%. Remissions hold: median duration of complete response not reached, 78% of complete responders still in response at 12 mo. Median PFS 4.9 mo with 37% at 12 mo; median OS 11.5 mo with 50% alive at 12 mo. CRS 63% but grade 3+ in only 4% and none fatal, almost all with the first 3 doses; ICANS-like events 8%, grade 3+ 3%. Grade 3-4 AEs 56%, grade 3+ infection 15%; 5% had a grade 5 event, none attributed to glofitamab. No complete responses among the 11 with high-grade B-cell lymphoma, 2 of whom had a partial response.

records.title: EPCORE NHL-1
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · I/II · 2023
records.body: CD20-positive mature B-cell neoplasm — DLBCL or other aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma, high-grade B-cell lymphoma and grade 3B follicular lymphoma — relapsed after or refractory to at least 2 previous lines of systemic therapy including at least 1 anti-CD20-containing regimen, having failed or been ineligible for autologous transplant; previous CAR T-cell therapy was permitted (single-arm) Subcutaneous epcoritamab in 28-day cycles, given until progression or unacceptable toxicity: step-up doses of 0.16 mg on day 1 and 0.8 mg on day 8 of cycle 1, then 48 mg from day 15 — weekly in cycles 1-3, every 2 weeks in cycles 4-9, and every 4 weeks from cycle 10. Prednisolone 100 mg before each cycle 1 dose and for 3 days after, as cytokine release syndrome prophylaxis. Inpatient monitoring for 24 h was required for the first full dose Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, duration of complete response, progression-free survival, time to response, overall survival, safety Epcoritamab is a subcutaneous bispecific given until progression, active in heavily pretreated large B-cell lymphoma including after CAR T-cell therapy. ORR 63% and CR 39% by independent review among all 157 treated, at 10.7 mo median follow-up; 39% had already received CAR T cells and their ORR was 54% with CR 34%. Median DoR 12.0 mo, and among complete responders the median is not reached with 89% still in response at 9 mo. Median PFS 4.4 mo with 44% at 6 mo; median OS not reached. Step-up dosing with prednisolone prophylaxis is mandatory in cycle 1: CRS 50% any grade but grade 3 in only 2.5% and no grade 4 or 5, almost all after the first full dose on day 15 of cycle 1, with a median onset of 20 h and resolution in 99%. ICANS 6.4%, including 1 fatal event. Grade 3+ AEs 61% and grade 3+ neutropenia 15%; 7.6% stopped treatment for toxicity.

records.title: STARGLO
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · III · 2024
records.body: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL not otherwise specified after at least 1 previous line; patients entering after only 1 line had to be transplant-ineligible on age 70 or over, end-organ dysfunction, ECOG 2 or worse, refusal of transplant, or another comorbidity precluding it by local practice. Lymphoma transformed from indolent disease, double- or triple-hit high-grade B-cell lymphoma and high-grade B-cell lymphoma not otherwise specified were all ineligible (2:1) Glofitamab + GemOx: obinutuzumab 1000 mg on cycle 1 day 1, then glofitamab step-up 2.5 mg on cycle 1 day 8 and 10 mg on cycle 1 day 15, then 30 mg on day 1 of cycles 2-12, with gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² every 21 days for 8 cycles vs R-GemOx: rituximab 375 mg/m² on day 1 with the identical GemOx every 21 days for 8 cycles. Glofitamab continues to cycle 12 and then stops; the chemotherapy backbone stops at cycle 8 in both arms. Overnight hospitalisation was required after the first glofitamab infusion; dexamethasone 20 mg 1 h before each glofitamab dose until 2 target 30 mg doses had been given without cytokine release syndrome Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, complete response rate, duration of complete response, objective response rate, duration of objective response, quality of life, safety Adding glofitamab to GemOx prolonged survival over R-GemOx in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL. The primary endpoint was met at an earlier interim analysis; at the updated interim cut with 20.7 mo median follow-up, investigator-assessed median OS 25.5 vs 12.9 mo (HR 0.62) with 53% vs 34% alive at 24 mo; and by masked independent review median PFS 13.8 vs 3.6 mo (HR 0.40) with 52% vs 25% progression-free at 12 mo, CR 59% vs 25% and ORR 68% vs 41%. Glofitamab is fixed-duration and stops at 12 cycles. At the same interim cut the cost is toxicity: grade 3+ AEs 78% vs 41%, serious infection 26% vs 13%, and 27% vs 13% discontinued a study drug for an adverse event. CRS 44% among glofitamab-exposed patients, grade 3 in only 2% and none higher, mostly after the first step-up dose; events consistent with ICANS 2%. Fatal AEs 8% vs 5% and treatment-related deaths 3% vs 1%. COVID-19 was the commonest serious infection at 18% vs 9%, and the trial ran through the pandemic.

records.title: SUNMO
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · III · 2025
records.body: Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma — DLBCL, high-grade B-cell lymphoma, grade 3B follicular lymphoma or transformed follicular lymphoma — after at least 1 previous line, in patients deemed ineligible for autologous transplant by the treating physician, with no objective criterion for that ineligibility given in the report (2:1) Subcutaneous mosunetuzumab 5 mg on day 1 and 45 mg on days 8 and 15 of cycle 1, then 45 mg on day 1 of cycles 2-8, on 21-day cycles and without any requirement for hospitalisation, with polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV on day 1 of cycles 1-6; corticosteroid premedication before each mosunetuzumab dose in cycle 1 only vs R-GemOx: rituximab 375 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² on day 1 of cycles 1-8, on 14-day cycles extended to 21 days for haematological toxicity. Both arms are fixed-duration and stop at 8 cycles; crossover was not permitted Primary: overall response rate, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, complete response rate, duration of response, duration of complete response, quality of life, safety Subcutaneous mosunetuzumab plus polatuzumab beat R-GemOx in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma and is given without hospitalisation for 8 cycles. At 23.2 mo median follow-up: ORR 70% vs 40%, CR 51% vs 24%; median PFS 11.5 vs 3.8 mo (HR 0.41) with 48% vs 18% progression-free at 12 mo; median DoR 15.6 vs 6.0 mo among responders. Survival has not separated at this interim analysis — median OS 18.7 vs 13.6 mo, HR 0.80 (0.5-1.2), statistical significance not reached. CRS is not the dose-limiting problem: CRS 26% with grade 3 in 0.7% and no grade 4 or 5, median onset 3 days and nearly all in cycle 1, tocilizumab in 4.4%. Grade 3+ AEs 64% in both arms; grade 3+ neutropenia 33% vs 31%; grade 3+ infection 16% vs 14%; pneumonitis 5.2% vs none. Grade 5 events 5.2% vs 6.3%, 2 per arm treatment-related and mostly COVID-19.

records.title: ELM-2
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · II · 2025
records.body: DLBCL, de novo or transformed, refractory to or relapsed after 2 or more previous lines of systemic therapy including an anti-CD20 antibody and an alkylator; double-hit and triple-hit high-grade lymphoma were accepted; previous CAR T-cell therapy was a protocol exclusion (single-arm) Odronextamab IV in 21-day cycles, with non-randomly allocated cycle 1 step-up schedules after a protocol amendment: original 1 mg split over days 1-2, 20 mg split over days 8-9, then 160 mg on day 15; revised 0.7 mg split over days 1-2, 4 mg split over days 8-9 and 20 mg split over days 15-16. Then 160 mg on days 1, 8 and 15 of cycles 2-4, then 320 mg every 2 weeks until progression or another protocol-defined stop. Sustained complete response for at least 9 months permitted dosing every 4 weeks; no fixed stop. Inpatient monitoring for 24 h was required after every infusion up to and including cycle 2 day 1; dexamethasone 20 mg IV 1-3 h before every infusion on both step-up regimens, until a full weekly dose was given without an infusion-related reaction or cytokine release syndrome Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety Odronextamab produces durable complete remissions in relapsed/refractory DLBCL after 2 or more lines, but at a high infection cost. ORR 52% and CR 32% by central review among all 127 treated, at 29.9 mo median follow-up; median DoR 10.2 mo overall and 17.9 mo among complete responders, 47% of whom were still in response at 24 mo. Median PFS 4.4 mo and median OS 9.2 mo. No patient had received prior CAR T cells; it was a protocol exclusion, so the row says nothing about the post-CAR-T setting. CRS was 55% overall, grade 3+ in 4.7% and none higher; in sequential non-randomized cohorts, grade 3 CRS was numerically lower with the revised vs original step-up schedule (1.7% vs 7.5%). No ICANS was reported, though neurological adverse events of any grade occurred in 43%. Infection is the real toxicity: 65% any grade, 39% grade 3+, and 15 patients died of infection, 5 of them of COVID-19. Grade 3+ AEs 84%; 16% died of a treatment-emergent event, 3.9% treatment-related.

records.title: POLARGO
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · III · 2026
records.body: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL, not otherwise specified or transformed from indolent disease, after at least 1 previous line, in patients ineligible for stem-cell transplant and for CAR T-cell therapy at recruitment (1:1) Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV + rituximab 375 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² (Pola-R-GemOx) vs R-GemOx alone, every 21 days for up to 8 cycles; primary G-CSF prophylaxis and anti-infective prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and herpes simplex virus were mandatory Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, complete response rate, overall response rate, event-free survival, best overall response, duration of response, quality of life, safety Pola-R-GemOx improved OS over R-GemOx in R/R DLBCL ineligible for transplant and CAR T-cell therapy: stratified HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.43-0.83), median OS 19.5 vs 12.5 mo. Stratified investigator-assessed PFS HR 0.37 (0.27-0.51), median 7.4 vs 2.7 mo; CR rate 40.3% vs 19.0% and ORR 52.7% vs 24.6% by central review. OS favoured Pola-R-GemOx across most prespecified subgroups, including both ABC and GCB cell of origin. Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (34.4% vs 26.4%) and neutropenia (33.6% vs 30.4%) were the most common toxicities; peripheral neuropathy 57% vs 29% (mostly grade 1, none above grade 3); fatal AEs 12% vs 4%, driven by infection including COVID-19, though investigator-attributed treatment-related fatal AEs were similar (3.1% vs 2.4%). Bendamustine-free alternative to Pola-BR; may preserve CAR-T eligibility. CAR-T and bispecific antibodies are complementary strategies.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print; JCO-25-02849)

records.title: GO29365
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · I/II · 2020
records.body: Biopsy-confirmed relapsed or refractory DLBCL after at least 1 previous line, ineligible for autologous transplant by investigator assessment or having failed a previous autologous transplant, with baseline peripheral neuropathy no worse than grade 1; transformed lymphoma was excluded and double-hit and triple-hit lymphoma were permitted (1:1) Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV on day 2 of cycle 1 then day 1 of later cycles + bendamustine 90 mg/m² IV on days 2-3 of cycle 1 then days 1-2 of later cycles + rituximab 375 mg/m² IV on day 1 of each cycle vs the same bendamustine-rituximab schedule, every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Fixed duration in both arms; no maintenance Primary: complete response rate at end of treatment, safety. Secondary: overall response rate at end of treatment, best overall response, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival Polatuzumab added to bendamustine-rituximab roughly doubled complete response and more than doubled survival in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL, on 40 patients per arm. CR at end of treatment 40% vs 18% by central review; median PFS 9.5 vs 3.7 mo (HR 0.36); median OS 12.4 vs 4.7 mo (HR 0.42); median DoR among responders 12.6 vs 7.7 mo. 18% of the polatuzumab arm were still in complete remission beyond 20 mo. The comparison was designed for precision rather than proof and the trial was never powered to prove superiority, so treat the size of the effect as an estimate. Among the 39 treated in each arm, 46% vs 23% completed all 6 cycles and toxicity is haematological and neuropathic: grade 3-4 neutropenia 46% vs 33%, thrombocytopenia 41% vs 23%, anaemia 28% vs 18%; grade 3-4 infection 23% vs 21%. Peripheral neuropathy 44% vs 8%, all grade 1-2. Fatal adverse events in 9 vs 11 patients, infection the commonest cause in both.

records.title: L-MIND
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · II · 2020
records.body: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL, including transformed indolent lymphoma with a subsequent DLBCL relapse, after 1-3 systemic regimens including an anti-CD20 antibody, not candidates for high-dose chemotherapy with autologous transplant; primary-refractory disease was excluded, on a definition widened mid-trial from relapse within 3 to within 6 months of frontline therapy; known double- or triple-hit disease, CNS involvement and previous anti-CD19 or immunomodulatory drugs were also excluded (single-arm) Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg IV on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of cycles 1-3, with an extra loading dose on day 4 of cycle 1, then on days 1 and 15 from cycle 4, with premedication against infusion-related reactions (antipyretics, H1 and H2 receptor blockers, glucocorticoids and meperidine); lenalidomide 25 mg orally on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle. Combination treatment for up to 12 cycles; patients with stable disease or better continued tafasitamab alone every 2 weeks until progression, with earlier discontinuation for toxicity or withdrawal Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: disease control rate, duration of response, time to next treatment, progression-free survival, time to progression, overall survival, safety Tafasitamab plus lenalidomide gives durable remissions in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL after 1-3 prior lines. ORR 60% and CR 43% by independent review among 80 treated; median DoR among 48 responders 21.7 mo, not reached among 34 CR vs 4.4 mo among 14 PR. Median PFS 12.1 mo with 50% progression-free at 12 mo; median OS not reached with 74% alive at 12 mo. Primary refractory disease was excluded under a definition widened from relapse within 3 to within 6 mo; the 19% enrolled subgroup came from pre-amendment patients relapsing or progressing at 3-6 mo. Among 81 who received either drug, grade 3+ neutropenia was 48%, thrombocytopenia 17% and febrile neutropenia 12%; 12% discontinued the study during combination treatment for an adverse event. After 12 cycles, patients with stable disease or better continued tafasitamab alone until progression.

records.title: LOTIS-2
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · II · 2021
records.body: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL by WHO 2016 after 2 or more multiagent systemic regimens — DLBCL not otherwise specified, high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, or primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma; transformed indolent lymphoma was not excluded, and previous CD19-directed therapy required biopsy-proven CD19 expression; bulky disease of 10 cm or more was permitted until protocol amendment 2 and excluded thereafter; active CNS lymphoma was excluded (single-arm) Loncastuximab tesirine 150 µg/kg IV over 30 min on day 1 of each 21-day cycle for 2 cycles, then 75 µg/kg from cycle 3, with dexamethasone premedication unless contraindicated and adjusted-body-weight dosing if BMI ≥35 kg/m²; outpatient treatment for up to 1 year or until relapse/progression, unacceptable toxicity, death, major protocol deviation, pregnancy, or patient, investigator or sponsor decision. Patients with clinical benefit could continue beyond 1 year with sponsor agreement Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, relapse-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety Loncastuximab tesirine produced outpatient single-agent activity after ≥2 prior systemic regimens: centrally reviewed ORR 48% (70/145) and CR 24% (35/145); 20/35 complete responders remained in CR at cutoff. Median DoR was 10.3 mo among 70 responders (13.4 mo for CR vs 5.7 mo for PR); median PFS 4.9 mo and OS 9.9 mo were still maturing. Prior CAR T-cell therapy was limited to 13/145; 15 later received CAR T cells, with 7 investigator-assessed responses including 6 CRs. Events considered payload-related included oedema/effusion 31%, skin/nail events 43%, and grade 3+ gamma-glutamyl transferase elevation 17%, the commonest cause of dose delay and discontinuation; grade 3+ neutropenia 26% and thrombocytopenia 18%. Peripheral sensory neuropathy 3%; 23% discontinued for toxicity. No fatal treatment-emergent event was considered related; 2/145 deaths after the adverse-event reporting period were considered possibly related.

records.title: ECHELON-3
records.subtitle: DLBCL · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · III · 2025
records.body: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL, including transformed DLBCL, after at least 2 previous lines of systemic therapy, in patients pretreated with or ineligible for haematopoietic stem-cell transplant or CAR T-cell therapy; the publication gives no operational definition of that ineligibility (1:1) Brentuximab vedotin 1.2 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + lenalidomide 20 mg orally once daily continuously + rituximab 375 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks (subcutaneous 1400 mg permitted from cycle 2) vs matched placebo IV every 3 weeks + the same lenalidomide and rituximab; 21-day cycles, each study treatment continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity; G-CSF prophylaxis was required at all cycles in both arms Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, overall survival in the CD30-positive subgroup, safety At the prespecified interim analysis, adding brentuximab vedotin to lenalidomide-rituximab prolonged OS in relapsed/refractory DLBCL after >=2 prior lines among patients ineligible for stem-cell transplant or CAR T-cell therapy. Median OS 13.8 vs 8.5 mo (HR 0.63) at 16.4 mo median follow-up; median PFS 4.2 vs 2.6 mo (HR 0.53); investigator-assessed ORR 64% vs 42%, with CR 40% vs 19%. Among patients with CR, median PFS was 21.5 mo vs not evaluable; among those with PR, 4.1 vs 4.1 mo. Among responders, median DoR was 8.3 vs 3.0 mo; among patients with CR, 18.9 mo vs not evaluable. In the safety population (n=112 vs 116), grade 3+ AEs occurred in 88% vs 77%; neutropenia 43% vs 28%, thrombocytopenia 25% vs 19%; serious TEAEs 60% vs 50% (pneumonia 11% vs 5%). Peripheral neuropathy occurred in 31% vs 24%, grade 3 in 6% vs 2%. Fatal TEAEs occurred in 12% vs 8%; COVID-19-related fatal events in 4% vs 3%.

records.title: GHSG HD10
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · III · 2010
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II with none of the trial's risk factors, the GHSG early-stage favourable category; aged 16-75. Nodular lymphocyte-predominant histology was eligible and made up 7.5% of subtyped patients. 1,370 were randomised and 1,190 analysed, after 180 exclusions of which most were incorrect initial staging 4 vs 2 cycles of ABVD, each followed by 30 vs 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy — a 2x2 factorial randomised 1:1:1:1 to 4 groups Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete response, toxicity. Halving chemotherapy and lowering the radiotherapy dose both held, and less treatment was markedly less toxic; 2 cycles of ABVD plus 20 Gy became the standard for favourable early-stage disease. Against a 7-percentage-point margin on 5-year freedom from treatment failure, 2 cycles gave 91.1% against 93.0% for 4 cycles, a difference of -1.9 points (95% CI -5.2 to 1.4), and 20 Gy gave 92.9% against 93.4% for 30 Gy, -0.5 points (-3.6 to 2.6). The least intensive group, 2 cycles plus 20 Gy, also sat within the margin against 4 cycles plus 30 Gy, -1.6 points (-6.3 to 3.1). 5-year overall survival was about 97% in all 4 groups. Toxicity moved the other way and by more: grade 3 or 4 acute events 33.2% with 2 cycles vs 51.7% with 4, and 2.9% with 20 Gy vs 8.7% with 30 Gy. 6 of the 7 deaths from toxicity of first-line treatment were in patients given 4 cycles, though all 5 deaths from salvage toxicity followed 2 cycles.
