records.title: GHSG HD16
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease in stage IB, IIA or IIB, without a large mediastinal mass, extranodal lesions, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas; aged 18-75. All 1,150 were randomised before any interim PET existed; the primary comparison rests on 628 PET-2-negative patients analysed per protocol 2 cycles of ABVD then 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy in all patients vs 2 cycles of ABVD then 20 Gy only where the interim PET after cycle 2 was positive on central review Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, negative interim PET rate, second malignancy, toxicity. Radiotherapy cannot be dropped after a negative interim PET: omitting it cost tumour control and non-inferiority was not met. Among the 628 PET-2-negative patients analysed per protocol, 5-year progression-free survival was 86.1% with ABVD alone against 93.4% with chemotherapy plus 20 Gy, a difference of -7.3 points (95% CI -13.0 to -1.6); the hazard ratio was 1.78 and its interval reached 3.12, above the 3.01 margin, so a 10-point loss could not be excluded. The mechanism was local: in-field recurrence 9% with ABVD alone vs 2%, while out-field recurrence was 5% vs 4%. Survival showed nothing either way on 12 deaths in total, 5-year overall survival 98.4% vs 98.1%, and there were more deaths in the arm with better tumour control, 9 of 328 vs 3 of 300. Interim PET was positive in 34% of the 1,007 scans centrally reviewed.

records.title: GHSG HD13
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease in stage IB, IIA or IIB only, without a large mediastinal mass, extranodal lesions, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas. 1,710 were randomised and 1,502 qualified for analysis; stage IA nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease was a named reason for exclusion 2 cycles of ABVD vs 3 reduced-intensity variants — ABV (no dacarbazine), AVD (no bleomycin) or AV (neither) — each followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy, randomised 1:1:1:1 Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete remission, toxicity. Neither dacarbazine nor bleomycin can be omitted from ABVD. Both dacarbazine-omitted arms were closed early for higher event rates, AV in September 2005 and ABV in February 2006, and each is compared with the ABVD patients recruited alongside it: 5-year freedom from treatment failure 77.1% with AV against 92.3%, hazard ratio 2.57 (95% CI 1.51-4.40), and 81.4% with ABV against 92.9%, 2.06 (1.21-3.52). The bleomycin-omitted variant ran to the end and also fell short: AVD 89.2% against 93.1% for ABVD, hazard ratio 1.50 (95% CI 1.00-2.26), whose upper bound exceeded the 1.72 margin, so non-inferiority was not shown. Overall survival was 94-98% across the 4 groups and did not separate. No death was due to toxicity of first-line treatment in any group, and grade 3 or 4 leucopenia tracked bleomycin, 17-18% with it against 11-12% without. Unmodified ABVD remains the standard; radiotherapy was 30 Gy in every group here, chosen before HD10 established 20 Gy.

records.title: GHSG HD7
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · N/A · 2007
records.body: Newly diagnosed, previously untreated, histology-proven Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical or pathologic stage IA-IIB without GHSG risk factors (large mediastinal mass, extranodal disease, massive splenic involvement, high ESR); all HL subtypes incl. lymphocyte-predominant; age 16-75, Karnofsky >70%; prior malignancy and composite lymphoma excluded 2 cycles ABVD → 30 Gy extended-field RT (spleen 36 Gy) + 10 Gy involved-field boost vs 30 Gy extended-field RT (spleen 36 Gy) + 10 Gy involved-field boost Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, complete remission, relapse, second malignancy, acute toxicity. Two cycles of ABVD before radiotherapy transformed disease control in favourable early-stage disease and is why chemotherapy became part of the standard: 7-year freedom from treatment failure was 88% with combined-modality treatment against 67% with extended-field radiotherapy alone, a 21-point difference driven almost entirely by relapse, 3.2% against 21.9%. Survival did not separate, 7-year overall survival 94% against 92%, and 51 of 627 patients died in all. Treatment-related deaths ran 2 with chemotherapy added against 7 with radiotherapy alone, most after the salvage those relapses required. Adding ABVD did not increase acute radiotherapy toxicity, grade 3 in a few percent of either arm, though ABVD itself gave grade 3 leukopenia in 11% and hair loss in 9.9%. Second malignancies were 18 against 21, 39 in total, with similar cumulative incidence, though the authors caution that numbers at risk beyond year 9 are small and more events will follow. Median observation 87 months.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2007;25:3495-3502   J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1999-2007 long-term follow-up update 28418763 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1444-1450 pooled late-relapse analysis (HD7-HD12) 28240973

records.title: GHSG HD14
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage IA, IB or IIA with at least one GHSG risk factor — a large mediastinal mass, extranodal involvement, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas — and stage IIB with only the last two of those. Median age 32, range 18-60. 1,655 were randomised and 1,528 qualified for the primary analysis 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP then 2 cycles of ABVD vs 4 cycles of ABVD, each followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, response, toxicity. Two cycles of escalated BEACOPP before ABVD improved tumour control decisively, and the price is acute toxicity. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 94.8% against 87.7% with 4 cycles of ABVD, a difference of 7.2 points (95% CI 3.8 to 10.5), hazard ratio 0.44 (95% CI 0.30 to 0.66); 5-year progression-free survival 95.4% against 89.1%. Superiority was reached at the third of five planned interim analyses and randomisation was stopped early for it. Overall survival was 97.0% at 5 years and did not separate. The cost is in the marrow: at least one grade 3 or 4 event in 87.1% against 50.7%, grade 4 in 56.6% against 5.9%, and grade 3 or 4 leukopenia in 79.0% against 23.5%. All 4 deaths from first-line treatment toxicity were on the intensified arm, though 6 of the 7 salvage-toxicity deaths were on ABVD. Median follow-up was 43 months, short of the 5-year landmarks these figures quote.

records.title: GHSG HD11
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2010
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma of any histology in clinical stage IA, IB or IIA with at least one GHSG risk factor — a large mediastinal mass, extranodal involvement, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas — and stage IIB with only the last two of those. 1,570 were randomised and 1,395 qualified for the chemotherapy analysis; 1,351 for the radiotherapy analysis 4 cycles of ABVD vs 4 cycles of baseline BEACOPP, each followed by 30 vs 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy — a 2x2 factorial in 4 groups Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, response, toxicity. Neither escalating the chemotherapy nor lowering the radiotherapy dose improved on 4 cycles of ABVD followed by 30 Gy, which the authors concluded should remain the standard. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 85.0% across the trial. At 30 Gy, baseline BEACOPP and ABVD did not differ, 1.6 points (95% CI -3.6 to 6.9); only at 20 Gy did BEACOPP come out ahead, 5.7 points (0.1 to 11.3). Dropping 30 Gy to 20 Gy after ABVD cost 4.7 points (-10.3 to 0.8), the bound falling outside the 7-point non-inferiority limit, so 20 Gy was not established there; after baseline BEACOPP the loss was 0.8 points (-5.8 to 4.2) and 20 Gy was non-inferior. The interaction between the two questions was not shown, at P=0.16. 5-year overall survival was 94-95% in all 4 groups. Baseline BEACOPP cost more acute toxicity, at least one grade 3 or 4 event in 73.8% against 51.5%, and 30 Gy more than 20 Gy, 12.0% against 5.7%.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2010;28:4199-4206  20713848 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1999-2007 long-term follow-up update 28418763 J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1444-1450 pooled late-relapse analysis (HD7-HD12) 28240973

records.title: UK RAPID
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage IA or IIA without mediastinal bulk, aged 16-75. 602 were registered and started ABVD; 571 were scanned after 3 cycles and 426 were PET-negative, of whom 420 were randomised; the 145 who were PET-positive received a fourth cycle with radiotherapy and were followed without randomisation After 3 cycles of ABVD and a negative PET: 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy vs no further treatment (single-arm follow-up for PET-positive patients, who received a 4th ABVD cycle plus radiotherapy) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: interim PET positivity rate, OS and cause of death, second cancers. Omitting radiotherapy after a negative PET was not shown to be non-inferior, though the absolute loss was small and survival was not harmed. Among the 420 randomised, 3-year progression-free survival was 90.8% without further treatment against 94.6% with radiotherapy, a difference of -3.8 points whose 95% interval ran to -8.8 and so fell outside the 7-point margin. Only 40 of the 46 events the trial was designed around had occurred. Per protocol the gap widened, 90.8% against 97.1%. Survival did not separate: 3-year overall survival 99.0% without radiotherapy against 97.1% with it, and of the 8 deaths in the radiotherapy arm 5 were in patients who never received it. The trade is a few points of tumour control against irradiating everyone, in a group whose 3-year survival exceeds 97% either way.

records.title: EORTC/LYSA/FIL H10
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated classic supradiaphragmatic Hodgkin lymphoma in Ann Arbor stage I or II, aged 15-70, assigned at entry to an EORTC favourable or unfavourable cohort. All 1,950 were randomised before any PET existed; treatment was then adapted to the PET after 2 cycles of ABVD, and the two cohorts were analysed separately PET-negative after 2 cycles of ABVD: 4 cycles of ABVD (favourable) or 6 cycles (unfavourable) with no radiotherapy vs 3 or 4 cycles plus involved-node radiotherapy. PET-positive: 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP plus involved-node radiotherapy vs continuing ABVD plus radiotherapy Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, second malignancy. Radiotherapy could not be dropped after a negative PET in either cohort, while intensifying after a positive PET improved control. In the favourable cohort 5-year progression-free survival was 87.1% with ABVD alone against 99.0% with ABVD plus involved-node radiotherapy, hazard ratio 15.8 (95% CI 3.79 to 66.07); in the unfavourable cohort 89.6% against 92.1%, 1.45 (0.84 to 2.50). Both upper bounds exceeded their margins, 3.2 and 2.10, so non-inferiority was not shown in either. Where the PET was positive, switching to 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP raised 5-year progression-free survival to 90.6% from 77.4%, hazard ratio 0.42 (0.23 to 0.74). Survival was not uniform: the PET-positive patients kept on ABVD with radiotherapy had 5-year overall survival of 89.3%, the lowest in the trial, against 96.0% with escalated BEACOPP, hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.19 to 1.07), which the authors call a trend. The PET-negative strands ran 96.7% to 100.0%.

records.title: GHSG HD17
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated stage IA, IB or IIA classical Hodgkin lymphoma or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease with at least one GHSG risk factor, or stage IIB with a raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas and neither a bulky mass nor extranodal disease; aged 18-60. All 1,100 were randomised at entry, before the PET after 4 cycles; 905 formed the per-protocol population on which the verdict rests 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP then 2 cycles of ABVD in both groups, followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy in all patients vs 30 Gy involved-node radiotherapy only where the PET after cycle 4 was positive Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, complete remission, PET-negative rate, late toxicity, second malignancy. Radiotherapy can be omitted after a negative PET in unfavourable early-stage disease. 5-year progression-free survival was 95.1% with PET-guided treatment against 97.3% when everyone was irradiated, a difference of 2.2 points whose upper bound of 5.3 stayed inside the 8-point margin, so non-inferiority was met; among the PET-negative patients alone it was 95.9% against 97.7%, a difference of 1.7 points with the same bound. The hazard ratio was 0.523 (95% CI 0.226 to 1.211) and crosses 1. 5-year overall survival was 98.8%, with 10 deaths among 1,096 patients and 1 attributed to treatment. Late toxicity, which is the whole reason to omit radiotherapy, is not reported here and is deferred to a later analysis; second malignancies were 7 of 546 against 8 of 550 so far. Median follow-up 46.2 months and 25 progression-free survival events against the 35 the trial was powered for, so the 5-year figures are early.

records.title: GHSG HD8
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · III · 2003
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma of any histology in clinical stage I or II with one or more risk factors, or in stage IIIA with none — the stage IIIA route is the inverse of the stage I-II one, not a selection within it. Nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease was enrolled. 1,204 were randomised and 1,064 were informative for efficacy 2 cycles of COPP plus ABVD followed by 30 Gy extended-field radiotherapy vs 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy, each with 10 Gy to initial bulk Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, toxicity, second malignancy. Shrinking the radiotherapy field from extended to involved cost nothing in disease control and spared considerable acute toxicity, which is why involved-field became the standard. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 84.2% with involved-field against 85.8% with extended-field, a difference of 1.6 points whose upper 95% bound of 5.9 stayed inside the 8-point inferiority limit the trial set; 5-year overall survival was 92.4% against 90.8%. The design tested equivalence rather than non-inferiority and reports no hazard ratio. Acute radiotherapy toxicity was the reason to change practice: nausea 29.1% against 62.5%, leukopenia 33.3% against 49.1% and thrombocytopenia 5.5% against 16.7%, all lower with involved-field. Second malignancies occurred in 2.8% against 4.5% and deaths in 6.4% against 8.1%, neither difference established.

records.title: GHSG HD9
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2003
records.body: Untreated advanced or unfavourable intermediate-stage Hodgkin lymphoma, ages 15-65: stage IIB or IIIA with a large mediastinal mass alone or with extranodal lesions or massive splenic involvement, stage IIIA with a raised sedimentation rate or 3 or more involved nodal areas, or any stage IIIB-IV; Karnofsky above 70%, HIV-negative. 1,282 were assigned and 1,196 assessable at 10 years (261, 469 and 466 by arm); COPP/ABVD closed early in 1996. 8 cycles COPP/ABVD vs 8 cycles baseline BEACOPP vs 8 cycles escalated BEACOPP (cyclophosphamide 1,200, etoposide 200, doxorubicin 35 mg/m2 with filgrastim from day 8); consolidation radiotherapy to residual or initially bulky disease Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, treatment outcome as complete remission or early progression, second malignancy, causes of death, acute toxicity, survival after relapse. Escalated BEACOPP held its advantage over COPP/ABVD to 10 years, at the price of secondary leukaemia. Freedom from treatment failure was 82% with escalated BEACOPP, 70% with baseline BEACOPP and 64% with COPP/ABVD, and overall survival 86%, 80% and 75% in the same order, at a median 111 months; escalated beat baseline BEACOPP on both (P<.0001 and P=.0053). Secondary leukaemia or myelodysplasia tracked dose - 3.0% with escalated BEACOPP against 1.5% and 0.4%, 10-year cumulative incidence 3.2%, 2.2% and 0.4% (P=.030) - and 13 of the 14 escalated-arm cases arose within 7 years. Second malignancy overall did not separate (cumulative incidence 6.5%, 7.9% and 5.3%, P=.82), non-Hodgkin lymphoma and solid tumours running the other way. COPP/ABVD was closed at the first interim analysis and contributes 261 patients against 469 and 466. This 10-year cut sits outside the trial's prespecified analysis schedule, so none of its comparisons is a protected result.

records.title: GHSG HD15
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2012
records.body: Untreated, histology-confirmed advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma: stage IIB with a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions, or any stage III or IV; ages 18-60; ECOG 0-2; HIV-negative and without concurrent disease. Expert-panel reference histology was mandatory and excluded 44 patients from all analyses. 2,182 were randomised and 2,126 analysed. 8 cycles escalated BEACOPP (21-day cycles) vs 6 cycles escalated BEACOPP vs 8 cycles BEACOPP-14 (baseline doses, 14-day cycles); by protocol 30 Gy radiotherapy was planned for residual masses of 2.5 cm or more that remained PET-positive, and withheld otherwise Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete remission, treatment-related toxicity. Independent endpoint: negative predictive value of PET. Six cycles of escalated BEACOPP were non-inferior to eight and less toxic, and the investigators concluded 6 cycles should be the treatment of choice. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 89.3% with 6 cycles, 84.4% with 8 cycles and 85.4% with 8 cycles of BEACOPP-14; both reduced-intensity arms met non-inferiority on a hazard-ratio margin of 1.51. Superiority on freedom from treatment failure was not established: 6 cycles separated from 8 there only in the trial's descriptive analysis, not in its protected one. Toxicity favoured 6 cycles: treatment-related death 0.8% vs 2.1%, secondary leukaemia or myelodysplasia 0.3% vs 2.7% (P=0.0001). 5-year overall survival was 95.3% vs 91.9%, a difference of 3.3 points (97.5% CI 0.2 to 6.5). Confining radiotherapy to PET-positive residua cut its use to 11%, with a negative predictive value of 94.1%. Reported at the fourth preplanned interim analysis, median 48 months and 3 years early.

records.title: RATHL
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2016
records.body: Previously untreated advanced classic Hodgkin lymphoma: stage IIB-IV, or stage IIA with bulky disease or 3 or more involved sites; aged 18 or over, no upper limit, fit for full chemotherapy. Of 1,214 registered and 1,203 eligible, 937 were PET-negative after 2 cycles of ABVD and 935 of those were randomised; of the 182 PET-positive, 172 escalated to BEACOPP without randomisation. After 2 cycles of ABVD and a negative central interim PET-CT: continue ABVD for cycles 3-6 vs omit bleomycin (AVD) for cycles 3-6; interim-PET-positive patients escalated to BEACOPP-14 or escalated BEACOPP Primary: 3-year progression-free survival. Secondary: PFS among interim-PET-positive patients given BEACOPP, OS, short- and long-term toxicity, respiratory function. Omitting bleomycin after a negative interim PET fell just short of the prespecified non-inferiority margin, so AVD was not formally established as non-inferior, though efficacy was not significantly lower and pulmonary toxicity was less. 3-year progression-free survival was 85.7% continuing ABVD and 84.4% with AVD; the 1.6-percentage-point difference carried a 95% CI of -3.2 to 5.3, whose upper bound exceeded the 5-point margin, and the hazard ratio was 1.13 (95% CI 0.81-1.57). 3-year overall survival was 97.2% and 97.6%. Pulmonary harm was lower with AVD: grade 3 or 4 pulmonary events 1% vs 3%, and a smaller fall in carbon monoxide diffusing capacity, differing by 7.4 points at end of treatment (P<0.001) and 4.6 points at 1 year. Escalating the 172 interim-PET-positive patients to BEACOPP gave 3-year progression-free survival of 67.5% and overall survival of 87.8%. Median follow-up 41.2 months.

records.title: GHSG HD18
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated, histology-confirmed classic or nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma: stage III-IV, or stage II with B symptoms plus a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions; ages 18-60, ECOG 0-2, HIV-negative. Of 2,101 recruited, 1,964 were randomised and 1,945 analysed; treatment was then assigned by central PET after 2 cycles, counting Deauville 3 as positive. All received 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP, then assignment by central PET-2. PET-2-positive: 8 cycles total vs 8 cycles plus rituximab 375 mg/m2 (maximum total 700 mg). PET-2-negative: 4 cycles total vs 6-8 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, assessed separately in the PET-2-positive and PET-2-negative cohorts. Secondary: OS, second malignancy, complete response, Hodgkin lymphoma-specific death, grade 3-4 toxicity, treatment-related morbidity, late toxicity, quality of life. HD18 met one primary objective and missed the other: adding rituximab to escalated BEACOPP after a positive PET-2 did not improve outcome, while cutting to 4 cycles after a negative PET-2 held tumour control and reduced harm. In the PET-2-positive cohort 5-year progression-free survival was 88.1% with rituximab against 89.7% without, hazard ratio 1.25 (95% CI 0.69-2.26), P=0.46, far short of the 15-percentage-point gain the trial was powered to detect. In PET-2-negative patients 4 cycles gave 92.2% against 90.8% for 6-8 cycles, a 1.4-point difference (95% CI -2.7 to 5.4) clearing the -6-point non-inferiority margin, on the per-protocol set. 4 cycles also cut harm: no treatment-related death against 6 of 504, severe infection 8% vs 15%, organ toxicity 8% vs 18%, and 5-year overall survival 97.7% vs 95.4% (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.72), though survival was not a protected endpoint. Median follow-up 66 months for the rituximab comparison and 55 months for the 4-cycle comparison.

records.title: ECHELON-1
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated stage III or IV classic Hodgkin lymphoma, aged 18 or over with no upper limit; ECOG 0-2. 1,334 were randomised and all analysed. 84 and 102 patients by arm were 60 or older, and enrolment continued after an amendment recommending primary G-CSF prophylaxis for patients yet to be enrolled. Brentuximab vedotin 1.2 mg/kg IV plus doxorubicin, vinblastine and dacarbazine on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for up to 6 cycles vs ABVD, the same regimen with bleomycin instead of brentuximab vedotin, on the same schedule; primary G-CSF prophylaxis recommended by amendment after 75% of enrolment Primary: modified progression-free survival by independent review. Secondary: OS. The trial's remaining secondary and exploratory endpoints are in its protocol, which is not filed. Brentuximab vedotin with AVD improved the trial's primary endpoint and reduced bleomycin lung injury, at the cost of neuropathy and neutropenia. That endpoint was MODIFIED progression-free survival, which counts noncomplete response plus subsequent therapy as an event: 2-year rate 82.1% vs 77.2%, hazard ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.60-0.98), P=0.04, at a median 24.6 months. Interstitial lung disease fell to 2% from 7%, while peripheral neuropathy rose to 67% from 43%, grade 3 or worse 11% vs 2%, and febrile neutropenia to 19% from 8%; 7 of the 9 on-treatment deaths were neutropenia-associated and almost all occurred without G-CSF prophylaxis, which the trial's monitoring committee then recommended. A separately reported interim survival analysis at a median 73 months showed a survival benefit: 6-year overall survival 93.9% vs 89.4%, hazard ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.40-0.88), P=0.009, with 1 death from a second cancer against 11.

records.title: GHSG HD21
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced-stage classic Hodgkin lymphoma, ages 18-60: stage III-IV, or stage II with B symptoms plus a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions. 1,500 were randomised and 1,482 analysed; treatment length was set by PET after 2 cycles, 4 cycles if negative and 6 if positive. PET-2-guided 4 or 6 cycles at 21-day intervals: BrECADD - brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg to a maximum 180 mg IV day 0 with etoposide, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, dacarbazine and dexamethasone - vs escalated BEACOPP Primary: treatment-related morbidity and progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, gonadal function, second malignancy, quality of life, safety. BrECADD met both co-primary endpoints: it caused less treatment-related morbidity than escalated BEACOPP and gave superior progression-free survival. Treatment-related morbidity was 42% vs 59%, relative risk 0.72 (95% CI 0.65-0.80), P<0.0001. 4-year progression-free survival was 94.3% vs 90.9%, hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.45-0.97), P=0.035, at a median 48 months, and 4-year survival 98.6% vs 98.2%, with no treatment-related death on BrECADD against 3 on escalated BEACOPP. The toxicity advantage is haematological rather than general: grade 3 or worse anaemia 30% vs 59% and thrombocytopenia 55% vs 72%, but organ toxicity did not differ (19% vs 17%, P=0.46) and neutropenic fever, cardiac and gastrointestinal events were commoner on BrECADD. Gonadal recovery was far better - 95.3% vs 72.5% in women and 86.0% vs 39.2% in men.

records.title: SWOG S1826
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced-stage classic Hodgkin lymphoma, aged 12 or over with no upper limit, including adolescents; stage III-IV. 994 were randomised and 970 formed the efficacy cohort after 24 were found ineligible. Nivolumab 240 mg IV, or 3 mg/kg capped at 240 mg if aged 12 to under 18, plus doxorubicin, vinblastine and dacarbazine on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for 6 cycles vs brentuximab vedotin 1.2 mg/kg IV capped at 100 kg plus the same AVD backbone and schedule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: adverse events, OS, event-free survival. Nivolumab with AVD roughly halved progression or death compared with brentuximab vedotin plus AVD. The trial was reported early at a planned interim analysis, at a median follow-up of only 12.1 months: hazard ratio 0.48 (99% CI 0.27-0.87), P=0.001, with 1-year progression-free survival 94% vs 86%. A later cut at a median 2.1 years gave 2-year progression-free survival 92% vs 83% and hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.30-0.65). Whole-trial survival is immature and unproven: hazard ratio for death 0.39, 95% CI 0.15-1.03, crossing 1. In planned subset analyses, 3 of 50 patients aged 60 or over died on nivolumab against 10 of 49 on brentuximab, with grade 3 or worse sepsis 6.1% vs 21.3%. Brentuximab was stopped early in 55.3% of them, nivolumab in 14%. Among the 236 adolescents, 3-year progression-free survival was 93% vs 82%, with protocol radiotherapy in only 3 of 236. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia was commoner with nivolumab, 48% vs 26%, but G-CSF was mandatory only on the brentuximab arm.
