records.title: GHSG/EBMT HD-R1
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · N/A · 2002
records.body: Relapsed Hodgkin's disease after chemotherapy for advanced disease, at first or later relapse, age 16-60 with Karnofsky >70; late first relapse eligible only if first-line therapy used 7-8 drugs, and stage I-II at relapse only with added risk factors or previously advanced-stage disease; results apply to the 117 chemosensitive after 2 induction cycles, who alone proceeded to the assigned arms Dexa-BEAM x2 → 2 further Dexa-BEAM cycles (4 total) vs Dexa-BEAM x2 → high-dose BEAM + autologous stem-cell transplant Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, ORR, complete response rate, safety High-dose BEAM with autologous transplant improved disease control but not survival in chemosensitive relapse, and became standard salvage: 3-yr freedom from treatment failure 55% vs 34% with 4 cycles of Dexa-BEAM (p=0.019); median time to treatment failure not reached vs 12 mo. Survival did not differ (3-yr OS 71% vs 65%; p=0.331), from a trial stopped early for slow accrual at 117 of the 150 chemosensitive patients it was designed to need. The advantage held in early first relapse (41% vs 12%) and late first relapse (75% vs 44%), but not in multiple relapses (34% vs 44%). Most toxic deaths fell on the shared induction: the 2 Dexa-BEAM cycles every patient received caused 8 treatment-related deaths; after that, 5 of 56 (9%) died early on Dexa-BEAM cycles 3-4 vs 1 of 61 (2%) after transplant. Grade 3-4 infection 47% vs 49%; oral mucositis 37% vs 24%.

records.title: Brentuximab vedotin (pivotal)
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · II · 2012
records.body: Relapsed or refractory Hodgkin lymphoma after high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem-cell transplant; CD30-positive Reed-Sternberg cells on central pathology review; age >=12, ECOG 0-1, FDG-avid measurable disease >=1.5 cm; prior allogeneic transplant excluded (single-arm) Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3w, maximum 16 cycles Primary: ORR. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, PFS, OS, safety Brentuximab vedotin gave durable responses after autologous transplant had failed, in patients with a median 3.5 prior regimens: ORR 75% (95% CI 64.9-82.6) on independent review with CR in 34%. Median PFS was 5.6 mo overall but 21.7 mo in complete remitters, whose median response duration reached 20.5 mo; median OS 22.4 mo. Responses were fast — median 5.7 weeks to response, 12 weeks to CR — and 94% had some tumour reduction; 8 responders proceeded directly to allogeneic transplant. Peripheral sensory neuropathy dominated toxicity: 42% any grade and 8% grade 3, with no grade 4, cumulative and dose-related (median onset 12.4 weeks); it forced dose reduction in 10 patients and discontinuation in 6, and resolved or improved in 80%. Grade 3+ neutropenia 20% with no febrile neutropenia; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: AETHERA
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · III · 2015
records.body: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma 30-45 days after autologous stem-cell transplant for relapsed or primary refractory disease, with >=1 risk factor for post-transplant progression: primary refractory disease, first remission <12 mo, or extranodal involvement at the start of pre-transplant salvage; CR, PR or SD to salvage required; prior brentuximab vedotin excluded Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3w x16 cycles starting 30-45 days after autologous transplant vs placebo Primary: PFS. Secondary: OS, safety Brentuximab vedotin consolidation after autologous transplant delayed progression without a shown survival gain: median PFS 42.9 vs 24.1 mo on independent review (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.40-0.81; p=0.0013), 2-yr PFS 63% vs 51%. Survival did not differ at the prespecified interim analysis (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.67-1.97; p=0.6204), confounded by crossover: 85% of the placebo group received brentuximab vedotin after progression vs 18% of the treated group. Peripheral neuropathy is the price — 67% any grade and 13% grade 3, none grade 4 — forcing dose modification in 31% and discontinuation in 23%; it resolved or improved in 85% over a median 23.4 weeks. Grade 3+ events overall 56% vs 32%; grade 3+ neutropenia 29% vs 10%, with 1 febrile episode.

records.title: CheckMate 205
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · II · 2016
records.body: One cohort of a multicohort trial: classical Hodgkin lymphoma progressing after both autologous stem-cell transplant and subsequent brentuximab vedotin, given in that order; refractoriness to brentuximab vedotin not required; ECOG 0-1; prior allogeneic transplant, prior PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 blockade, and brentuximab vedotin given before transplant all excluded (single-arm) Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: ORR. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, PFS, OS, safety, quality of life Nivolumab produced frequent but mostly partial responses after failure of both autologous transplant and brentuximab vedotin: ORR 66.3% (95% CI 54.8-76.4) on independent review, with CR in 9% and PR in 58%. Investigators scored the same patients at 72.5% ORR and 28% CR, and central review downgraded 13 of 19 investigator-assessed CRs. Median response duration 7.8 mo and median PFS 10.0 mo at a median follow-up of 8.9 mo; 6-mo OS 98.7%, with no median OS reported. Responses came early, 58% by the first scan at week 9. Drug-related events affected 89%, grade 3 in 21% and grade 4 in 4%, most often neutropenia (5% grade 3) and raised lipase; pneumonitis occurred in 3%, both cases resolving on steroids, and 5% stopped for toxicity. 3 patients died, none of a treatment-related cause.

records.title: KEYNOTE-204
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory disease — salvage, transplant & novel agents · III · 2021
records.body: Relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma, second line or later, either after autologous stem-cell transplant or judged ineligible for one, so a transplant-eligible patient not yet transplanted did not qualify; prior brentuximab vedotin allowed only where it produced a complete or partial response; allogeneic transplant within 5 years and prior non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids excluded Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w vs brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3w, both up to 35 cycles or until progression Primary: PFS, OS. Secondary: ORR, complete response rate, duration of response, safety Pembrolizumab prolonged PFS over brentuximab vedotin in the second line and beyond: median 13.2 vs 8.3 mo on central review (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48-0.88; p=0.0027), ORR 65.6% vs 54.2%, CR 25% vs 24%, median response duration 20.7 vs 13.8 mo. Overall survival, a co-primary endpoint, was not analysed at this second interim cut. Only 37% had had an autologous transplant; the PFS advantage was clearest in those never transplanted (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.42-0.89) and did not separate in the previously transplanted (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.42-1.23), with no interaction test reported. The toxicities differ in kind: any-grade immune-mediated events 33% vs 7%, including pneumonitis 11% vs 3% any grade and 5% vs 1% grade 3-5; brentuximab vedotin gave treatment-related peripheral neuropathy in 15% grade 1-2 and 3% grade 3. 1 treatment-related death, from pneumonia, on pembrolizumab.

records.title: Lugano Classification (Cheson et al.)
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Staging & response assessment — Lugano classification · N/A · 2014
records.body: Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, all subtypes N/A — staging and response assessment framework, not a trial N/A Made PET-CT the standard for staging and response in FDG-avid lymphoma — all but CLL/SLL, lymphoplasmacytic, mycosis fungoides and marginal zone, which use the CT criteria. Response is scored on the Deauville 5-point scale, and the document is not consistent about what counts as complete: table 3 accepts 1 to 3 with or without a residual mass, the text only 1 or 2. It calls a score of 3 a good prognosis on standard treatment, and says de-escalation trials may prefer to treat it as inadequate. Marrow biopsy is dropped in Hodgkin lymphoma once PET-CT is done, and in DLBCL only where the scan is negative and discordant histology would change management; 2.5 cm unilateral biopsy stands elsewhere. The X suffix for bulk is retired for the largest diameter, A and B symptoms are kept for Hodgkin alone, and CRu is abolished. Bulk in Hodgkin stays 10 cm or a third of the transthoracic diameter, with none set for non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Surveillance scanning is discouraged. Consensus, ungraded.

records.title: TROG 99.03
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Limited-stage (stage I–II) — radiotherapy & adjuvant systemic therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Treatment-naive Ann Arbor stage I–II follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, staged by CT and bone marrow biopsy, with a life expectancy over 5 years and fit for involved-field RT; PET staging was permitted throughout but never required; excludes thoracic disease too extensive to irradiate safely. A 2006 amendment added rituximab to the systemic arm, which therefore spans two eras — 44 patients given CVP and 31 R-CVP IFRT 30-36 Gy → 6 cycles CVP (R-CVP after the 2006 amendment) vs IFRT 30-36 Gy alone Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, histologic transformation, safety Adding systemic therapy after involved-field RT improved PFS in early-stage follicular lymphoma: 10-yr PFS 59% vs 41%, HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.33-0.95). OS did not differ (10-yr 95% vs 86%; HR 0.62) and transformation was not reduced (4 vs 10 of 75 per arm). Only 2 of 148 irradiated patients had isolated in-field progression, so RT controlled local disease and the systemic benefit lay in preventing distant relapse. The rituximab-era effect looks larger (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.07-0.97) but is post-hoc and rests on few events. Toxicity after IFRT was mostly grade 1-2, grade 3-4 in 2%, with late salivary-gland toxicity in 8 (5%) and late skin toxicity in 4 (3%); among the 69 who started systemic therapy grade 4 neutropenia occurred in 10 (14%), grade 3 infection in 8 (12%) and grade 3 vincristine neuropathy in 3 (4%), with 2 late grade 3 vincristine neuropathies. One patient died of myelodysplasia in remission after IFRT plus CVP.

records.title: Ardeshna (NCRI)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — timing of therapy & single-agent rituximab · III · 2014
records.body: Asymptomatic, treatment-naive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, stage II–IV, ECOG 0–1, entered within 3 months of diagnostic biopsy; low tumour burden was the entry gate, defined as normal LDH, no mass over 7 cm, no more than 3 nodal sites with nodes over 3 cm, spleen up to 16 cm and no significant effusion; excludes histological transformation and near-critical organ compression. The rituximab-induction-only arm closed to recruitment in 2007 Rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×4 → maintenance q2mo ×2 yr vs rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×4 vs watch-and-wait Primary: time to start of new treatment, quality of life at month 7. Secondary: spontaneous remission rate, response at month 25, overall survival, quality of life, progression-free survival, time to histological transformation, safety Early rituximab markedly delays new treatment but did not improve the quality of life it was co-designed to test. At 3 yr, 88% on rituximab maintenance vs 46% on watch-and-wait had not started new therapy (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.14-0.31); median 31.1 mo with observation, not reached with maintenance. The quality-of-life co-primary — better functional wellbeing, less anxiety and depression at month 7 — was not met (p=0.87, 0.51, 0.70), though mental adjustment to cancer favoured rituximab (p=0.0004). OS showed no difference (3-yr 97% vs 94%; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.34-1.54) but is immature at 28 deaths in 379; transformation was not reduced (7% vs 11%). Induction alone matched maintenance for time to new treatment (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.41-1.34) but was worse on PFS (3-yr 60%; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.32-0.87, p=0.011). 18 rituximab-related serious adverse events, 12 grade 3-4, mainly infection and neutropenia; no treatment-related deaths. Observation remains reasonable for asymptomatic low-burden disease.

records.title: GLSG (Hiddemann)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2005
records.body: Previously untreated stage III–IV follicular lymphoma, WHO grade 1–2, all requiring treatment at entry — B symptoms, bulky disease (mediastinal over 7.5 cm or other over 5 cm), impaired haematopoiesis, or rapidly progressive disease — so asymptomatic non-bulky disease suitable for watch-and-wait was out of scope; excludes grade 3 follicular lymphoma. Central pathology confirmation was not a gate before randomisation, still pending in 38 of 428 at analysis Induction: R-CHOP vs CHOP, both 6-8 cycles q3w → in responders under 60, a second randomisation to DexaBEAM then myeloablative radiochemotherapy with peripheral blood stem-cell transplantation vs interferon-α maintenance; all responders 60 and over received interferon-α maintenance Primary: time to treatment failure. Secondary: overall response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, time to next therapy, overall survival, safety Adding rituximab to CHOP cut treatment failure by 60% and established R-CHOP as the frontline standard in advanced follicular lymphoma: 28 of 223 failed on R-CHOP vs 61 of 205 on CHOP (p<0.001). Response was higher (96% vs 90%) though CR was not clearly different (20% vs 17%); duration of response and time to next therapy were both longer. Survival also favoured R-CHOP at this early follow-up, 6 vs 17 deaths within 3 yr (p=0.016), with lymphoma progression accounting for 1 vs 9. Median follow-up was only 18 mo, so these are early estimates. Grade 3-4 granulocytopenia was commoner with R-CHOP (after 63% vs 53% of cycles) but infections were as frequent in both arms (5% vs 7% of courses), and 4 patients in each arm died of infection, 8 of the 23 deaths; infusion reactions occurred in 7% of first rituximab infusions.

records.title: PRIMA
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2011
records.body: Previously untreated follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, with at least one high-tumour-burden criterion — a mass over 7 cm, 3 or more nodes of 3 cm or more, symptomatic splenomegaly, organ compression or effusion, raised LDH or beta2-microglobulin, or B symptoms; excludes grade 3b and transformed disease. Randomisation to maintenance required a complete or partial response to R-CVP, R-CHOP or R-FCM induction and no major induction toxicity, so it applies only to responders who tolerated induction Rituximab 375 mg/m² q8wk ×12 (2 yr) vs observation Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, time to next chemotherapy, time to next antilymphoma treatment, overall survival, response rate at end of maintenance, quality of life, safety 2 yr of rituximab maintenance after frontline immunochemotherapy improved 3-yr PFS 74.9% vs 57.6% (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.44-0.68) and raised CR/CRu at the end of maintenance to 71.5% vs 52.2%; 52% of those in partial response at randomisation converted to CR/CRu vs 30%. Time to next antilymphoma treatment (HR 0.62) and to next chemotherapy (HR 0.60) were both longer. OS did not differ (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.51-1.47) and quality of life did not differ (FACT-G 86.6 vs 87.2). Grade 3-4 adverse events 24% vs 17%, grade 2-4 infections 39% vs 24%, discontinuation for toxicity 4% vs 2%, and 1 death from fulminant hepatitis B without antiviral prophylaxis, reported as possibly treatment-related. Maintenance is a standard option for responders, at the cost of added infection risk and no survival gain so far.

records.title: FOLL05 (FIL)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2013
records.body: Previously untreated follicular lymphoma, WHO grade 1–3a, Ann Arbor stage II–IV, with active disease requiring treatment, aged 18–75; excludes grade 3b, stage I disease, histological transformation and CNS involvement. Central pathology review was required only for grade 3 or ungraded cases, all others entering on local diagnosis R-CVP ×8 cycles vs R-CHOP ×6 cycles vs R-FM ×6 cycles, all q3w Primary: time to treatment failure. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, overall response rate, complete response rate, safety R-CHOP and R-FM both beat R-CVP on 3-yr time to treatment failure (62% and 59% vs 46%; HR 0.62 and 0.63) and on 3-yr PFS (68% and 63% vs 52%), with no difference between R-CHOP and R-FM (p=0.76 for time to treatment failure). Response was similar across arms (ORR 88-93%, CR 67-73%) and 3-yr OS was 95% for the whole series, with no between-arm comparison made. R-FM carried the worst toxicity — grade 3-4 neutropenia 64% vs 50% with R-CHOP and 28% with R-CVP, thrombocytopenia 8% vs 3% and 0%, and 14 of the 23 second malignancies — so R-CHOP has the better risk-benefit balance and became the preferred backbone. Grade 3-4 infections were uncommon in all arms (2.4-4.7%) and there were no treatment-related deaths, but granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, not routinely given under protocol, was used at least once by 46% overall and unevenly by arm: 30% with R-CVP, 52% R-CHOP, 57% R-FM (p<0.001).

records.title: StiL NHL1 (Rummel)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2013
records.body: Treatment-naive stage III–IV CD20-positive indolent lymphoma — follicular grade 1–2, lymphoplasmacytic/Waldenström, small lymphocytic or marginal-zone — or mantle-cell lymphoma, WHO performance status 0–2; the indolent subtypes also had to need treatment, on cytopenia, B symptoms, bulk over 7.5 cm or 3 sites over 5 cm, organ compression, rapid progression or hyperviscosity, while mantle-cell entered on stage alone Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² q4w vs R-CHOP q3w, both up to 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate, complete response rate, overall survival, time to next antilymphoma treatment, event-free survival, safety Bendamustine-rituximab more than doubled median PFS over R-CHOP in untreated indolent and mantle-cell lymphoma: 69.5 vs 31.2 mo, HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.44-0.74), on the 514 of 549 randomised analysed per protocol. The trial was designed as a non-inferiority comparison. Time to next treatment was longer (HR 0.52) and CR higher (40% vs 30%), with the same overall response (93% vs 91%). OS did not differ (43 vs 45 deaths). On exploratory subgroups the gain was seen in follicular (HR 0.61), mantle-cell (0.49) and Waldenstrom (0.33) disease but not in marginal-zone lymphoma (0.70, 95% CI 0.34-1.43). BR was the better tolerated arm: grade 3-4 neutropenia 29% vs 69%; and at any grade, no alopecia at all against 100% of those given 3 or more R-CHOP cycles, infectious episodes 37% vs 50% and paraesthesia 7% vs 29%; 1 vs 5 deaths from sepsis. Commoner with BR were grade 3-4 lymphocytopenia (74% vs 43%) and, at any grade, erythematous (16% vs 9%) and allergic (15% vs 6%) skin reactions.

records.title: BRIGHT
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2014
records.body: Treatment-naive CD20-positive indolent NHL — follicular grade 1–2, lymphoplasmacytic, or splenic, extranodal MALT or nodal marginal-zone — or mantle-cell lymphoma, ECOG 0–2, needing treatment for B symptoms, bulk (over 3 cm at 3 or more sites or over 7 cm at 1), lymphoma-related complications or hyperviscosity; excludes CLL/SLL, grade 3 follicular lymphoma, stage I disease, transformed disease and CNS involvement Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² q4w vs R-CHOP or R-CVP q3w (the comparator regimen chosen by the investigator before randomisation), all 6 cycles and up to 8 Primary: complete response rate. Secondary: overall response rate, progression-free survival, event-free survival, duration of response, overall survival, quality of life, safety Bendamustine-rituximab was non-inferior to R-CHOP or R-CVP for complete response in untreated indolent NHL and MCL — 31% vs 25% by blinded independent review, with a higher overall response (97% vs 91%). The CR gap did not clear the trial's superiority test. By histology it narrows: non-inferiority was not reached in the indolent-NHL subgroup (CR-rate ratio 1.16, 95% CI 0.81-1.65) and only approached in follicular lymphoma (1.27, 0.87-1.84). BR bettered standard therapy only in MCL (1.95, 1.01-3.77), on 33 standard-therapy patients. PFS, EFS, duration of response, OS and quality of life are unreported here, immature at this cut. Toxicity differed rather than lessened: against R-CHOP, BR gave less grade 3-4 neutropenia (39% vs 87%) but more grade 3-4 lymphopenia (61% vs 33%), and less alopecia (4% vs 51%) and neuropathy (9% vs 44%), both any grade; against R-CVP, more any-grade nausea (63% vs 39%), vomiting (25% vs 13%) and hypersensitivity (13% vs 3%). 12 deaths (5%) vs 9 (4%).

records.title: GALLIUM
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2017
records.body: Previously untreated CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, stage III–IV or stage II with a mass of 7 cm or more, ECOG 0–2, with treatment indicated by GELF tumour-burden criteria. GALLIUM also randomised a marginal-zone cohort, but was powered for the follicular stratum and only that stratum is reported here Obinutuzumab 1000 mg + chemotherapy (CHOP, CVP or bendamustine, stipulated by site) → obinutuzumab q2mo ×2 yr in responders vs rituximab 375 mg/m² + the same chemotherapy → rituximab q2mo ×2 yr in responders Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate at end of induction, event-free survival, disease-free survival, duration of response, overall survival, time to new antilymphoma treatment, safety Obinutuzumab-based immunochemotherapy with obinutuzumab maintenance lengthened investigator-assessed PFS over the rituximab equivalent in untreated advanced follicular lymphoma: 3-yr PFS 80.0% vs 73.3%, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.51-0.85); independent review of the same endpoint gave HR 0.71 (0.54-0.93). These are interim results, at 245 of the 370 planned events. OS did not differ (3-yr 94.0% vs 92.1%, HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.49-1.17), nor did response at end of induction (88.5% vs 86.9%), and CR was numerically lower with obinutuzumab (19.5% vs 23.8%). The cost is toxicity: grade 3-5 events 74.6% vs 67.8%, serious events 46.1% vs 39.9%, fatal events 4.0% vs 3.4%, grade 3-5 infusion reactions 12.4% vs 6.7%, grade 3-5 infection 20.0% vs 15.6% and grade 3-5 neutropenia 45.9% vs 39.5%; 6 obinutuzumab patients (1.0%) developed a second haematological cancer and no rituximab patient did.

records.title: RELEVANCE
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Advanced-stage frontline — immunochemotherapy, antibody choice & maintenance · III · 2018
records.body: Histologically confirmed CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3a, needing treatment by GELF tumour-burden criteria, with no previous systemic therapy for lymphoma; stage I–II disease was not excluded Rituximab + lenalidomide 10-20 mg/day ×18 cycles → rituximab q8wk ×12 vs rituximab + investigator's choice of CHOP, bendamustine or CVP → rituximab q8wk ×12; 120 weeks of treatment in both arms Primary: confirmed or unconfirmed complete response rate at 120 weeks, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, duration of response, histologic transformation, safety Chemo-free rituximab-lenalidomide did not beat rituximab-chemotherapy in untreated follicular lymphoma, and neither co-primary endpoint was met: confirmed or unconfirmed CR at 120 wk 48% vs 53% (p=0.13) and PFS HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.85-1.43, p=0.48) at the first interim look. 3-yr PFS 77% vs 78%, no median reached for PFS or OS; OS immature, 3-yr 94% in both arms. Best CR at any point in the trial separated further, 59% vs 67%. The one subgroup interaction was by stage: among the 70 with stage I–II disease, CR at 120 wk was 10 of 30 on lenalidomide vs 30 of 40 on chemotherapy. Toxicity is the trade: lenalidomide gave more grade 3-4 skin reactions (7% vs 1%) and, at any grade, tumour flare (6% vs under 1%), with dose reduction in 36% vs 14% and discontinuation in 11% vs 3%; chemotherapy more grade 3-4 neutropenia (50% vs 32%) and, at any grade, febrile neutropenia (7% vs 2%) and infection with grade 3-4 neutropenia (12% vs 5%). Overall grade 3-4 events were similar, 65% vs 68%.

records.title: EORTC 20981 (van Oers)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — immunochemotherapy & maintenance · III · 2006
records.body: Relapsed or resistant CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3, Ann Arbor stage III–IV at initial diagnosis, after no more than 2 prior non-anthracycline regimens, WHO performance status 0–2; excludes prior anthracycline, prior rituximab, prior stem-cell transplantation and histological transformation, so the result does not extend to an anthracycline- or rituximab-exposed relapse. Only patients in complete or partial remission after induction entered the maintenance randomisation Induction: CHOP vs R-CHOP, both q3w ×6 → in responders, a second randomisation to rituximab 375 mg/m² q3mo for up to 2 yr vs observation Primary: response to induction, progression-free survival from the maintenance randomisation. Secondary: progression-free survival and overall survival from the first randomisation, overall survival from the maintenance randomisation, safety Rituximab maintenance after salvage immunochemotherapy improved both progression-free and overall survival in relapsed follicular lymphoma. Among the 334 responders randomised a second time, median PFS was 51.5 vs 14.9 mo with observation (HR 0.40) and 3-yr OS 85.1% vs 77.1% (HR 0.52, p=0.011). The gain held in patients who had already had rituximab during induction (51.8 vs 23.0 mo, HR 0.54), which is the trial's structural point. At the first randomisation R-CHOP beat CHOP for induction response (85.1% vs 72.3%) and CR (29.5% vs 15.6%) and for PFS (33.1 vs 20.2 mo, HR 0.65), but induction OS did not differ (3-yr 82.5% vs 71.9%, p=0.096). Maintenance cost more grade 3-4 infection (9% vs 2.4%, p=0.009); neutropenia was 10.8% vs 5.4%, which did not reach statistical significance; 6 of 167 stopped for toxicity and no death was attributed to it. Efficacy is on the 465 of 474 randomised with a valid consent form.

records.title: GADOLIN
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — immunochemotherapy & maintenance · III · 2016
records.body: Rituximab-refractory CD20-positive indolent NHL — follicular grade 1–3a, marginal zone, small lymphocytic or Waldenström's — after previous anti-lymphoma treatment including up to 4 chemotherapy-containing regimens, ECOG 0–2; refractory meant failure to respond to or progression during a previous rituximab-containing regimen, or progression within 6 months of the last dose; excludes histological transformation and bendamustine within the previous 2 yr Obinutuzumab 1000 mg + bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 q4w ×6 → obinutuzumab 1000 mg q2mo for up to 2 yr in non-progressors vs bendamustine 120 mg/m² d1-2 q4w ×6 Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, disease-free survival, event-free survival, time to next antilymphoma treatment, quality of life, safety Obinutuzumab-bendamustine then obinutuzumab maintenance prolonged survival in rituximab-refractory indolent NHL: at a median 31.8 mo, OS HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.47-0.96), with median PFS by investigator 25.8 vs 14.1 mo (HR 0.57) and time to next treatment 40.8 vs 19.4 mo (HR 0.59); in the 335 with follicular lymphoma OS HR was 0.58. The primary endpoint was met earlier, at a 2014 interim analysis of the 396 randomised by then, on independent review: median PFS not reached vs 14.9 mo, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.40-0.74); survival had not separated at that cut (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.52-1.30), and no PFS benefit was shown in the 75 with non-follicular histology (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.46-1.90), a cohort the authors call too small to establish a difference. Response at end of induction did not differ (66.7% vs 64.4%). Grade 3-5 events 72.5% vs 65.5%, most commonly neutropenia (34.8% vs 27.1%), with infusion reactions (9.3% vs 3.4%); serious events 43.6% vs 36.9%; fatal events 7.8% vs 6.4%.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2016;17:1081-1093   J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2259-2266 updated analysis, median 31.8 mo (OS HR 0.67) 29584548

records.title: AUGMENT
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — immunochemotherapy & maintenance · III · 2019
records.body: Relapsed or refractory CD20-positive follicular lymphoma grade 1–3a or marginal-zone lymphoma needing treatment, after at least 1 prior systemic therapy and at least 2 prior rituximab doses, ECOG 0–2; patients refractory to rituximab were excluded. Also excludes grade 3b follicular lymphoma, transformed disease, prior lenalidomide, neuropathy above grade 1 and CNS involvement Lenalidomide 20 mg/day d1-21 (10 mg if creatinine clearance 30-59 mL/min) + rituximab vs placebo + rituximab, both up to 12 cycles of 28 days Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, overall survival, event-free survival, time to next antilymphoma treatment, histologic transformation, safety Adding lenalidomide to rituximab nearly tripled median PFS in relapsed indolent lymphoma that was not refractory to rituximab: 39.4 vs 14.1 mo by independent review, HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.34-0.62), with higher response (78% vs 53%) and CR (34% vs 18%). The benefit is a follicular-lymphoma result: in the 63 patients with marginal-zone lymphoma PFS did not differ (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.47-2.13) against HR 0.40 in follicular disease, which the authors call difficult to interpret because of the small number and baseline imbalance, without excluding a lack of effect. Survival is immature (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.33-1.13, no p value reported) and transformation occurred in 2 vs 10 patients. Toxicity is the trade: grade 3-4 events 69% vs 32%, driven by neutropenia (50% vs 13%), serious adverse events 26% vs 14%, and 2 fatal adverse events in each arm.

records.title: inMIND
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — immunochemotherapy & maintenance · III · 2026
records.body: Relapsed or refractory CD19-positive, CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, grade 1/2 or 3A, after at least 1 prior line including an anti-CD20 antibody, ECOG 0–2 and judged by the investigator to need treatment; excludes transformed lymphoma, and progression within 24 months of diagnosis required a fresh biopsy to rule it out. A marginal-zone cohort was randomised under the same protocol and is not described in this publication Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg + lenalidomide 20 mg/day d1-21 + rituximab vs matched placebo + the same lenalidomide-rituximab, both up to 12 cycles of 28 days Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: PET-complete response rate, overall survival, overall response rate, duration of response, time to next treatment, quality of life, safety Adding tafasitamab to lenalidomide-rituximab cut the risk of progression or death by more than half in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma: median PFS 22.4 vs 13.9 mo, HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.58), and independent review agreed (HR 0.41). The key secondary endpoint was also met — PET-complete response 49% vs 40% (OR 1.5, p=0.029) — with higher overall response (84% vs 72%) and longer response duration (21.2 vs 13.6 mo). Benefit was consistent whether or not disease had progressed within 24 months of diagnosis and whether or not it was refractory to a prior anti-CD20 antibody. Survival is immature (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.31-1.13), with the formal analysis due at 5 yr. Toxicity was little different from lenalidomide-rituximab alone: grade 3-4 events 71% vs 69%, grade 3-4 neutropenia 40% vs 38%, serious events 36% vs 32%, and no treatment-related death on tafasitamab against 2 on placebo.

records.title: Idelalisib (Study 101-09)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — targeted oral agents · II · 2014
records.body: Relapsed indolent B-cell NHL — follicular grade 1–3a, small lymphocytic, marginal zone, or lymphoplasmacytic/Waldenström's — after at least 2 prior systemic therapies and refractory to both rituximab and an alkylating agent, meaning less than a partial response or progression within 6 months of completing prior therapy; Karnofsky 60 or above; excludes histological transformation and active CNS lymphoma (single-arm) Idelalisib 150 mg PO twice daily, continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: time to response, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Idelalisib gave a 57% response rate (95% CI 48-66) by independent review in indolent NHL refractory to both rituximab and an alkylating agent, with CR in 6%, median duration of response 12.5 mo and median PFS 11.0 mo; responses came at a median of 1.9 mo. Median OS was 20.3 mo at a median follow-up of 9.7 mo. Much of the toxicity is late: grade 3+ diarrhoea or colitis in 16%, beginning at a median of 6 mo, and grade 3+ pneumonia in 7%. On laboratory testing, grade 3+ transaminitis occurred in 13% at a median of 6.3 wk, asymptomatic and reversible in every case with 10 of 14 rechallenged patients able to continue, and grade 3+ neutropenia in 27%. 34% needed a dose reduction and 20% stopped for toxicity. 28 patients (22%) died, 11 on treatment or within 30 days — 3 of progressive disease and 3 of pneumonia.

records.title: Tazemetostat (E7438-G000-101)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — targeted oral agents · II · 2020
records.body: Follicular lymphoma, grade 1–3b including transformed disease, relapsed after or refractory to at least 2 prior systemic therapies, ECOG 0–2, with tumour tissue available for central EZH2 testing whose result assigned the patient to the EZH2-mutant or wild-type cohort; excludes another non-cutaneous malignancy and CNS involvement (single-arm) Tazemetostat 800 mg PO twice daily, continuous 28-day cycles, until progression or unacceptable toxicity, to a maximum of 2 yr Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, disease control rate, time to first response, safety Tazemetostat is an oral EZH2 inhibitor with modest activity and little toxicity in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma. Two cohorts were enrolled, each tested against a fixed response benchmark; the trial was not designed to compare them. Response by independent review was 69% (95% CI 53-82) in the 45 patients with EZH2-mutant disease and 35% (23-49) in the 54 with wild-type disease, CR 13% and 4%; the authors attribute the gap mainly to the EZH2 mutation itself, though within the POD24 subgroup they note the wild-type cohort held more grade 3b or transformed disease. Median duration of response was 10.9 mo in the mutant cohort and 13.0 mo in the wild-type, median PFS 13.8 and 11.1 mo, at 22.0 and 35.9 mo median follow-up. Grade 3+ treatment-related events were uncommon — thrombocytopenia 3%, neutropenia 3%, anaemia 2%; 8% stopped for toxicity and no death was treatment-related. 1 patient developed myelodysplastic syndrome and 1 acute myeloid leukaemia on treatment.

records.title: ZUMA-5 (axi-cel)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — CAR T-cell & bispecific antibody therapy · II · 2022
records.body: Relapsed or refractory indolent NHL — grade 1–3a follicular lymphoma or nodal/extranodal marginal zone lymphoma — after at least 2 prior lines including an anti-CD20 antibody with an alkylating agent, ECOG 0–1; that 2-line minimum was introduced by a 2017 amendment, so earlier enrolees could have had fewer; excludes CNS involvement, prior allogeneic transplant and prior CD19-directed therapy (single-arm) Axicabtagene ciloleucel 2 × 10⁶ CAR T cells/kg as a single IV infusion, after conditioning fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² daily on days −5 to −3 Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, time to next therapy, safety Axicabtagene ciloleucel produced high and durable remissions in relapsed or refractory indolent NHL and reached almost everyone enrolled: 148 of the 153 leukapheresed (97%) were infused. Response by independent review was 92% with CR 74%, and 94% with CR 79% in follicular lymphoma. At a median 23.3 mo, 59% of patients had an ongoing response and 73% of complete responders remained in remission; 18-mo PFS was 64.8% and OS 87.4%, with median duration of response and PFS not reached in follicular disease. In the 23 evaluable marginal-zone patients ORR was 83% and median PFS 12.0 mo. Cytokine release syndrome affected 82% of those treated (7% grade 3+) and neurologic events 59% (19% grade 3-4); among the 24 marginal-zone patients CRS reached 100% and grade 3-4 neurologic events 38%, against 78% and 15% among the 124 with follicular lymphoma. Grade 3+ events overall were 86%, mostly cytopenias (70%) and infections (18%). 4 patients (3%) died of adverse events, 1 attributed to axi-cel.

records.title: ELARA (tisa-cel)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — CAR T-cell & bispecific antibody therapy · II · 2022
records.body: Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma grade 1, 2 or 3A on central pathology review — refractory to, or relapsed within 6 months of, a second or later line containing an anti-CD20 antibody and an alkylating agent; or relapsed on or within 6 months of anti-CD20 maintenance; or relapsed after autologous stem-cell transplantation — ECOG 0–1; excludes histological transformation, grade 3B disease, and prior anti-CD19 therapy or allogeneic transplant (single-arm) Tisagenlecleucel 0.6-6 × 10⁸ CAR-positive viable T cells as a single IV infusion, after lymphodepletion with fludarabine 25 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 250 mg/m² daily ×3 or bendamustine 90 mg/m² daily ×2 Primary: complete response rate. Secondary: overall response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety Tisagenlecleucel produced a 69.1% complete response rate (95% CI 58.8-78.3) by independent review in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, with ORR 86.2%, and was deliverable in 97 of the 98 enrolled. At this prespecified interim analysis, median follow-up 16.6 mo, median duration of response, PFS and OS were all not reached, 12-mo PFS was 67% and 69.1% of patients had an ongoing response at last assessment; 15 of 31 patients in partial remission at 3 mo later converted to CR. CR was 59.0% in the 61 whose disease had progressed within 24 months of first-line treatment and 87.9% in the 33 in whom it had not. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 48.5% and none of it was grade 3 or worse; neurologic events occurred in 37.1%, 3.1% of them grade 3+. Cytopenias are the dominant toxicity: grade 3+ in 69.1% within 8 wk, neutropenia 32%, and grade 3+ lymphopenia still present at 12 mo in 20%. 7 patients (7.2%) died, 5 of lymphoma and 1 of CRS; none was assessed as treatment-related.

records.title: Mosunetuzumab (GO29781)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — CAR T-cell & bispecific antibody therapy · II · 2022
records.body: Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, histologically confirmed grade 1–3a, after at least 2 prior lines that together included an anti-CD20 antibody and an alkylating agent, ECOG 0–1 (single-arm) Mosunetuzumab IV in 21-day cycles with cycle-1 step-up dosing — 1 mg d1, 2 mg d8, 60 mg d15, then 60 mg on d1 of cycle 2 and 30 mg from cycle 3 — with corticosteroid premedication; fixed 8 cycles in complete responders, up to 17 otherwise Primary: complete response rate. Secondary: overall response rate, duration of response, duration of complete response, progression-free survival, overall survival, time to next treatment, safety Mosunetuzumab, a CD20×CD3 bispecific given intravenously for a fixed duration, produced a 60.0% complete response rate by independent review (95% CI 49.1-70.2) against a 14% historical benchmark, with response in 80.0%. At a median 18.3 mo median PFS was 17.9 mo and median duration of response 22.8 mo, though only 4 patients remained at risk by then and the authors caution that median may not be robust; 70.2% of complete responders were still in remission at 18 mo and median OS was not reached. Cytokine release syndrome affected 44%, nearly all grade 1-2 (26% and 17%) with 1 patient each at grade 3 and grade 4, mostly confined to cycle 1 and graded on the ASTCT scale rather than the Lee 2014 criteria used in the CAR T-cell trials, so the rates are not directly comparable. Neurological events were grade 1-2 only. Grade 3-4 neutropenia 27%, hypophosphataemia 17%; serious events 47%; 1 death from lymphoma progression and 1 of unknown cause.

records.title: TRANSCEND FL (liso-cel)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — CAR T-cell & bispecific antibody therapy · II · 2024
records.body: Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma grade 1–3A after at least 1 prior line containing an anti-CD20 antibody with an alkylating agent — third-line-or-later cohorts, plus a high-risk second-line cohort defined by progression within 24 months of diagnosis and/or modified GELF criteria; PET-positive disease required before lymphodepletion (single-arm) Lisocabtagene maraleucel 100 × 10⁶ CAR-positive T cells as a single infusion, after fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² daily ×3 Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety Lisocabtagene maraleucel produced near-universal remissions in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, in 2 cohorts tested separately: response by independent review was 97% (95% CI 91.6-99.4) with CR 94% in the 101 evaluable patients treated in the third line or later, and 96% with every responder in CR in the 23 treated in the second line. The trial was not designed to compare the cohorts. Results are early — median duration of response, PFS and OS were all unreached, with 90% of patients censored from the survival analysis, which the authors name as their first limitation; 12-mo rates in the later-line cohort were 82% for response duration, 81% PFS and 92% OS. Liso-cel was manufactured for 133 of 139 leukapheresed (96%) and 130 were treated; 38% needed bridging. Grade 3+ events 75%; cytokine release syndrome 58% on Lee 2014 criteria, 1 patient at grade 3 and none higher; neurological events 15%; prolonged cytopenia 22%; grade 3+ infection 5%. 13 died, 2 attributed to liso-cel.

records.title: EPCORE NHL-1 (epcoritamab)
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — CAR T-cell & bispecific antibody therapy · II · 2024
records.body: Relapsed or refractory CD20-positive follicular lymphoma grade 1–3A after at least 2 prior lines including an anti-CD20 antibody with an alkylating agent or lenalidomide, ECOG 0–2; excludes CNS lymphoma, active infection, and prior CD3×CD20 bispecific or recent CAR T-cell therapy (single-arm) Epcoritamab 48 mg SC in 28-day cycles — weekly cycles 1-3, fortnightly 4-9, then 4-weekly — after cycle-1 step-up priming, until progression or unacceptable toxicity; a separate optimisation cohort added a 3 mg intermediate dose on d15, with dexamethasone in place of prednisolone and IV hydration, and dropped mandatory hospitalisation Primary: overall response rate, cytokine release syndrome rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, time to next therapy, minimal residual disease negativity, quality of life, safety Subcutaneous epcoritamab produced an 82.0% response rate by independent review with CR 62.5% in multiply relapsed follicular lymphoma, median 1.4 mo to response. At 18 mo, 58.4% of responders and 72.2% of complete responders remained in response, 49.4% were progression-free and 70.2% alive. Response fell with more prior therapy: 89% after 2 lines against 68% after 4 or more, and 76% in double-refractory disease against 97% otherwise. Cytokine release syndrome affected 66%, nearly all grade 1-2, with 2 patients (2%) at grade 3 and none higher. A second cohort of 86 tested a modified priming schedule as its own primary endpoint: adding a 3 mg intermediate dose, dexamethasone and hydration brought cytokine release syndrome to 49% with nothing above grade 2, and 54% of them were not admitted for monitoring at the first full dose. Grade 3-4 neutropenia 25%; 19% stopped for adverse events, mostly infection; 13 had a fatal adverse event, 6 from COVID-19, none judged treatment-related.

records.title: EPCORE FL-1
records.subtitle: Indolent NHL · Relapsed / refractory — CAR T-cell & bispecific antibody therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Relapsed or refractory CD20-positive follicular lymphoma, classic grade 1–3A, Ann Arbor stage II–IV, after at least 1 prior regimen containing an anti-CD20 antibody with chemotherapy, ECOG 0–2, meeting at least 1 GELF criterion for needing treatment Epcoritamab 48 mg SC after cycle-1 step-up priming, weekly cycles 1-3 then 4-weekly to cycle 12, + lenalidomide 20 mg/day d1-21 ×12 cycles + rituximab 375 mg/m² vs the same lenalidomide-rituximab alone; fixed 12 cycles in both arms Primary: overall response rate, progression-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, overall survival, minimal residual disease negativity, duration of response, time to next antilymphoma treatment, event-free survival, quality of life, safety Adding epcoritamab to lenalidomide-rituximab met both primary endpoints in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma: response by independent review 95% vs 79%, a 16-point difference, and PFS HR 0.21 (95% CI 0.14-0.31) with median not reached vs 11.7 mo. CR rose to 83% vs 50%. Survival favoured the combination but did not clear its prespecified boundary — HR 0.38 (0.18-0.80), nominal p=0.0039 — so the testing sequence stopped there and minimal residual disease was never formally tested. These are interim results at a median follow-up of 14.8 mo. Toxicity is substantially greater: grade 3+ events 90% vs 68%, grade 3+ neutropenia 69% vs 42%, grade 3-4 infection 33% vs 16%, serious events 56% vs 29%, and 19% vs 12% stopped for toxicity. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 35% vs under 1%, none above grade 2, and was 26% with the 3-step priming schedule. Fewer patients died on the combination, 4% vs 10%.

records.title: Dostarlimab (Cercek, multi-tumour expansion)
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · Mismatch repair deficiency / MSI-H · II · 2025
records.body: Newly diagnosed stage I-III dMMR solid tumours at any site, amenable to curative-intent surgery; entry by mismatch-repair protein loss on immunohistochemistry; rectal and nonrectal cohorts (single-arm) Neoadjuvant dostarlimab 500 mg IV Q3W for 6 months (9 cycles) → response-adapted nonoperative management; residual disease was to receive standard neoadjuvant therapy and surgery Primary: overall response; sustained clinical complete response at 12 months. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, safety Across the multi-tumour study, 84 of 103 patients who completed dostarlimab had a clinical complete response and 82 did not undergo surgery. Rectal cohort: 49 of 49 completers had a clinical complete response; 37 had sustained it for >=12 months after treatment by the data cutoff, meeting the second co-primary endpoint. Nonrectal cohort, exploratory: 35 of 54 had a clinical complete response and 33 chose nonoperative management. Two-year RFS was 92% across all 117 analysed patients at 20.0-month median follow-up; 5 recurrences occurred (1 rectal primary regrowth, 4 nodal only) and no deaths. Adverse events occurred in 65% of 124 treated; 60% were reversible grade 1-2; 5 grade 3 events and 1 grade 4 febrile neutropenia.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (Marabelle, MSI-H/dMMR basket)
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · Mismatch repair deficiency / MSI-H · II · 2020
records.body: Previously treated adults with histologically or cytologically confirmed, unresectable or metastatic, incurable MSI-H/dMMR noncolorectal solid tumours across 27 histologies, after progression on or intolerance to standard therapy; ECOG 0–1; no prior PD-1/PD-L1/PD-L2 therapy Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles (~2 years) (single-arm) Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Across 233 previously treated patients with MSI-H/dMMR noncolorectal solid tumours spanning 27 histologies, pembrolizumab produced a centrally reviewed ORR of 34.3% (80/233; 95% CI 28.3–40.8); 23 had a complete response and 57 a partial response. Median duration of response was not reached (range 2.9–31.3+ months), and an estimated 86.9% of responders remained in response for at least 12 months. Median PFS was 4.1 months (95% CI 2.4–4.9) and median OS 23.5 months (95% CI 13.5–not reached) at 13.4 months' median follow-up. Cholangiocarcinoma was one descriptive subset (22 patients; ORR 40.9%, 9/22; 95% CI 20.7–63.6). Grade 3–5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 14.6% (34/233), including 1 fatal pneumonia.

records.title: DESTINY-PanTumor02
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · HER2-directed basket evidence · II · 2024
records.body: Adults with locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic HER2-expressing (IHC 3+/2+) solid tumours after >=1 systemic treatment for advanced/metastatic disease or with no satisfactory option, across biliary, bladder, cervical, endometrial, ovarian, pancreatic and other cohorts; breast, colorectal, gastric/GEJ and NSCLC excluded; noninfectious ILD/pneumonitis requiring steroids or suspected ILD not ruled out on imaging excluded; 5 cervical IHC 1+ patients entered after a protocol trigger (single-arm) Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks until progression, withdrawal or protocol discontinuation Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety T-DXd produced responses across multiple pretreated HER2-expressing cohorts. Investigator-assessed confirmed ORR was 37.1% overall (99/267; 95% CI 31.3-43.2); descriptive cohort ORR ranged from 4.0% in pancreatic to 57.5% in endometrial cancer, without formal cross-cohort testing. Among 75 patients with centrally confirmed IHC 3+ tumours, investigator-assessed confirmed ORR was 61.3% (46/75; 95% CI 49.4-72.4), median DoR 22.1 mo, PFS 11.9 mo and OS 21.1 mo. Overall median DoR was 11.3 mo, PFS 6.9 mo and OS 13.4 mo (66% maturity). Grade >=3 drug-related AEs occurred in 40.8%; adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis in 10.5%, including 3 fatal cases (1.1%).

records.title: ROAR (multi-tumour final analysis)
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · BRAF V600E · II · 2023
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed BRAFV600E-mutated advanced rare cancer and no standard treatment options: ATC, BTC, GIST, small-intestinal adenocarcinoma, WHO grade 1-2 or 3-4 glioma, hairy-cell leukaemia, or multiple myeloma; ECOG 0-2; prior BRAF/MEK inhibitors excluded. Dabrafenib 150 mg orally twice daily + trametinib 2 mg orally once daily, continuously until progression, unacceptable toxicity or death Investigator-assessed ORR by histology At the final 2021 data cut (n=206; single arm), investigator-assessed response rates varied by histology: HCL 89% (49/55), small-intestinal adenocarcinoma 67% (2/3), ATC 56% (20/36), low-grade glioma 54% (7/13), BTC 53% (23/43), myeloma 50% (5/10), high-grade glioma 33% (15/45), and GIST 0% (0/1). Exact 95% CIs were wide in the smallest cohorts; no pooled efficacy estimate or between-cohort test was reported. Across all 206 treated, grade 3-4 AEs occurred in 59.2%, serious AEs in 45.1% (22.3% treatment-related), dose interruptions in 56.3%, dose reductions in 44.2%, and discontinuation for AEs in 13.6%; 9 grade-5 AEs (4.4%), none treatment-related.

records.title: Larotrectinib (NTRK fusions)
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · NTRK / ROS1 fusions · I/II · 2018
records.body: Advanced TRK fusion-positive solid tumours (incl. NSCLC) Larotrectinib 100 mg twice daily (single-arm, tumour-agnostic); to progression Objective response rate Larotrectinib produced a 75% response rate across TRK fusion-positive cancers irrespective of tumour type; a landmark tumour-agnostic therapy applicable to NTRK+ NSCLC.

records.title: Selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-001)
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · RET fusions · II · 2022
records.body: RET fusion-positive non-lung/non-thyroid solid tumors (incl. salivary gland) in a tumor-agnostic basket Single-arm selpercatinib 160 mg twice daily, continuous 28-day cycles, to progression (LIBRETTO-001) Objective response rate Tumor-agnostic ORR 43.9% with durable responses (median DoR 24.5 months); supports RET inhibition in the small subset of RET fusion-positive salivary cancers.

records.title: eNRGy
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · NRG1 fusions · II · 2025
records.body: Advanced NRG1 fusion-positive cancer, any tumor type (12 tumor types enrolled; NSCLC and pancreatic cancer most represented) Zenocutuzumab 750 mg IV Q2W (single-arm, tumour-agnostic; NRG1 fusion) Overall response rate (investigator-assessed) Pivotal, registrational phase 2 trial across 12 tumor types with NRG1 fusions. Overall response rate 30% (95% CI 23-37), median duration of response 11.1 months, median PFS 6.8 months. Responses seen across tumor types including NSCLC (29%) and pancreatic cancer (42%). Adverse events mostly grade 1-2 (diarrhea, fatigue, nausea). Established zenocutuzumab as the first approved tumor-agnostic therapy for NRG1 fusion-positive cancer, including a cholangiocarcinoma subset with 36.8% ORR.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2025;392:566-576   Cleary et al. - 2026 - Efficacy and Tolerability of Zenocutuzumab in Advanced NRG1 Fusion-Positive Cholangiocarcinoma [fa06a148]

records.title: KRYSTAL-1 (adagrasib, other solid tumors)
records.subtitle: Tumour-Agnostic Basket Trials · KRAS G12C · II · 2023
records.body: Advanced solid tumors (excluding NSCLC/CRC) with KRAS G12C mutation, tumor-agnostic (pancreatic, biliary tract, appendiceal, ovarian, endometrial, gastroesophageal, small bowel, breast, glioblastoma) Adagrasib 600 mg twice daily (single-arm, tumour-agnostic; KRAS G12C) Objective response rate Largest phase 2 tumor-agnostic dataset for KRAS G12C-mutated solid tumors excluding NSCLC/CRC. ORR 35.1% (all partial responses), including 33.3% in pancreatic and 41.7% in biliary tract cancer; median PFS 7.4 months, median OS 14.0 months. Adverse events mostly grade 1-2. Suggests adagrasib may be useful as a tumor-agnostic agent for KRAS G12C-mutated cancers.

records.title: ASCO Guideline (Gyawali et al.)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Myeloid growth factors (CSFs) · N/A · 2026
records.body: Adults with cancer receiving myelosuppressive therapy N/A — clinical practice guideline, not a trial N/A ASCO guideline update on hematopoietic colony-stimulating factors (G-CSF/GM-CSF, including biosimilars). Primary prophylaxis to reduce febrile neutropenia (FN) is warranted when the chemotherapy FN risk is ~20% or higher and no equally effective, safer lower-risk regimen exists; for regimens with <20% FN risk, primary prophylaxis may still be warranted when patient-related factors put the patient at high FN risk. Secondary prophylaxis after a prior neutropenic complication; therapeutic CSFs for established FN in selected high-risk patients. For stem-cell mobilization, CSFs may be used alone or after chemotherapy, with a CXCR4 inhibitor added in selected cases. 2026 update reaffirmed prior guidance.

records.title: RECITE
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Myeloid growth factors (CSFs) · III · 2026
records.body: Persistent chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia (platelets ≤85×10⁹/L on trial day 1) on oxaliplatin-based multiagent chemotherapy for colorectal, gastroesophageal or pancreatic cancer, with ≥3 further cycles planned Weekly subcutaneous romiplostim, dose-titrated to platelets 100-250×10⁹/L, from trial day 1 through up to three further chemotherapy cycles vs Weekly subcutaneous placebo on the same schedule (randomised 2:1) Absence of CIT-induced chemotherapy dose modification in both cycle 2 and cycle 3 First phase 3 trial to show benefit for chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. The primary endpoint - no CIT-driven chemotherapy dose modification in both cycle 2 and cycle 3 - was met in 84% (92 of 109) with romiplostim vs 36% (20 of 56) with placebo: risk ratio 2.77 (95% CI 1.78-4.30), odds ratio 10.16 (95% CI 4.44-23.72), p<0.001, one comparison expressed two ways rather than two tests. Non-completion of chemotherapy, whether through discontinuation or death, was counted as a dose modification; 11 patients never restarted chemotherapy during the trial, 3 on romiplostim and 8 on placebo. Grade >=2 bleeding was formally tested and did not differ (4.0 vs 7.6 per 100 patient-years; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.04-6.77, p=0.63); the fixed testing sequence stopped there, so overall survival, platelet transfusion and week-4 platelet response were never tested and support no claim. Grade >=3 adverse events were 37% vs 22% all-cause but 3% vs 4% treatment-related, the excess reflecting chemotherapy rather than drug. Thromboembolism occurred in 2 of 110 (2%) vs 0 of 55 in the safety population, both at platelet counts within the 100-250 target range. On every imbalance the authors name, the romiplostim arm was the sicker one (stage 4 disease 72% vs 61%, ECOG >0 53% vs 41%, previous bevacizumab 35% vs 20%), which they list as a limitation. Confined to oxaliplatin-based multiagent chemotherapy in gastrointestinal cancers.

records.title: Ponsegromab (Groarke)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Cancer cachexia · II · 2024
records.body: Cancer cachexia (NSCLC 40%, pancreatic 32%, colorectal 29%) with serum GDF-15 ≥1500 pg/mL Ponsegromab (anti–GDF-15 mAb) 100, 200, or 400 mg SC Q4W for 3 doses vs placebo Change from baseline in body weight at 12 wk Dose-dependent weight gain vs placebo: +1.22 kg (100 mg), +1.92 kg (200 mg), +2.81 kg (95% CrI 1.55–4.08; 400 mg). The 400-mg dose also improved appetite, cachexia symptoms and physical activity; AEs 70% vs 80% with placebo. First positive anti–GDF-15 therapy in cancer cachexia.

records.title: ASCO–CAP HER2 Testing Guideline (2023 Update)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Biomarker testing & classification · N/A · 2023
records.body: Invasive breast cancer being assessed for HER2 status to select HER2-targeted therapy (IHC ± in-situ hybridisation) Guideline framework, not a trial arm comparison — see Key Findings n/a (HER2 classification/testing standard, not an efficacy endpoint) ASCO–CAP Update Panel systematic review (173 abstracts; 5 candidate publications) found no signal to revise the 2018 recommendations, which are affirmed — the IHC and ISH scoring algorithms are unchanged. The update acknowledges the new trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) indication for HER2-low disease (IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-nonamplified) established by DESTINY-Breast04. Notes IHC 0 tumours were excluded from DESTINY-Breast04 and that current data do not support a distinct IHC 0 versus 1+ prognostic/predictive threshold, so formal new categories (HER2-Low, HER2-Ultra-Low) are deemed premature — but best practices to distinguish the often subtle IHC 0 vs 1+ difference are now clinically relevant. Adds a new HER2 reporting comment to that effect. Co-published in J Clin Oncol and Arch Pathol Lab Med.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3867-3872   Wolff et al. - 2023 - HER2 Testing in Breast Cancer (Arch Pathol testing algorithms)

records.title: API-CAT (Mahé)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Cancer-associated thrombosis · III · 2025
records.body: Active cancer + proximal DVT or PE after ≥6 months of anticoagulation Oral apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily (reduced dose) vs 5.0 mg twice daily (full dose) for 12 months Centrally adjudicated recurrent VTE (noninferiority; upper 95% CI of sHR < 2.0) Reduced-dose apixaban noninferior to full-dose for recurrent VTE — 2.1% vs 2.8% (adj sHR 0.76; 95% CI 0.41–1.41; noninferiority P=0.001) — and caused less clinically relevant bleeding (12.1% vs 15.6%; adj sHR 0.75; 95% CI 0.58–0.97; P=0.03). Mortality 17.7% vs 19.6% (adj HR 0.96; 95% CI 0.86–1.06). Supports reduced-dose apixaban for extended cancer-associated VTE.

records.title: IV Magnesium for Cisplatin-AKI (Gupta)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Chemotherapy nephrotoxicity · N/A · 2025
records.body: Adults with cancer receiving first dose of IV cisplatin; 5 US cancer centers, 2006–2022 IV magnesium (median 2 g) vs no IV magnesium on day 1 of cisplatin (inverse-probability-weighted) Composite cisplatin-associated AKI or death (AKI = ≥2× baseline creatinine or kidney-replacement therapy within 14 d) Prophylactic IV magnesium associated with lower risk of cisplatin-AKI or death — 2.7% vs 5.3% (adj OR 0.80; 95% CI 0.66–0.97); consistent across sensitivity analyses incl. 90-day major adverse kidney events. Largest human evidence for IV-Mg renal protection during cisplatin; observational, so RCTs needed.

records.title: Dose Adjustments in Renal/Hepatic Impairment (Krens)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Dose adjustment / organ impairment · N/A · 2019
records.body: Adults with cancer receiving anticancer drugs who have renal or hepatic impairment N/A — systematic review (PK data, regulatory labelling, expert recommendations) across anticancer agents N/A (dose-adjustment reference, not an efficacy endpoint) Evidence-based dose-adjustment recommendations for anticancer drugs in renal or hepatic impairment — a practical reference across many cytotoxics and targeted therapies (PK summary, available evidence, authors' recommendations). Updated and expanded in 2023 (Giraud et al.). Use to dose safely when eGFR is reduced or liver function impaired; recommendations are largely labelling- and expert consensus–based (high-quality PK evidence is limited for many agents).

records.title: CaPP3
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Cancer chemoprevention · III · 2026
records.body: Adults with Lynch syndrome (germline pathogenic MMR-variant carriers), age >18 years; recruited via clinical genetics centres in the UK, Australia, Finland, Israel, Spain Aspirin 100 mg once daily vs aspirin 300 mg once daily vs aspirin 600 mg once daily (enteric-coated; 2 years double-blind then 3 years open-label, 5 years total) Incident Lynch syndrome (MMR-deficient) cancers; dose non-inferiority of 100 mg and 300 mg vs 600 mg (non-inferiority margin: upper 95% CI of HR and IRR < 1.5) 100 mg/day non-inferior to 600 mg in the ITT analysis (HR for time to first Lynch cancer 0.97 [95% CI 0.67-1.42]; cancer-burden IRR 0.94 [0.65-1.38]); per-protocol mixed (burden IRR 0.90 [0.55-1.46] non-inferior, time-to-first-cancer HR 1.00 [0.61-1.63] not). 300 mg/day not non-inferior in either analysis. Median follow-up 66.4 months; 216 Lynch cancers in 176 of 1866 participants. Suggests a lower (100 mg) dose may retain CAPP2's preventive benefit with better tolerability, but per-protocol non-inferiority was incomplete; follow-up to 10 years planned.
records.keywords: Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2026; published online Jul 9  42425127

records.title: SAKK 96/12 REDUSE
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · SRAE prevention · III · 2026
records.body: Metastatic breast cancer or castration-resistant prostate cancer with at least 3 bone metastases (784 breast cancer; 596 CRPC) Denosumab 120 mg Q4W vs denosumab 120 mg Q4W ×4 loading doses, then Q12W Time to first on-trial symptomatic skeletal event (noninferiority margin: HR upper bound <1.20) Denosumab Q12W after a 3-month loading phase was noninferior to Q4W: median time to first SSE 56.5 vs 56.6 months; stratified HR 1.023 (90% CI 0.874–1.197). Time to first and subsequent SSEs was also noninferior (HR 1.043, 90% CI 0.907–1.198). Hypocalcemia was lower with Q12W (30% vs 46%), as was osteonecrosis of the jaw (6.9% vs 8.5%).

records.title: D-TORCH
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · HAND-FOOT syndrome prevention · III · 2024
records.body: Adults with breast or GI malignancies starting capecitabine ≥1,000 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 every 21 days, alone or with systemic therapy, in neoadjuvant, adjuvant or palliative settings; ECOG 0–2; no grade ≥2 neuropathy or hand/foot dermatosis confounding HFS assessment; excluded concurrent NSAIDs/pyridoxine and NSAID hypersensitivity Topical diclofenac 1% gel, 1 g per hand twice daily from the start of capecitabine for 4 cycles/12 weeks or until HFS, applied to palmar and dorsal surfaces of both hands vs Matched placebo gel on the same schedule and for the same duration Primary: Incidence of CTCAE v5.0 grade 2-3 hand-foot syndrome within 12 weeks. Secondary: Grade 1-3 HFS incidence, HFS-related capecitabine dose changes, Time to HFS, HFS14 quality of life, Topical gel adherence, Safety Topical diclofenac reduced grade 2–3 capecitabine-associated HFS at 12 weeks: 3.8% vs 15.0% (absolute reduction 11.2%; NNT≈9). Grade 1–3 HFS was 6.1% vs 18.1%; HFS-related capecitabine dose reductions 3.8% vs 13.5%; among complete cases assessed at baseline and at grade 2-3 HFS or 12 weeks, HFS14 worsening was 3.5 points (110/130) vs 12.4 points (106/133), although secondary outcomes were not formally tested. Grade 3 AEs were 11.5% vs 13.5%; no cardiovascular events or AE-related capecitabine discontinuations. Single-centre Indian trial; gel and HFS assessment were limited to hands; outcomes beyond 12 weeks were not assessed.

records.title: Baseline Fatigue & Toxicity Risk (Unger)
records.subtitle: General Onc & Supportive Care · Toxicity risk prediction · N/A · 2026
records.body: Patients with cancer receiving systemic therapy in 17 SWOG phase 2/3 trials (enrolled 1990-2022); prostate, lung, colorectal, lymphoma, breast, melanoma, ovarian, or pancreatic cancer N/A — observational exposure analysis: baseline patient-reported fatigue (5-point Likert scale; any vs none/minimal, and by severity), not an intervention Risk of CTCAE grade ≥3 (severe), grade ≥4 (life-threatening), and grade 5 (fatal) adverse events by baseline fatigue level (odds ratios via generalized estimating equations, clustered by trial, adjusted for age/sex/race/obesity) Among 7086 patients (mean age 61.1y; 29.7% female) pooled across 17 SWOG trials, 39.1% reported some/more baseline fatigue. Any baseline fatigue vs none/minimal was associated with higher odds of grade ≥3 toxicity (OR 2.11, 95% CI 1.59-2.78; P<.001), grade ≥4 (OR 1.98, 95% CI 1.39-2.82; P<.001), and grade 5/fatal toxicity (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.07-5.19; P=.03); a dose-response was seen, with 'quite a lot/very much' fatigue conferring ~5-fold higher odds of fatal toxicity (OR 4.99, 95% CI 1.84-13.51; P=.002). Findings were consistent across symptomatic, hematologic, and nonhematologic AE categories. Baseline fatigue may serve as an early clinical marker of toxicity risk to inform individualized treatment planning and symptom monitoring.
